scope: Indonesia-first with Phase 2 ASEAN job discovery

jobs.title: Marketing Dealer
jobs.description:
cun motor ponorogo membuka lowongan posisi marketing dealer. tugas utama meliputi penjualan produk sepeda motor honda, menjalankan kegiatan promosi di lapangan serta event perusahaan, dan memanfaatkan media sosial untuk meningkatkan penjualan. fasilitas mencakup komisi penjualan, tunjangan absensi, bonus bulanan dan triwulan, jenjang karir, serta pelatihan pengembangan diri.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat dengan fresh graduate dipersilakan melamar. memiliki pengalaman kerja di bidang sales atau marketing khususnya industri otomotif menjadi nilai tambah. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi, negosiasi, dan persuasi yang baik. berorientasi pada target dan mampu bekerja di bawah tekanan. aktif menggunakan media sosial sebagai sarana penjualan. memiliki kendaraan pribadi serta sim c. berpenampilan rapi, percaya diri, dan memiliki sikap kerja yang baik. bersedia bekerja secara mobile di lapangan dan mengikuti kegiatan promosi serta event perusahaan.

jobs.title: Sales & Operational Manager, Sales/Retailer Officer (RO), Admin & Creative
jobs.description:
berkah taniijo membuka kesempatan kerja untuk tiga posisi: sales & operational manager untuk wilayah jawa tengah-diy, sales/retailer officer (ro) dengan penempatan di pemalang atau ungaran, serta admin & creative yang berbasis di magelang. posisi ini mencakup tanggung jawab manajerial, operasional lapangan, serta pengelolaan konten kreatif dan administrasi.

untuk sales & operational manager: s1 dengan pengalaman minimal 3 tahun, mampu memimpin tim, analisis, problem solving, disiplin, jujur, bertanggung jawab, domisili magelang, dan bersedia mobile di jateng-diy. untuk sales/retailer officer: minimal d3, diutamakan berpengalaman sales distribusi, komunikatif, negosiasi, pelayanan pelanggan, siap kerja lapangan, jujur, dan proaktif. untuk admin & creative: minimal d3-s1 semua jurusan, menguasai administrasi, media sosial, desain grafis (canva), mampu dokumentasi foto/video, memahami dasar coding (nilai tambah), dan wajib melampirkan portofolio.

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
bukuwarung sedang mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk melakukan akuisisi merchant dan penjualan mesin edc di berbagai wilayah di jawa tengah dan diy. posisi ini bertanggung jawab untuk memperluas jaringan merchant dengan dukungan gaji pokok, tunjangan pulsa dan transportasi, serta jaminan bpjs.

pria atau wanita dengan usia maksimal 35 tahun dan pendidikan minimal sma sederajat. kandidat wajib memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, serta memiliki kendaraan roda dua dan sim c aktif. pengalaman dalam menjual mesin edc dan akuisisi sangat diutamakan.

jobs.title: Team Event
jobs.description:
posisi team event di pt. primafood international batam bertanggung jawab dalam pengelolaan event, pelaksanaan strategi marketing, serta melakukan perjalanan mobile untuk mendukung operasional ritel modern.

pria atau wanita, lulusan minimal sma/smk semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman minimal 1 tahun di bidang retail, sales marketing, atau event organizer. menguasai ms. office, memiliki kemampuan negosiasi dan public speaking yang baik, serta mampu melakukan analisa data. wajib memiliki kendaraan bermotor dan sim c (sim a lebih disukai) serta bersedia melakukan perjalanan mobile.

jobs.title: Junior Online Picker
jobs.description:
posisi junior online picker di tetangga teknik bertugas mengelola dan memproses pesanan masuk dari platform online shopee dan tiktok hingga diserahkan ke jasa kurir. selain itu, posisi ini bertanggung jawab melayani pelanggan yang datang ke toko offline maupun melalui pesan whatsapp, memberikan rekomendasi produk terkait alat teknik dan suku cadang, menjaga ketersediaan stok barang toko, serta membantu penerimaan barang masuk dari pusat atau pemasok.

kandidat pria dengan pendidikan minimal smk (latar belakang teknik mesin menjadi nilai tambah). bersedia menginap di mess yang disediakan di toko. memiliki pengetahuan seputar microsoft excel menjadi nilai tambah. jujur, memiliki niat bekerja yang tinggi, dan terbuka untuk lulusan baru (fresh graduate). pelamar pria tidak harus berdomisili di area tangerang.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi middle mile supervisor di spx express surabaya bertanggung jawab untuk memantau dan memimpin operasional middle mile baik dari 3pl maupun in house. anda akan bekerja sama dengan tim lm, mm, dan fm untuk mengelola lead time, durasi pengiriman, dan kebutuhan trip. selain itu, anda bertugas berkoordinasi dengan tim fleet untuk memastikan kesiapan unit, melakukan pemetaan rute, memaksimalkan penggunaan unit, serta mengalokasikan perencanaan sumber daya untuk implementasi baru di distribution center.

pendidikan minimal sma atau diploma dari jurusan apapun. memiliki pengalaman kerja selama 3-5 tahun di industri transportasi, logistik, atau rantai pasokan. berpengalaman dalam menangani operasi darat, udara, maupun laut. mahir mengoperasikan microsoft office dan memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shifting dan ditempatkan di area yang telah ditentukan.

jobs.title: Procurement Officer, Global Procurement (Multi-Category Generalist)
jobs.description:
**Background**

The Global Procurement Unit, within Global Supply Chain, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for IRC. It is organized around categories, with category owners responsible for sourcing strategy, supplier ecosystem development, and contract and supplier performance across programmatic and corporate spend.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Officer provides procurement execution support for assigned corporate and professional services requests, under the guidance and review of the Senior Manager and relevant category owners. Assignments are limited to an agreed subset of travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, and People & Culture services, based on workload and complexity. The officer maintains audit-ready records and supports value for money, timely procurement and compliance with applicable IRC requirements.

The Procurement Officer is a hands-on, execution-focused individual contributor supporting assigned sourcing, contract administration and supplier follow-up. The line manager and category owners provide direction and review the officer’s work; category strategy, complex negotiations and award approvals remain with authorized leads.

The role enables IRC to move quickly without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Officer is the day-to-day procurement focal point for assigned requests and escalates material risks, exceptions, and strategic decisions to the category owner or Senior Manager.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Category Coverage and Procurement Planning**

- Support assigned sourcing events, renewals and supplier requests from intake to award recommendation, under the guidance and review of the line manager and category owners and in line with agreed priorities.
- Analyze spend and market data to support demand aggregation and procurement plans for assigned requests, following IRC standard operating procedures and agreed timelines.
- Support category owners with market assessments and supplier landscape reviews for assigned categories, including ahead of framework renewals, by compiling information on capability, pricing, lead times, risk and total cost of ownership.
- Provide evidence and options to support category strategy and supplier selection; maintain approved supplier lists and support the establishment of framework agreements under category-owner guidance.
- Prepare documentation for justified waiver and single-source requests and route them through the required approval process.

**B. Sourcing Execution and Negotiation**

- Support requests for information (RFI), proposals (RFP) and tenders by coordinating bidder communications and preparing evaluation records, commercial comparisons and draft award recommendations. Run assigned requests for quotation (RFQ) under the guidance and review of the line manager or category owner and within delegated authority.
- Help business teams prepare clear specifications, scopes of work and evaluation criteria.
- Support negotiation of pricing, terms, service levels and performance commitments under the direction of the line manager or category owner and within the agreed mandate.
- Identify procurement savings opportunities through price benchmarking and competitive sourcing. Calculate and document hard savings and cost avoidance separately against approved baselines, submit them for validation under IRC's methodology, and avoid double counting.
- Support requesters with procurement intake forms (PIFs) and purchase requisitions (PRs), and create and track purchase orders (POs) in Integra as assigned under approved workflows. Provide procurement documentation for payment requests in ServiceNow, maintaining segregation of duties.
- Process assigned urgent and emergency procurement requests under approved procedures, using available frameworks where appropriate and documenting required approvals. Follow up supplier milestones and coordinate delivery with the responsible operational teams; escalate delays and capacity constraints to the line manager.

**C. Category-Specific Sourcing Support**

The officer supports a defined subset of the following corporate and professional services categories, agreed with the line manager. Assignments are proportionate to the role’s grade and workload and do not imply responsibility for all categories simultaneously.

- **People & Culture services:** support sourcing of recruitment, staffing, payroll, benefits and learning providers, coordinating reviews with People & Culture, Legal and Finance as applicable.
- **Travel:** support sourcing and administration of travel provider agreements, comparing rates, fees and service levels with input from the responsible travel and duty-of-care teams.
- **Translation services:** support sourcing and administration of translation and interpretation agreements, comparing rates, turnaround times and service requirements with relevant business teams.
- **Insurance:** support sourcing and administration of insurance provider and broker agreements, coordinating documentation and specialist reviews with the responsible business owners, Legal and Finance.
- **Cash and financial services:** support sourcing of financial service and payment providers with Finance, Treasury and program teams, coordinating required licensing, financial, screening and data protection reviews.

**D. Contracting, Framework Agreements and Supplier Performance**

- Prepare contract, framework agreement and statement-of-work drafts using approved templates. Coordinate Legal and specialist review of applicable clauses, route documents for authorized signature, and maintain executed agreements and amendments.
- Administer assigned framework agreements and contracts: maintain approved price lists, supplier records, expiry and notice dates; alert stakeholders early to renewal needs; and communicate approved terms to relevant requesters and Country Programs.
- Maintain scorecards for designated suppliers, coordinate reviews according to the agreed schedule and supplier tier, and record agreed improvement actions with business owners.
- Resolve routine supplier and contract queries within the agreed mandate, escalate material issues, and coordinate follow-up on agreed corrective actions. Liaise with Accounts Payable and requesters on payment delays and report recurring causes.

**E. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate vendor risk assessments and due diligence, risk-based and proportionate to category, value, and data sensitivity: conflict of interest, code of conduct, sanctions, anti-terrorism (ATC) and debarment screening, privacy and data protection, information security, legal, donor compliance, financial viability, implementation risk, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Track required reviews and clearances with Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, Compliance and Finance before the applicable award or commitment stage. Escalate outstanding reviews; specialist assessments and risk acceptance remain with authorized functions.
- Identify and escalate requests involving high-risk suppliers, personal or confidential data, AI-enabled tools, client-facing services, or unapproved vendors; for AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC's AI governance and assessment requirements.
- Keep procurement files complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements, stored in Box; track and follow up missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews; support audit document retrieval.

**F. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented support, helping stakeholders move through the process without unnecessary delay while maintaining compliance and risk controls; serve as first point of contact for routine queries and guidance on global vendors and frameworks.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines, and encourage early engagement before commitments are made to vendors.
- Support the rollout of category sourcing guides, tools, and SOPs, including communication and training materials, and track adoption and gaps.

**G. Reporting, Spend Analytics and Continuous Improvement**

- Maintain the sourcing tracker for assigned activities, covering status, cycle time, approvals, risks, documentation and validated benefits. Report progress and recurring intake or requisition issues to the line manager and relevant category owners.
- Extract, clean and validate Integra data for assigned spend analyses and draft review reports. Report against agreed performance indicators, flag material trends and suggest practical improvements.
- Identify recurring issues across categories and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Internal:** Senior Manager, Global Procurement – Corporate & Professional Services; relevant category owners and Global Procurement peers; Global Supply Chain, Country Program and regional supply chain teams; People & Culture; Finance, Treasury and Accounts Payable; travel and duty-of-care teams; relevant business owners; IT and Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Master Data Management; and other specialist reviewers as required for assigned requests.
- **External:** Vendors, service providers, brokers and agencies within the assigned corporate and professional services portfolio; financial service providers; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

- Bachelor's degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, finance, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- At least 2 years of procurement or sourcing experience, preferably in corporate and professional services or indirect procurement.
- Experience supporting competitive sourcing processes (RFQs, RFPs and tenders) and exposure to contract negotiations.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and compliance risk reviews, including data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Proficiency in Excel and ERP or procurement systems; ability to prepare accurate spend analysis and reports.
- Fluency in written and spoken English, with strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal stakeholders across diverse functions.
- Strong organizational skills to manage assigned procurement activities and deadlines, identify workload conflicts early, and exercise sound judgment on compliance and escalation.

**Preferred**

- Professional procurement certification such as CIPS (Level 2 or above), CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- NGO, humanitarian, or donor-funded organization experience, including familiarity with donor requirements such as U.S. Government (e.g. State Department), FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Experience in one or more of the assigned categories (travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, or People & Culture services), and willingness to develop knowledge of other categories within the agreed portfolio.
- Experience with Microsoft D365, ServiceNow, Power BI, or similar procurement, workflow, and analytics tools.
- Experience with contract and supplier performance management, framework agreements, and emergency procurement.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Country Director
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The mission of the IRC is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future.

**IRC Chad strategy**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of Darfur refugees into eastern Chad, starting with the Ouré Cassoni refugee camp. Today, the IRC supports Sudanese refugees and host communities in 14 camps and host villages in the east, and since April 2023 has expanded its response to assist refugees fleeing the conflict in Sudan. Services in the east include health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), economic recovery and development, women’s empowerment and protection. The IRC also works in Guéra province to address malnutrition and in the Lac region to respond to the Boko Haram crisis, with projects in health, nutrition, protection and response to gender-based violence. Across the country, IRC Chad combines humanitarian, nexus and development responses to help the most affected populations exercise their rights with dignity and access quality basic social services that meet their needs.

IRC Chad’s strategy focuses on three outcome areas: health (nutrition, child health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and climate-resilient WASH), safety (high-impact targeted individual assistance) and economic wellbeing (food security, basic needs, early recovery and resilience). It is underpinned by commitments to gender equality, diversity and inclusion, cash and voucher assistance, and investment in partnerships with relevant ministries and local partners.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director will provide the strategic vision and leadership for the country program with the primary focus on ensuring IRC Chad’s programs meet the expressed needs of the beneficiaries we serve. S/he is responsible for ensuring the delivery of quality programs, maintaining/expanding donor and government relations, engaging strategic local organizations, fundraising and budget management, security and operations management, and developing a motivated and professional team.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary leadership abilities who deploys strong communications and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will enjoy developing networks to build partnerships and diversify program resources. Given the operating environment, the Country Director is expected to be attentive to risk management. S/he will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design and deliver responsive, high-quality programs; ensuring efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance and focused, timely reporting; and oversight of financial management and compliance systems.

Reporting to the Regional Vice President, this position receives support from regional and headquarters staff in the areas of program quality, new business development, safety and security management, finance, operations management, and external affairs. The Country Director is additionally expected to actively participate in defining the IRC’s public advocacy positions.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Provide exemplary leadership by fostering a strong team spirit, open communication, and an inclusive and empowering work environment.
- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with: Chad Government authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private); UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups.
- Position IRC as a key partner for major international donors and seize opportunities to promote IRC’s work.
- Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Initiate and sustain strong, mutually beneficial, and authentic partnerships with Chadian organizations.
- Seek out and pursue opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Chad, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Development***

- Ensure that the country program’s strategic vision and direction are aligned with the IRC’s strategy to serve populations through responsive, high-quality, and accountable programming, and secure the necessary resources for its implementation.
- Ensure the country program’s alignment with the IRC strategy and the implementation of the strategic action plan.
- Ensure program quality through rigorous design, M&E, and accountability processes, and investments in staff development and partner capacity sharing.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure country program alignment with and involvement in meeting regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities to expand programming and ensure continuous contextual monitoring.
- Oversee the development and submission of competitive, high-quality proposals; lead partnerships with local civil society organizations in line with PEERS standards, lead negotiations with donors; and build relationships with Chad Ministries.

***Safety Security and Access Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Oversee the management of all security issues, including appropriate response to emergency situations as they arise.
- Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including trainings and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation and contingency plans up to date and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety & Security Director on safety security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.

***Staff Performance Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide constructive feedback and counsel on appropriate career paths and professional development for IRC staff.
- Oversee the management, coaching and development of all staff to build a cadre of skilled, committed and motivated personnel.
- Pursue nationalization of senior management positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Undertake regular reviews of labor laws, and salary markets in Chad for the purpose of enhancing the competitiveness of the IRC’s overall compensation package for team members.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to comply with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure appropriate support for all departments (HR, Finance, Supply Chain) and the consistent implementation of the IRC Way.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Chad country program’s financial position.
- Ensure rigorous budget monitoring of grants and discretionary funds and identify opportunities for operational optimization

***Communications***

- Model and encourage active practice of the principles of the “IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct” throughout the Chad country program.
- Maintain a healthy and empowering office environment that encourages open, honest and productive communication among IRC staff and with partner organizations.
- Maintain open communication with regional management staff, regional technical advisors, and HQ departmental staff.

**KEY REPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**The position reports to**: Regional Vice President, WACAR

**The position directly supervises:** Deputy Director Programs, the Deputy Director of Finance, the Deputy Director Field Management, the People and Culture Coordinator, Humanitarian Access and Security Coordinator, Communication and media coordinator, Safeguarding and Compliance Coordinator.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

- Graduate degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience
- At least seven years of progressively responsible international work experience, including at least three years in a leadership role at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment.
- Experience of building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization
- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in a cross-cultural setting, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and international development donors.
- Experience of managing security in a fluid environment
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations. Experience with organizational capacity strengthening and partnership building helpful.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities
- Established capacity to deal with ambiguity in stressful situations.
- French and English fluency
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Previous experience working in Chad or in the West and Central Africa region preferred.

This position is based in N’djamena and is fully accompanied with an estimated 33% of the Country Director’s time spent in other locations in Chad and the region.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**CONTEXTE**

L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) répond aux pires crises humanitaires du monde et aide les populations à survivre et à reconstruire leur vie. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC apporte des soins vitaux et une aide qui transforme des vies, notamment auprès des réfugiés contraints de fuir la guerre ou les catastrophes. Présente aujourd’hui dans plus de 40 pays, l’IRC rétablit la sécurité, la dignité et l’espoir pour des millions de personnes qui luttent pour leur survie. Sa mission est d’aider les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été brisés par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, à se relever et à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir.

**Stratégie de l’IRC au Tchad**

L’IRC a lancé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire provoquée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour dans l’est du pays, en commençant par le camp de réfugiés d’Ouré Cassoni. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC soutient les réfugiés soudanais et les communautés d’accueil dans 14 camps et villages d’accueil de l’Est et, depuis avril 2023, a élargi son intervention pour venir en aide aux réfugiés fuyant le conflit au Soudan. Les services fournis dans l’Est comprennent la santé, la nutrition, l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement (EHA), le relèvement et le développement économiques, l’autonomisation des femmes et la protection. L’IRC intervient également dans la province du Guéra pour lutter contre la malnutrition, et dans la région du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram, avec des projets en santé, nutrition, protection et réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG). Dans l’ensemble du pays, l’IRC Tchad combine réponses humanitaires, approches de nexus et actions de développement afin d’aider les populations les plus touchées à exercer leurs droits dans la dignité et à accéder à des services sociaux de base de qualité répondant à leurs besoins.

La stratégie de l’IRC Tchad s’articule autour de trois domaines de résultats : la santé (nutrition, santé de l’enfant, santé et droits sexuels et reproductifs, et EHA résilient face au changement climatique), la sûreté (assistance individuelle ciblée à fort impact) et le bien-être économique (sécurité alimentaire, besoins de base, relèvement précoce et résilience). Elle repose sur des engagements en faveur de l’égalité de genre, de la diversité et de l’inclusion, de l’assistance en espèces et par coupons, ainsi que sur l’investissement dans des partenariats avec les ministères concernés et les partenaires locaux.

**PÉRIMÈTRE DU POSTE**

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays assure la vision stratégique et le leadership du programme pays, avec pour priorité de garantir que les programmes de l’IRC Tchad répondent aux besoins exprimés par les bénéficiaires que nous servons. Il/elle est chargé(e) de veiller à la qualité des programmes, d’entretenir et d’élargir les relations avec les bailleurs et le gouvernement, de mobiliser des organisations locales stratégiques, d’assurer la levée de fonds et la gestion budgétaire, de superviser la sécurité et les opérations, ainsi que de constituer une équipe motivée et professionnelle.

La réussite à ce poste exige une personne dotée d’un leadership exemplaire, capable de mobiliser efficacement de solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, tant en interne qu’en externe. Le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) devra développer des réseaux afin de bâtir des partenariats et de diversifier les ressources des programmes. Compte tenu du contexte d’intervention, le/la Directeur(trice) Pays doit porter une attention particulière à la gestion des risques. Il/elle est directement responsable de la coordination d’ensemble et de l’orientation stratégique du programme pays ; assure la supervision et le coaching des cadres supérieurs qu’il/elle encadre directement ; dirige les équipes du programme pays dans l’identification, la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes réactifs et de grande qualité ; veille à une gestion efficiente des subventions publiques et des fonds privés, axée sur les résultats, la conformité et la remise de rapports ciblés dans les délais ; et supervise les systèmes de gestion financière et de conformité.

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays, placé(e) sous l’autorité du/de la Vice-Président(e) régional(e), bénéficie de l’appui du personnel régional et du siège en matière de qualité des programmes, de développement de nouvelles opportunités de financement, de gestion de la sûreté et de la sécurité, de finances, de gestion des opérations et d’affaires extérieures. Il/elle est en outre appelé(e) à participer activement à la définition des positions de plaidoyer public de l’IRC.

**RESPONSABILITÉS SPÉCIFIQUES**

***Leadership et Représentation***

- Faire preuve d’un leadership exemplaire en favorisant un fort esprit d’équipe, une communication ouverte et un environnement de travail inclusif et valorisant.
- Développer et entretenir des relations stratégiques avec : les autorités gouvernementales tchadiennes à différents niveaux ; les bailleurs de fonds (institutionnels, non institutionnels et privés), dont l’Union européenne ; les Nations Unies et les autres organisations internationales ; les ONG internationales et locales ; ainsi que les réseaux tels que les mécanismes de coordination des ONG internationales et les groupes de travail pertinents.
- Positionner l’IRC comme un partenaire clé des grands bailleurs de fonds internationaux et saisir les occasions de promouvoir son action.
- Acquérir et maintenir une connaissance approfondie des priorités des bailleurs et des financements qu’ils prévoient.
- Nouer et entretenir des partenariats solides, authentiques et mutuellement bénéfiques avec des organisations tchadiennes.
- Rechercher et saisir les occasions de mieux faire connaître le travail de l’IRC et de ses partenaires au Tchad, ainsi que les conditions de vie et les besoins des personnes que l’IRC s’efforce de servir.

***Orientation Stratégique, Qualité et Développement des programmes***

- Veiller à ce que la vision et l’orientation stratégiques du programme pays soient alignées sur la stratégie de l’IRC afin de servir les populations à travers des programmes réactifs, de grande qualité et redevables, et mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre.
- Veiller à l’alignement du programme pays sur la stratégie de l’IRC et à la mise en œuvre du plan d’action stratégique.
- Garantir la qualité des programmes grâce à une conception rigoureuse, à des processus de suivi-évaluation et de redevabilité, ainsi qu’à des investissements dans le développement du personnel et le renforcement des capacités des partenaires.
- Se tenir informé(e) des enjeux nationaux et régionaux qui touchent le programme pays et les partenaires, et élaborer des stratégies adaptées afin de pouvoir poursuivre la mission de l’IRC de manière appropriée en cas d’évolution du contexte.
- Veiller à ce que le programme pays soit aligné sur les objectifs régionaux et contribue à leur réalisation.
- Identifier les possibilités d’extension de la programmation et suivre en continu l’évolution du contexte.
- Superviser l’élaboration et la soumission de propositions compétitives et de grande qualité ; piloter les partenariats avec les organisations locales de la société civile conformément aux standards PEERS ; mener les négociations avec les bailleurs ; et nouer des relations avec les ministères tchadiens.

***Gestion de la sûreté, de la sécurité et de l’accès***

- Assumer la responsabilité principale de la gestion globale de la sûreté et de la sécurité du programme pays.
- Superviser la gestion de toutes les questions de sécurité, y compris la réponse adaptée aux situations d’urgence au fur et à mesure qu’elles surviennent.
- Créer et entretenir, au sein du programme pays, une culture de sensibilisation à la sûreté et à la sécurité, notamment par des formations et des séances d’information qui préparent l’ensemble du personnel à prévenir les incidents de sécurité et à y répondre.
- Tenir à jour les plans de sécurité, d’évacuation et de contingence, et les rendre accessibles au personnel du programme pays.
- Maintenir une coordination et une communication étroites avec le/la Directeur(trice) régional(e) de la sûreté et de la sécurité au sujet des préoccupations en la matière et des évolutions susceptibles de nuire au personnel ou aux opérations de l’IRC.

***Gestion de la performance et développement du personnel***

- Encadrer et accompagner les collaborateurs placés sous sa responsabilité directe, notamment en communiquant des attentes claires, en fixant des objectifs de performance, en leur donnant régulièrement et en temps utile un retour sur leur performance, et en conduisant des évaluations semestrielles documentées.
- Donner au personnel de l’IRC des retours constructifs et des conseils sur son parcours de carrière et son développement professionnel.
- Superviser la gestion, le coaching et le développement de l’ensemble du personnel afin de constituer un vivier de collaborateurs compétents, engagés et motivés.
- Poursuivre la nationalisation des postes d’encadrement supérieur.
- Promouvoir et suivre la prise en charge et le bien-être du personnel. Montrer l’exemple en matière d’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée. Soutenir les interventions adaptées aux besoins de bien-être identifiés, tant pour le personnel national que pour le personnel international.
- Examiner régulièrement la législation du travail et les niveaux de salaire pratiqués sur le marché au Tchad afin de renforcer la compétitivité de l’ensemble du dispositif de rémunération de l’IRC pour les membres de l’équipe.

***Gestion responsable des ressources et des opérations***

- Promouvoir l’excellence opérationnelle afin d’atteindre une efficience et un rapport coût-efficacité optimaux dans l’ensemble des fonctions et opérations du programme pays.
- Superviser l’élaboration, le déploiement et l’utilisation de politiques, procédures et systèmes financiers et opérationnels conformes aux exigences de l’IRC et des bailleurs.
- Assurer un appui adéquat à l’ensemble des départements (RH, Finance, Chaîne d’approvisionnement) et veiller à la mise en œuvre cohérente de l’IRC Way.
- Assurer une supervision rapide et efficace de la situation financière du programme pays du Tchad.
- Assurer un suivi budgétaire rigoureux des subventions et des fonds discrétionnaires et identifier les possibilités d’optimisation opérationnelle.

***Communication***

- Incarner les principes de « l’IRC Way – Normes globales de conduite professionnelle », et en encourager activement l’application dans l’ensemble du programme pays du Tchad.
- Maintenir un environnement de travail sain et valorisant, qui favorise une communication ouverte, honnête et productive entre les membres du personnel de l’IRC et avec les organisations partenaires.
- Maintenir une communication ouverte avec l’équipe de direction régionale, les conseillers techniques régionaux et le personnel des départements du siège.

**PRINCIPALES RELATIONS HIÉRARCHIQUES ET FONCTIONNELLES :**

**Le poste est rattaché à** : Vice-Président(e) régional(e), WACAR

**Le poste encadre directement :**le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Programmes, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Finances, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Gestion du terrain, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Personnes et Culture, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Acces Humanitaire et Sécurité, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Communication et médias, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Sauvegarde et Conformité

**Principaux contacts internes :** Équipe régionale WACAR ; Gestion des subventions, Opérations et Stratégie, Finance, Qualité des programmes, Plaidoyer, Département juridique, Éthique et Conformité ; autres Directeurs(trices) Pays de la région WACAR ; personnel des départements du siège, selon les besoins.

**Principaux contacts externes :** Organisations partenaires, représentants du gouvernement du pays d’accueil, agences de bailleurs publics et privés, ONG internationales et nationales, agences des Nations Unies, gouvernements étrangers.

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

- Diplôme de niveau master (bac+5) dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience équivalente.
- Au moins sept ans d’expérience internationale à des postes de responsabilité croissante, dont au moins trois ans à un poste de direction de niveau Directeur(trice) Pays, à la tête d’opérations multisites et multisectorielles dans un environnement d’intervention complexe.
- Expérience dans la constitution de réseaux personnels de haut niveau, ayant permis d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives à l’organisation.
- Expérience avérée de leadership et de gestion d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire en contexte interculturel, avec un mentorat et un coaching actifs.
- Expérience avérée de supervision, à un niveau approprié, d’un portefeuille de projets complexes de grande envergure financés par des bailleurs.
- Solide expérience de représentation et de levée de fonds, y compris auprès de bailleurs européens, américains et d’autres bailleurs internationaux du développement.
- Expérience en gestion de la sécurité dans un environnement instable.
- Capacité avérée à négocier et à collaborer avec des organisations partenaires. Une expérience en renforcement des capacités organisationnelles et en développement de partenariats est un atout.
- Solides compétences en supervision budgétaire et financière.
- Capacité confirmée à gérer l’ambiguïté en situation de stress.
- Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans les délais impartis, tout en produisant des résultats de grande qualité.
- Une expérience préalable au Tchad ou en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre est souhaitée.

Ce poste est basé à N’Djamena, en statut accompagné. Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays consacrera environ 33 % de son temps à des déplacements dans d’autres localités du Tchad et de la région.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

jobs.title: Oficial de Preparación de Desastres - Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Preparación de Desastres** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**:

Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Base / Líder de Equipo de Preparación para Desastres (DP), el/la oficial de DP estará directamente involucrado y velará por la ejecución diaria de las actividades de DP, especialmente en las áreas de intervención. Apoyará al Líder de Equipo en la facilitación de actividades de DP, elaboración de materiales de información, apoyo en las comunicaciones y sensibilizaciones a personas con necesidades específicas. El/la oficial de DP apoyará al líder de equipo con las actividades de Acción anticipatoria y respuesta ante desastres.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

- Apoyar al líder de equipo a identificar las necesidades de evaluación ralacionadas a DP en los desplazados internos y las comunidades de acogida en Zulia y en cualquier otra zona.
- Apoyar la identificación y selección de los beneficiarios con la ayuda de las autoridades locales y otras derivadas de los equipos de protección, Recuperación Económica y WASH. Además, contribuir que se establezcan los informes correctos de entendimiento con los proveedores de servicios relevantes/partes interesadas.
- Implementar los proyectos de DP utilizando las herramientas adecuadas para garantizar los entregables a tiempo, dentro de presupuesto y con la calidad esperada.
- Tomar en cuenta las vulnerabilidades de las comunidades con Riesgos de protección y participar en cada uno de los ciclos de proyectos relacionados con las actividades de DP.
- Participar en las capacitaciones sobre DP, Acciones Anticipatorias y también apoyar las actividades de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias de WASH.
- Contribuir a la elaboración de materiales de formación y orientación. Documentar los resultados y las lecciones aprendidas de la implementación del programa de DP y Acciones Anticipatorias, incluida la preparación y respuesta ante emergencias, para promover el intercambio de conocimientos con las contrapartes y las partes interesadas en materia de DP.
- Apoyar con el enlace con otros actores/ONG relevantes, administradores locales y líderes de desplazados internos para los esfuerzos de colaboración, entre otros.
- Asegurar que todas las partes interesadas relevantes tengan información sobre los antecedentes, el programa, los objetivos, las áreas de trabajo, la duración de los programas y las actividades en el campo de la organización.
- Completar los formularios y la documentación adecuada del sector DP para los proyectos de intervención, incluido el transporte de coordenadas GPS y el mapeo de las actividades/áreas del proyecto, entre otras.
- Contribuir con la planificación de contingencias para una posible respuesta de emergencia en materia de DP.
- Apoyar el proyecto de DP con la estrecha coordinación del Gerente de Programa y el especialista de DP.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el equipo de DP.
- Desarrollar/apoyar con simulacros y ejercicios de preparación para garantizar la eficiencia del equipo.
- Contribuir en el desarrollo e implementación de planes integrales de preparación ante desastres.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia en el campo de DP, Acciones Anticipatorias y otros.
- Excelente comprensión de la capacitación básica en programación de DP, métodos de capacitación participativa, movilizaciones comunitarias y creación de redes.
- Licenciado en Trabajo Humanitario, Licenciatura en Administración de desastres, Ciencias Políticas, Ciencias Ambientales y otras carreras afines o similares. Los estudios superiores agregan valor para el proceso de selección.
- Implementación efectiva y oportuna de todas las intervenciones descritas en el proyecto y cualquier otra actividad programática relacionada con DP.
- Experiencia laboral y conocimiento del lugar de destino local.
- Capaz de adaptarse a situaciones cambiantes según sea necesario.
- Capaz de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.

Deseable:

- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de Protección, WASH o Recuperación Económica.
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de liderar un equipo y crear buen ambiente de equipo;
- Manejo del inglés
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**DRC como empleador**
Al trabajar en DRC, te unirás a una fuerza laboral global de alrededor de 6000 empleados en 30 países. Nos enorgullecemos de nuestro:

- Profesionalismo, impacto y experiencia
- Enfoque humanitario y el trabajo que realizamos
- Propósito, significado y contribución personal
- Cultura, valores y liderazgo sólido
- Compensación justa y desarrollo continuo

jobs.title: Grants, Partnerships and Communication Coordinator
jobs.description:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

***Fluency in both English & Spanish required***.

***Funding until September 30, 2027, potential to extend***.

**BACKGROUND**

Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.

In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.

The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

**Purpose of the role:** IRC Colombia and Venezuela is seeking an experienced business development, grants, and partnerships professional for the role of Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator. This role is responsible for leading resource mobilization and the timely production of high-quality funding proposals, modification requests and donor reports; playing a lead role in the full award management cycle, including compliance; facilitating partnership development and management processes; leading the communications strategy that positions the IRC’s work with donors, partners and the public and protects the organization’s reputation; and coordinating grants management-related capacity building efforts among IRC staff and partners. The Grants, and Partnerships Coordinator ensures the quality of and efficient processes for proposal development and grants management, and manages the delivery of the IRC’s partnership ambitions while supporting program coordinators and country leadership to ensure that IRC Colombia and Venezuela lives up to the partnership principles of responsibility, results-oriented approaches, equality, transparency, and complementarity.

The postholder will need to work under tight deadlines and deal with competing and changing priorities. The postholder will need to gather inputs by influencing other functions and roles while submitting quality and timely deliverables, will work with diverse country, region and headquarters-based teams, and will need to ensure adherence to organizational and donor compliance requirements. The position will be based in Bogota with frequent visits to field sites in Colombia and Venezuela.

**Scope and authority:** The Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator will lead a team of 15 members (both direct and indirect) divided in three sub-teams: grants, partnerships, and communications. The postholder will line manage 6 direct reports.

**Key Accountabilities & responsibilities:**

***Business Development and Resource Mobilization:***

- Lead the development and annual update of a resource mobilization strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country Strategy Action Plan, with clear targets by donor, sector and geography.
- Manage the funding pipeline: investigate and track funding opportunities, maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker, and regularly report on its status to country leadership.
- Lead the Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, assessing strategic fit, competitiveness, implementation capacity, risks, cost recovery and compliance requirements, and facilitate timely decisions with country leadership.
- Drive donor diversification and positioning beyond traditional institutional donors, including pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund), multilateral agencies and development banks, the private sector and foundations, and funding dedicated to localization and to partnerships with local organizations.
- Lead program design workshops for new business development opportunities with relevant IRC staff, and partners’ staff where applicable.
- Develop, lead, and track proposal development processes, including consortium proposals, directly coordinating and managing the development of proposals and concept notes in collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders; write sections of proposals and conduct final reviews, editing, and polishing of proposal documents for accuracy and quality control.
- Assist in compiling and editing proposal budgets and ensure communication and coordination between all departments (finance, programs, and operations) in drafting of budgets, bringing a strategic and competitive lens to the process.

***Grants/Sub-Grants Management:***

- Ensure that IRC awards and sub-awards in Colombia and Venezuela are well-administered and implemented in compliance with the relevant donor regulations and IRC procedures throughout the full award cycle.
- Lead award start-up, including grant summaries and kick-off meetings (pre-award and opening meetings) with programs, finance, operations and partners, so that all teams understand donor requirements from the outset.
- Lead the review and negotiation of grant and sub-grant agreements, in coordination with the Awards Management Unit, finance and other relevant departments.
- Coordinate award modifications, including cost and no-cost extensions, budget realignments and changes in scope, ensuring timely submission and donor approval.
- Take the lead on internal and external reporting in coordination with programs, MEAL, and finance, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and IRC requirements. Maintain close collaboration with all relevant departments in preparation of donor reports.
- Maintain award tracking systems, including the grants tracker, reporting and deadline calendars and award dashboards, ensuring that information is accurate and available to budget holders and senior management.
- Supervise the GPU in the coordination and facilitation of project cycle meetings.
- Lead award close-out processes, ensuring that final reports, financial reconciliation, asset disposition and documentation are completed on time.
- Coordinate the preparation for and follow-up of donor audits, verifications and monitoring visits, including the implementation of their recommendations.
- Play a significant role in efforts to strengthen and maintain country program project management capacities.
- Ensure that sub-grantees are being monitored for donor compliance and progress against objectives, and that key compliance monitoring information and learning are documented.
- Assist program technical leads, operations staff, and partners with understanding the reporting and other compliance requirements on their grants and sub-grants.
- Proactively identify compliance risks throughout the portfolio and advise programs, operations, finance and senior management on necessary actions.

***Partnerships Management:***

- Play a lead role in stakeholder analysis and potential partner mapping and vetting.
- Working closely with other senior staff, play a lead role in identifying, liaising on, and negotiating teaming arrangements with potential partners; collaborate with other departments as needed to verify and issue various types of partnership agreements.
- Ensure and coordinate adherence to IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) in the selection and management of IRC Colombia and Venezuela’s partnerships.
- Co-lead the review of the performance of different partnerships, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Support country leadership in promoting an enabling environment for effective work in partnership.
- Provide a quarterly Partnership Management Report to the CD, incorporating input from technical coordinators and operational leads as appropriate.

***Staff management and capacity building***

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of donor policies, regulations, and procedures and build this knowledge among grants team members.
- Build grant management capacity of field staff, and provide supportive supervision in report writing, budget management, indicator tracking, IRC-specific tools, and other topics as/if needed.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Maintain documentation of institutional knowledge and program activities in coordination with relevant sector coordinators and department leads.

***Communications***

- **Communications strategy:** Lead the development and implementation of a communications strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country strategy, resource mobilization priorities and IRC regional and global communications.
- **Brand management and visibility:** Ensure consistent and appropriate use of the IRC brand across materials, events, field sites and partner activities; provide advice on donor visibility requirements and proactively engage with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility.
- **Creation of communication materials:** Lead Colombia and Venezuela’s efforts in designing, writing and editing key communication materials (factsheets, capacity statements, stories from the field, digital content or special reports on IRC’s activities) in coordination with DDPs, program leads, and sector and field coordinators.
- **Crisis communications and reputational risk:** Develop and maintain protocols for crisis communications and reputational risk management, and advise the CD and senior management on sensitive issues, including security, data protection and the political context in Colombia and Venezuela.
- **Internal communications:** Promote clear and timely internal communication across offices and teams in Colombia and Venezuela, so that staff are informed about the country program’s priorities, results and key decisions.
- **Media:** Support media and communications activities in coordination with IRC regional and global communications teams, ensuring the safety, dignity and informed consent of clients.
- **Advocacy:** Support the CD and DDPs as needed.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Country Director, Colombia and Venezuela

**Position directly supervises:** Grants, Partnerships and Communications Unit staff

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Venezuela Country Manager and Venezuela senior management team, with whom the postholder works closely on the Venezuela portfolio; Colombia/Venezuela Deputy Directors of Programs and leads of programs, Finance and Operations, Budget Officers/Managers, HR Lead, Access & Security Department; MEAL Unit; Awards Management Unit (Regional), regional partnerships advisor, regional and global communications teams, and Technical Advisors.

**External:** Donors and pooled fund managers, consortium partners, local partner organizations, UN agencies and humanitarian coordination mechanisms, other NGO counterparts and media, as needed and indicated by Country Director, Country Manager or Deputy Director of Programs.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline, Master’s degree desired.
- At least five years international work experience in humanitarian and development programs; experience in a similar position/role is desired.
- Demonstrated, successful experience in program design and writing proposals for public and private donors.
- Solid knowledge of donor rules and regulations, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, UN agencies and OCHA-managed pooled funds; knowledge of other European, multilateral and private donor requirements is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience managing the full award cycle, including compliance, modifications, audits and close-out, and in managing partnerships with local organizations.
- Experience in communications, brand management or external relations in a humanitarian or development organization is desirable.
- Demonstrable understanding of project planning and management cycles.
- Highly organized, close attention to detail, and ability to effectively prioritize tasks in a fluid environment.
- Demonstrable high-level performance management and team-working skills, and well developed negotiation skills.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence and represent the organization with external organizations and stakeholders.
- Effective people- and program-management skills in acute emergency contexts: can train and lead staff productively under stressful circumstances.
- Flexible, focused and reliable, with the ability to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures in an environment of changing demands.
- Experience in the region is an asset; knowledge of the Colombian and Venezuelan contexts is strongly desired.
- Digital literacy and strong computer skills: MS Word, Excel & email applications required.

**Language Preference**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish, with high quality copywriting and editing skills in both languages.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate around: 10,051,500 COP/monthly). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.
