jobs.title: Oficial de Ayuda Legal - Santa bárbara del Zulia
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Ayuda Legal** altamente calificado con sede en **Santa Bárbara, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**:

El objetivo principal del Oficial de Ayuda Legal es implementar las actividades legales en el marco del programa de Protección de DRC. Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección implementará las actividades de ayuda legal y es responsable de brindar asesoría legal y gestión de casos para restablecer los derechos de refugiados, migrantes y retornados en materia civil, administrativa y constitucional. Es responsable para la implementación de sesiones informativas sobre temas legales en estrecha colaboración con el equipo de protección.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Principales Responsabilidades**

Este rol tiene un enfoque de área y garantiza el cumplimiento de los objetivos de asistencia/asesoría legal bajo los procedimientos y las pautas de DRC dentro del área. El rol contribuye al desempeño de los planes de acción y proporciona apoyo y orientación técnica para operaciones legales en el terreno.

- Trabajar en estrecha cooperación con el equipo de protección de DRC y responder a las necesidades legales documentadas;
- Implementar las actividades de asesoría y servicios legales conforme a los objetivos meta de los proyectos;
- Elaborar documentos de asesoría y servicios legales, determinando la mejor estrategia para los casos de beneficiarios bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección;
- Implementar asesoría y servicios legales en las zonas de intervención seleccionadas por el programa según el plan mensual establecido;
- Planear y proporcionar citas individuales para el asesoramiento jurídico a las personas de interés, según sea necesario.
- Recopilar información de los beneficiarios gestionando archivos de manera confidencial y completa; trasferir diariamente las informaciones relevantes en la base de datos legales para permitir el seguimiento de los casos legales identificados o remitidos.
- Proporcionar asesoramiento individual en temas de protección incluyendo protección internacional, reunificación familiar, registro civil y nacionalidad, afiliación en el sistema de seguridad social, acceso a salud, educación y vivienda y otros casos de derecho civil y administrativo que requieran asistencia jurídica;
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario;
- Apoyar a la Gerencia de Protección en la elaboración de estrategias y procedimientos estándares para facilitar la implementación de las actividades legales.
- Mantener buenas relaciones con las entidades e instituciones públicas pertinentes para que la coordinación y la articulación sea fortalecida.
- Proporcionar información para informes semanales según sea requerido.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas

**Responsabilidades sectoriales**:

- Incidencia sobre los derechos de las personas de interés en el contexto de su desplazamiento, asesoría legal y gestión de casos para restablecer los derechos de refugiados, migrantes y retornados en materia civil, constitucional y administrativa.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades legales en terreno.
- Abordar las necesidades de asesoría y servicios legales de los beneficiarios.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 2-3 años de experiencia relevante como abogado/a.
- Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos.
- Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal, seguimiento de casos y litigio.
- Optimas habilidades de escritura informes.
- Optimas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Optimas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.
- Experiencia con los procedimientos y directrices estándar.
- Alta ética profesional.

**Nivel educativo:**

- Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos. Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal, seguimiento de casos y litigio

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

jobs.title: Project Management Support Specialist [Counter Terrorism]
jobs.description:
## **Job Highlight**

This is a position in UNOPS for supporting projects carried out for or in the United Nations Office of Counter Terrorism (UNOCT). The position supports the work of the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (PRR) . The incumbent of this position will be a personnel of UNOPS under its full responsibility.

## **About the Region**

The UNOPS Global Portfolios Office (GPO) brings together diverse expertise to help partners deliver impact worldwide. With hubs in New York, Geneva, and Vienna, and expert teams operating globally, GPO leads multi-regional initiatives that advance sustainable development, climate action, and peacebuilding - including in some of the world’s most challenging environments. By leveraging our collective expertise and global networks, GPO supports UNOPS’ strategic priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals across more than 130 countries. We work closely with major global partners - including governments, international financial institutions, and UN agencies - to deliver a wide range of services, such as project management, fund management, hosting services, and HR support.

## **About the Country/Multi-Country Office**

UNOPS Development and Special Initiatives team works with UN partners and Member States. This portfolio offers support for various initiatives and priorities of the UN Secretary-General in pursuit of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Additionally, it helps the UN Secretariat in implementing global programs in areas such as political affairs, climate, counterterrorism and peacebuilding, among others.

## **Job Specific Context**

UNOPS DSI has signed an agreement with the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism to implement project activities under the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation, and Reintegration (PRR).

The United Nations Office of Counter Terrorism (UNOCT) was established by the General Assembly in June 2017. UNOCT has five mandated functions:

(1) Provide leadership on the General Assembly counter-terrorism mandates entrusted to the Secretary-General from across the United Nations system;

(2) Enhance coordination and coherence across the Global Counter-Terrorism Coordination Compact entities to ensure the balanced implementation of the four pillars of the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy;

(3) Strengthen the delivery of United Nations counter-terrorism capacity-building assistance to Member States;

(4) Improve visibility, advocacy and resource mobilization for United Nations counter-terrorism efforts; and

(5) Ensure that due priority is given to counterterrorism across the United Nations system and that the important work on preventing violent extremism is firmly rooted in the Strategy.

## **Role Purpose**

Under UNOPS supervision and working in close collaboration with UNOCT, the Project Management Support Specialist will support the implementation of activities under the Global Programme on PRR.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

Under the supervision of the UNOPS Project Manager and in close collaboration with the UNOCT Programme Manager of the Global Programme on Prosecution, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (PRR), the Project Management Support Specialist will support the delivery, coordination, monitoring and development of project activities and will be responsible for the following:

**1. Project Delivery and Performance**

- Support in the planning, implementation and monitoring of project activities in line with approved work plans, budgets and quality standards.
- Coordinate project activities and develop project management tools to ensure timely delivery of outputs and adherence to UNOPS and donor/partner requirements.
- Support the design and development of programmes and projects, including the preparation of project documents, implementation plans, budgets and results frameworks.
- Conduct or support needs assessments, stakeholder consultations and gap analyses to inform programme development and implementation.
- Manage and monitor progress against scope, time, cost and quality tolerances. Identify risks and deviations, propose corrective actions, and escalate when required.
- Support resource mobilization efforts through the preparation of concept notes, project proposals, donor briefs and related documentation.
- Embed sustainability principles - including gender equality, social inclusion and environmental considerations - across project activities.
- Contribute to the identification and development of new project opportunities or extensions of existing engagements.

**2. Financial and Procurement Management**

- Support financial planning, monitoring and reporting to ensure effective budget utilization and cost control in line with UNOPS Financial Rules and Regulations.
- Support procurement and grant management processes, including preparation of Terms of Reference (ToRs).

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

- Maintain effective working relationships with donors, partners, national authorities and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated delivery and alignment with project objectives.
- Coordinate project steering committees and country level coordination mechanisms.
- Support the development and implementation of stakeholder engagement and communication plans, ensuring timely and consistent information sharing.
- Facilitate internal coordination among project teams, technical experts and support functions.
- Represent the project in meetings, consultations and external engagements as delegated by the supervisor.

**4. Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor project performance against agreed indicators, preparing progress, financial and completion reports in accordance with UNOPS and donor/partner standards.
- Conduct data analysis and provide inputs for management decisions and strategic planning.
- Ensure quality assurance processes are applied to all deliverables, documents and outputs.
- Support compliance with internal audit and quality standards, coordinating corrective action as required.

**5. Knowledge Building and Sharing**

- Support the organization, facilitation and delivery of capacity building workshops.
- Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and Communities of Practice (CoPs), contributing insights and lessons learned.
- Conduct research on PRR-related topics and contribute to the drafting of reports, summaries and briefing notes.

## **Education Requirements**

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent), preferably in law, political science, international relations, management, economics or related fields with five (5) years of relevant experience is required; or
- First-level university degree (bachelor's degree or equivalent), preferably in law, political science, international relations, management, economics or related fields with seven (7) years of relevant experience is required.

A globally recognized professional certificate or membership in Project Management is desired.

## **Experience Requirements**

Required

- Relevant experience is defined as work in programme and project management in areas related to preventing and countering violent extremism or PRR.
- Demonstrable proficiency in the use of collaboration and productivity tools (e.g. MS Office, G-Suite, etc) and web-based management systems.

Desired

- Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country.
- Experience in development or peacekeeping contexts.

## **Language Requirements**

Fluent English is required.

Fluent Arabic is desirable.

jobs.title: Officer, Planned Giving - South
jobs.description:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee's (IRC) External Relations (ER) department enables the IRC to respond to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Within ER, the Philanthropy team leads on the organization’s work with High-Net-Worth Individuals and planned giving donors.

**Job Overview**:

The Officer, Planned Giving, will work with donors and prospects in an assigned geography across the Southern U.S. to support an increased number of legacy gift commitments and a growing and engaged legacy society. They will support the securing and sustaining of planned gifts by working directly with prospects and donors and Philanthropy colleagues to help ensure a healthy financial future for our humanitarian work. This may entail following up on new leads; soliciting donors for planned gifts; building positive relationships to steward legacy donors; carrying out cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies, set with the Senior Director, to connect with and inspire planned giving donors and prospects; supporting colleagues on collaborations; and reporting results of efforts.

The Officer will be expected to understand the needs of older donors and prospects, communicate and connect superbly with colleagues and supporters, use knowledge of various gift planning instruments to assist colleagues and donors, continue to learn about IRC programs, and maintain accurate donor records to support the IRC’s donor relationships and prospecting with high wealth individuals and families.

Additionally, the Officer will be expected to work directly with other development officers, ER colleagues, and local area leadership to increase awareness about planned giving, support education opportunities, and support planned giving conversations and asks for appropriate donors across Major and Principal Giving portfolios.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Manage an assigned portfolio of planned gift prospects and donors.
- Provide timely follow-up to new marketing leads to educate prospects, creating new planned gifts for the IRC.
- Implement meaningful engagement opportunities for planned giving donors and prospects, in line with the team’s stewardship plan, to deepen their understanding of the mission and the benefits of legacy giving and gifts of complex assets.
- Execute regional donor trips, with travel plans approved by manager, maximizing geographic clusters of donors and prospects
- Focus on significant interactions during in person visits, events, and digital and mail communications.
- Support engagement with the IRC legacy society (Changemakers) to recognize and retain committed donors, including an annual in-person recognition event in NYC and other regional market events.
- Partner with Major Gifts and Principal Gifts colleagues on planned gift conversations for appropriate prospects within their portfolios, with strategy set by senior staff
- Contribute to internal education across ER teams and IRC regional office leadership (RAI) on planned giving’s role and process with the organization, using materials developed by the team
- Successfully meet individual goals for significant interactions, prospect conversions, lead identification, and outright giving, in alignment with overall team goals.
- Review donor file data (Salesforce) to flag prospects and bring portfolio balance recommendations to manager
- Timely and accurately input opportunity data into Salesforce to drive pipeline activity, report on progress towards goals, and find areas of improvement.
- Promote and practice inclusive behavior and demonstrate a willingness to learn about the IRC’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion.

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience:**

- 3-5 years of experience working with individual donors, preferably in major gifts, annual giving, or planned giving.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of or familiarity with planned giving vehicles and benefits preferred;
- Ability to communicate effectively with older donors about the IRC’s mission and planning tools;
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines, in consultation with manager;
- Effective collaboration with colleagues at all levels across the organization;
- Proficient with Microsoft Office; experience with CRM databases such as Salesforce or Raiser’s Edge preferred;
- Outstanding attention to detail and commitment to timeframes;
- Commitment to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor information;
- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization.
- Driver’s license and ability to travel up to 25% of the time, including overnight travel, is required.

**Working Environment:** This role is remote and ability to travel to see donors and prospects required. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $77,600-$93,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Oficial MERL
jobs.description:
**\*\*CONTRATACION SUJETA A APROBACION Y DISPONIBILIDAD FINANCIERA DE PROYECTO\*\***

La Organización

A través de su trabajo en 80 países con economías en desarrollo en África, Asia y las Américas, Plan International busca alcanzar la mayor cantidad de niños y niñas que sea posible, particularmente aquellos y aquellas que son excluidos/as o marginados/as, con programas de alta calidad que entregan beneficios duraderos, a través de incrementar sus ingresos, trabajando en asocio con otros y operando de manera efectiva.

¡Plan promueve los derechos de la niñez y está comprometida con la protección de los niños y las niñas, así como con la igualdad de género, por lo tanto toma las medidas necesarias para que sus intervenciones y el actuar de su personal sean acordes con esta política, asimismo, respetamos el principio de igualdad de oportunidades y no discriminación a personas por su raza, color, género, edad, origen, lengua, discapacidad, orientación sexual, religiosa y/o política, estatus marital o embarazo!

Propósito

Diseñar, implementar y supervisar el sistema de Monitoreo, Evaluación, Rendición de Cuentas y Aprendizaje (MERL) del proyecto de focalización, instalación y entrega de asistencia alimentaria, asegurando la recolección, análisis y uso de la información para mejorar la calidad, transparencia y efectividad de las intervenciones. El especialista MERL deberá anticipar y gestionar de manera oportuna los desafíos relacionados con la recolección, sistematización y análisis de información, incluyendo posibles retrasos en el flujo de datos desde terreno o limitaciones técnicas en las plataformas de monitoreo. Será responsable de organizar adecuadamente los tiempos para la consolidación de bases de datos, verificación de calidad de la información y elaboración de reportes, garantizando el cumplimiento de los plazos establecidos por el proyecto y el donante. Asimismo, deberá proponer ajustes metodológicos y soluciones prácticas que aseguren la calidad, confiabilidad y trazabilidad de los datos en un contexto humanitario dinámico y de alta demanda.

Responsabilidades generales

\- Apoyar el diseño y la implementación de un sistema de seguimiento y evaluación (MERL) para la respuesta humanitaria de Plan International con el fin de supervisar el progreso programático, garantizando la incorporación de un enfoque de igualdad de género y protección a las niñas, niños y adolescentes, empoderamiento de las mujeres.
\- Proporcionar asistencia técnica y formación al equipo del proyecto.
\- Acompañar, monitorear y reportar el cumplimiento de la calidad en el alcance e impacto del proyecto, a través del apoyo permanente al trabajo de campo, planificación, monitoreo y evaluación bajo un enfoque de derechos e igualdad de las niñas en el marco de os principios humanitarios y a acción sin daño.
\- Vinculación estratégica de indicadores globales de Plan International con indicadores a los que se deberá responderán y según requerimiento del donante.
\- Diseñar mecanismo de Rendición de Cuentas y Retroalimentación a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP) tomando en cuenta las exigencias y formalidades de Plan International y el donante
\- Liderar y brindar orientaciones indicadoras al personal del proyecto, garantizando la ejecución de las actividades, el alcance de los objetivos, cumplimiento de políticas y procedimientos tanto de Plan International como del donante, resultados e indicadores del proyecto, de acuerdo a la propuesta aprobada.
\- Coordinación del proceso de elaboración y edición del Informe mensual de progreso del proyecto.
\- Promoción de la gestión del conocimiento en el marco de las acciones del proyecto.
\- Coordina con el equipo técnico MERL de Plan, el mantener las bases de datos actualizadas de registro de beneficiarios y garantiza que la información se reporte en los tiempos establecidos.
\- Mantener constante comunicación con Asesor MERL, Coordinadores de proyectos humanitarios, Subgerente de preparación y Respuesta Humanitaria, para asegurar el cumplimiento de los objetivos, resultados e indicadores, establecidos en la lógica de intervención de cada proyecto.

Conocimiento, habilidades, conductas, y experiencia requerida para lograr los objetivos del puesto:

Requisitos:
Educación:
\- Se requiere un título universitario en Ciencias Sociales, Desarrollo, Análisis de datos, Economía, Administración, Matemáticas Aplicadas o carreras a fin.

Conocimientos:
\- Planificación, implementación y evaluación de programas y proyectos especialmente de respuesta humanitaria.
\- Experiencia calificada demostrable de tres años en monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos humanitarios.
\- Experiencia demostrable de 3 años en la recopilación, generación y análisis de datos.
\- Experiencia demostrable de 3 años en el seguimiento de proyectos con un enfoque orientado a los resultados.
\- Experiencia demostrable de 3 años en elaboración de indicadores, y metodologías para el monitoreo y evaluación de planes y/o programas
\- Se valorará la experiencia en gestión de proyectos, incluyendo el diseño, seguimiento y evaluación de proyectos de desarrollo, preferiblemente relacionados con uno o más de los temas el sector humanitario y emergencia:
\- Se valorará conocimiento del contexto de Gestión de Riesgos, humanitario, desarrollo y sus principios.
\- Se valorará la experiencia de trabajo con entidades gubernamentales, organizaciones de la sociedad civil y organizaciones internacionales.
\- Capacidad demostrada para redactar, editar y elaborar informes orientados a los resultados.
\- Conocimiento avanzado de MS Office, Access, Project y programas estadísticos como: EPI-INFO, SPSS o similares.
\- Conocimiento del contexto humanitario.
\- Conocimiento sobre gestión integral de proyectos y uso de aplicaciones para el campo en el ámbito humanitario.

Habilidades específicas del puesto
\- Redacción de informes y sistematización de información
\- Manejo avanzado de plataforma Power BI
\- Manejo avanzado en plataforma SPSS y MaxQDA deseable.
\- Manejo de aplicaciones para recolección de datos, recomendable experiencia de manejo de la aplicación Kobo Collect.
\- Manejo y experiencia intermedia en uso de la plataforma ArqGIS o alguna otra aplicable a geo referenciación y mapas digitales deseable.
\- Enfoque de derechos, edad, género y diversidad.
\- Habilidad para trabajar bajo presión
\- Habilidades gerenciales.
\- Habilidad de análisis estadísticos.
\- Habilidades de comunicación apropiadas a las diferentes audiencias.
\- Resolución de problemas.
\- Capacidad de trabajar en un ambiente multidisciplinario y multicultural.
\- Atención al detalle.

Otros requisitos:
\- Interés y compromiso de trabajo y protección con niñas y niños.
\- Sensibilidad social
\- Disposición de viajar al interior y exterior del país
\- Experiencia en conducción de vehículos 4x4

Comportamientos de liderazgo:
\- Fuertes habilidades de trabajo en equipo y liderazgo.
\- Fomenta una cultura de Monitoreo, evaluación y aprendizaje en los equipos implementadores.
\- Promueve la innovación y el aprendizaje.

jobs.title: Head of IT Operations - HQ
jobs.description:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Job Summary**

As Head of IT Operations, you’ll own INSO’s IT infrastructure and make sure it is secure, reliable, and efficient. You’ll report to the Director of Operations and lead the IT team, set its goals, and hold it to high standards. You’ll also lead the secure and responsible use of AI and automation across INSO’s operations. The technology you run helps keep humanitarian workers safe in some of the world’s most difficult environments.

**Major Responsibilities**

*Strategy and policy*

- Set and maintain INSO’s IT vision, strategy and roadmap, aligned with organisational goals and operational needs
- Write and maintain IT policies and standards that comply with GDPR, the EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 27001
- Advise HQ departments, projects and Country Offices on infrastructure, systems and technology, including evaluating and integrating new software
- Agree a clear IT ownership and governance model with HQ Directors. IT is accountable for identity and access management, security standards, licensing, technical integration and architecture
- Manage software licences across HQ and Country Offices for compliance, cost and fit
- Review existing systems to keep them secure, resilient and fit for purpose
- Assess emerging technologies, including AI, for their operational, security, compliance and financial impact, and recommend what to adopt
- Manage strategic relationships with global technology vendors and partners to get the best service, value and innovation

*AI in IT infrastructure and support systems*

- Contribute to INSO’s AI strategy and lead its implementation within IT operations
- Own the AI acceptable use and security policy (approved tools, data handling, access and compliance), developed with DTL
- Lead AI integration into infrastructure and support systems such as Microsoft 365, finance, HR and IT service management
- Advise on and review the infrastructure, security and compliance (GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001) side of AI features in INSO-developed software and programme platforms, which DTL owns and leads
- Identify and manage AI and automation projects in support processes (finance, HR, logistics and administration) across HQ and Country Offices, working with system owners and referring programme-related opportunities to DTL
- Lead staff training on the safe use of INSO-approved AI tools and the AI policy, coordinating with DTL on training for the AI solutions it builds for programmes
- Track and report on the adoption, cost and benefits of AI tools to inform reviews of the AI strategy

*IT risk*

- Identify, assess and reduce risks to the security, resilience and availability of INSO’s IT
- Keep the IT and information security entries in the INSO Risk Register up to date, including mitigation measures, risk owners and residual risk
- Lead IT risk management, including data classification and protection, data loss prevention, incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery, cybersecurity awareness
- Monitor new threats and regulations, and put the right controls in place
- Build and test a disaster recovery framework (policies, plans, testing and procedures) so critical systems can be restored quickly
- Report regularly on risk exposure, how well controls are working and significant security incidents

*Leadership*

- Lead, manage and mentor the IT team, building a culture of collaboration, accountability and growth
- Plan, prioritise and delegate work so projects and support are delivered on time
- Own the IT budget, making sure resources are used well and give value for money
- Take on other duties as needed

**Requirements**

*Essential*

- At least 8 years of progressive IT management experience, including in humanitarian or NGO settings.
- Proven experience of managing IT, delivering projects together with service and supplier management.
- Experience administering Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, and Azure environments.
- Experience deploying, managing, and governing AI tools (e.g. Microsoft 365 Copilot) and business process automation solutions.
- Demonstrated ability to analyse information critically, evaluate risks and opportunities, develop effective solutions, and manage multiple priorities while consistently meeting deadlines.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field.

*Desirable*

- Solid project management skills related to organisational development projects and international, cross-functional, and integrated teams with a proven history of delivering results.
- Working knowledge of information security and data protection frameworks, such as ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR and the EU AI Act.
- Experience of working within a matrix organisation structure.
- Working knowledge of either French, Arabic, Dutch, or Spanish.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

This is a full-time, fixed-term (renewable) position based in The Hague, Netherlands, with office presence required. The full-time package, based on 40 hours a week, is €6700 gross per month, 8% vacation pay, and 2.5 days of annual leave per month. INSO provides Basic Premium ONVZ health insurance for the staff member and dependents. The position is eligible for a Highly Skilled Migrant visa and relocation. **Be aware that INSO’s employment terms do not include transport and pension benefits.** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Global Security Advisor - HQ
jobs.description:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. **Job Summary**

As the Global Security Advisor, you will work with INSO’s Country Offices to ensure they are prepared to manage security risks and operate in line with INSO’s Global Security Policy, Crisis Management Policy, and Organisational Risk Management Framework. You will monitor compliance, support country teams in addressing operational risks, and help ensure that risk management is embedded into day-to-day decision-making and ways of working.

You will also contribute to building security and risk management knowledge across the organisation, helping teams strengthen their understanding, apply good practice, and maintain a consistent approach to safety and risk management throughout INSO’s operations.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

*Strategy and planning*

- Shape INSO’s safety, security, crisis and risk management policies, templates and global security strategy
- Run the framework that holds offices accountable for safety and security
- Advise Regional Directors and Country Offices on security needs in proposals and annual plans
- Line-manage the Deputy Global Security Advisor and support their growth

*Field support and compliance*

- Make sure every office has current risk assessments, security plans, SOPs and contingency plans
- Find capacity gaps and build plans to close them, together with country management and the Safety and Training Manager
- Visit offices to support their Safety and Security Management Plans in person

jobs.title: Consultancy - Economic and Financial Analysis - Central Asia
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
**Background:**

Acted is an independent, international organization headquartered in Paris, France. Founded in Afghanistan in 1993, Acted now supports 20 million people across 43 countries worldwide in pursuit of its triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development actor in response to the triple planetary crisis.

Acted has been operating continuously in Central Asia since 1996, working to address the region’s main challenges and, as a result, has long standing partnerships with communities, government agencies, and development partners. In line with Acted's global "3Zero" [Strategy](https://www.3zero.org/): Zero Exclusion, Zero Poverty, Zero Carbon, Acted works across a broad range of sectors to foster inclusive and sustainable development, including Natural Resource Management (NRM), Climate Change Adaption (CCA) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) through its STREAM approach.

Acted is an accredited GCF entity preparing a Full Funding Proposal (PAP) for Fin-Fergana, targeting submission January 2027. The programme addresses climate-driven water insecurity in the Fergana Valley.

**Objectives:**

Acted seeks an external consultant to: (i) conduct a societal-perspective cost-benefit analysis (CBA) with positive Economic Net Present Value and Benefit-Cost Ratio > 1; (ii) develop institution- and beneficiary-perspective financial analyses with and without GCF, assessing minimum concessionality; (iii) build a formula-driven Excel model using GCF official Annex 11 templates; and (iv) write the Annex 11 narrative to GCF submission standards.

## Qualification requirements

**Essential:** Advanced degree in economics, finance or agricultural economics; ≥7 years' experience in economic CBA and/or financial analysis for development or climate projects; at least one approved GCF Full Funding Proposal EFA (Annex 11) — eliminatory criterion; experience with blended finance and lending through financial intermediaries; proficiency in multi-sheet Excel modelling (P&L, cash flow, DSCR, WACC, IRR); CBA experience in water or agriculture; excellent technical English.

**Desirable:** Experience in Central Asia; agricultural microfinance; FX risk; gender-disaggregated economic analysis.

## Duties

**Economic analysis (CBA).** Societal perspective; shadow prices; 15-year analysis period; SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Quantify costs from the approved budget (Annex 4) and benefits for both outcomes: water savings, productivity gains, non-market co-benefits (Outcome 1); incremental farm-level gains and revolving-lending multiplier (Outcome 2). Calculate ENPV, EIRR and BCR per outcome and in aggregate. Sensitivity analysis on discount rate, cost drivers, climate scenario and portfolio performance; disaggregation by country and beneficiary group.

**Financial analysis.** Market prices; institution/beneficiary perspective. Outcome 1: O&M affordability assessment; cost-effectiveness analysis where full CBA is not feasible. Each lending facility (Oxus KG; Uzbekistan PFI(s)): P&L, cash flow and balance sheet projections; DSCR, NPV, IRR, payback; model the revolving mechanism and recycling multiplier; with- and without-GCF comparison; WACC and minimum concessionality via GCF Grant Equivalent Calculator (GCF/B.21/24, GCF/B.23/19); FX risk and hedging. Farm-level analysis for at least three representative investment cases. Sensitivity and scenario analysis throughout.

**Model and narrative.** Consolidated GCF Annex 11 Excel model with central parameters tab; facility-level and aggregate views; no hard-coded values. Annex 11 narrative covering methodology, results, sensitivity and distributional analysis, cross-referenced with Annexes 3, 4, 12 and 13.

## Conditions

Submit to kyrgyzstan.tender@acted.org by the deadline to be communicated. Subject line: EoI — GCF EFA — Fin-Fergana — \[Name\]. Include: (1) CV(s) highlighting GCF EFA, CBA and financial modelling experience; (2) technical proposal (max. 5 pp) with methodology and work plan; (3) at least one GCF EFA example or equivalent sample; (4) financial proposal with total fixed fee (USD) broken down by deliverable; (5) two references. Evaluation: 70% technical (GCF EFA experience 30%, methodology 25%, qualifications 15%) / 30% financial (value for money 20%, person-days 10%). Applications without at least one approved GCF FP EFA will not be evaluated.

**Key Reference Documents**

Annex 11 [template](https://www.greenclimate.fund/document/economic-and-financial-analyses-templates-annex-11) and [guidance](https://www.greenclimate.fund/document/guidelines-preparing-economic-and-financial-analysis-annex-11-pap-proposals).

Provided on contract signature: draft Feasibility Study (Annex 2).

## About company

Acted is committed to the promotion of a 3Zero world of Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty. Acted has been active in Central Asia since 1996, helping to address the region’s main development challenges and fostering opportunities for sustainable and inclusive development, especially in rural and remote communities. This includes a special focus on civil society development and transparent and effective governance.

jobs.title: Feasibility Study Consultant in Abyan, Yemen
jobs.description:
**Organisation**

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V.

[www.hoffnungszeichen.de](http://www.hoffnungszeichen.de), [www.sign-of-hope.org](http://www.sign-of-hope.org)

**Position**

Feasibility Study Consultant

**Type of Contract**

Short-Term Consultancy

**Location**

Home-based with field mission travel to Aden and Abyan, Yemen

**Relevant languages**

English, Arabic (required)

**Application Deadline**

27/11/2026

**Starting Date**

09/12/2027

**Project Title**

Building resilience in Rasad through improved agricultural and WASH infrastructure and climate-resilient income-generating opportunities

**Total Project Budget**

555,556 EUR (to be approved)

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is announcing **an open tender procedure for consultancy services for a feasibility study in Yemen**.

**Background and Organisational Setting**

SoH is a Christian motivated organisation for Human Rights, Humanitarian Assistance and Development Cooperation. From its base in Constance, Germany, SoH is committed to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

This feasibility study is commissioned, prior to project implementation, under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) budget for development projects run by private organisations.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Relief and Development Peer Foundation (RDP)being the local implementing partner.

**Project Summary**

Project region: Rasad District, Abyan Governorate, Yemen (IRG-controlled areas).

Overall objective:
Contribute to reduced vulnerability and enhanced resilience and well-being of vulnerable populations in Rasad through strengthened food security, diversified climate-resilient livelihoods, and sustainable and equitable access to safe water and sanitation services.

Target groups:
Smallholder farmers; women-headed households; vulnerable youth; internally displaced persons; households with persons with disabilities/specific needs; marginalized groups; elderly-headed households; and households affected by conflict, climate shocks and loss of productive assets or income.

Implementation period: July 2027 – June 2030 (fixed).

The resilience and living conditions of vulnerable households in the Rasad district are being improved through enhanced food security, diversified livelihood opportunities and sustainable access to safe WASH services. 75 smallholder farmers are increasing agricultural productivity and resilience through climate-resilient farming methods, supported by targeted training and appropriate agricultural inputs. 90 households are improving their incomes and economic resilience through climate-resilient community projects and access to livelihood and enterprise development opportunities.

The target communities make sustainable use of drinking water and sanitation services through climate-resilient infrastructure, effective community-based management systems and improved hygiene practices, contributing to a reduction in health risks, better public health and an overall increase in well-being.

**Feasibility Study Objectives**

The purpose of the feasibility study is to provide SoH with a sound basis for developing a complete project concept, by identifying project prerequisites, opportunities and risks. This process includes an assessment of the feasibility of the proposed project intervention to assess if it can plausibly achieve planned objectives given existing contextual realities.

This comprehensive study will verify relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the proposed project intervention. The study will provide concrete and practical recommendations that will assist with the finalisation of project design elements, including the logframe, risk analysis, problem analysis and relevance of the proposed project intervention, stakeholder analysis, among others.

The study will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process regarding the funding of the proposed project activities.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The selected Consultant will work in close cooperation with the responsible SoH Officer and the local implementing partner.

The duties and responsibilities of the consultant will include:

- Develop a work plan outlining the proposed research methodology, geographical coverage, and schedule to conduct the feasibility study,
- Carry out a project site visit to the project location to conduct research, collect data and establish contact with the local implementing partner, potential beneficiaries and relevant project stakeholders,
- Review existing policies and structures, government development strategies as well as relevant studies and research projects that could serve as a basis for the feasibility study,
- Identify relevant project stakeholders at various levels (local, district and national if applicable), including local governing bodies, academia and industry as well as lessons learned and best practises of similar on-going and implemented projects relevant to the project,
- Evaluate all available data and sources providing background information on identified issues, the problem analysis as well as the selected intervention to address identified needs (baseline data with focus on the qualitative analysis),
- Assess the proposed activities, as well as their timing and required financial resources.
- Examine institutional, technical, staffing and financial capacities of the selected implementing partner, as well as its relationship with the target group. Based on the findings, determine if there are areas in which capacities of the local implementing partner need to be developed,
- Review main governmental and non-governmental stakeholders with a purpose to see if there is a potential overlap or conflict of interest as well as opportunities for coordination with the aim of creating synergies and new cooperation partnerships,
- Examine the identified target group, its needs and role in the broader social context as well as the relevance of the planned project activities for addressing their needs,
- Identify potential obstacles and alternatives to overcome the foreseen challenges,
- Review and analyse all available project design elements and draft documents related to the project concept, if necessary,
- Critically review the planned project in terms of OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability (please see [www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html](http://www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html)),
- Prepare a report containing the findings on the above items, specific recommendations for the project concept with a view to planning and implementing foreseen project activities.
- Conduct a context-specific security and operational risk assessment of the proposed project area, taking into account the evolving security situation, potential escalation risks, movement restrictions and other factors that may affect the safety of personnel, access to target communities and the delivery of proposed activities.
- Assess the practical feasibility of conducting project activities and the feasibility study fieldwork under the prevailing security conditions, including the availability of safe access routes, transport and logistics, local acceptance, coordination with relevant authorities and community structures, and the capacity to maintain effective field monitoring and supervision.
- Identify appropriate risk mitigation and contingency measures, including possible adjustments to implementation geographical coverage and data collection approaches. Where the proposed project area is assessed as unsuitable or presents risks that cannot be adequately mitigated, provide evidence-based recommendations on alternative locations or implementation arrangements, clearly explaining their feasibility and implications for the proposed project objectives.

**Methodology**

- Desk review of project documents, BMZ guidance, secondary datasets, and previous studies.
- Rapid scoping and transparent target-community/site selection to focus detailed fieldwork on the most viable locations.
- Quantitative household survey using a statistically and operationally justified sample, with appropriate geographic and demographic coverage.
- Focus Group Discussions with relevant groups, including women, men, youth, farmers, IDPs/marginalized groups and persons with disabilities/specific needs where feasible and appropriate.
- Key Informant Interviews with authorities, technical offices, community leaders, service providers, NGOs, market actors, financial service providers, TVET (Technical Vocational and Educational Training) and relevant SoH/RDP staff.
- Direct observation and site-specific technical inspections of candidate infrastructure and community assets.
- Agriculture, market and labour-market/livelihood assessment.
- Water-source/hydrogeological review and field testing/quality testing where relevant and feasible.
- Participatory tools, such as mapping, ranking, seasonal calendars, and community validation, where useful.
- Mapping and photographic documentation of selected sites.
- Market-based costing using supplier/contractor quotations or documented price references where feasible.
- Triangulation of quantitative, qualitative, technical and secondary evidence; identification of inconsistencies and confidence/limitations.

**Expected Deliverables**

The study will produce the following deliverables:

- a feasibility study outline, including the proposed methodology and data collection tools, table of content and a timeline of research activities (inception report) prior to the site visit to the project location,
- a summary containing a brief overview and the main findings of the study,
- a comprehensive report of a maximum of 30 pages with practical recommendations and relevant annexes,
- a review of the main project design elements and provision of concrete recommendations for improvement,
- an analysis of the institutional structure required for project implementation, stipulating the roles and responsibilities of staff members involved, a detailed problem analysis, a stakeholder analysis, a revision of the target group, an analysis of the potential risks and recommendations on how to mitigate these risks, a schedule of project activities, a financial plan (planning budget), a detailed project logframe with SMART indicators for the project objective and results listing related activities and required resources,
- a “Do-no-harm analysis” including recommendations on how to mitigate potential harm and conflict situations that can potentially arise during or as a result of the project activities
- a Gender mainstreaming analysis identifying potential risks and recommendations to ensure gender equality in all aspects of the project design and implementation.

A template will be provided to serve as a guide and suggested structure for the final report.

**Process/Timeframe**

A total duration of the assignment is up to 20 working days within the period of 09/12/2026 to 05/01/2026.

- A planning meeting with RDP, handover of relevant documents 1 day
- Initial document review and preparing inception report 3 days
- Sharing inception report with SoH and RDP 1 day
- Data collection site visit to a project location 5 days
- Data analysis, draft report with annexes, presenting to SoH 5 days
- Incorporating received feedback and finalising the report 5 days

**Qualifications and Experience**

Essential:

- Minimum of 5 years of project evaluation and/or implementation experience in the result-based management framework
- Proven experience of conducting feasibility studies, evaluations and other research projects
- Technical and methodological knowledge to conduct research projects and formulate conclusions based on a solid methodology, assessing projects for relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of projects
- Experience working with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and partnered projects
- Fluency in written and spoken English & Arabic
- Legally registered in Aden

Desirable:

- Experience in the relevant field
- Professional familiarity with the project country/region
- Practical experience of working for and/or evaluating BMZ-funded projects

Desired Technical Team Capacity of the Consultant:

- Team Leader / Feasibility & Development Specialist
- WASH / Water / Civil Engineering Specialist
- FSL / Agriculture / Livelihoods Specialist
- MEAL / Research / Data Specialist
- Field coordination / Enumerators

**Academic Background**

An advanced level university degree (Masters’ degree or equivalent) in social sciences, public administration, international development studies, law and/or another relevant field. A first-level university degree in combination with additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted.

The consultant is to be independent and impartial with no liabilities to any other organisation or government entity regarding this evaluation.

jobs.title: Spécialiste Protection genre et inclusion
jobs.description:
Lieu : Antananarivo, Madagascar
Date souhaitée de démarrage : Janvier 2027
Durée de contrat : 12 mois

En raison de l'urgence de ce recrutement, nous encourageons les candidat.es intéressé.es à soumettre leur candidature dès que possible. Nous examinerons les candidatures de manière continue.

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : .

CONTEXTE :
Humanité et Inclusion (HI) est présent à Madagascar depuis 38 ans et est actuellement présente au niveau de 7 régions. Son expertise porte sur l’éducation, les approches inclusives, et les interventions auprès des groupes les plus vulnérables, dont les personnes handicapées, dans les domaines de l’éducation et de la formation professionnelle, la santé (santé maternelle et infantile, épilepsie, réadaptation, santé mentale) et dans le domaine de la gestion des risques et catastrophes. Le volume du budget du programme oscille entre 2,5 M€ et 3,5 M€ ces dernières années et le nombre de staff est autour de 100.

Les principaux bailleurs sont l’AFD, ECHO, le MAE-Luxembourg, la DCI Monaco, Unicef…

Chaque année, dans la région Atsinanana, plus de 16,000 personnes peuvent être directement affectées par des cyclones et des inondations, avec 13 systèmes, dont 4 atteignent le statut de cyclone tropical. De l’autre côté, la commune urbaine de Tuléar a enregistré 7 systèmes cycloniques durant une même période, y compris les 2 cyclones tropicales qui ont révélé la vulnérabilité aux risques d’inondation de la zone et la nécessité d’améliorer le SAP.

Comme chaque année, le programme Madagascar répond aux appels du financement HIP de Echo et pour 2026, HI a été demandé de rejoindre le consortium mené par PAM pour leur troisième phase du projet RUP, Strengthening Government-Led Urban Preparedness, Anticipatory Action, and Disaster Risk Management Systems for Inclusive and Multi-Hazard Resilient Responses in Southern Africa. Le projet sera mis en oeuvre dans les villes de Antananarivo, Sambava, Toamasina et Toliara. Il répond aux problématiques liées aux aléas pouvant causer des dégâts physiques et matériels, des déplacements, et occasionner des risques de protection (VBG, enfants) et des risques accrus d’exclusion des personnes handicapées et autres groups marginalisés. Il vise également à renforcer l’approche PGI Protection Genre Inclusion, jugée insuffisante, dans préparations et la réduction des risques. Comme objectif, le projet veut ainsi renforcer la préparation urbaine menée par le gouvernement, l'action anticipatoire et les systèmes de gestion des risques de catastrophe pour des réponses inclusives et résilientes face aux dangers en zones urbaines. Du côté de HI, étant un projet bi-pays, implémenté à Madagascar et au Mozambique, le ou la Spécialiste PGI viendra en appui aux deux pays, tout étant basé à Madagascar. Une mission d’appui technique au Mozambique est programmée dans le contexte de ce poste .

VOTRE MISSION :

Dans le cadre du projet régional financé par ECHO visant à renforcer les systèmes de préparation urbaine et d’Action Anticipatoire en Afrique australe, le/la Spécialiste Protection assure le leadership technique de HI sur l’intégration transversale de la Protection, Genre et Inclusion dans les interventions mises en œuvre à Madagascar et au Mozambique.

Vos responsabilités comprennent notamment l’appui technique aux activités de préparation urbaine, d’analyse des vulnérabilités, de ciblage et de protection sociale réactive aux chocs, afin de garantir que les besoins spécifiques des femmes, hommes, filles et garçons, y compris les personnes handicapées, les personnes âgées et les autres groupes à risque, soient systématiquement pris en compte dans les cadres, outils, procédures et systèmes développés par le projet.

Cette fonction contribue en particulier à l’intégration de la PGI dans les cadres nationaux d’évaluation de la vulnérabilité urbaine, les mécanismes de ciblage, les bases de données urbaines interopérables et les systèmes de protection sociale liés à l’Action Anticipatoire et à la réponse aux crises, in synergy with shock-responsive social protection mechanisms managed by INAS and the strategic orientations of INGD in Mozambique.

Vous supervisez et accompagne techniquement les ressources spécialisées des deux pays, notamment le/la Senior Technical Officer Protection au Mozambique, afin d’assurer la cohérence, la qualité technique et la capitalisation des approches développées dans les différents contextes d’intervention.

Vous veillez également à l’intégration des principes de protection, d’inclusion du handicap, d’égalité de genre, de sauvegarde, d’accessibilité et de redevabilité envers les populations affectées dans les cadres de préparation urbaine, les mécanismes d’alerte précoce, les exercices de simulation, les systèmes de coordination et les dispositifs d’Action Anticipatoire développés par les autorités nationales et municipales.

Dans ce cadre vous collaborez étroitement avec les STO DRR ( Reduction des risques de catastrophe) and the strategic partners (such as WFP) .Au-delà de l’appui direct à Madagascar et au Mozambique, le poste contribue à la diffusion des apprentissages, des bonnes pratiques et des approches PGI à l’échelle régionale à travers les plateformes de coordination de la SADC.

Responsabilités et missions

1\. EXPERTISE TECHNIQUE

- Conduit la stratégie sectorielle et contribue à la réflexion stratégique
- Assure un appui technique aux projets conformément aux cadres et standards techniques
- Appuie l’intégration de la PGI dans les systèmes de préparation et de gestion des risques
- Assure le contrôle qualité technique et le suivi

2\. DÉVELOPPEMENT STRATÉGIQUE ET DÉVELOPPEMENT D’OPPORTUNITÉS

- Assure une veille stratégique et technique
- Développe des partenariats stratégiques
- Soutient le développement de nouveaux projets
- Représente HI dans les espaces de coordination, d’influence et de plaidoyer
- Contribue à la visibilité technique et à la communication externe

3\. GESTION DES CONNAISSANCES ET APPRENTISSAGE

- Coordonne la gestion des connaissances et favorise l’innovation
- Assure le renforcement des capacités

SPECIFICITES/PARTICULARITES DU POSTE :

Le poste de Spécialiste PGI est basé à Antananarivo ou la vie sociale et culturelle est très agréable et développée. Tana offre tout le confort des capitales modernes et le désagrément d’une pollution atmosphérique élevée. La criminalité y est présente : les vols à l’arraché sont courants en ville et il existe des cas de vols au domicile avec violence. Un brieifng à l’arrivée et des mesures de sécurité sont mise en place par le programme pour réduire les différentes menaces. Les missions dans les régions Sud et de l’Est de Madagascar seront fréquentes et suivront le cadre sécuritaire de HI

Enfin, Madagascar est réputé pour ses paysages et son offre touristique qui permettent beaucoup de belles découvertes.

Le titulaire du poste sera amené à fournir un appui technique au Mozambique et devra effectuer, à cet effet, une mission d'une durée estimée entre 8 et 10 jours.
Exigences

A. Formation

- Diplôme de niveau Master en sciences sociales, anthropologie sociale, droit, études de genre, sociologie, études culturelles, action humanitaire, développement international ou tout autre domaine pertinent.

B. Expérience professionnelle

- Minimum de 5 années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le secteur de la protection au sein d’une ONG ou d’une ONG internationale.
- Expérience démontrée dans les approches de genre et l’intégration du genre dans les programmes humanitaires et/ou de développement.
- Au moins 3 années d’expérience terrain dans une fonction technique en protection.

Avantages

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle :

· Contrat International de 12 mois à compter idéalement de Janvier 2027;

· Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :

Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
Assurance retraite ;
Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;

· Salaire : à partir de 2757€ brut/mois ; selon expérience professionnelle ;

· Perdiem : 623 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;

· Congés payés : 25 jours par an ;

· Poste Non accompagné :

o Prise en charge des frais de transport, de visas et de transport de vos effets personnels

o A partir de 12 mois de mission : une allocation enfant de 100 € versée à partir de 2 enfants à charge, versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;
