jobs.title: Chargé(e) de communication Opérations et Campagnes Siège Dakar - H/F
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION DE L’ONG**

ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) est une ONG humanitaire médicale internationale, créée en 2009. Elle offre des soins de santé de qualité aux populations vulnérables confrontées à des crises sanitaires, des [épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) ou des catastrophes naturelles.

ALIMA intervient lors des crises humanitaires, dans les [zones de conflits](https://alima.ngo/conflits-populations-deplacees/), [d’épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) et de malnutrition où les besoins médicaux sont les plus urgents. ALIMA associe des [soins d’urgence](https://alima.ngo/reponse-urgences/) à des [projets de recherche de plus long terme](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) pour développer de nouvelles solutions et améliorer durablement la prise en charge des populations les plus vulnérables.

8 domaines d’expertise

- [Épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/)
- [Malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/)
- [Santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/)
- [Pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/)
- [Santé mentale](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-mentale/)
- [Recherche et innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/)
- [Renforcement du système de santé](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/renforcement-systeme-sante/)
- [Chirurgie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/chirurgie-humanitaire/)

ALIMA collabore avec des autorités sanitaires nationales et locales, des [ONG locales](https://alima.ngo/agir/nous-soutenir/devenir-partenaire/partenaires-operationnels/), des communautés, et des instituts de recherche pour bâtir des solutions humanitaires innovantes et adaptées. Son siège opérationnel à Dakar reflète son ancrage au plus près du terrain et 95 % de ses équipes viennent des pays d’intervention.

Depuis 2009, ALIMA a soigné plus de 46 millions de personnes dans [16 pays](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/nos-operations/), principalement en Afrique. L’organisation se distingue par son expertise en [malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/), [pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/), [santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/) et [réponse aux épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/), entre autres.

Grâce à la [recherche et à l’innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) issues de l’expérience sur le terrain, et au renforcement des capacités locales dans nos pays d’opération, ALIMA s’efforce de transformer la médecine humanitaire et de mieux protéger les populations des crises sanitaires de demain.

**PRÉSENTATION DU POSTE**

**Liens hiérarchiques et fonctionnels :**

Superviseur hiérarchique : Responsable Communication Opérations

Personnels sous sa responsabilité hiérarchique : aucun

Il/elle collabore avec :

- Les Missions dans les pays et les Desks au Siège de Dakar
- L’équipe Bailleurs
- L’équipe Communication (siège et pays)
- L’équipe Développement / Collecte (Sénégal, France, USA, UK, Suisse)
- Les équipes et partenaires Recherche
- Les prestataires externes (agences…)

**Enjeux du poste :**

Combiner :

- Une communication à 360° relative à votre portefeuille de pays
- Une communication institutionnelle créative

**Missions et objectifs :**

Conformément aux orientations stratégiques et aux priorités fixées par la Directrice de la Communication, vous avez pour missions principales de :

- **Communiquer sur les actions humanitaires et les travaux de recherche d’ALIMA relatifs à votre portefeuille de pays**
- Aujourd’hui les pays concernés sont : Cameroun, Mali, Mauritanie, Guinée (cette liste est susceptible d’évoluer en 2027 selon les besoins de l’ONG).
- Cela couvre tous les aspects de la communication : stratégies de communication (plans de communication par pays et par bailleurs), suivi de l’ensemble des budgets communication du portfolio pays, mise en oeuvre des plans de communication et production de contenus, reporting bailleurs, communication de soutien au fundraising, site web et social media, relations presse, communication scientifique / recherche, communication interne, événementiel au niveau des pays (le cas échéant).
- Cela cible des audiences B to B et B to C, en France, aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni et plus largement à l’international.
- Cela s’effectue en collaboration avec les directions et services concernés.
- **Si besoin, concevoir et déployer des campagnes de communication créatives**
- Selon les besoins, elles pourront être institutionnelles ou de collecte, B to B ou B to C, en France ou dans un autre pays.

Vos objectifs sont à la fois :

- **Qualitatifs :** développer la visibilité d’ALIMA, valoriser son positionnement et son impact ;
- **Quantitatifs :** contribuer à augmenter l’audience d’ALIMA au sein des diverses communautés, le trafic sur le site ALIMA, les dons en ligne…

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

1. **Définir, formaliser et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de communication 360° dans votre portefeuille de pays.**

- Définir et mettre en oeuvre un plan de communication annuel pour chaque pays de votre portefeuille de pays (incluant la gestion afférente du budget) :
- Planifier des opportunités de communication complémentaires en lien avec l’actualité (ex : crise sanitaire), les temps forts de l’année (ex : Journée mondiale) et les temps forts du calendrier des projets (ex : ouverture d’un nouveau projet, résultats d’un essai clinique)
- Concevoir la partie Communication des propositions (“proposals”) faites aux partenaires financiers (bailleurs, fondations privées), en coordination avec l’équipe chargée des relations avec les bailleurs et les grands donateurs. S’assurer de leur pertinence, de leur faisabilité et de leur rationalisation. Assurer le reporting auprès des bailleurs.
- Suivre le contexte géopolitique et de l’actualité impactant l’activité d’ALIMA dans vos pays.
- Organiser des reportages sur les projets afin de produire des contenus textes, photos, vidéos - par conséquent, voyager parfois dans les pays pour assurer la bonne production - avec ou sans prestataire - de ces contenus ;
- Assurer les processus administratifs et budgétaires nécessaires (ex : termes de référence, devis/factures, contrats prestataires, etc.) ;
- Mettre à jour les brochures pays pour chaque pays de votre portefeuille de pays, et produire tout autre document ou support de visibilité (ex : panneaux, signalétique) ou de communication institutionnelle nécessaire (kakemono, poster, etc. ) si besoin pour vos pays.
- La direction demande chaque année un stagiaire pour mettre à jour la Media Gallery. La priorité est que la Media Gallery soit gérée par ce stagiaire. Toutefois, en cas d’absence de stagiaire (ex : gap, non renouvellement, problème budgétaire), il sera demandé au Chargée de communication de mettre à jour lui-même la Media Gallery avec les contenus photos relatifs à son portefeuille de pays.
- Appuyer les missions de vos pays sur les aspects techniques de communication lors de commande d’outils visibilité (création d’outils, respect des règles établies, validation de BAT).

1. **Contribuer activement à la communication digitale**

- Proposer des contenus relatifs à votre portefeuille de pays, nourrissant le calendrier éditorial digital (ex : article web, post RS, script vidéo…)
- Développer un réflexe “communication digitale” au sein des Missions dans votre portefeuille de pays et former régulièrement les équipes des Missions pour les rendre autonomes dans la production de contenus photos et vidéos exploitables pour la Communication.

1. **Contribuer activement aux relations presse**

- Traiter les demandes médias, organiser les interviews, préparer les porte-parole (éléments de langage, etc.), faire le suivi jusqu’à la parution de la retombée presse
- Se coordonner avec les agences de relations presse prestataires en France et aux Etats-Unis pour proposer des sujets qui retiennent l’attention des journalistes (ex : , pitch média sur un sujet à “vendre” aux journalistes, décryptage d’une actualité pays, interview d’un porte-parole, organisation d’un reportage sur le terrain…).
- Contribuer à la conception et la production de contenus et de supports pertinents pour les relations presse (ex : communiqués de presse)
- Contribuer à identifier les journalistes clefs couvrant l’actualité et les thématiques dans votre portefeuille de pays. Être identifiée comme personne ressource par ces derniers.
- Développer un réflexe “relations presse” au sein des Missions dans les pays et former régulièrement les équipes des Missions à la prise de parole et à la gestion des journalistes sur le terrain.
- Coordonner d'éventuelles visites de presse dans votre portefeuille de pays, en collaboration avec les équipes terrain et le Desk - par conséquent, voyager dans les pays pour assurer le bon déroulement de ces visites.
- Entretenir des relations étroites et régulières avec le pool de porte-parole d’ALIMA issus des pays d’opérations (ex : Responsable Desk, Chef de Mission pays) ou de thématiques (ex : Recherche, Nutrition) de façon à pouvoir les activer facilement. Les former en media training particulièrement lorsque l’équipe se renouvelle.

1. **Contribuer activement à la communication interne**

- Valoriser en interne l’activité humanitaire et de recherche menée par les Missions du portefeuille pays (ex : concevoir et diffuser des emailings internes sur l’avancée d’un projet de recherche)
- Valoriser en interne la communication relative à l’activité d’ALIMA dans vos pays ou aux campagnes de communication menées par ALIMA (ex : emailing interne sur une belle séquence médiatique)

1. **Piloter, le cas échéant, la conception, la production et la diffusion des campagnes de communication d’ALIMA, lorsque celles-ci sont jugées pertinentes au regard des priorités et des besoins de l’organisation.**

- Définir et rédiger les briefs créatifs relatifs aux campagnes
- Identifier les prestataires les plus pertinents
- Prendre en charge la sélection des prestataires (appels d’offres) puis gérer les prestataires dans le cadre de la gestion de projet
- Assurer la gestion de projet des campagnes, du brief créatif à la mesure d’efficacité de la campagne après diffusion
- Se coordonner le cas échéant avec les autres services et directions concernés par ces campagnes (ex : fundraising, digital)
- Assurer le suivi budgétaire de ces campagnes

**COMPETENCES ET EXPERIENCES**

**Niveau d’étude**

Diplôme d'études supérieures en communication, journalisme, gestion de projet ou domaine équivalent.

**Expériences**

- Expérience professionnelle similaire confirmée, idéalement dans une ONG, une organisation internationale, une association ou une agence de communication
- Expérience en communication : plans de communication, production de contenus et de supports, rédaction, chaîne graphique, relations presse, digital, événementiel…
- Expérience avérée en relations presse : traitement de demandes de journalistes, organisation de reportage sur le terrain
- Expérience avérée en conception, production et diffusion de contenus : articles, videos, newsletters, posts réseaux sociaux, campagnes digitales
- Expérience en gestion de prestataires
- Expérience en suivi budgétaire et gestion de projets
- Une expérience en environnement multiculturel et anglophone est un plus
- Une connaissance du continent africain est un plus

**Connaissances linguistiques**

La maîtrise du français (niveau natif impératif) et de l’anglais (niveau B2 minimum) est indispensable.

**Compétences techniques**

- Capacité à gérer des projets complexes en FR et en EN
- Capacité à s’exprimer et à rédiger en FR et EN
- Excellent rédactionnel
- Sens stratégique, capacité à penser, formaliser et déployer des stratégies de communication
- Maîtrise de la gestion de projet
- Maîtrise parfaite des outils informatiques, maîtrise de Canva, Monday

**Qualités recherchées**

- Excellente capacité d’organisation et de gestion de projet
- Capacité à prioriser dans un environnement exigeant
- Rigueur et fiabilité
- Capacité à vulgariser des sujets complexes à s’adapter à son public
- Autonomie et rigueur
- Bon relationnel, capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs variés en milieu multiculturel

## Conditions

- - **CDI de droit sénégalais**
- **Prise de poste** : Dès que possible
- **Salaire** : selon la grille de salaire en vigueur au Siège de Dakar.
- Avantages extra contractuels :
- Cinq semaines de congés payés par an et système de jours de récupération pour les déplacements
- Prise en charge des frais de scolarité pour les enfants à charge, dans le cadre de la politique et des plafonds ALIMA en vigueur ;
- Couverture santé complémentaire pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.

jobs.title: Request for Proposals: Provision of Professional Background Screening Services
jobs.description:
**RFP Reference:** RFP-ISH-11-12
**Issuing Organization:** [inSupply Health](https://insupplyhealth.com/)
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya
**Issue Date:** 12 November 2026
**Proposal Submission Deadline:** 20 November 2026 at 12:00 noon EAT

**About inSupply Health**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming for business sustainability while achieving our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, contextualized supply chain learning and innovations so local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with a subsidiary office in Dar es Salaam and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). Our team of dynamic local consultants works closely with public and private sector clients to design optimized, responsive and resilient supply chain systems that deliver essential health products such as antimalarial and HIV medications, vaccines and contraceptives in complex settings. We pioneer innovative approaches by taking proven methodologies from the commercial sector to adapt them for the context, but also co-create solutions with our clients so they can own, implement and continuously improve their systems independently in the long term.

**Purpose of the RFP**

inSupply Health invites qualified and experienced professional background screening service providers to submit proposals for the provision of comprehensive background screening services to support its recruitment and human resource management processes.

The selected provider will be expected to deliver reliable, timely, confidential and legally compliant background screening services across African countries relevant to inSupply Health's operations and recruitment needs.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The provider shall offer the checks below as requested for each candidate or staff member, subject to applicable law, candidate notice and consent where required, and the availability of reliable records.

1. **Identity and name verification**: Confirm identity details using appropriate, lawful sources.
2. **Academic and professional qualification verification**: Verify qualifications, certificates, licences and other credentials with the issuing institution or relevant authority, where feasible.
3. **Employment history verification**: Confirm employment dates, positions held and other agreed employment details with previous employers or authorised referees.
4. **Professional membership verification**: Confirm current or historical membership, registration or good standing with relevant professional bodies, where applicable.
5. **Reference and character checks:** Obtain structured references from agreed referees to assess relevant work history, conduct and professional suitability.
6. **Criminal record checks**: Obtain available criminal record or police clearance information through lawful channels in the relevant jurisdiction.
7. **Sanctions and watchlist screening**: Screen against relevant sanctions, restricted-party and other legally appropriate watchlists, and provide context for any potential match.
8. **Credit checks:** Conduct only where relevant to the role, lawful, appropriately authorised and supported by applicable consent or other legal basis.
9. **Statutory and regulatory compliance checks:** Where relevant to the role and legally permissible, verify specified regulatory or statutory compliance information. Any business-level checks must be separately authorised and clearly distinguished from checks on an individual.
10. **Safeguarding-related checks**: Conduct relevant checks permitted by law to identify substantiated or recorded concerns related to child protection, sexual misconduct or other safeguarding risks, where reliable records and lawful processes are available.

The provider shall identify which checks can be conducted directly and which rely on local partners or third-party databases. The provider must not represent a search as completed where records are unavailable; such cases should be reported as “unable to verify” or an equivalent clear status, with the reason and any recommended next step.

**Geographic Coverage:**

The provider should be able to conduct checks in Africa relevant to inSupply’s recruitment needs. The proposal must specify:

- Countries and jurisdictions covered, distinguishing direct service delivery from partner supported checks.
- Types of checks available in each country and any limitations or exclusions.
- Local partner arrangements and quality assurance measures, where applicable.
- Country-specific pricing, additional fees, taxes and currency.
- Expected turnaround times by check type and country.

**Deliverables and Service Standards**

- A clear, candidate specific screening report covering each check requested, the method or source used, the result, the date completed and any limitations.
- A summary of verified discrepancies, potential matches, safeguarding concerns or other material findings, with supporting details sufficient for inSupply to assess them.
- Prompt notification to the designated inSupply contact of material concerns, potential safeguarding risks or delays; urgent safeguarding concerns should be escalated without undue delay.
- A status update where a check is delayed, inconclusive or cannot be completed, including the reason and expected next step.
- Secure handling and transmission of reports and supporting records, with access restricted to authorised recipients.
- A target turnaround time of no more than 10 working days per screening request, unless otherwise agreed. The provider must state when the clock starts, identify dependencies on candidate documentation or third parties, and notify inSupply of anticipated delays.
- A named account contact and a clear process for queries, corrections, complaints and escalation.

**Confidentiality, Data Protection and Ethical Standards**

- Comply with applicable data protection, privacy, employment and background screening laws in each relevant jurisdiction.
- Collect, access, use, retain, transfer and dispose of personal data only for authorised purposes and on a valid legal basis, with candidate notice and consent where required.
- Apply appropriate technical and organisational security measures, including role-based access controls and secure data transfer.
- Use reputable and lawful sources; maintain an auditable record of checks and verification steps; and avoid discriminatory or irrelevant screening.
- Limit disclosure to information relevant to the requested check and the role. Clearly distinguish verified facts, potential matches, third-party statements and unverified information.
- Notify inSupply promptly of any actual or suspected data breach affecting its information and cooperate with reasonable incident response requests.
- Disclose any subcontractors or local partners involved in processing data and ensure they are subject to appropriate confidentiality, security and compliance obligations.

**Provider Qualifications**

The service provider should demonstrate:

- A proven track record delivering professional background screening in Africa or international jurisdictions.
- Experience verifying academic credentials, employment history, identity, professional standing and safeguarding-related information.
- Appropriate registrations, licences or authorisations required to provide the services in relevant jurisdictions.
- Established quality assurance, information security and data protection procedures.
- Access to reliable databases, issuing institutions, relevant authorities and vetted local partners.
- Capacity to meet the required turnaround times and provide responsive client support.

**Contract Duration**

The proposed engagement period will be **two (2) years**, commencing on a mutually agreed date. The engagement will be subject to annual performance reviews by inSupply Health.

**Proposal Submission Requirements**

Interested service providers are required to submit both technical and financial proposals containing:

1. Company profile, registration details and relevant experience.
2. Valid statutory documentation, including company registration documents, KRA Tax PIN and Tax Compliance Certificate, where applicable.
3. Detailed methodology and workflow for each proposed screening service.
4. Country-by-country coverage, available check types, use of local partners and known limitations.
5. Financial proposal with pricing by check type and country, inclusive of applicable taxes, additional fees, currencies and volume-based rates, where available.
6. Expected turnaround times by check type and country, including service-level and escalation arrangements.
7. Data protection, confidentiality, information security, data retention and breach-response measures.
8. At least three client references, preferably from corporate or NGO clients for comparable background screening services.

See full RFP Requirements [**Here.**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UlheOHHQxrnPySDn37545ApAbW7gOeqP/view?usp=drive_link)

**Child Safeguarding**

inSupply Health is committed to safeguarding children and promoting their safety and well being. The provider must demonstrate how its screening approach supports this commitment, including the lawful use of relevant safeguarding checks and the prompt escalation of material concerns. The provider must not guarantee that any check can establish the complete absence of safeguarding risk; it should clearly describe the checks performed and their limitations.

**Evaluation and Selection**

Proposals will undergo a preliminary review for completeness and compliance with the RFP requirements. Responsive proposals will be evaluated on a best-value basis, considering technical capability, service quality, geographic coverage, pricing, turnaround times and relevant past performance.

Proposals will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and inSupply Health reserves the right to notify successful applicants before the submission deadline.

inSupply Health reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals and is under no obligation to make an award as a result of this RFP.

**Primary Supervisor:** Finance Director

**Location:** Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

We are seeking an experienced **Senior Finance & Accounting Officer** to lead and coordinate the finance function in our Tanzania Country Office.

The successful candidate will provide day-to-day leadership of the Tanzania Finance Unit, ensuring effective financial management, accurate accounting, timely financial reporting, statutory and donor compliance, strong internal controls and accountability in the utilisation of organisational and donor resources.

Working under the technical and functional oversight of the Finance Director and in close collaboration with the Country Director, the role will ensure that country-level financial operations align with organisational policies, donor requirements and applicable Tanzanian regulatory frameworks.

**Responsibilities:**

1. ## **Finance Unit Leadership & Management**

- Lead and coordinate the day-to-day operations of the Tanzania Finance Unit.
- Supervise, mentor and provide technical guidance to the finance Analyst.
- Strengthen financial processes, systems, internal controls and accountability.
- Ensure accuracy and integrity of financial transactions and ERP data.

## **2. Accounting & Financial Reporting**

- Oversee accurate and complete accounting records, including general ledger, accounts payable, receivables, payroll accounting and bank reconciliations.
- Coordinate monthly, quarterly and annual financial close processes.
- Ensure timely preparation and submission of accurate financial reports.
- Review financial transactions, reconciliations and supporting documentation.

## **3. Budget Management & Financial Monitoring**

- Coordinate preparation and review of country-level and project budgets.
- Monitor budget utilisation, expenditure, commitments and variances.
- Prepare budget-versus-actual reports and financial analysis.
- Maintain grant financial tracking schedules and support financial sustainability projections.
- Provide financial insights to support management and resource allocation decisions.

## **4. Donor Financial Management & Compliance**

- Review grant agreements, subaward agreements and amendments to identify financial obligations and donor requirements.
- Ensure compliance with donor financial management requirements and approved budgets.
- Coordinate preparation and review of donor financial reports.
- Monitor project expenditure, cost allocation and supporting documentation.
- Identify and escalate financial compliance risks and unsupported expenditure.

## **5. Statutory Compliance, Taxation & Regulatory Reporting**

- Ensure compliance with applicable Tanzanian financial, tax, statutory and regulatory requirements.
- Coordinate preparation and timely submission of statutory returns and tax declarations.
- Liaise with relevant government agencies and tax authorities.
- Monitor changes in financial legislation and advise management on their implications.

## **6. Internal Controls, Risk Management & Audit**

- Implement and monitor effective internal financial controls.
- Identify financial control weaknesses and recommend corrective measures.
- Coordinate internal and external audits for the Tanzania Country Office.
- Follow up on audit findings and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions.
- Lead the monthly financial close process and ensure timely submission of management accounts.

## **7. Stakeholder Engagement & Financial Advisory**

- Provide financial guidance to the Country Director, project managers, programme teams and budget holders.
- Work closely with the Finance Director to ensure consistency in financial management and reporting.
- Support management in understanding the financial implications of operational decisions.
- Coordinate with banks, auditors, tax consultants, government agencies and other relevant stakeholders.

**Qualifications & Experience**

### **Academic & Professional Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics or a related field from a recognised university.
- Full professional accounting qualification such as CPA (T), ACCA or an equivalent internationally recognised qualification.
- Active membership or eligibility for registration with a recognised professional accounting body, such as NBAA (Tanzania) or an equivalent recognised professional body.

**Professional Experience**

- At least 5 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, particularly in grants management, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury management and donor compliance.
- In-depth knowledge of accounting principles, practices, standards, laws and regulations.
- Strong knowledge of Tanzanian accounting standards, taxation, financial regulations and statutory requirements.
- Experience managing multi-donor projects and donor financial reporting is highly desirable.
- Experience working in the health or non-profit sector is an added advantage.
- Experience using accounting and ERP systems, with Microsoft Dynamics experience an added advantage.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial reporting tools.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a professional who demonstrates:

- Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting standards, donor compliance requirements and applicable Tanzanian financial regulations.
- Strong financial analysis, problem-solving and risk-management skills.
- Excellent budgeting, forecasting, expenditure monitoring and financial variance analysis skills.
- Strong planning, organisation and documentation management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present financial information clearly.
- Strong leadership, collaboration and stakeholder-management skills.
- Ability to provide financial guidance and strengthen the financial management capacity of staff and budget holders.
- High levels of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and deliver accurate work within tight deadlines.

## **Why Join Us?**

At inSupply Health, you will work with a **collaborative, purpose-driven team** committed to transforming health systems across East Africa.

You will have the opportunity to contribute to impactful multi-country programmes, work alongside diverse technical and operational teams, strengthen systems and processes, and grow your professional expertise in a dynamic and learning-oriented environment.

jobs.title: ESOL Tutor
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Since 1933, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers life-saving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster.

The International Rescue Committee UK is part of the IRC global network, which is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through over 20 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

***This position has an end date of January 31, 2027.***

**IRC UK**

IRC UK was established in London in 1997 to support the organisation’s global activities and particularly to diversify its donor base and be able to better advocate with European policy-makers on behalf of the people we serve. Since its establishment IRC UK has grown rapidly and is now acknowledged for its high-quality project management, technical expertise in governance and rights and economic recovery, and innovative thinking on early recovery and gender-based violence. IRC UK comprises approximately 240 staff. The IRC UK launched its first Resettlement Asylum and Integration (RAI) programme in the UK called RISE in 2020, working in partnership with local councils, to provide integration support to resettled refugees in Southeast England. The IRC now supports refugees and asylum seekers throughout England.

**The Purpose of the Role**

We are seeking an experienced and dedicated hourly paid ESOL Tutor to deliver online ESOL sessions in a safe and supportive learning environment. The ideal candidate will bring creativity and flexibility, adapting their teaching methods to meet the diverse needs of learners.

As an ESOL Tutor, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality ESOL provision across multiple IRC projects, empowering adult learners to achieve their goals and thrive in their communities.

**Key Working Relationships:**

The position reports to the ESOL coordinator.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES**

- Plan, prepare, and deliver engaging and interactive online ESOL lessons for refugees at different levels.
- Apply trauma-informed teaching practices to foster safe and supportive learning environments.
- Prepare and adapt teaching resources, including materials for pre-entry level ESOL and basic literacy learners from refugee and migrant backgrounds.
- Set, mark and provide constructive feedback on homework and classwork.
- Follow safeguarding, data protection and equality and diversity policies

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

- Holds a recognized ESOL teaching qualification.
- Proven experience in designing and delivering online ESOL programmes, ideally for refugees and learners with low literacy in their first language.
- Experience in developing ESOL resources.
- Ability to adapt content and delivery methods to meet the diverse needs of participants.
- Demonstrated cultural sensitivity and understanding of trauma-informed practice.
- Strong digital skills and proficiency in using online learning platforms.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Fluency in Farsi, Dari, or Pashto is desirable

**You must have the right to work in the UK.**

IRC UK strives to be an equal opportunities employer. IRC-UK is committed to equality of opportunity and to non-discrimination for all job applicants and employees, and we seek to ensure diversity in our workforce regardless of gender, race, religious beliefs, nationality, ethnic/national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.

IRC UK welcomes applications from all candidates, including underrepresented groups and refugees who have the right to work in the UK.

**Compensation:** (36,000 GBP - pro rata). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) - Remote USA
jobs.description:
**ABOUT SPARK MICROGRANTS**

Spark MicroGrants believes in a world where everyone lives with dignity and determines their own positive future. Spark has worked in 1000+ villages in 6 countries and has pioneered a community-driven development model in sub-Saharan Africa. Spark works with NGO and Government partners to scale the model's adoption and impact on rural communities - on their own terms. Our model combines facilitated community meetings with a small, discretionary grant to catalyze local action and institution building. Read more about our [Approach](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/the-spark-process), [Impact ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/impact)and [Values ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/about-spark#about-our-values)on our [website](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/).

**OVERVIEW**

The Senior Manager, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) will bridge the gap between high-level vision for new partnerships and funding relationships and the creation of realistic budgets, reports and financial narratives that meet donor needs and clearly communicate the relationship between outcomes and funding. They will have deep experience in financial analysis, reporting, systems and tools, and are equally comfortable estimating high level information and building detailed models to support financial analysis and decision making. This role is an individual contributor and is a hands-on producer of value-added financial analysis, modeling, and reporting, and will report directly to the CFO. The incumbent will collaborate with senior leadership, and work extensively with the fundraising team on donor and Board deliverables and on helping the organization and its stakeholders understand the financial impacts of new projects and partnerships.

They will also lead enterprise functions including risk management and cash forecasting, and lead key aspects of financial operations on behalf of the CFO. They will implement effective tracking and monitoring of Global and US operations OKRs, metrics and customer deliverables, and ensure appropriate follow-up and communication with stakeholders.

Due to the amount of coordination with the fundraising team they will need to be based in the US and available on US East Coast time schedules, as well as being available to meet with teammates in Africa during cross-over time zones.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Financial reporting, analysis and scenario modeling in support of fundraising**

- Model the cost of new projects, programs and partnerships and build repeatable tools and processes to increase the efficiency of generating external-facing budgets.
- Own financial processes for donor budgets, including templates, guidelines, metrics and analysis.
- Collaborate with program and functional teams to provide value added analysis and model future scenarios.
- Lead financial due diligence responses, and ensure adequate policies and practices are in place to satisfy key donor expectations and deliverables.

**Annual Budget, forecasting, and actual versus budget analysis**

- Forecast quarterly, annual and long term revenue and cash flows, and model alternative scenarios, in support of budgeting and strategic planning processes.
- Ensure effective and timely tracking of forecasted revenues, cash flows and donor restrictions.
- Provide financial guidance to global support functions, including Operations, Fundraising, Executive and Innovation teams, and execute the annual budget process together with these teams. They will also provide reporting and analysis in support of the monthly Budget vs Actual (BVA) process and quarterly forecasting updates.

.**Financial support to the Innovation team on proposals, pilot projects and research**

- Work with the Chief Innovation Officer to model new opportunities, and to provide budgeting, reporting and analysis of pilot projects.
- Support the implementation of new processes and systems required to accommodate new workstreams, and coordinate the hand-over of expanding programs to the core finance team.
- Provide financial support for Social Return on Investment calculations and other financial metrics that aid decision making on where to allocate resources.

**Build organization-wide financial reporting and optimize finance tools**

- Work closely with the Head of Finance and CFO to design and build financial reporting models to meet internal and external needs,
- Ensure optimal use of the current Netsuite reporting tools to ensure that reporting meets customer needs.
- Use AI effectively and responsibly to help the finance team become more efficient.
- Create effective materials to report financial status and forecasts to the internal Executive Committee, as well as to the Board, and Board Finance Committee.
- Implement financial processes, reporting, templates and budgets in support of new grants and projects, before handing off to the Country Finance team.

**Risk Management**

- Implement enterprise risk tracking and action registers.
- Coordinate enterprise insurance policies and other risk mitigations.
- Work with Country Finance Managers and the Head of Finance to ensure appropriate funds available in each region.
- Lead the development of key global policies and procedures including those related to risk management, treasury, and legal.

**US & Global Operations**

- Lead the implementation and effective use of operations dashboards, metrics, and global procedures.
- Coordinate US Operations including financial operations, procurement, and compliance with state and federal regulations.
- Lead strategic Finance and Operations projects and cross-functional initiatives.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**Education:**

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

MBA or Professional accounting certification (CPA, or equivalent) is desirable.

**Experience:**

- 5-10+ years of progressively responsible experience in financial analysis, budgeting and reporting, preferably in an NGO or international development context.
- Experience designing and creating value-added reporting for internal and external stakeholders.
- Proven experience implementing useful financial tools and improving the timeliness, accuracy and usefulness of financial information.
- Experience with non-profit programs, grants finance, and donor budgets is highly desirable.
- Netsuite, Google workspace, Business intelligence tools, and strong Excel/google sheets skills.

**Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong analytical and judgment skills: You know when to estimate and when to do more detailed analysis, and you are good at both: You see patterns in the data and incorporate them to make effective estimates, and to provide support for financial decisions.
- Excellent execution skills: You get things done and you also set them up to be done efficiently the next time.
- Financial Tools and Systems: You are an early adapter of new technology and like to find efficient ways to produce analysis and reporting. You use AI effectively in your day to day work and continue to add new skills and tools to your toolkit.
- Adaptability: You like new projects and challenges, and enjoy finding solutions.
- Strong Communicator: You can translate financial concepts for non-financial audiences and provide clear explanations of information and analysis to audiences of varying levels.
- Strategic thinking with the ability to support organizational growth and change
- Solutions-oriented and proactive
- Detail oriented but also able to create high level summarized analysis
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, multi-country environment.
- Committed to Sparks mission and values
- Willingness to travel to Africa periodically

**OTHER INFORMATION**

Job Location: New York or other remote locations in the US, East Coast time zone preferred.

Reporting to: CFO

Start Date: As soon as possible

Salary: The preliminary salary range for this role is approximately $70,000 - $100,000, with final compensation based on experience and skills. We provide a comprehensive benefits package, including 100% employer-paid health insurance premiums for employees and 50% coverage for dependents, a 401(k) plan with a 3% employer contribution, generous paid leave, and a professional development stipend, among other benefits.

Probation period: Three months probation period with learning and performance objectives

How to Apply: Follow the link to apply: [https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/177](https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/177)

**SAFEGUARDING**

Our safeguarding follows a do no harm principle. All Spark staff are expected to respect and uphold the safeguarding procedures and principles to minimize harm to stakeholders, program participants, and the environment, in compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and national legislation in the countries where we operate.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**

Spark Microgrants provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals. Employment decisions at Spark are based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. Spark does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by the law. Spark will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in undue hardship to daily operations.

jobs.title: Head of Logistics
jobs.description:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Head of Logistics**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognising the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organisation from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa (MSF EA) is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Head of Logistics is responsible for providing strategic leadership and coordinated oversight of MSF Eastern Africa's Procurement and Facilities units through the Procurement Team Leader and Facilities Manager. The position will strengthen service quality, value for money, business continuity and collaboration across MSF EA, hosted entities and the Movement, and lead strategy, planning, budgets, governance, performance, coordination, delegation and risk escalation.

This position will be **hierarchically** and **functionally** accountable to **Deputy General Director.**

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

**Strategic Responsibilities**

- Translate MSF EA's Strategic Plan and annual priorities into an integrated logistics and procurement strategy, workplan, budget, service standards, performance indicators and improvement roadmap.
- Provide the Deputy General Director (DGD) and Management Team with timely analysis, options and recommendations on procurement, facilities, workplace services, assets, logistics, risks and resource priorities.
- Maintain a clear operating model across Procurement and Facilities, ensuring responsibilities, decision rights, escalation pathways and service expectations are understood and applied.
- Anticipate changing organizational and humanitarian support needs and guide proportionate, practical solutions that strengthen readiness, resilience and service continuity.
- Act as a strategic business partner in translating the logistics unit’s needs to workforce solutions.
- Champion digital transformation across procurement and facilities promoting automation and workflow optimization, and efficiency in governance and controls.

**Technical and Operational Responsibilities**

***Procurement governance and performance oversight***

- Drive strategic direction and management of major procurements and compliances to improve planning, execution and expenditures monitoring supplier relationships & value creation.
- Provide oversight for procurement planning, sourcing, tendering, contracting, supplier management, purchasing and procurement analytics, with operational delivery led by the Procurement Team Leader.
- Ensure transparent, fair and competitive procurement in line with MSF policies, delegated authority, segregation of duties, the four-eye principle, applicable law and ethical standards.
- Oversee procurement plans, high-value or high-risk sourcing processes, framework agreements, contract portfolios and supplier-risk controls; escalate material exceptions and decisions to the Deputy General Director or appropriate authority.
- Promote value for money through demand planning, market intelligence, category strategies, supplier performance management, spend analysis and responsible sourcing, without reducing decisions to cost alone.
- Roll-out procurement planning and ensure procurement systems, records, dashboards and reporting on real-time visibility, commitments, compliance & quality, supplier dependency, cost effectiveness.

***Facilities, workplace and support services oversight***

- Set direction and provide oversight for safe, functional, inclusive and welcoming workplaces.
- Provide strategic oversight of the organization's fleet and facilities maintenance programmes, ensuring vehicles, buildings, technical installations and critical equipment are maintained through preventive and corrective maintenance plans that maximize reliability, safety, operational availability and cost efficiency.
- Ensure comprehensive preventive maintenance schedules are developed, implemented and monitored for buildings, office and guest-houses infrastructures, fleet, electrical installations, plumbing, fire protection systems and other critical assets.
- Monitor fleet performance, vehicle utilization, maintenance costs, fuel efficiency and replacement planning to ensure safe, reliable and cost-effective transport services.
- Promote quality workforce experience through facility contribution to staff well-being and productivity.
- Oversee space planning, leases, fit-outs, maintenance, utilities, physical access arrangements, workplace equipment and facilities service contracts to support staff wellbeing and organizational effectiveness.
- Enhance workspace optimization through efficient utilization of office space and facility resources
- Ensure preventive maintenance, statutory inspections, accessibility, occupational safety, emergency preparedness and business-continuity measures are planned, resourced and monitored.
- Guide decisions on workplace utilization and service improvements using staff feedback, operational evidence, cost, safety, sustainability and duty-of-care considerations.

***Asset, inventory and lifecycle stewardship***

- Ensure an organization-wide framework for planning, acquisition, receipt, tagging, assignment, movement, maintenance, verification, loss reporting and disposal of assets and inventory.
- Clarify ownership and controls across Procurement, Facilities, ICT, Finance, P&C and user departments, including secure data handling and environmentally responsible disposal of ICT and other sensitive assets.
- Ensure proper assets management, inventory optimization and replacements, through planning, lifecycle forecasting, appropriate stocking strategies, reduction of obsolete inventories, and capital investment recommendations.
- Ensure effective fleet lifecycle management including acquisition planning, registration, insurance, preventive maintenance, licensing, utilization monitoring, replacement planning and environmentally responsible disposal of vehicles.
- Ensure that maintenance records, asset histories, service schedules, warranties and technical documentation are accurately maintained and regularly reviewed to support lifecycle management and audit readiness.
- Monitor asset utilization, condition, insurance, stock exposure and disposal decisions so that resources remain traceable, useful and appropriately safeguarded throughout their lifecycle.

***Risk, compliance, safety and sustainability***

- Maintain logistics and procurement risk registers and ensure proportionate controls for fraud, conflicts of interest, supplier dependency, contract failure, service interruption, safety incidents, information exposure and environmental impacts.
- Work with Legal, Finance, Data Protection, ICT, ASA/Security, Safeguarding and other relevant functions to integrate contractual, financial, cybersecurity, privacy, security, duty-of-care and safeguarding requirements into decisions and services.
- Ensure facilities and fleet operations comply with applicable statutory inspection requirements, occupational health and safety standards, vehicle licensing regulations, environmental obligations and manufacturer maintenance recommendations.
- Provide oversight of outsourced maintenance contractors and fleet service providers to ensure contract compliance, service quality, timely interventions and continuous performance improvement.
- Ensure concerns, incidents, audit findings and policy exceptions are reported promptly, investigated through the appropriate channels and followed by documented corrective action.
- Advance practical environmental commitments, including energy and water efficiency, renewable energy options, waste reduction, responsible purchasing, sustainable mobility and carbon-conscious supplier practices.
- Ensure third party risk management practices are applied across suppliers, contractors and services providers throughout the contract lifecycle.
- Promote environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations, innovation and climate smart considerations in procurement, facility and supplier management with MSF operational priorities.

***People leadership and functional capability***

- Lead planning, coaching, delegation and mentorship support to the Procurement and Facility Units through clear objectives, regular dialogue, constructive feedback, performance management, succession plan and opportunities for professional growth.
- Create a respectful, inclusive and psychologically safe working environment in which managers and teams can raise concerns, learn from mistakes, collaborate and exercise appropriate professional judgement.
- Ensure the function has suitable capacity, role clarity, succession arrangements and technical capability; support recruitment, induction, learning and workload prioritization as needed.
- Encourage cross-functional teamwork and shared problem-solving while avoiding unnecessary operational interference or duplication of the managers' delegated responsibilities.

***Financial management, assurance and improvement***

- Provide strategic financial needs analysis and scenario modeling to support efficient and cost-effective strategic investment and resource prioritization.
- Oversee maintenance and fleet operating budgets, ensuring lifecycle costs, preventive maintenance investments and replacement plans are financially sustainable and aligned with organizational priorities.
- Develop long-term capital replacement plans for facilities infrastructure, fleet and major operational equipment to minimize operational disruptions and optimize total cost of ownership.
- Develop and control the unit budget, monitor expenditure and commitments, and ensure that forecasts, recharges and financial information are accurate, timely and aligned with approved plans.
- Establish meaningful service and performance indicators and lead regular reviews of cost, quality, timeliness, compliance, user experience, sustainability and risk.
- Coordinate responses to audits and reviews, ensure recommendations are addressed, and foster continuous improvement through documented learning, process simplification and appropriate digital tools.
- Ensure technology supports professional judgement, transparency and efficiency, with appropriate human review, access controls, data quality checks and accountability for decisions.

***Stakeholder, vendor and movement collaboration, and Reporting***

- Build trusted relationships with departments, hosted entities and MSF counterparts, ensuring needs are understood, priorities are agreed and service challenges are addressed transparently.
- Develop strategic partnerships with maintenance contractors, fleet service providers, equipment manufacturers and technical specialists to ensure high-quality service delivery, innovation and business continuity.
- Represent MSF EA in relevant internal and external forums and contribute to joint sourcing, shared services, contract mutualization and movement-wide learning where these add value and preserve MSF EA accountability.
- Promote professional, fair and respectful relationships with vendors and service providers, including clear expectations, regular performance dialogue and responsible resolution of disputes.
- Provide regular executive reporting to the DGD and management Team where applicable on strategic initiatives, risks and improvement opportunities.
- Represent MSF EA in strategic supplier engagements at appropriate external logistics or procurement forum

**Other Responsibilities**

- Ensure accurate integration of EDI & Safeguarding aspects into all policies and practices within the Procurement and Facilities units.
- Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
- Compliance Assurance - Ensure that all data processing activities within the Procurement and Facilities comply with relevant data protection laws and regulations, including the Data Protection Act, 2019 and support the team to receive necessary training in this area.
- Policy Adherence - Enforce data protection policies, procedures, and guidelines within the Procurement and Facilities units, ensuring that all team members are aware of and adhere to these protocols.
- Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
- Recognize and reinforce strong performance in supervisees; identify and encourage improvement where needed; and ensure quality and timely performance management process is carried out for supervisees.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Bachelor's degree in logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration, facilities management, engineering or another relevant field.
- A relevant postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.
- Recognized professional certification or membership in procurement, supply chain, logistics, facilities or contract management is strongly desirable.
- Professional fluency in English; knowledge of French or another language used within the MSF movement is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in logistics, procurement, supply chain, facilities or corporate support services, including at least three years leading managers or multidisciplinary teams.
- Sound knowledge of procurement and supply-chain principles, facilities and workplace management, contract and supplier management, asset lifecycle controls, budgeting, risk management and business continuity.
- Knowledge of applicable Kenyan procurement, contracting, occupational safety, environmental, employment and data-protection requirements relevant to the function; familiarity with international humanitarian standards is an advantage.
- Strong digital literacy, including procurement/ERP systems, contract and asset registers, data analysis and performance dashboards; able to apply technology responsibly while retaining human oversight and accountability.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing procurement and facilities portfolios, budgets, contracts, suppliers, assets, workplace projects and organizational risk in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
- Experience strengthening systems, governance, service quality and team capability while maintaining operational responsiveness.
- Experience in an international, humanitarian, health, non-profit or matrix organization is strongly desirable; prior MSF experience is an advantage but not essential.

**Competencies**

- **Technical**
- Strong understanding of end-to-end supply-chain and procurement procedures, including demand planning, sourcing, tendering, contracting, supplier management and procurement analytics.
- Facilities, workplace, maintenance, transport, asset and inventory management oversight.
- Contract governance, commercial judgement, negotiation and value-for-money analysis.
- Budgeting, forecasting, cost control, recharge principles and performance reporting.
- Enterprise risk, internal controls, audit readiness, business continuity, safety and incident management.
- Strategic planning, project and change management, process improvement and responsible use of digital systems and data.
- **Behavioural**
- People-centred leadership: builds trust, listens actively, coaches’ managers and creates conditions for teams to do their best work.
- Strategic thinking and judgement: connect operational realities to long-term priorities and make balanced, evidence-informed decisions.
- Integrity and accountability: acts transparently, protects resources, addresses conflicts of interest and takes responsibility for outcomes.
- Collaboration and influence: works across functions and entities, manages competing expectations and builds workable agreements without relying only on hierarchy.
- Service orientation: understands user needs and improves services while maintaining policy, safety, quality and financial discipline.
- Communication: explains complex matters clearly, gives constructive feedback and adapts messages to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Adaptability and composure: remains practical, respectful and decisive during uncertainty, incidents and shifting priorities.
- Inclusion and respect: values diverse perspectives, addresses bias and exclusion, and supports safe, accessible and equitable workplaces and services.
- Learning and improvement: encourages reflection, uses feedback and data responsibly, and turns lessons into proportionate improvements.
- Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:***

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya)

## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for two Deployment Officers** - **Single Data Entry (SDE) program**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **medium** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Single Data Entry (SDE) project is a transformational initiative led by MSF to significantly improve the quality and efficiency of supply chain data entry in stock management processes (cargo reception, order preparation, stock count) across all OCs. The solution uses QR codes and OCR technologies to automate data capture and integrate with MSF’s existing supply chain tools. With planned deployment across over 120 countries, the SDE project is a complex, multi-OC endeavour requiring a dedicated Deployment Officer to lead and coordinate its successful field implementation.

**Mission :**

The Deployment Officer is responsible for ensuring the effective execution, training and reporting on the SDE solution’s deployment in all designated missions. He/she will ensure readiness checks are validated, conduct deployment with the end users et post deployment follow up, ensure stakeholder engagement, and effective user training. They will collect feedback from the users, monitor performance, and contribute towards improvement of deployment processes based on field experience and feedback.

The Deployment Officer, based in Nairobi, will conduct deployments in MSF missions and projects both in-person and remotely. The role requires frequent travel to field locations (up to 75% of the time). In addition to deployment execution, the Deployment Officer plays a key role in enabling user adoption through user training and change management, acting as a bridge between the field and the SDE product team to ensure that user feedback is collected, and escalated for incorporation into the product as solutions adapted to mission realities. This role also demands strong political acumen to navigate the diverse cultures, organizational dynamics, and power structures across multiple OCs.

The Deployment Officer will also be involved in the facilitation of (TOT) workshops for end users in collaboration with multiple team members.

This position will be **hierarchically** and **functionally** accountable to the **SDE Deployment Manager**.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

**1. Deployment Execution & Technical Readiness**

- Send out, follow up on, and consolidate pre-deployment readiness checklists for target field missions and projects.
- Physically or remotely inspect site readiness based on specific location requirements (e.g., Pharmacies & Warehouses)
- Coordinate with field focal points to secure resource availability for upcoming deployment cycles
- Execute on-site deployment activities, including user onboarding, Go-Live support, and immediate troubleshooting

**2. Field Readiness & Stakeholder Engagement**

- Ensure missions are fully deployment-ready by bridging coordination between field leadership, IT, and supply teams
- Facilitate local change management initiatives to actively drive stakeholder engagement and user buy-in
- Support capacity transfer to field teams to enable autonomous post-deployment troubleshooting, progressively reducing central support reliance

**3. Training Workshops & Capacity building**

- Collaborate with training stakeholders to prepare localized training materials and pre-workshop checklists
- Conduct high-impact in-person training and interactive webinars for various trainee demographics
- Facilitate Training of Trainers (TOT) workshops to build autonomous, sustainable local capacity

**4. Go-Live, Adoption & Deployment Material Evolution**

- Monitor user adoption metrics and address deployment resistance or localized blockers
- Track and report key deployment KPIs to the Deployment manager, including time-to-deploy, adoption rates, error reduction, and user satisfaction
- Capture lessons learned from field deployments and share with the Deployment manager for updates to the central deployment kit, tools, and user guidance
- Ensure all deployment materials remain adapted to local mission contexts, infrastructure, and user profiles (connectivity, language, literacy)

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Degree in Supply Chain, Project Management, IT Systems, Pharmacy Stock/Warehouse management or related field.
- Relevant certifications (Training of Trainers, Change Management) are assets.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience in project deployment, ideally within new digital tools in complex field environments.
- Strong MSF field experience in supply chain, logistics or pharma (minimum 1 year).
- Proven experience in conducting complex roll-outs and change management in challenging humanitarian settings.

**Languages:**

- Fluent in English (written and spoken); French is essential.
- Spanish or Arabic an asset

**Competencies**

- ***Technical Competencies***
- Strong understanding of supply chain workflows, particularly stock management.
- Strong capacity building and knowledge transfer skills.
- Solid knowledge of deployment of IT solutions is an advantage.
- Familiarity with UniField, Isystock, or other MSF-relevant tools preferred.
- ***Behavioral/General Competencies***
- Highly Organized: Able to manage multiple locations in different phases of deployment in parallel.
- Agile Problem Solver: Strong troubleshooting abilities with ability to spot patterns to resolve challenges on the fly.
- Independent & Mobile: High flexibility to navigate various travel contexts independently with minimal assistance.
- Interpersonal dynamics: Strong influencing, negotiation, and cross-cultural communication skills tailored for matrixed, non-hierarchical environments.

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya), or Johannesburg (South Africa).

## Acted

**Who we are**
Acted works with 19 million people across 43 countries at the intersection of humanitarian, development, climate and environmental programming. We draw on deep contextual knowledge and embrace emerging technologies to save lives, alleviate suffering, and protect and restore our planet. Working in collaboration with a growing ecosystem of local, national and international partners, we pursue one shared objective: a 3Zero World – Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon and Zero Poverty.

**Who we are looking for**
You bring the core competencies required for classical humanitarian and development work, alongside an active climate and environmental conscience, and you can navigate the challenges that arise when human and environmental suffering intersect. You have an entrepreneurial mindset: you see opportunities, connect dots, adapt your approach to different environments, and take measured risks in pursuit of results. You balance principles with pragmatism, and ambition with humility.

## Acted Occupied Palestinian Territory - OPT

Acted has been present in the West Bank since 2007 and in the Gaza Strip since 2008. With its office in Jerusalem, Acted has been responding to humanitarian needs and development challenges in the Occupied Palestinian Territory through an integrated approach. In view of the worsening of the humanitarian situation in recent years, and even more so since 7 October 2023, Acted is mobilized to respond to the basic needs of the populations affected by the conflict.

## You will be in charge of

The Country Security Manager is responsible for overseeing daily security management of all Acted premises and project sites, ensuring a permanent monitoring and assessment of the security situation in country, as well as reviewing and implementing Acted security management guidelines and protocols. He/she will also advise the Country Director and Senior Management Team on all issues of safety and security and provide appropriate security training and mentoring.

***Main duties***

1\. Department management

2\. Context & Risk analysis

3\. Develop and update Country Security Plans, SOPs and Contingency Plans

4\. Daily Security Management

5\. Crisis management

- *Adapt crisis management protocols to the local situation;*
- *Act as a key member of the Crisis Management Team so that safety policies and procedures are implemented;*

6\. Reporting

7\. Training and briefing

- *Conduct security briefing for each new international staff arriving in country;*
- *Design security training modules for Country Director’s approval and HQ endorsement;*

8\. Develop and maintain a security network

9\. Ensure external representation

## Expected skills and qualifications

- At least 3-5 years of working experience in insecure environments; preferably in Africa, Asia, or the Middle East;
- Extensive experience in security management and procedures;
- Demonstrated communication and organizational skills;
- Ability to train, mobilize, and manage both international and national staff Flexibility and ability to multi-task under pressure;
- Ability to work well in unstable and frequently changing security environments;
- Willingness to work and live in often remote areas under basic conditions;
- Proven ability to work creatively and independently both in the field and in the office;
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English;
- Knowledge of local language and/or regional experience highly desirable.

## Terms of reference

For more information about the position, [click here ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/csm-opt-2026.pdf).

Présente en Haïti depuis 2004, Acted répond aux urgences et soutien le relèvement des populations dans le besoin, notamment dans les domaines de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la reconstruction. En collaboration avec la société civile et les institutions, Acted développe et met aussi en œuvre des programmes axés sur le développement socio-économique et l’adaptation au changement climatique. Acted travaille actuellement dans 5 départements en Haïti à savoir la Grand’Anse, le Sud, le Sud-Est, l’Ouest, et le Centre, et prochainement dans les Nippes.

Concernant les réalisations majeures d’Acted en 2020-2021 :

• 5 562 personnes ont reçu une assistance monétaire afin de subvenir à leurs besoins prioritaires
• 12 centres de santé réhabilités et soutenus afin de répondre à la pandémie de COVID-19

• 1 125 personnes relogées grâce à la reconstruction de leur maison

Suite au tremblement de terre du 14 aout 2021 qui a dévasté les départements du Sud, de la Grande Anse et des Nippes en Haïti, Acted recrute. Acted a été une des première organisation humanitaire à mener des évaluations rapides pour déterminer l’ampleur des dégâts et des besoins, et est déjà fortement mobilisée pour apporter une aide d’urgence aux victimes du séisme, en étroite collaboration avec les autorités haïtiennes. ## **Acted**

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète.
