11. Develop and strengthen links with local, regional and international media to promote the work of IOM in Burundi.
12. Provide input and coordinate the project development/monitoring and evaluation work plan and the development and updating of projects, as well as reporting and contract schedules for all IOM Burundi projects in line with the donors’ requirements.
13. Participate in inter-agency media and communication working groups to encourage information flow across agencies and to develop complementary media strategies.
14. Advise field and programme staff in the sub-offices on public information, media, and communication issues.
15. Identify and organize outreach activities and assist the CoM in carrying out initiatives to promote IOM’s image and to increase awareness of IOM activities in the country. Advise the CoM and Programme Managers on media and communication issues/campaigns.
16. Consolidate and analyse data on programme implementation and Mission’s activities, to ensure the preparation of donor reports as well as mission, regional and Headquarters periodic and activity-specific reports, as may be required.
17. Facilitate the generation and use of knowledge to promote improved policy engagement, project development and management in Burundi and the region.
18. Participate in mission key events and workshops and undertake field duty travel as needed to acquire material, including photographs of work being undertaken in the field, that would promote IOM with donors and governments.
19. Liaise closely with programme managers to regularly update the mission website.
20. Provide input, as necessary, to Public Information (PI) products with regard to donor coordination and relevance and assist the departments with regular reporting, infographics and situation reports.
21. Provide and coordinate inputs for information requests from Headquarters, the RO, other IOM missions, and external partners, such as donors, partner agencies, implementing partners, etc.
22. Represent IOM Burundi at various stakeholder meetings, conferences, or workshops as needed.
23. Perform such other related duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, International Development, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Work experience in technical writing, editing, and reporting in English and French; and,
- Experience in donor relations and report writing for relevant donors is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Familiarity with a multitude of international development and humanitarian areas of intervention;
- Advanced research, writing, outreach and communications skills;
- Familiarity with monitoring and evaluation concepts and methods; and,
- Demonstrable knowledge of Burundi political and humanitarian issues.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

jobs.title: Housing Counseling Program Manager
jobs.description:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The Program Manager, Housing Counseling provides technical and administrative support for the development of network-wide Housing Counseling toolkits, curricula, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that build IRC’s capacity to deliver and sustain housing counseling services under IRC’s Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Housing Counseling Multi-State Organization (MSO). The role will support local offices in expanding housing counseling activities that strengthen client housing stabilization and homelessness prevention. This role will also support IRC’s housing programs and services in collaboration with the HQ Resettlement Team, Economic Empowerment Team, and other teams across RAI US. The position sits within the HQ Resettlement Housing Team and reports to the Director, Initial Resettlement.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Draft and update Housing Counseling curricula, toolkits, and SOPs aligned with HUD regulations and guidance (e.g., Handbook 7610.1 and 24 CFR part 214) and IRC’s Strategy 100, for use by housing counseling staff across IRC’s U.S. network and those preparing to take the HUD Housing Counselor Certification exam.
- Prepare client-facing housing counseling curriculum materials for in-person counseling and workshop, plus online LMS platforms.
- Maintain and update Resource Navigation tools that map available local, state, and federal housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and rental assistance resources across the network.
- Help plan and facilitate Housing Counseling and counselor certification training, as well as other IRC housing training, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing opportunities across the network, including through the Monthly Housing Call, Communities of Practice, Switchboard, and similar forums.
- Serve as a first point of contact for day-to-day operational questions, providing technical assistance to support offices in launching, expanding, and sustaining housing counseling programming and other IRC housing programs and their requirements.
- Respond to office requests for guidance on housing counseling program design, documentation, and compliance, applying established HUD requirements and IRC guidance, and escalating complex or ambiguous cases as needed.
- Collaborate with the HQ Housing Team, HQ Economic Empowerment Team, Resettlement colleagues, and other HQ departments (e.g., Preferred Communities and Policy) to support the alignment of housing counseling programming with IRC’s broader housing and resettlement strategy.
- Support data collection, outcome tracking, and HUD-required reporting (e.g., HUD Form 9902), compile and summarize program data to flag trends and gaps for program improvements, and contribute to housing related grant proposals, donor reports and applications, including mapping local funding opportunities in collaboration with field offices and HQ staff.
- Draft standardized practices and quality assurance protocols (e.g., case file review guidance, supervisory monitoring templates) that align affiliate housing counseling practice with HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements, for review and approval.
- Monitor changes to HUD Housing Counseling Program regulations and guidance, flag their implications for the network, and update network tools, curricula, and training materials as directed.
- Attend HUD, intermediary, and national housing counseling meetings or forums, as assigned, and share key updates with the team.
- Other duties as assigned.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Social Work, Urban Planning, Public Policy and Administration, or a related field preferred.
- HUD Housing Counselor Certification strongly preferred, or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire; demonstrated working knowledge of HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements (24 CFR part 214, HUD Handbook 7610.1) required. Experience supporting HUD-approved housing counseling agency in compliance, technical assistance and capacity-building support preferred.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in housing counseling, affordable housing programs, or housing case management, including experience contributing to curricula, SOPs, or training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to draft, adapt, and facilitate curricula, toolkits, and training materials for adult learners across diverse organizational contexts.
- Excellent project management and organizational skills, with experience supporting multi-site or multi-state initiatives, and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other underserved populations preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of integrity, service, equality, and accountability.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office required; familiarity with types of AI solutions for operational productivity and accuracy required; experience with the HUD Housing Counseling System (HCS), client management systems (CMS), reporting, and other software used for counseling and IRC housing services is a plus.
- Ability to travel up to 25% of the time to visit IRC field offices and affiliates as required. Preference for candidates living within reasonable proximity of an IRC Housing Counseling location, to perform housing counseling activities as needed.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $60,000-75,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Middle East, Regional Expert
jobs.description:
**About ACLED**
ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data) is an independent, impartial conflict and protest monitoring organization providing real-time data and analysis on violent conflict and protest in all countries and territories across the world.

**The Role**
ACLED seeks a Regional Expert on Gulf security politics who will assess how regional conflict dynamics shape the security politics and policy decisions of the Gulf states, and what those decisions mean for national security and business interests, including critical infrastructure, supply lines, trade corridors. The role covers the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — and their security relationships with Iran, Iraq, Yemen, Israel, the Horn of Africa, and other theaters where Gulf states project influence or face security challenges. This is an opportunity to shape ACLED’s analysis of one of the world’s most consequential security environments.

The Regional Expert analyzes how conflict dynamics and security policy affect these interests, and how these interests in turn shape security policy. The role covers conflict and security analysis only; the Regional Expert will not model trade data, map supply chains, or assess investments directly.

You will work with ACLED’s industry-leading conflict data and alongside a dedicated regional team of conflict monitors who produce daily event data and context information. This frees you to focus on analysis rather than raw collection. You will combine these data with your own knowledge of the region and your network in policy circles to analyze conflict developments, make risk assessments, and inform government policymakers, private-sector clients, and international media. The analyses you create will be clear, concise, timely, and informed by locally grounded information, and will speak directly to the concerns of the governments, business sector and organizations who rely on it.

Analysis is the core of the role. Your work with clients and stakeholders will also surface new opportunities, and you will have the chance to develop these alongside the revenue and regional team. As one of ACLED’s public voices on the Middle East, you will feature frequently in international media and represent ACLED at high-level venues in the region.

As Regional Expert you are located within the Middle East regional team of the Global Data Collection department and report to the Middle East Regional Team Lead. You will work together with other regional experts on the Middle East and with experts and monitors on the Africa team regarding the Horn of Africa. Your work also intersects with ACLED’s Risk Centre, External Affairs, Global Engagement, and Revenue teams who you directly engage with for risk outputs, client briefings, media commentary and commercial opportunities.

ACLED is a fully remote organization, and this position offers the flexibility to work from anywhere. You will work with clients and colleagues across time zones, typically US mornings, Europe afternoons, and Asia evenings, and will travel to the Gulf states and the wider region to meet clients and stakeholders in person.

**Analysis and risk assessment**

- Monitor conflict and political developments affecting the Gulf states and assess their consequences for Gulf national security policy and for business interests in and linked to the region.
- Explain how regional conflict dynamics shape Gulf security decisions, including threat perceptions of Iran and its partners, the Houthi movement and Red Sea maritime security, Iraqi armed groups, the Israel–Iran confrontation, and instability in the Horn of Africa.
- Analyze Gulf states’ security policy choices and their drivers, such as defense partnerships and basing arrangements, de-escalation and normalization diplomacy, hedging between major powers, and direct or proxy involvement in regional conflicts.
- Explain how these dynamics affect, and are affected by, Gulf states’ economic interests, including attacks on energy and port infrastructure, threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, sanctions-related escalation, and spillover from conflicts where Gulf states hold interests, for example those in the Horn of Africa.
- Produce forward-looking risk assessments for countries, critical sites, and maritime corridors, built on evidence and observed trends, with clear indicators, thresholds, scenarios, and stated confidence levels behind each judgment.
- Produce other regular and ad hoc outputs, including risk briefs, crisis alerts, regional outlooks, and contributions to ACLED’s thematic reports.

**Data and methodology**

- Work with data collection, risk, and data science teams to strengthen ACLED coverage of conflict relevant to Gulf security, including cross-border, maritime, and long-range strike activity, and conflict that matters for critical infrastructure and economic risk.

**Client and stakeholder engagement**

- Brief government policymakers and private-sector clients and partners on Gulf security and conflict risk in writing and in meetings, remotely and in person.
- Build and maintain a network of contacts in Gulf and international policy circles, including government, security, diplomatic, and research communities.
- Develop opportunities that arise from client and stakeholder contact with the revenue team, contributing to demonstrations, tailored briefings, and product development.
- Provide expert commentary to international media and represent ACLED at conferences, policy forums, and other high-level events in the region and beyond.

**Project development**

- Support develop new products and projects on Gulf security, critical infrastructure, and economic risk.
- Contribute to proposals and partnerships.

**Requirements ( Skills and Experience)**

- A master’s degree in international relations, political science, security studies, Middle East studies, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- At least five years of professional experience in political or security risk analysis, conflict research, or policy analysis focused on the Gulf or the wider Middle East, in a consultancy, government, research, or in-house role.
- In-depth knowledge of Gulf security politics, the foreign and defense policies of the GCC states, and the regional conflicts that shape them.
- An established network in Gulf or international policy circles.
- A record of published or client-facing analysis, such as risk assessments, policy briefs, or forecasts.
- Fluency in English, with excellent writing and briefing skills.
- Fluency in Arabic is necessary.
- Ability and willingness to travel to the Gulf states.
- Ability to work across time zones, with flexibility during crises.

**What you bring**

- Sound judgment grounded in evidence and reason, and the confidence to make clear assessments without fear of being proven wrong.
- Rigor in assessing the reliability of sources and the validity of information, and the ability to draw insight from large volumes of data and reporting.
- The ability to turn complex regional dynamics into concise, actionable analysis for both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
- Comfort engaging with senior government and private-sector stakeholders, and an instinct for spotting where ACLED analysis can meet client needs.
- An understanding of how businesses and governments use risk analysis to make decisions.
- Familiarity with conflict event data, ideally including ACLED data, and an interest in strengthening data-driven analysis.
- Independence and good time management in a remote team, alongside a collaborative approach across departments.

**Compensation and Benefits**
The salary range for this position is 50,000-60,000 (USD) annually, depending on previous experience and seniority. Other benefits vary according to local legislation in the country of employment.

**Terms**

Start Date: January 2027, Type of Position: Remote, Full-Time Employment.

jobs.description:
**Background/IRC Summary:**

The International Rescue Committee responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees, IDPs, and others affected by war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and in 22 U.S. cities, the IRC restores safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. We address both the immediate, lifesaving needs of conflict-affected people in an emergency and the reconstruction needs in post-conflict societies. This position is based in the Airbel Impact Lab, within the Research and Innovation team at the IRC’s headquarters. It will also collaborate closely with technical and country teams within the Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU).

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The IRC is a pioneer in violence prevention and response research and programming, spanning women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law.

The Violence Prevention and Response Senior Researcher sits within the IRC’s Airbel Impact Lab with a dual reporting line into the VPRU, and provides oversight, guidance and support to the VPRU’s research portfolio on the prevention of and response to violence against children, women and other vulnerable individuals in crisis- and conflict-affected contexts. The Senior Researcher will be responsible for coordinating the implementation of the violence prevention and response research portfolio, including: i) designing and managing studies; ii) engaging proactively with relevant research networks and university partners; iii) ensuring a strong pipeline of research funding; and iv) summarizing and sharing the results of protection research and learning to ensure protection programming is based on the best available evidence. Close attention to the ethics of research on violence against children and women is paramount in this work.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Research Coordination and Study Support: Oversee the coordination of active studies in collaboration with external academic partners and internal IRC stakeholders, including supporting data collection activities and designing survey tools, interview guides, study protocols and referral pathways; ensure research adheres to IRC research standards and ethical guidance on violence research; and contribute to drafting policy reports and academic articles, including as first author.
- Research Agenda Leadership: In collaboration with VPRU Global Practice Leads and the VPRU MEAL lead, lead the development and oversee the roll-out of the violence prevention and response research agenda in line with the VPRU's safety strategies across the three Global Practice Areas (Child Protection, Women’s Protection and Empowerment, Protection and Rule of Law) and Impact at Scale priorities, including contributing to the development of novel and inclusive measurement tools and data collection approaches.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Evidence-Informed Programming: Liaise with internal stakeholders across VPRU and country-based teams to ensure that VPRU programming is evidence-based, assessing upcoming and ongoing protection programming so that it reflects recent developments and the best available practice and evidence.
- External Collaboration, Business Development and Thought Leadership: Proactively build partnerships, foster cross-learning, and strengthen collaboration with key research organizations and networks, particularly those in IRC contexts. Represent the IRC at key external research fora. Identify business development opportunities to finance the research agenda, including delivering a robust business development plan, engaging university partners, and steering individual bids, to secure research funding and advance IRC's position as a leader in protection evidence generation.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director of Research, Airbel Impact Lab

**Other key relationships:** VPRU team members (including the VPRU MEAL lead), country-based teams supporting research priorities, and academic partners.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** PhD preferred in public health, child development, psychology, or another relevant quantitative or qualitative discipline.

**Work Experience:** PhD with 3–5 years of experience, or Master’s degree with 6–8 years of experience, working in research on topics related to violence against children and women, child protection, humanitarian emergencies or other relevant topics.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Experience conducting research in child protection, women’s protection and empowerment, and violence prevention and response in humanitarian settings.
- Knowledge of ethical principles related to sensitive study topics, such as child protection, women’s protection and GBV, and violence research.
- Ability to work across sectors, coordinating research studies and bringing together people with different perspectives to work collaboratively.
- Proven qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis skills.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills and attention to detail.
- Strong research publication and funding track record.
- Commitment to upholding Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion principles, data protection principles and Safeguarding standards.
- English is required, French is highly preferred, and Arabic, Spanish, Swahili or other languages would be beneficial.

**Working Environment:** Standard office work environment; up to 30% travel to countries of implementation.

***This contract position is expected to end on July 31, 2027.***

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

jobs.description:
## **Contrat à durée déterminée : 12 mois à partir du 18/01/2027**

## **PUI aux quatre coins du monde**

**Forte de ses 40 années d’expérience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Vient en aide à près de **6** millions de bénéficiaires
- Avec un budget de plus de **100** millions € par an
- Répartis dans **22** pays, sur **5** continents

Grâce à l’implication et l’engagement de :

- Plus de **2000** collaborateurs nationaux
- Environ **200** expatriés de 45 nationalités différentes
- Et **90** salariés au siège

PUI œuvre dans 10 secteurs d’intervention et se distingue par la mise en place d’une approche intégrée dans sa réponse. Cette méthode vise à identifier et comprendre l’ensemble des besoins des personnes touchées par une crise. Nos équipes se mobilisent pour apporter une réponse globale à l’ensemble des besoins fondamentaux des populations victimes de crises humanitaires dans l’urgence jusqu’à leur permettre de retrouver autonomie et dignité.

Pour en savoir plus sur [notre histoire](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [nos valeurs](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [nos domaines d’intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **Et le.la Adjoint·e Directeur.trice Pays Supports dans tout ça?**

En tant qu’Adjoint·e Directeur.trice Pays Support, vous serez responsable de l’effectivité, de l’efficience et de la qualité du support aux opérations humanitaires implémentées par PUI. A cet effet, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes :

- **Coordination des fonctions supports de la mission** : Vous superviserez, coordonnerez et guiderez les départements supports de la mission de PUI (Logistique, Administration & Finances, Ressources Humaines, Audit Interne) et vous assurerez du développement de synergies et d’améliorations intra- et inter-départementales.
- **Supervision des équipes nationales et internationales supports** : Vous encadrerez hiérarchiquement les coordinateurs supports et l’auditeur interne, fournirez un support fonctionnel aux responsables terrains et contribuerez au renforcement des capacités en support de l’ensemble du personnel de la mission. Vous veillerez à ce que votre équipe soit garante d’un management RH de qualité sur la mission et qu’une bonne communication soit appliquée.
- **Suivi logistique** : Vous soutiendrez le Coordinateur Logistique dans la mise en œuvre d'un cadre logistique mission adapté et organisé autour d'une chaîne d'approvisionnement efficace et d'une logistique de support correctement dimensionné.
- **Suivi administratif et financier** : Vous vous assurerez que les procédures administratives et financières respectent le Code du travail du pays autant que les standards et les formats internes, que les règles et régulations bailleurs, de l’efficience et de l’efficacité du support financier au dimensionnement et à l’optimisation des opérations.
- **Suivi Ressources Humaines** : Vous vous assurerez que les procédures ressources humaines respectent les standards et les formats internes autant que les règles et régulations bailleurs, de l’efficience et de l’efficacité des politiques RH pour la fidélisation, le développement du personnel actuel et l’attractivité RH de la mission.
- **Sécurité** : Vous assisterez le Directeur.trice Pays dans l’analyse du contexte sécuritaire et la gestion de la sécurité.
- **Gestion des Risques** : Vous définirez, adapterez et superviserez la mise en œuvre d’un cadre de gestion des risques intégrés (RH/log/admin/juridiques/sécuritaires/etc.)

## **Les défis qui vous attendent**

- Garantir une coordination stratégique et intégrée des fonctions supports, afin d'optimiser la performance opérationnelle, tout en renforçant la transversalité et les synergies entre les différents départements support.
- Assurer la maîtrise des risques, la conformité et la redevabilité dans un environnement opérationnel complexe, caractérisé par une augmentation du volume opérationnel dans un contexte volatile.
- Garantir la continuité opérationnelle et l'adaptabilité des fonctions supports face aux défis contextuels, notamment en développant des dispositifs visant à optimiser l'efficience des services supports et à maximiser l'utilisation des ressources disponibles.
- Développer un leadership fédérateur et renforcer les capacités des équipes supports dans un contexte de forte pression, tout en préservant un climat social constructif et en améliorant la communication interne.

## **Ce qu'il vous faudra pour réussir**

- **Formation** : Vous pouvez justifier d’un diplôme supérieur (Master 2 ou équivalent) en Logistique, Finances, Ressources Humaines ou Relations Internationales.
- **Expérience** : Vous êtes fort d'au moins trois ans d’expérience sur une fonction de coordination mission support pour une ONG internationale. Si vous avez également de l’expérience en logistique support et/ou en approvisionnement, ce sera apprécié. Vous avez déjà travaillé avec Première Urgence Internationale ? Ce sera un atout indéniable !
- **Compétences** : Vous maitrisez le management d'équipe, vous avez une connaissance approfondie des règles et procédures des principaux bailleurs de fonds (en particulier ECHO, BHA, PAM, UNHCR, CDCS, AFD et BPRM). Vous disposez d'excellentes capacités rédactionnelles.
- **Qualités requises** : Vous montrez de solides compétences en matière de leadership et de prise de décisions. Vous disposez de bonnes capacités d'analyse et de synthèse, êtes un bon négociateur et un bon communiquant, autant à l’écrit qu’à l’oral, et savez garantir des résultats efficaces sous la pression des délais. Vous faites preuve d'organisation, de rigueur, de flexibilité et d’une forte résistance au stress.
- **Langues** : Le français et l’anglais n’ont aucun secret pour vous ? Tant mieux, c’est indispensable pour ce poste !

## **Le mot du manager**

*« Acteur incontournable de la réponse humanitaire dans le pays, PUI joue depuis plusieurs années un rôle clé auprès des populations affectées par les crises. Depuis l’émergence de l’épidémie d’Ebola, l’organisation n’a cessé de renforcer ses interventions sanitaires et humanitaires grâce à l’appui de ses partenaires et à l’engagement de ses équipes sur le terrain.*

*Derrière chaque intervention réussie se trouvent des fonctions support solides, véritables piliers de nos opérations. Dans des contextes complexes et parfois difficiles d’accès, elles garantissent la continuité, l’efficacité et l’impact de notre action au quotidien. Vous avez une solide expérience dans la gestion des fonctions support et souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service d’une mission porteuse de sens ? Rejoignez une équipe engagée, professionnelle et résolument tournée vers l’action.*

*Ensemble, relevez les défis d’une crise humanitaire prolongée et contribuez concrètement à faire la différence auprès des populations les plus vulnérables. »*

## **PUI vous proposera**

- **Statut:** Cadre en Contrat à Durée Déterminée
- **Salaire brut mensuel:** 3 310,00 - 3 510,00 EUR selon votre expérience en solidarité internationale + 50€ par semestre d'ancienneté avec PUI
- **Assurance** comprenant couverture médicale et complémentaire santé, assistance 24h/24, rapatriement et prévoyance
- **Hébergement** en maison collective
- **Frais de vie** ("Per Diem")
- **Régime de break:** 5 jours ouvrés à 3 et 9 mois de mission + prime de break
- **Régime de Congés Payés:** 5 semaines de CP/an + billet d'avion A/R au domicile tous les 6 mois

## **Nos engagements**

PUI s'engage à prévenir tout type de comportement indésirable au travail, y compris le harcèlement, l'exploitation et l'abus sexuels, le manque d'intégrité et l’inconduite financière, et à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants et des adultes avec lesquels PUI est en contact. PUI attend de toutes les personnes employées qu’elles s'acquittent de leurs tâches et responsabilités professionnelles conformément au Cadre Éthique de PUI.
Toutes les personnes employées par PUI suivront des formations appropriées, et s’engagent dans la promotion, la diffusion et le respect des principes édictés dans sa charte éthique.
Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura potentiellement accès à des données personnelles concernant des enfants et des adultes vulnérables dans le cadre de son travail (catégorie 2 dans la classification de risques du recrutement sûr). Ainsi, toutes les offres d'emploi seront soumises à des références satisfaisantes et à des vérifications appropriées, qui peuvent incluront des vérifications du casier judiciaire et du financement du terrorisme.
Première Urgence Internationale considère la diversité des nationalités, genres, croyances, profils et statuts au sein de ses Ressources Humaines comme un atout majeur pour son action humanitaire, et s’astreint donc au strict respect du principe de non-discrimination tout au long de son processus de recrutement. Nous encourageons les personnes candidates issues de milieux divers à postuler.
Veuillez noter que Première Urgence Internationale ne sollicitera en aucun cas une participation financière pour des frais administratifs liés au recrutement. Toute information allant dans ce sens serait frauduleuse, merci de ne pas en tenir compte.

**Nous vous encourageons à postuler au plus vite si le poste vous intéresse, car nous pourrions mettre fin au processus avant la date mentionnée ci-dessus si un candidat approprié est identifié.**

Vous vous reconnaissez dans ce profil et vous adhérez à nos engagements ? Vous vous sentez prêt·e à relever le **challenge** et à rejoindre la **grande famille PUI ?**

jobs.title: Safety Advisor - Afghanistan
jobs.description:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Job Summary**

The Safety Advisor position is based in the INSO Palestine office in Amman, Jordan. The Afghanistan mission is a remote programme. The Safety Advisor will cover the Afghanistan context remotely and will have the unique opportunity to deliver safety advice, analysis and coordination remotely to NGOs operating in Afghanistan.

The Safety Advisor will build and/or have their own local networks to explore local dynamics and develop an understanding of what is relevant to NGOs seeking to inform strategic decision-making and programming. You will be outgoing and resilient, with the ability to analyse complex issues and contexts, give practical safety and security advice, and share INSO’s commitment to humanitarian principles.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Establish and maintain an active information network to obtain credible and relevant safety information.
- Provide NGOs with timely and credible safety information and contextual analysis of the local operating environment.
- Develop analytical products on regional and country-wide dynamics or developments of relevance to NGOs.
- Facilitate and lead NGO roundtables.
- Assist NGOs in developing their own safety management capacities by reviewing policy documents, conducting site surveys, and assisting in crisis planning.
- Effectively represent, promote and protect INSO's mandate of independence, impartiality and neutrality.

**Requirements**

- Proven writing, editing, and analytical skills and the keenest eye for detail.
- Experience in conflict and post-conflict environments.
- Experience in the humanitarian and/or risk management and/or humanitarian access sectors.
- Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
- Fluency, written and spoken, in the working language of the context (e.g. Dari and/or Pashto)
- Personal and professional resilience in a fast-moving, high-output, quality-driven program.
- Independent drive, motivation, and excellence, and the ability to operate and sustainably manage staff under strict systems and deadlines.
- Well-developed personal, organisational, and management skills and standards in a diverse multi-cultural setting.
- Demonstrable understanding of humanitarian safety practices and principles.
- Bachelor-level education in a relevant field

**Nice to Have**

- Prior experience in Afghanistan
- Experience with NGO security and/or project management.
- Existing information networks in Afghanistan

jobs.title: MEAL Manager - Damascus
jobs.description:
The MEAL Manager leads the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning systems across DCA programmes in Syria. The role ensures the availability of high-quality data for decision-making, donor compliance, adaptive programme management, and organizational learning. Through effective oversight of MEAL processes and teams, the position supports evidence-based programming, accountability to affected populations, and improved programme outcomes\*\*.\*\*

**Functional Responsibilities:**

- Projects Managers and Technical Advisors – collaborate, advise, and support – ensure MEAL systems are integrated into programme design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting
- Field Teams – coordinate and build capacity – strengthen data collection, quality assurance, and evidence-based programme adjustments.
- Grants and Business Development Teams – contribute and review – support proposal development, logframes, indicators, targets, and donor reporting requirements.
- MEAL Staff and Enumerators – supervise, mentor, and guide – ensure consistent implementation of MEAL standards, tools, and methodologies.
- Local Partners – support and strengthen capacities – ensure compliance with MEAL requirements and promote data quality and accountability standards.
- Senior Management Team – provide analysis and recommendations – support strategic decision-making through evidence, performance data, and learning products.
- Donors and External Evaluators – coordinate and communicate – ensure timely reporting, evaluations, assessments, and compliance with donor expectations.
- Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of organizational MEAL systems, frameworks, tools, and standard operating procedures.
- Ensure the quality, integrity, protection, analysis, and utilization of programme data through robust data management and verification processes.
- Oversee the development of indicators, monitoring plans, databases, assessments, baseline studies, evaluations, and learning initiatives.
- Establish and manage accountability mechanisms, including feedback and complaints systems, ensuring safe, accessible, and responsive channels for affected populations.
- Produce and disseminate programme performance analyses, dashboards, lessons learned, and evidence products to support adaptive management and strategic planning.
- Lead MEAL capacity strengthening efforts for staff and partners through training, mentoring, coaching, and technical support.
- Exercise decision-making authority regarding MEAL methodologies, data quality standards, monitoring approaches, and learning priorities; escalate significant compliance, safeguarding, data protection, or operational risks to senior management for review and action.

**Minimum Required Knowledge & Experience:**

- Master's degree in Monitoring & Evaluation, Statistics, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Policy, or related field.
- Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in MEAL within humanitarian and/or development programs, including at least 3 years in a management role.
- Strong experience designing MEAL frameworks, logical frameworks, indicator tracking systems, evaluations, assessments, and accountability mechanisms.
- Advanced skills in data analysis and visualization tools (Power BI, Excel, Kobo, ODK, CommCare, DHIS2 or similar platforms).
- Demonstrated experience managing MEAL teams and supporting donor-funded programs (ECHO, DANIDA, FCDO, UN agencies, etc.).

**Nice-To-Have Competencies As An Additional Asset:**

- Experience in conflict-affected or cross-border humanitarian contexts, particularly Syria or the Middle East.
- Knowledge of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), CHS commitments, and safeguarding standards.
- Experience supporting organizational learning, research, impact evaluations, and evidence generation.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted data analysis, dashboard automation, and digital MEAL solutions.
- Arabic language skills and previous experience working with national NGOs and partners.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities, or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy. DCA conducts an anti-terror check along with professional reference check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment with us. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Code of Conduct, Staff Policy on the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

jobs.title: Deputy Head of Mission - Aerial monitoring operations
jobs.description:
## About SOS MEDITERRANEE

**SOS MEDITERRANEE** is a European maritime and humanitarian organization founded in 2015 in response to the humanitarian tragedy and the persistent absence of adequate state-led rescue capabilities on the Central Mediterranean route — the deadliest migratory route in the world since 2014.

Created by a collective of European citizens committed to upholding human dignity, our organization operates with a clear mission:

1. To rescue people in distress at sea;
2. To protect and assist survivors on board our rescue vessel;
3. To bear witness and raise public awareness about the ongoing crisis in the Mediterranean.

Since launching operations in 2016, SOS MEDITERRANEE has rescued more than 42,000 people in coordination with its network across Germany, France, Italy, and Switzerland, using the ships Aquarius and Ocean Viking.

With the aim of increasing contextual awareness in the Central Mediterranean and to document the human rights violations and interceptions happening in this maritime region, SOS MEDITERRANEE, as a humanitarian civilian association, in partership with HPI (Humanitarian Pilots Initiative) deployed a **civilian aerial monitoring** mission based in **Lampedusa, Italy**.

To strenghten the current team, we are now looking for **Deputy Head of Mission.**

## Job description

Under the line management of the Head of Mission (HoM), the Deputy Head of Mission (Dep – HoM) supports the HoM in the day-to-day preparation, follow-up and implementation of the Mission's activities, contributing to monitoring operations either from ground either as aicraft flying crew, and to the effective implementation of established procedures and processes of the Mission.

The Deputy HoM may be required to assume the HoM's responsibilities, either in full or in part, when requested or necessary, including during the HoM's absence or unavailability, within the framework of delegated responsibilities.

**Main responsibilities:**

**Strategy** :

- Monitor and analyze the humanitarian and political context of the Mission, and the context on the island of Lampedusa.
- Participate in the definition of SOS MEDITERRANEE aerial operational strategy with consistency with the association's policies and the needs of the people in distress at sea
- Contribute to propose new operational directions in line with changing contexts
- Participate in developing and streamlining overall organization framework/processes, to ensure operational sustainability (short, mid, and long term) with the end objective of efficient monitoring operation.

**Monitoring Operations** :

- When covering ground shift during flight operations:
- Support the supervision and monitoring of operations before, during and after flights,
- Assess the operational readiness from non-aeronautical perspectives,
- Ensure the mission plans are communicated to concerned people: air crew, ground crew, and to SAR operational actors
- Ensure SAR communication with all relevant actors and authorities and other operational assets
- Support the Tactical Coordinator in their assessment
- Contribute to the data collection and documentation in collaboration with Air Liaison and Logistic Officer (ALLO).
- When not covering ground shift:
- Participate in monitoring flights embarking on the aircraft as embarked aircrew, under the guidance of the TACCO in command
- Support the in flight debriefings process and ensure appropriate operational follow-up.

**Safety & Security** :

- Support the Head of Mission in the safety and security risk assessment and analysis, as well as the safety and security protocols design, review and update.
- Contribute to ensuring strict application and implementation of safety, security protocols and rules by all air and ground team, especially supporting the TACCO during flights.
- Ensure the familiarization of all team members or guests/visitors with the necessary safety and security measures, rules, roles and responsibility.
- Report safety and security incidents to Head of Mission and contribute to the implementation of follow up action plan.

**Representation** :

- Represent SOS MEDITERRANEE with the authorities in Lampedusa when requested or delegated by the HoM
- Represent SOS MEDITERRANEE with NGO actors and local networks in Lampedusa and contribute to maintain good work and cooperative relationships.
- Participate in testimonies, interviews and press release and other communication to the general public about the situation on the Aerial Mission, within the communication lines of SOS MEDITERRANEE, as other team members, after comms validation and relevant training

**Reporting** :

- Support the reporting of mission data, relevant advocacy and comms events.
- Ensure an effective handover with the HoM and liaise with other shore-based managers, when necessary, to ensure continuity and completion of tasks during periods when the Aerial Mission team is off duty or not deployed.
- Contribute to the preparation of operational reports and other internal reporting requirements.

**Support to the mission management** :

- In coordination with the HoM, share responsibility for mission opening and closing activities and the remote follow-up of pending tasks, ensuring continuity of operations during periods when the team is not deployed in Lampedusa.
- Contribute to daily logistical and organizational tasks as required by the operational needs of the Mission.
- Contribute to ensure the respect of the procedures and processes established at institutional level.
- Contribute to the debriefing of team after missions
- Contribute to maintaining a positive and respectful working environment for team members.
- Identify team management issues and bring them to the attention of the HoM when necessary.

## Profile

**Diploma(s) and certification(s)**

*Desirable :*

- Bachelor in Management, Humanitarian Aid, Project Coordination, International Law or related fields
- IMO SAR on-scene coordinator course or relevant professional experience

**Technical expertise**

- Knowledge of Maritime Law and regulations.
- Nautical knowledge (navigation, meteorology, etc.)
- Knowledge of safety and security within SAR or humanitarian context
- Knowledge of SAR operations, IAMSAR manual procedures and vocabulary and IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases.
- Aerial search and rescue knowledge and/or civilian monitoring operation is desirable

**Experience**

*Essential*

- 3 years’ relevant professional experience in Search and Rescue and/or Civilian Monitoring operation
- Previous experience in a management position
- Work experience in multicultural environment

*Desirable*

- Experience in maritime SAR operations
- Experience in decision making related role in Central Mediterranean including communication with authorities
- Experience in humanitarian operations
- Work experience in non-profit maritime projects
- Previous experience on board monitoring or search and rescue aircraft
- Previous experience with SOS MED is an asset

**Languages**

- Fluent in English (spoken and written)
- Knowledge of Italian and Arabic are strong assets

**IT/SI**

- Good command with MS Excel, Word, and emailing services.
- MS Teams/SharePoint
- Deep knowledge with electronic charts systems and weather predicting softwares
- Knowledge in aerial and ship telecommunications

**Soft skills**

- Ability to organize their work and time management skills;
- Decision making skills;
- Adaptability;
- Autonomy and sense of initiative;
- Stress management skills;
- Adequate communication and conflict resolution skills;
- Ability to work in team;

jobs.title: Country Program Lead
jobs.description:
## About Trickle Up

Trickle Up works with women living in extreme poverty to build sustainable livelihoods. We partner with local organizations and governments to expand access to Economic Inclusion, including through the Graduation Approach.

## About the role

Trickle Up is seeking an experienced development professional to help build and strengthen its Economic Inclusion work in Côte d’Ivoire. This role offers the opportunity to provide ongoing technical and implementation support, develop lasting government and partner relationships, and help shape a growing country program.

The Country Program Lead will work closely with the Vice President, Africa, and the Economic Inclusion team to support partners, resolve implementation challenges, and turn learning into better results. We are looking for someone who takes initiative, follows through on commitments, and is interested in contributing to the continued development of Trickle Up’s work in Côte d’Ivoire. This is intended as a longer-term engagement, initially offered through a one-year consultancy agreement. Any extension will depend on funding, program needs, satisfactory completion of agreed deliverables, and the appropriate engagement arrangement.

## Key responsibilities

### Program planning and implementation

- Coordinate agreed implementation priorities for the Man pilot and other funded initiatives, supporting partners to address challenges and follow through on actions.
- Maintain a practical monthly workplan and track progress, budgets, donor commitments, risks, and dependencies. Recommend corrective actions and follow up on agreed decisions.

### Government and partner relationships

- Build and maintain productive relationships with relevant ministries, implementation partners, development partners, financial institutions, cooperatives, and other stakeholders.
- Clarify roles and technical assistance priorities, prepare inputs for stakeholder and financing discussions, and follow up on commitments that support program adoption and expansion.

### Program quality and partner capacity

- Provide technical support on operating procedures, targeting, coaching, training, supervision, assessments, livelihoods, and market linkages.
- Work closely with the Economic Inclusion team to adapt tools, curricula, and delivery approaches and strengthen partner capacity. Promote women’s agency, inclusion, safeguarding, and accessible participant feedback.

### Evidence and learning

- Work with the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Manager and technical specialists on data collection and quality, locally appropriate tools, key indicators, and issues requiring technical guidance.
- Use evidence, participant feedback, delivery capacity, costs, and risks to improve implementation and inform expansion and financing plans. Document lessons for Trickle Up’s wider Economic Inclusion practice and approved external use.

### Program development

- Develop agreed concept notes, proposals, partnership opportunities, and future program designs with Trickle Up’s Africa, Economic Inclusion, and business development teams.
- Identify practical opportunities to strengthen and grow the country portfolio, taking account of partner capacity and confirmed or potential funding.

### Country establishment

- Coordinate requested information and documentation with designated legal, tax, registration, and other advisers, and follow up on establishment activities.
- Track progress, dependencies, and risks.

## Monthly priorities and results

At the beginning of each month, the Consultant and the Vice President, Africa will agree on specific deliverables, expected results, timelines, estimated consulting days, and criteria for assessing completion or satisfactory progress. The recurring areas below will guide this work as the country program develops.

- **Workplan and priorities:** An updated plan with agreed activities, expected outputs, timelines, and dependencies.
- **Implementation and partner support:** Evidence of progress, support provided, implementation challenges, and corrective actions.
- **Program quality and technical support:** Completion or advancement of agreed technical outputs, tools, training, and livelihood or market activities.
- **MEL and learning:** Progress on data collection and quality, indicators, lessons, and issues requiring technical guidance.
- **Partnerships and stakeholder engagement:** A brief record of engagement, decisions, and agreed follow-up actions.
- **Program development:** Progress on concepts, proposals, partnerships, and future program design.
- **Progress and action report:** A concise monthly summary of work and outputs, days worked, outstanding actions, risks or dependencies, and priorities for the following month.

## Working Relationships and Authority

- The Consultant will coordinate with Trickle Up’s Africa and Economic Inclusion teams, relevant Côte d’Ivoire personnel, implementation partners, and approved advisers.
- The Consultant may provide technical guidance, coordination, mentoring, and recommendations within the agreed scope. The engagement does not include authority to hire, terminate, discipline, set compensation for, or formally evaluate Trickle Up employees.
- The Consultant may participate in technical discussions with government agencies, donors, partners, and other stakeholders as authorized. The Consultant may not sign agreements, make financial, legal, programmatic, employment, or institutional commitments, issue formal correspondence in Trickle Up’s name, or publicly state an organizational position without prior written authorization.
- The Consultant is responsible for organizing the manner and method of performing the services, while meeting agreed deadlines, safeguarding standards, confidentiality and data-protection requirements, and applicable laws.

## Required Qualifications

- At least seven years of relevant experience in Economic Inclusion, social protection, livelihoods, or a closely related field, including at least five years advising or leading complex programs, multidisciplinary teams, partnerships, or technical-assistance engagements.
- Fluent French and strong professional English, including written reporting and collaboration with international teams.
- Demonstrated experience supporting Ivorian government programs or institutions through technical assistance, such as operating procedures, capacity strengthening, frontline training, costing, budgeting, or implementation support.
- Experience working with government and development partners on program adoption, scale, public financing, cash transfers, or related social-protection initiatives.
- Applied understanding of Economic Inclusion and the Graduation Approach, including program delivery, partner management, budgeting, donor commitments, and capacity strengthening.
- Ability to assess data quality, interpret findings, synthesize stakeholder input, and translate evidence into clear recommendations.
- Demonstrated experience working as an independent consultant or adviser and managing deliverable-based assignments requiring independent professional judgment.
- A relevant degree or equivalent professional experience and a demonstrated commitment to women’s agency, inclusion, safeguarding, and ethical practice.

## Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with market systems, digital coaching tools, or field coordination of impact evaluations, including randomized trials.
- Established professional knowledge of Côte d’Ivoire’s social-protection, livelihoods, public-finance, and development-partner environment.

## Application Requirements

Applicants should submit the following by November 30, 2026:

- A résumé or curriculum vitae.
- A brief cover letter describing relevant experience and proposed approach to the consultancy.
- A financial proposal stating the proposed professional fee, currency, and any applicable taxes.
- Availability during the anticipated consultancy period.
- Contact information for at least two professional references.

## Independent Consultancy and Safeguards

The selected consultant will be engaged under a written consultancy agreement and Terms of Reference. The engagement is not intended to create an employer-employee relationship. The consultant will be responsible for applicable registration, tax, social protection, insurance, and other obligations associated with independent professional activity, subject to applicable law and the final agreement.

Trickle Up is committed to safeguarding, inclusion, confidentiality, responsible data handling, and preventing sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment. The selected consultant will be required to comply with applicable contractual safeguards and Trickle Up policies relevant to the assignment.

jobs.title: Consultance internationale avec une représentation au Tchad ou Nationale
jobs.description:
La mission d’évaluation consiste à porter un jugement sur la performance, les résultats et la valeur ajoutée du projet ARIANE dans le Wadi Fira, afin d’identifier les facteurs de succès, les leçons apprises et les bonnes pratiques, tout en appréciant sa contribution à l’amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire, la thérapie de stimulation, l'appui psychosociale, de la nutrition, de l’inclusion socioéconomique et des conditions de vie des populations.

**Objectifs spécifiques**

Evaluer les réalisations et les résultats du projet, notamment sa contribution à la prévention et à la réduction de la malnutrition ainsi qu’à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des communautés.

Analyser la pertinence, l’efficacité et l’efficience du projet, y compris les modalités de mise en oeuvre, les dispositifs institutionnels et le rapport qualité-prix.

Apprécier l’appropriation et l’inclusivité du projet, en examinant la participation des acteurs locaux, des femmes, des personnes handicapées et des autres groupes cibles.

Formuler des recommandations opérationnelles pour renforcer la conception, les approches et la mise en oeuvre des futures interventions

**Destinataires de l’évaluation**
\- L’Ambassade de France : Servir de moyen d’information sur la pertinence, l’efficacité, le changement apporté à travers les actions du projet d’une part, et potentiellement pour soutenir ses politiques et priorités d’autres part
\- Les membres du consortium : Identifier les facteurs de succès et/ou d’échec du projet, et à vérifier les bonnes pratiques et leçons tirées de l’expérience par les acteurs du projet
\- Les bénéficiaires directs : Être Informer sur les résultats atteints après la mise en oeuvre du projet en faveur des populations vulnérables

**Acteurs impliqués dans la mise en oeuvre de l’action**
**Acteurs partenaires Rôles**
HI
TGH
ADES
Délégations provinciales de l'agriculture et des antennes de ANADER
District sanitaire Délégation de l'action sociale et de affaires humanitaires
Délégation de la femme et de la petite enfance

**Organisation de la mission**
**La présente mission serait sous l’égide du comité de pilotage avec les rôles et responsabilités ci -après :**
\- Appuyer l’organisation logistique de la mission
\- Facilitateur l’accès aux partenaires, bénéficiaires, équipes projets ;
\- Briefer l’équipe des évaluateurs/trices sur les considérations éthiques à prendre en compte pendant l’évaluation
\- Disponibiliser les ressources financières nécessaire à la conduite de l’évaluation finale
\- Mettre à la disposition des évaluateurs/trices toute documentation jugée utile ;
\- Faire la revue des outils de collecte de données avant leur déploiement sur le terrain
\- Faire la revue et amender les différents livrables (provisoire et final)
\- Mettre à la disposition des évaluateurs/trices la cartographie de la zone d’intervention du projet
\- Veiller à la facilitation de toute activité nécessaire pour le bon déroulement de l’évaluation
\- Analyser, valider et diffuser les résultats de l’évaluation, notamment auprès des acteurs et bénéficiaires du projet

**Les principales responsabilités de l’évaluateur/(ice) sont entre autres :**
\- Fournir une méthodologie claire de tout le processus aboutissant à la conclusions et recommandations
\- Conduire l’évaluation de façon indépendante sans aucune forme d’influence dans le respect des principes et valeurs de l’organisation commanditaire
\- Prendre en compte les aspects éthiques et la protection des bénéficiaires et acteurs dans le déroulement de la mission terrain
\- L’analyse et l’évaluation des performances du projet sur la base des questions clés classées dans les différents critères et questions évaluatifs
\- Fournir les différents livrables mentionnés dans les présents termes de référence

**Expertise recherchée du ou des consultant-(es )**
L'évaluateur(s) travaillera \[sur place et à distance\] avec un niveau d'effort d’effectuer une mission terrain d’au moins 2 semaines dans la province d’intervention du projet. La période globale de la consultance s’étalera sur 1 mois allant de la phase de contractualisation à la fourniture de tous les livrables sus mentionnés. L'évaluateur(s) travaillera sous la supervision générale du CoPil. Des orientations supplémentaires sur la mission seront coordonnées avec l’ambassade des affaires étrangères au Tchad.

jobs.title: Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs- Khartoum - SOUDAN
jobs.description:
## Short term contract : **4 months from 01/12/2026**

## **PUI all around the world**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **What about the Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs ?**

As Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs, you will be responsible for monitoring the effective implementation of the program at the base level and for monitoring PUI's contractual obligations and reporting. You will also be responsible for representing PUI on programmatic issues to other humanitarian actors and to technical and administrative state authorities at the local level. For this purpose, you will be responsible for :

- **Strategic Development, follow-up of operations and reporting**: You will coordinate the project teams through the program managers and ensure the proper implementation of the operational and qualitative aspects of the programs (objectives monitoring, respect of deadlines and budgetary deadlines, quality control, team synergy in accordance with the contractual documents and in compliance with PUI policies and procedures. You will ensure that contractual obligations are respected and coordinate the writing of reports. You will ensure that the programs developed are in line with PUI's mandate and strategy and will propose new interventions according to the evolution of the humanitarian situation in the region.
- **MEAL**: You will coordinate the MEAL department and ensure the implementation of the activities of this department as well as the interactions with the programs and the design of relevant tools.
- **Representation**: You will participate in technical forums (working groups) at the local level in collaboration with the project leaders. You will assist the Field Co in coordination meetings between NGOs or with political and administrative authorities.
- **Human Resources**: You will be the direct supervisor of the project managers in this base and will ensure that appropriate support and capacity building is provided to senior program staff.
- **Logistics and Administration**: You will support the project managers in supervising the logistical and administrative tasks of the projects with the support of the logistics and administration departments.

## **The challenges that await you**

- Operationalization and development of our emergency response and longer-term activities in the whole region
- Improvement of program quality through MEAL and the integration of cross-cutting themes (gender, protection, environment…)
- Develop PUI capacity to respond to population movements (IDPs and returnes)

## **What you will need to succeed**

- **Training**: You hold a Master ‘s degree in a field related to project management, international development and/or social sciences.
- **Experience**: You are strengthened by minimum 2 years of experience in project management and/or monitoring, and at least 2 years as a humanitarian project manager. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!
- **Skills**: You master the methodology and the project management cycle; you have competence in studies and diagnosis. If you have knowledge of humanitarian donors, of database management and statistical software packages, it would be appreciated.
- **Qualities**: You have strong leadership and management skills, the ability to make decisions, a sense of analysis (discernment, pragmatism) and synthesis. You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate organization, rigor, flexibility, and a strong commitment to support/build capacity of project leaders. You also have a good resilience to stress.
- **Languages**: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

## **A word from the manager**

*« Are you ready to make a meaningful impact in one of today’s most challenging humanitarian contexts? By joining PUI in Sudan, you will contribute to the response to the world’s largest humanitarian crisis while leading a dedicated team delivering critical health and nutrition interventions. Beyond the impact you will have on the ground, this role offers a unique opportunity to deepen your expertise, tackle complex operational challenges, and grow professionally within a dynamic and highly committed humanitarian environment.”*

## **PUI will offer you**

- **Status :** Employé(e) with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income :** 2 660,00 - 2 800,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Housing** in collective accommodation
- **Daily Living Expenses** ("Per Diem")
- **Break Policy :** 5 working days + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy :** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year

## **Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.
**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments ? You feel ready to take up the **challenge** and to join **PUI great family ?**

jobs.title: Consortium Project Manager Colombia Bogota
jobs.description:
All NRC employees are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s core values: dedication, innovation, inclusivity, and accountability. These attitudes and beliefs shall guide our actions and relationships.

## What we are looking for

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a **highly qualified,** **resilient, and dynamic professional** to take up the role of **Consortium Manager – Emergency Response** for Colombia. The purpose of the position is to **ensure MIRE+ emergency and early recovery responses are implemented with quality, in a coordinated and timely manner, in compliance with donors and partners’ strategies and policies and in accordance to target populations’ needs in a rapidly evolving context. The Consortium Manager should strive to maintain MIRE+ positive reputation as Colombia’s largest rapid response mechanism, always seeking to improve technical and operational processes to achieve optimal efficiency and quality in the response. He/She should show leadership and adaptability as well as strong problem-solving skills and positive, assertive communication capacities.**

## What you will do

1. Provide overall direction and leadership of the Consortium to ensure seamless operations, leveraging complementarity among multi-disciplinary partners.
2. Ensure day-to-day strategic and operational coordination with NRC management leadership as leader of the consortium.
3. Oversee day-to-day management of the project, including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and budget spending, ensuring the project is always on scope and schedule.
4. Represent the Consortium towards relevant stakeholders, including national authorities, donors, humanitarian country team and counterparts, promoting the best interests of the Consortium.
5. Line manager and supervise the work of the Consortium Management Unit; carry out any needed recruitment, including consultants.
6. Lead the consultations, design and preparation of the next strategic cycle of the Consortium based on evidenced needs, donor expectations and drawing from partners’ diverse expertise.
7. Contribute to fundraising initiatives to diversify the Consortium’s portfolio, actively seeking new relationships with donors and developing funding proposals.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCGbGBJjy3XS5T_HgandSoAAewHPGz5AdIi2R2sH6YMgYs?e=rWpSar)to learn more about the position.

What you will bring

- Minimum 5-7 years of experience in the sector, with progressively increasing responsibilities in humanitarian crises’ contexts.
- At least three of those years in a leadership position involving the management and coordination of similarly sized, international donor supported programmes.
- Proven ability to communicate a common vision among diverse partners and the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams.
- Experience in complex and volatile settings.
- Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish.
- Knowledge and experience of working in Latin America is strongly preferred. Specific knowledge and experience of the context in Colombia is desirable.
- Demonstrated experience in emergency response management and international best practice.
- Well-versed in humanitarian architecture in the region.
- Knowledge of the particular dynamics of ethnic communities and regulatory frameworks.
- University Degree in International Development, Social or Human Sciences, Project Management, Emergency Response or related field.

## What we offer

- **Duty station: Bogotá, Colombia** (with extensive travel within the country)
- **Contract: national or international contract**
- Travel: up to 30%
- Salary/benefits**: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale**, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

## Important information about the application process

- *Internal candidates only: please click on the suitcase icon labelled “I am an employee” to be redirected to NRC’s internal careers site.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email aela.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line.

## Why NRC?

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We contribute to the development of policy aiming to protect the rights of the displaced and we call for increased humanitarian funding and engagement on processes that will generate structural changes in protection and assistance in the region.

NRC implements a multi-country Colombia-Panama-Ecuador strategy to respond to the complex crises and emergencies across the sub-continent. In Colombia, we provide assistance to IDPs and victims of the armed conflict in hard-to-reach areas where authorities struggle to protect civilians and provide help. We also help Colombians in need of international protection in Ecuador and Panama, as well as Venezuelans who were triggered to flee their country as a result of the growing political instability and humanitarian crisis. We provide protection, legal assistance, education, livelihoods and food security, WASH and shelter services to affected populations.

Within this context, NRC leads an intersectoral Rapid Response Mechanism (MIRE+ consortium) together with Action Against Hunger (ACF), Médecins du Monde (MdM) and Pastoral Social - Cáritas Colombia funded by EU Humanitarian Aid (ECHO), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the Spanish Agency for International Development (AECID) and Swiss Development Cooperation (COSUDE/SDC). Under a triple nexus framework, the consortium delivers multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance responding rapidly to emergencies resulting from the armed conflict in Colombia, natural hazards and early recovery activities. MIRE+ operates across all the country, prioritizing response in hard-to-reach areas and bringing support to people that have been affected by multiple compounding crises. The consortium has just entered a new two-year strategic cycle. We are therefore searching for an experienced and dynamic Chief of Party to lead the multi-donor emergency and early recovery Consortium. Whilst this position is hosted by NRC, the Consortium Manager will represent the MIRE+.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

### About Us
