The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Occupational safety and health, first aid and fire safety trainings
jobs.description:
**1. CONTEXT**
Handicap International Federation (HI), operating as Humanity & Inclusion, is an international organisation working alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations. In Kenya, HI operates from Nairobi and from field locations including Kakuma and Dadaab, where staff often work in demanding, remote and humanitarian settings that expose them to stress, critical incidents and workplace hazards.
HI Kenya wishes to comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2007, which requires employers to ensure the safety, health and welfare of their employees, including the provision of first aid, fire safety arrangements and training.
To support this, HI is seeking a qualified service provider to deliver Occupational Safety and Health, First Aid and Fire Safety trainings for HI staff in Kenya.

**2. DESCRIPTION OF THE EXPECTED SERVICE**
The contracted service provider is to provide the following services: -
2.1 Specific objectives of the assignment
• To build the capacity of HI staff in Occupational Safety and Health, First Aid and Fire Safety in line with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2007 and its subsidiary legislation.
• To equip staff with the practical skills needed to prevent, respond to and manage workplace accidents, medical emergencies and fire incidents.
2.2 Responsibilities and Tasks
The service provider will carry out the following activities: -

a) Training Needs Assessment and Planning
• Conduct a training needs assessment and develop a training plan and schedule for approval by HI.
• Develop and share training materials with HI for approval before each training.

b) Trainings
The service provider shall deliver the following practical trainings to HI staff:

i. Occupational Safety and Health Training covering, but not limited to:
• Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2007 and subsidiary regulations, and the duties of employers and employees
• Hazard identification and workplace risk assessment
• Roles and functions of the workplace safety and health committee
• Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements and usage
• Office, electrical and ergonomic safety
• Road safety and safe driving for field travel
• Handling and storage of hazardous materials
• Accident and incident reporting and investigation
ii. First Aid Training covering, but not limited to:
• Role and responsibilities of a first aider, and assessing a casualty
• Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), use of an automated external defibrillator (AED) and management of choking
• Management of bleeding, wounds, burns, fractures, sprains and shock
• Management of seizures, poisoning, fainting and other common medical emergencies
• Contents, use and maintenance of first aid kits
• Hands-on practical sessions and assessment leading to certification
iii. Fire Safety Training covering, but not limited to:
• Causes of fire, fire prevention and the classes of fire
• Types of fire extinguishers and practical, hands-on fire-fighting exercises
• Fire detection and alarm systems
• Emergency evacuation procedures, escape routes and assembly points
• Roles of fire wardens or marshals, and the conduct of evacuation drills

c) Training Delivery and Support
• Provide all training equipment and aids, including CPR manikins, extinguishers and first aid supplies for practicals.
• Conduct pre-training and post-training assessments, keep attendance registers and collect participant evaluations.
• Issue certificates of participation or competence from a recognised accrediting body to successful participants.
• Ensure training venues, materials and methods are accessible and inclusive for staff with disabilities.
• Recommend the frequency of refresher trainings and any further actions to strengthen staff safety.

**3. Scope and Target**
The assignment covers HI Kenya staff based in Nairobi and in the field locations of Kakuma and Dadaab. The estimated number of staff to be trained is 31
The scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

• Conducting a training needs assessment and developing a training plan.
• Delivering Occupational Safety and Health training to HI staff.
• Delivering accredited First Aid training to HI staff.
• Delivering Fire Safety training, including practical fire-fighting and evacuation drills.
• Assessing training outcomes and issuing certificates to participants.
• Preparing and submitting the reports and deliverables listed in this TOR.

**4. Profile of the service provider**
The service provider will need to have the following capacities:
• Registered business entity in Kenya with a proven track record of delivering Occupational Safety and Health, First Aid and Fire Safety trainings to organisations. Experience with NGOs or humanitarian organisations is an added advantage.
• Occupational Safety and Health trainers must have knowledge of the Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2007 and subsidiary regulations, and the firm must be registered with the Directorate of Occupational Safety and Health Services (DOSHS), Ministry of Labour and Social Protection.
• First Aid trainers must be certified by a recognised accrediting body, such as St John Ambulance Kenya or the Kenya Red Cross Society.
• Fire Safety trainers must hold recognised fire safety training certification and have experience delivering practical fire-fighting and evacuation drills.
• Ability to deliver trainings in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab, in English and Kiswahili.
• Experience in or commitment to disability inclusion is an added advantage.

**5.Duration and Place of Performance of the Service**
The assignment will be for a maximum period of three (3) months from the date of signing. The trainings shall be carried out in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab on dates agreed with HI.

**6.Work Plan**
Based on the proposed assignment, the timeline shall be agreed upon by the service provider and HI. The service provider shall submit a detailed work plan and training schedule within one (1) week of signing the contract.

**7.Report**
The service provider shall provide the following deliverables:-
• Work plan and training plan
• Training needs assessment report
• Training materials for HI approval before each training
• Training report for each training, with attendance registers, pre-test and post-test results, participant evaluations and recommendations
• Certificates for participants who successfully complete the trainings
• Final end-of-assignment report
All reports shall be submitted in both editable electronic format and PDF format.

**8.Contact Person**
During the performance of the service, the service provider will be assisted by the Human Resources Officer – Kenya in coordinating schedules and logistics with the field offices.

**9. Appendices**

Willingness to adhere to Handicap International's Federation institutional policies (Prevention and fight against corruption, Child Protection, Protection of Beneficiaries against sexual abuse and harassment). Available on the website: [https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies](https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies).

**10. Evaluation**

Application documents submitted will be evaluated in three (stages);
**1.General Mandatory Evaluation Criteria**
**For firms or institutions**

For Occupational Safety and Health Trainings 2026
1 Certificate of Registration
2 Trade license Certificate/ Business Permit
3 PIN/VAT Registration Certificate
4 Current Tax Compliance Certificate
5 Personal Accident Insurance cover
6 Valid DOSHS registration and First Aid accreditation of the firm and proposed trainers

**For Individuals**

For Occupational Safety and Health Trainings 2026
1 National ID
2 Relevant certifications, professional licences and accreditations
3 PIN/VAT Registration Certificate
4 Current Tax Compliance Certificate
5 Personal Accident insurance cover

**2. Technical Capacity Evaluation**
a) Profile and experience of the service provider:
i. The firm should have proven expertise and experience in providing Occupational Safety and Health, First Aid and Fire Safety trainings. Attach three reference letters

ii. Provide a list of assignments of similar scope of work undertaken within the last 2 years, along with names of clients (including contact person, email contacts, postal address and telephone numbers – this must include the three referees provided above)

b) Professional/technical capacity/ capability
i. The proposed trainers should have relevant experience and professional qualifications in the relevant field
ii. The proposal should describe the proposed training methodology, materials and approach to practical sessions

**3.Financial Evaluation**
At the Financial stage, the Lowest Competitive Evaluated bidder and within budget estimates will be considered for the award of the contract.

jobs.title: Regional Referent GIS (Geographic Information Systems) W/M – Emergency Pool
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organization created in 1971 that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters.

In collaboration with the Emergency Unit and the Emergency Logistics Coordination team, the Regional GIS Referent serves as the primary GIS focal point at regional level, providing strategic technical support to coordination and field teams in the countries within their region, in accordance with MSF GIS Unit policies, guidelines, and procedures, in order to support the overall operational objectives of the missions. This position is regional in scope and may also be intersectional.

**Main Responsibilities :**

- At the request of coordination teams and based on the terms of reference established by them (Logistics Coordinator, Medical Coordinator, Head of Mission, Field Coordinator), conduct GIS assessments in the countries of the region and propose strategies adapted to operational needs.
- Liaise with the GIS Unit, GIS focal points at headquarters, and GIS staff within the region; contribute to the definition and improvement of GIS policies by providing feedback based on professional experience. Formulate recommendations regarding programs and broader operational objectives, as well as their implementation or enhancement, in accordance with MSF GIS Unit policies, guidelines, and procedures.
- Provide technical support within the assigned geographical area, with assistance from the GIS Unit when necessary.
- Monitor the implementation of GIS projects and activities in the countries of the region and conduct, at least annually, an analysis of GIS projects.
- Develop a network and maintain in-depth knowledge of local GIS stakeholders within the geographical area (institutions, volunteer groups, NGOs, training centers, suppliers, etc., as relevant).
- Upon request from missions within the region, contribute to the development of GIS-related training content and facilitate training sessions.
- Draft mission reports and annual activity reports.
- Participate, when requested, in emergency operations within the geographical area.
- Contribute to discussions on ethics and personal data protection within the mission, particularly concerning GIS-related data and activities.

**Required Qualifications**

- University degree required.
- Specialization in GIS (Geographic Information Systems) or a closely related field.

**Experience**

- Field experience with international NGO projects is required.
- Previous experience with MSF is an asset.
- Significant professional experience in the relevant specialty area (minimum two years) is required.
- Strong project management skills, as well as knowledge of management and training methodologies.

**Competencies**

- Geographic Information Systems (GIS): Level 4
- Strategic Vision: Level 2
- Leadership: Level 2
- People Management and Development: Level 3
- Service Orientation: Level 3
- Teamwork and Cooperation: Level 4

**Languages**

- Excellent command of French (minimum B2 level) and English (minimum B2 level).
- Knowledge of additional languages is an asset.

**Contract conditions**

- Field-based position with regular visits to headquarters in Paris.
- Full-time fixed-term contract (12 months, 100%), with the possibility of extension.
- Desired start date: As soon as possible.
- Gross salary: According to the MSF salary scale, Level 12.
- Special benefits under the Emergency Contract framework.
- Additional benefits: Health insurance coverage.

*At MSF, we value diversity and strive for an inclusive and accessible working environment. We encourage all suitably qualified people to apply, regardless of their ethnic, national or cultural origin, age, gender, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability or any other aspect of their identity.*

jobs.title: Consultoría de apoyo a la revisión financiera, documental y de procesos de compra
jobs.description:
eser International (MI) es la agencia internacional de ayuda humanitaria de la Orden Soberana de Malta. Desde hace más de 60 años brindamos asistencia humanitaria y apoyo a la recuperación de las personas durante y después de conflictos y desastres en todo el mundo. Los valores cristianos y los principios humanitarios constituyen la base de nuestro trabajo. En más de 30 países de África, América, Asia, Europa y Oriente Medio, apoyamos a las personas necesitadas independientemente de su religión, origen o convicciones políticas.

Como parte de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto que impactó Venezuela el 24 de junio de 2026, Malteser International implementa un proyecto de asistencia humanitaria a través de organizaciones socias nacionales. Debido al volumen de documentación financiera y de adquisiciones generado durante la implementación, se requiere apoyo especializado para fortalecer los procesos de seguimiento financiero y control documental.

**Por este motivo, Malteser International busca apoyo de consultoría para el seguimiento financiero y el control documental en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia en Venezuela.**

La consultoría brindará apoyo en la revisión periódica de registros financieros, comprobantes de gasto, vouchers, expedientes de compra y documentación de respaldo presentada por los socios implementadores, asegurando su cumplimiento con los procedimientos administrativos, financieros y logísticos de MI, así como con los requisitos documentales del proyecto.

Los requisitos para la presentación de ofertas se detallan en los [Términos de Referencia](https://www.malteser-international.org/fileadmin/Files_sites/malteser-international/A-About_us/E-Service/Z-Tenders/TdR_Consultoria_Voucher_Verification_261112.pdf).

jobs.title: Business Development Senior Officer (d/f/m) (ECHO)
jobs.description:
## *\*\*\*in Berlin / Bonn or Remote (within Germany) | ASAP |*

## *\*\*\*full-time (40 hours/week) | Initially for 2 years*

**About Us**

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. In 2016, IRC Germany was founded and engages in global humanitarian work as well as throughout Germany in the areas of education, economic wellbeing, and safety, legal protection, and empowerment.

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department runs the IRC’s humanitarian, recovery, and development programs in five regions: West & Central Africa, East Africa, Middle East and North Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Within CRRD, the Award Management Unit (AMU)’s Grants Operations & Analytics Team (GOAT) supports pre- and post-award work for projects managed by Technical Excellence, Global Supply Chain and Airbel.

**Major Responsibilities**

The Business Development Senior Officer (ECHO), will be responsible for leading a portfolio of business development opportunities, ensuring that all proposals are compelling and submitted in accordance with IRC and Donor policies.

**Business Development Process (80%)**

**ECHO oversight**: Provide IRC Germany oversight to opportunities submitted under ECHO’s Strategic Policies and Strategic Humanitarian Supply Chain HIPs. This will include completing ECHO pre-award checklists and uploads to APPEL.

**Proposal leadership**: Outside of the ECHO HIP season, will serve as Proposal Lead for funding opportunities assigned by the Head of Business Development.

- Lead the overall proposal development process to ensure submissions are compliant, responsive, and compelling.
- Support the technical team to position for anticipated calls, including pre-development of concept notes.
- Project manage proposals ensuring internal approvals in line with external submission deadlines.
- Coordinate with country programs and partners to collect the documents and inputs needed for each proposal.

**Proposal Budget development**: Serve as Budget Lead for funding opportunities assigned by the Head of Business Development.

· Develop proposal budgets to ensure consistency and accuracy across projects. Design, draft, refine, and finalize budgets and budget narratives (as needed) that are reflective of program design costs.

· Ensure appropriate internal formats and donor formats for budget development are used.

· Coordinate and liaise with country program finance and grants staff on proposals, providing guidance and feedback on workplans, deadlines, and proposal parameters.

· Secure approvals across departments for submissions.

**Process Support and Feedback (10%)**

**BD Process Improvements**: Work on departmental and organisational initiatives to improve IRC’s BD processes.

· Support refinement of business development processes for Technical Excellence.

· Attend key cross-unit and cross-departmental meetings regarding business development to maintain an in-depth understanding of IRC funding streams and business development priorities.

**ECHO Awards Management and Compliance (10%)**

**Awards Management:** Act as IRC Germany’s post-award focal point for Technical Excellence and Global Supply Chain ECHO awards.

· Provide ad-hoc compliance guidance to grants team on ECHO awards

· Coordinate with grants team to ensure timely submissions of reports on APPEL.

· Monitor ECHO portfolio through participation in project implementation meetings, ensuring progress against objectives and compliance with ECHO guidelines.

· Manage donor relationship with ECHO across portfolio.

**Your Profile**

**Essential**

· Experience preparing or submitting proposals to ECHO

· 5+ years of progressive work experience connected to business development and working in or closely with Technical teams

· Highly collaborative and pro-active colleague with a talent for delivering results with cross-functional groups

· Advanced Microsoft Office skills (Excel, PowerPoint) and experience with organizational information and financial systems

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a multi-cultural environment

· University degree in Business Administration, Finance, International Development or a relevant field, or equivalent work experience

· You have English language skills at C1 and German B1 according to the[Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CERF)](https://www.europaeischer-referenzrahmen.de/)

**Desired**

· Experience working with IRC systems is a plus

· Dedication to diversity, equity and inclusion, and a strong passion for our mission

· Comfortable adapting to new challenges and dynamic priorities, while maintaining professional grace

· Fluency in French, Spanish or Arabic language a plus

**We Offer**

- Meaningful work within a collaborative team
- A starting salary between 60,028 and 67,090 Euro gross per year as well as an annual salary increase
- Attractive employee benefits such as gym membership, company pension scheme, shopping vouchers, childcare subsidy, job bike leasing, subsidized Deutschlandticket (national public transport), and access to timely and confidential psychological support if needed
- 30 days of annual leave and special leave days
- Flexible hybrid-work options (working hours, office/homebased)
- Training and professional development opportunities, including access to free language courses
- Assistance services for people with disabilities, if required.

jobs.title: Senior Innovation Associate
jobs.description:
**ABOUT SPARK MICROGRANTS**

Spark MicroGrants believes in a world where everyone lives with dignity and determines their own positive future. Spark has worked in 1000+ villages in 6 countries and has pioneered a community-driven development model in sub-Saharan Africa. Spark works with NGO and Government partners to scale the model’s adoption and impact on rural communities - on their own terms. Our model combines facilitated community meetings with a small, discretionary grant to catalyze local action and institution building. Read more about our [Approach](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/the-spark-process), [Impact ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/impact)and [Values ](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/about-spark#about-our-values)on our [website](https://www.sparkmicrogrants.org/).

**ABOUT THE INNOVATION TEAM**

The Innovation team works to channel more resources and decision-making to the village level by partnering with the World Bank and other multilateral institutions. Community-driven development (CDD) has a proven track record of delivering lasting change with communities in the lead and momentum for it is building. Our work focuses on three mutually reinforcing areas: building a community of senior CDD champions across governments, development finance institutions, and major donors; partnering with the World Bank to support the effective design of community-led programs and the tools and standards behind them; and exploring new financing pathways, including a dedicated CDD fund.

**OVERVIEW**

Spark seeks a Senior Innovation Associate to partner closely with the Chief Innovation Officer and the Innovation team as we work to bring more resources and decision-making to the village level through partnerships with the World Bank and other multilateral institutions.

The Senior Innovation Associate is a trusted, senior individual contributor to the Innovation team who owns significant areas of work and drives them independently. Think of the role as a Chief-of-Staff-style partner focused on sector building: framing new opportunities, owning the systems and relationships that keep the team ahead, and taking projects from idea to done with minimal oversight. The role blends research, project management, and communication to increase the pace and quality of Spark’s work to bring more resources to the village level.

**WHO YOU ARE**

You are a self-starter who owns outcomes and doesn’t wait for direction to figure out how to make a project or process better. You bring the rare combination of being highly organized, i.e. nothing drops, and genuinely curious: you like chasing down a question, learning something new, and turning it into something useful. You are a strong writer and a clear thinker who exercises sound judgment on ambiguous, high-stakes work, and you are comfortable representing the team’s thinking to senior partners. You do not want to do development as usual, and you care about expanding high-impact work through new modalities. You are motivated to join at a crucial juncture in our growth, as we build the coalitions, evidence, and financing needed to make CDD the default approach in contexts where it works.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Innovation Associate helps the Innovation team operate with clarity, focus, and execution excellence across a globally distributed team, advancing the future-facing work of the Chief Innovation Officer and owning key workstreams that turn strategy into action.

**1. Research and Opportunity Development**

Lead research and analysis to inform decisions on emerging opportunities, independently framing the questions and surfacing the data, evidence, and context the team needs to move quickly and well. This includes exploring new financing pathways and partners, such as the design of a dedicated CDD fund, pooled funds, and collaborations with other multilaterals.

- Lead research on new opportunities, partners, funding mechanisms, and multilateral institutions, and recommend which are worth pursuing.
- Draft concept notes and briefs, selecting the most relevant data, evidence, and figures and framing the options for possible pathways and growth scenarios.
- Synthesize findings into clear, decision-ready recommendations that make it easy for decision-makers to act.

**2. Network Mapping and Relationship Tracking**

Own the systems and strategy for keeping Spark’s relationships with World Bank teams, multilateral institutions, their clients, and other sector actors organized, current, and easy to draw on at strategic moments. This directly supports building and sustaining a senior community of CDD champions across governments, development finance institutions, and major donors.

- Design, build, and own the systems for mapping and tracking champions, contacts, and engagement history across partner institutions and sector actors.
- Establish the baseline for the champion network and track how it grows over time, including through the Africa CLD forum, curated learning exchanges, and 1:1 follow-up with high-potential contacts.
- Prepare background and engagement strategy on stakeholders ahead of meetings, forums, learning trips, and strategic moments, and drive follow-ups for timely, coordinated outreach.

**3. Project Management**

Own projects from initiation to close on behalf of the Chief Innovation Officer and the Innovation team, taking full accountability for the quality and timely completion of deliverables. This spans efforts such as convening the annual practitioner forum, coordinating design support to World Bank programs, and developing practical tools — financial frameworks, facilitation guides, national planning templates, and community-facing technology.

- Take ownership of priority and ad hoc projects, driving them from initiation to close as needed by the Innovation team.
- Establish and own trackers, timelines, and implementation calendars that keep engagements, forums, and tool development moving.
- Identify bottlenecks and proactively unblock or escalate them.

**4. Communications and Research Dissemination**

Lead internal and external communications on behalf of the Chief Innovation Officer and the Innovation team, keeping partners, champions, and staff aligned and informed. This includes packaging research and results into accessible, high-quality products and supporting the thought leadership and evidence sharing (e.g., evidence briefs, policy briefs, research roundtables) that builds the case for CDD among decision-makers.

- Produce and own communications, including evidence briefs, policy briefs, partner updates, annual reports, and internal messages.
- Lead the preparation of materials for forums, learning exchanges, roundtables, and stakeholder engagements.
- Help keep the team and wider organization informed about priorities and progress.

**WHAT TO BRING**

- 5+ years of relevant experience, ideally in a global, mission-driven organization, with a track record of owning workstreams independently
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with sound judgment and discretion
- Strong research and synthesis skills, with the judgment to frame questions and draw conclusions with limited direction
- Highly organized, with a track record of keeping projects and details on track
- A strong bias toward action and full ownership of outcomes; comfortable operating with autonomy
- Self-driven and professional, with an entrepreneurial spirit’
- A genuine interest in community-driven development and sector-building work, ideally with exposure to multilaterals, development finance, or the World Bank
- Proven ability to drive cross-time zone collaboration and to engage credibly with senior external partners

**OTHER INFORMATION**

Job Location: Based in one of Spark’s countries of operation: Ghana, Uganda, Rwanda, or Malawi. (Elsewhere in Africa may also be considered for very strong candidates, if candidates already possess valid, legal work authorization for other requested job locations.)

Reporting to: Chief Innovation Officer - under Innovation Team

Start Date: As soon as possible

Salary: Salary is based on geographic location and commensurate with experience

Probation period: Three months probation period with learning and performance objectives

Time commitment: Full time. We are also open to part-time arrangements, at a minimum of three days per week.

How to Apply: Follow the link to apply: [https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/179](https://sparkmicrogrants.bamboohr.com/careers/179)

**SAFEGUARDING**

Our safeguarding follows a do no harm principle. All Spark staff are expected to respect and uphold the safeguarding procedures and principles to minimize harm to stakeholders, program participants, and the environment, in compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and national legislation in the countries where we operate.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**

Spark Microgrants provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals. Employment decisions at Spark are based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. Spark does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by the law. Spark will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in undue hardship to daily operations.

jobs.title: Human Resources Manager
jobs.description:
**Starting position: January 1, 2026**

**Duration : 12 months**

**Place of work : Damascus, Syria**

**Status : National contract, fixed- term**

**Deadline for applications:** Terre des hommes does not set a deadline for applications for this position, recruitment is open until the position is filled.

Terre des hommes (Tdh) :

The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), with headquarters in Lausanne and an office in Zurich, is the leading Swiss child rights organisation with more than 2000 employees worldwide. We stand together with children to uphold their rights, protect their lives and improve their well-being. We achieve this through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have a positive and sustainable impact.

**Context :**

The HR Manager is responsible for providing strategic leadership and operational management of all Human Resources functions within Tdh Syria. This role ensures that the delegation is staffed with qualified, competent, and motivated personnel who actively contribute to improving the lives of children and their families. As a key member of the Senior Management Team, the HR Manager plays a pivotal role in shaping organizational culture, promoting staff engagement, and aligning HR practices with Tdh’s mission and strategic objectives. The position oversees workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, and employee relations, while ensuring compliance with Tdh’s Global Code of Conduct, internal policies, Child Safeguarding standards, and HR procedures. In addition to strategic responsibilities, the HR Manager manages core administrative functions such as payroll, leave administration, contract management, and benefits, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and adherence to local labor laws and organizational policies. Furthermore, the HR Manager works to build the capacity of HR staff at mission level, fosters a safe and respectful work environment, and supports managers in applying best practices in people management. Ultimately, this role serves as a trusted advisor to leadership and staff, ensuring that HR systems and processes enable the organization to achieve its humanitarian goals effectively and ethically.

**Main responsibilities:**

**HR Strategy & Governance**

- Translate operational and institutional needs into local HR strategies aligned with Tdh’s global People Strategy.
- Provide strategic input on workforce planning, organizational design, and talent needs.
- Conduct HR organizational assessments and propose improvements.
- Ensure Tdh’s values and safeguarding principles are respected.
- Contribute to building an HR information system, and provide analysis to inform and improve HR related decision making processes.

**Policy, Compliance & HR Framework**

- Develop, update, and implement HR policies and SOPs in line with local labor law and global standards.
- Ensure compliance with staff regulations, labor laws, and internal governance standards.
- Oversee data protection, confidentiality, and compliant personnel record management.
- Deliver training to managers and staff on HR policies and compliance requirements.

**Workforce Planning & HR Operations**

- Oversee recruitment, hiring, onboarding, and workforce planning processes.
- Ensure accurate payroll checks and compliance with HR operations.
- Conduct or contribute to salary and benefits benchmarking; advise on compensation and reward strategies.

**Performance Management & Talent Development**

- Implement and monitor performance management systems and processes.
- Support goal setting, coaching, and career development initiatives.
- Prepare annual capacity building plans aligning with Tdh’s strategic objectives.
- Promote continuous feedback and staff development opportunities.

**Employee Relations, Engagement & Well-Being**

- Act as focal point for employee relations, including grievances, disciplinary processes, and mediation.
- Promote open and constructive dialogue between employees and management.
- Foster a positive, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace.
- Promote mental health support and psychosocial well-being initiatives.
- Organize team building activities.

**Budget & Compliance**

- Monitor HR budgets, staffing costs, and FMT allocations.
- Ensure Staff archving is complete and uploaded to respective HR country folders.

**Crisis Management**

- Anticipate HR needs in crisis contexts, including surge capacity and duty-of-care measures.
- Act as HR focal point during emergencies, ensuring timely workforce deployment and staff well-being.
- Coordinate with Operations, Security, and Staff Health during crises.

**External Relations & Representation**

- Liaise with legal advisors, labor authorities, and HR networks.
- Represent Tdh in HR forums and conduct sector benchmarking to maintain best practices.

**Core Competencies:**

- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple HR and administrative tasks with a results-oriented approach.
- Strategic thinking and ability to align HR initiatives with organizational goals.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic.
- Strong interpersonal skills to work effectively with employees at all levels and maintain positive professional relationships.
- High attention to detail, accuracy, and thoroughness in documentation, data entry, and filing.
- Ability to plan, prioritize, and follow up on tasks efficiently, especially under tight deadlines.
- Confidentiality and professionalism in handling sensitive employee information and HR documentation.
- Good understanding of HR procedures, recruitment steps, and administrative workflows.
- Self-motivated, proactive, and able to work independently and as part of a team, with flexibility and adaptability to changing operational needs.
- **\*\*The full Job Description will be shared with shortlisted candidates.\*\***

**Profile :**

**Education :** Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field; a master’s degree is an asset.

**Experience / Skills :**
- Minimum of five years of professional experience in Human Resources, with at least two years as head of an HR department.
- At least two years of experience within an NGO is required.

**Languages :**

Fluency in Arabic and English is required.

**IT knowledge :**

Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to work with HR systems and digital archiving.

Experience working with an HRIS is an advantage.

Salary :

As per Tdh Salary scale in Syria.

**Tdh General Code of Conduct and Ethical Policies** :

- Commits to promoting and complying with the Global Code of Conduct, systematically reporting any violations of the Code through Tdh's formal reporting mechanisms and dealing with any violations of procedures and processes appropriately.
- Raises awareness of the Foundation of the risks of policy non-compliance, violence and abuse, and related rights, towards children, community members and our own employees.
- Undertakes to comply with key ethical policies and guidelines, including the Safeguarding Policy, the Anti-Fraud and Corruption Policy, the Conflict-of-Interest Policy and other policies related to the prevention of terrorist financing and criminal activities, as well as workplace behavior.
- Commits to putting values and principles into practice through exemplary behavior, in full compliance with the Code of Conduct, and always respecting established procedures and processes.
- Commits to developing a compliant and enlightened management culture within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we operate.

**Procedure:**

Only complete applications (CV + covering letter) posted on our official website will be processed. Additional documents (diplomas, work certificates, etc.) will be requested at a later date. We will only contact those candidates selected for further recruitment.

**References :**

Please note that all job offers will be subject to satisfactory references and checks (criminal record and anti-terrorism funding check). Terre des hommes will ask the Human Resources of previous organisations to provide references on any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment as well as fraud and corruption, during employment, or incidents under investigation at the time the candidate left employment.

jobs.title: Country Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Assistant – Kyiv, Ukraine
jobs.description:
**Department:** MEAL unit – Operations

**Duty Station:** Kyiv

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Direct report:** MEAL Coordinator

**Grade:** Assistant

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this Role?**

The MEAL Assistant will provide technical and operational support to the MEAL function of Geneva Call Ukraine, contributing to the effective implementation of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities.

The position is primarily focused on operational MEAL and data management support, including field data collection and entry, routine monitoring, maintaining and updating programme databases, data entry and cleaning, data quality assurance, supporting digital data collection processes, and assisting with routine MEAL activities and reporting.

The position ensures data quality, supports evidence-based decision making, and strengthens accountability to affected populations through effective feedback and learning processes.

Methodological decisions, indicator definitions, analytical approaches and final validation of MEAL findings remain under the responsibility of the MEAL Coordinator.

## **Work Relations**

The MEAL Assistant will work under the direct supervision of the MEAL Coordinator and in close coordination with Programme and other relevant teams as follows.

- **Internal:** Country Director, Head of Programme, Programme Coordinator, Programme and support staff, MEAL Coordinator, HQ MEAL Unit, Policy, Research and Legal (PRL) Unit, and other relevant support functions as required.
- **External:** Implementing partners, service providers, and relevant coordination platforms.

## **Duties and Responsibilities**

**Database Management and Data Quality Assurance**

- Maintain, update and regularly review programme databases, monitoring trackers and MEAL-related records, including participant lists, training databases and indicator tracking tools.
- Consolidate data collected through different sources, including Microsoft Forms, KoboToolbox, Excel and other digital data collection platforms.
- Perform routine data entry, cleaning, validation and quality checks to identify missing, duplicate, inconsistent or erroneous entries, and verify data against source records.
- Coordinate with relevant colleagues to clarify discrepancies and ensure consistency of data across different databases, trackers, reporting tools and programme records.
- Organise and maintain electronic records, ensuring proper file naming, version control and documentation.

**Data Processing and Analysis Support**

- Process and organise quantitative data collected through pre- and post-training tests, feedback questionnaires, monitoring forms and other MEAL tools.
- Support the calculation of basic MEAL indicators, including training participation, knowledge and attitude changes, and feedback results.
- Prepare summary tables, charts and basic visualisations using Excel and Power Bi, as well as other relevant tools. Support the preparation and updating of Power BI dashboards and other data visualisation tools, as required.
- Assist in consolidating data for internal monitoring, donor reporting and programme reviews.
- Identify data gaps and trends and communicate relevant observations to the MEAL Coordinator.

**Digital Data Collection Support**

- Assist with the updating of digital data collection forms such as Microsoft Forms, KoboToolbox or ODK, following standard templates and instructions.
- Support the maintenance of digital forms, QR codes, data collection links and related documentation.
- Assist with downloading, exporting and consolidating collected data.
- Maintain organised records of data collection tools and their respective versions.

**Routine MEAL Activities and Reporting**

- Assist with field data collection and routine monitoring activities, including participant feedback collection, follow-up surveys and third-party monitoring arrangements.
- Support enumerators with field data collection and practical arrangements, and promptly report monitoring and data quality issues.
- Support the preparation and organisation of monitoring documentation and supporting evidence, and assist in compiling quantitative information for periodic programme and donor reports.
- Support the maintenance of MEAL trackers, indicator monitoring tools and reporting databases.
- Assist with the organisation and documentation of lessons learned and other MEAL-related activities, and perform other MEAL-related tasks assigned by the MEAL Coordinator.

**Data Protection and Confidentiality**

- Handle programme and participant data in accordance with Geneva Call’s data protection, confidentiality and information management requirements.
- Ensure that personal and sensitive information is accessed, stored, processed and shared only through authorised channels.
- Apply data minimisation principles and follow established procedures for anonymisation and secure data storage.
- Assist with the implementation of Geneva Call’s organisational guidance on Accountability to Affected People (AAP).

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- University degree in Statistics, Social Sciences, Economics, Information Management, Data Analysis or another relevant field.

**Experience (Essential)**

- At least 1 year of relevant professional experience in data management, data entry, information management, monitoring and evaluation, or a related field. Relevant internship experience may also be considered.
- Experience working with databases, trackers and structured datasets.
- Experience working with digital data collection tools (Microsoft Forms, KoboToolbox, Google Forms or similar) as well as SharePoint, Microsoft Teams and cloud-based document management.
- Experience with Power Query, Power BI or other data analysis and visualisation tools.
- Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including formulas, sorting, filtering, data validation and pivot tables.
- Basic understanding of MEAL concepts and a good understanding of data quality principles.
- Ability to work with multiple datasets and maintain accuracy when handling repetitive tasks.

**Experience (Desirable)**

- Familiarity with MEAL concepts, indicator tracking and results-based management.
- Basic knowledge of quantitative data analysis and descriptive statistics.
- Experience working in an NGO, INGO or humanitarian/development organisation.
- Exposure to partner coordination and multi-stakeholder environments.

**Job related Competencies** **and Technical Skills**

- Strong analytical and data interpretation skills.
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
- Experience supervising data collection teams.
- Solid report writing and documentation skills.
- Understanding of humanitarian programming and sectoral approaches.

**Organizational competencies**

- Understanding and respect for humanitarian principles and Geneva Call’s vision, mission and confidentiality.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Collaborative, team‑oriented and solutions‑oriented approach.
- Uphold Geneva Call’s core values: humanity, neutrality, impartiality, accountability, dedication and respect.

**Languages**

- Proficiency in Ukrainian required.
- At least intermediate level of English (B1–B2 level) required.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call brings together people of diverse nationalities, cultures, languages and perspectives, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

Joining Geneva Call offers the opportunity to contribute to humanitarian action by supporting the effective implementation of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities. As MEAL Assistant, you will play an important role in ensuring the quality, accuracy and reliability of programme data, supporting evidence-based decision-making and strengthening accountability to affected populations. This position provides an opportunity to contribute to meaningful programme monitoring and learning processes while supporting the delivery and continuous improvement of Geneva Call’s activities in Ukraine.

jobs.title: Programme Director - Mozambique
jobs.description:
The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR delivers large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also support the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Position Title:** Programme Director

**Location:** Cabo Delgado

**Reporting to:** HQ Programme Manager

**Duration:** 10-month contract

**Closing date of applications**: 17 November 2026

**Start date:** Immediate

**Requirements for the role**

- Diploma: Project Management, International Development or a related field.
- Minimum of five years’ experience managing field-level humanitarian and health/vector-borne disease control programmes.
- Fluent in both Portuguese and English (written and spoken).
- Familiar with NGO operational environments, donor regulations and standard procedures.
- Solid experience working in complex, high-risk security contexts (preferably in northern Mozambique/Cabo Delgado).
- Proven experience in field team management, programme coordination, operational logistics, and field financial monitoring.
- Strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills under pressure.
- Excellent operational communication skills.

**Overall job purpose**

MENTOR seeks an experienced and highly motivated professional with a strong interest in vector-borne disease control to lead and develop some of its country programmes, partnering with a strong headquarters team.

The successful candidate will be trained in our systems and approaches to lead one of our in-country programmes.

The Programme Director (PD) is based in Cabo Delgado and responsible for the overall operational leadership, technical execution, and field coordination of MENTOR’s activities in the province. Working under the direct supervision of the HQ Programme Manager, the PD oversees field teams, programme logistics, operational security, and local financial/administrative compliance to ensure programme objectives are met efficiently and safely.

The PD will lead in-country organisational representation and is responsible for the management of all fundraising financial and grant management, human resources management, technical programme support and logistics support.

The PD will coordinate the different programmes to ensure consistent levels of high-quality delivery, accountability and transparency across them all.

**Task and responsibilities**

**Security management**

In close collaboration with the HQ Programme Manager and HQ Security Officer, the Programme Director is responsible and accountable for operational security management across Cabo Delgado bases and field operations:

- Maintain solid local networks and regular information collection and analysis regarding the security situation in Cabo Delgado.
- Directly manage the implementation and regular updating of local security plans and guidelines for all MENTOR bases in the province.
- Ensure route assessments are completed, reviewed and approved within 72 hours prior to any team movement.
- Deliver comprehensive security briefings to all incoming team members, consultants and visitors arriving in Cabo Delgado.
- Ensure strict compliance with all general security rules, communication protocols, and security-related technology by all field team members.
- Liaise with local security actors and humanitarian security mechanisms in Cabo Delgado (for example, INSO, UNDSS, local focal points).
- Ensure that security-related logistical support (vehicles, communication gear, hibernation kits, base physical security) is fully operational.
- Report all security alerts, incidents and developments immediately to the HQ. Programme Manager and Security Officer, submitting detailed incident reports as required.

**Programme implementation and coordination**

- Lead the day-to-day coordination and delivery of MENTOR’s vector-borne disease control, health and WASH activities in Cabo Delgado.
- Oversee the operational planning and delivery of field interventions, including WASH support, Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS), health facility support, and IEC/BCC community campaigns.
- Supervise and support project managers, officers and technical field staff to ensure activities follow agreed work plans, donor targets and technical standards.
- Ensure effective data collection, monitoring and field reporting systems are maintained for project monitoring and evaluation.
- Compile, review and draft high-quality monthly, quarterly and interim narrative field reports for submission to the HQ Programme Manager.

**Field financial and administrative oversight**

In collaboration with the country finance team and HQ Grants Manager, ensure financial integrity and compliance at the field level:

- Oversee local cash management, cash advances and field expenditure security in accordance with MENTOR standard operating procedures.
- Monitor local project burn rates and budget lines against planned field activities.
- Review and approve field financial documentation, local procurement requests, payroll, and monthly cash requests before submission to HQ.
- Ensure full compliance with national labour laws, local regulations and tax requirements applicable to operations in Cabo Delgado.

**Human Resources management and team leadership**

- Provide line management, leadership and supervision to the field coordination team in Cabo Delgado.
- Lead the recruitment, onboarding and management of national staff in compliance with Mozambican labour legislation.
- Organise and conduct regular briefing and debriefing sessions for field personnel and incoming consultants.
- Carry out regular performance evaluations for directly supervised staff and ensure team managers complete reviews for their teams.
- Build a harmonious, collaborative and professional working environment through weekly team planning meetings.
- Enforce strict adherence to MENTOR’s Code of Conduct, PSEA and Safeguarding policies across all operational bases in Cabo Delgado, reporting any policy violations immediately to HQ.

**Field logistics and operations support**

In close collaboration with the Field Logistics team:

- Oversee local procurement processes to ensure transparency, timely delivery and alignment with donor guidelines.
- Ensure effective stock management of medical supplies, vector control equipment, tools and assets at Cabo Delgado warehouses.
- Monitor fleet management, vehicle maintenance and driver safety protocols for all field movements.
- Ensure maintenance and proper usage of all field communication systems (VHF, HF, satellite phones, internet).

**Operational communication and coordination**

- Internal: Maintain constant and transparent communication with the HQ Programme Manager, holding regular update meetings and submitting field SITREPs.
- External (Local/Provincial Level): Represent MENTOR in local humanitarian cluster meetings (Health, WASH, Shelter/NFI), operational working groups, and technical field coordination forums within Cabo Delgado.
- Maintain positive working relationships with local health authorities (DPS/SDSMAS), district government officials, and community leaders in project implementation areas.

**Other responsibilities**

- Undertake any other operational duties as assigned by the HQ Programme Manager.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Director of Advocacy
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview:**
As the Director of Advocacy, you will lead development of the IRC’s advocacy efforts to support key priorities across crisis and solutions-driven global influence priorities for the International Rescue Committee. You are responsible for crafting our influence strategies using IRC’s programmatic and research evidence, surgical policy and practice solutions, and trusted brand to inspire collective action. You are the expert for understanding current federal legislative and policy trends in the US and how our policies cut across political agendas. You will engage key stakeholders across government and civil society. You will work across the IRC to develop advocacy campaigns and build relationships including with Congressional representatives, U.S. and other government officials in D.C. as well as foundations, think tanks, multilateral organizations, and other humanitarian organizations. You will also look across IRC’s global priorities, engaging relevant embassies and crafting specific advocacy messages for donor governments.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Advocacy Strategy:** Lead advocacy strategies for specific policy goals, including thought leadership objectives relevant to the U.S. market, collaborating with policy leads to advance IRCs key influence priorities and maximize the opportunity for IRC to advance our influence objectives. Engage across the IRC with all relevant stakeholders. Craft advocacy strategies, drawing on IRC’s policy expertise, that are suited to global donor government priorities.
- **Influence Analysis:** Develop U.S. power maps for key policy issues to identify influence priorities. Cultivate relationships across the U.S. Government and lead Congressional engagement. Work with team to support development and execution of creative influence strategies, including with nontraditional partners. Look across IRC’s global priorities and ensure they are integrated into advocacy and influence strategies.
- **Advocacy:** Support efforts to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships by engaging with key policy stakeholders and supporting opportunities to raise IRC’s profile at key meetings and fora. Collaborate closely with other U.S. market staff and global policy and advocacy staff, contributing to efforts designed to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships in Washington.
- Legislative and Policy Tracking. Expand IRC’s legislative reach by tracking and analyzing shifting Congressional and Executive branch positions, individuals engaging on our issues, and the politics around our issues. Translate policy asks into legislative asks. Engage U.S. Government stakeholders relevant to the IRC’s work in the U.S. Track U.S. legislative and executive processes.
- **Policy Engagement:** Contribute to policy generation by providing U.S.-specific analysis that increases the credibility and efficacy of our solutions through constant collaboration. Support IRC’s policy team in identifying and developing policy priorities that are impactful and achievable in the U.S. as well as in global markets.
- **Communications:** Provide market and audience expertise to communications team to shape policy communications specific to the U.S.Support the team in developing communications strategy and develop materials for advocacy targets. Support planning and implementation of strategic activities including events. Facilitate development and editing of internal and external advocacy products to ensure resonance in U.S. market and adherence to high standards of quality.
- **Steward Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** both in the culture of IRC, as well as in the policy solutions we develop and the ways we wield influence.
- **Spokesperson:** Act as an IRC influence spokespersonon focused advocacy areas. Act as key interlocutor with legislative and governmental staffers**.**
- **Board and Advisors:** Support relationships with IRC's Board and Advisors by identifying points of mutual interest and opportunities around our priority issues.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Potential supervision of Senior Advisor or other staff.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Senior Director, Advocacy & Influence and Vice President of Policy and Advocacy
- **Internal contacts:** Policy and Advocacy colleagues across the globe; Technical Excellence leads; International Programs leads; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Communications; Awards Management; President’s Office, External Relations Department
- **External contacts:** Key Opinion Formers and policy makers in the U.S. Government and U.S. Congress, other humanitarian leaders and thinktanks, relevant embassies, multilateral institutions

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Degree in relevant field such as Public Policy, Law or International Relations

***Work experience:***

- Demonstrated experience in advocacy and advocacy strategy development with a focus on creativity and strategic thinking
- 10-12 years of experience working on complex humanitarian and/or development issues
- Knowledge of U.S. Government functioning and prior work the U.S. Government or Congress are a plus.
- Understanding of global issues, multilateral engagement experience.

***Demonstrated skills and competencies:***

- Examples of influence/impact on legislative and executive policy. Strong network of influencers and policy makers
- Deep understanding of global issues related to the humanitarian field.
- Ability to think strategically and creatively, being solutions-oriented
- Extensive knowledge of humanitarian aid and refugee issues, particularly around the complex drivers of humanitarian need
- Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate successfully with experts, high level decision and policy makers, and colleagues in the humanitarian and development fields. Good public speaking skills.
- Excellent writing skills and the ability to translate complex material and data into coherent narratives that resonate with policymakers
- Fluency with key parts of the IRC’s strategy and existing policy strategy
- Ability to work on tight deadlines and juggle competing demands
- Self-motivated

**Working Environment:** Remote

**Compensation:** ***($130,000 - $156,000 - annually).*** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: External consultancy - MEAL and Program Data Management best practices documents
jobs.description:
1\. INTRODUCTION

1.1. PRESENTATION OF PREMIERE URGENCE INTERNATIONALE

Première Urgence Internationale is a non-governmental organisation dedicated to international solidarity – non-profit and with no political or religious affiliation. Its teams is mobilized, by carrying out humanitarian and development work across the globe, without discrimination, to support of civilian who are at risk, marginalised or excluded due to the effects of armed conflict, natural disasters or economic collapse resulting from political upheaval or the consequences of environmental and climate degradation.
The Association runs around 200 projects a year, including in the fields of Health, Nutrition, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, Food Security and Livelihoods, Protection, Water, Hygiene and Sanitation. PUI supports nearly 7 million people in around 24 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Latin America.

1.2. GENERAL CONTEXT OF THE CONSULTANCY

As a humanitarian organization implementing numerous projects in various contexts and across several sectors, PUI needs to foster its capitalization to improve Institutional Knowledge Building (IKB).
Since 2022, the PUI MEAL and Program Data Unit launched a capitalization cycle with all MEAL Cos to build on mission best practices documents to later develop a library of documents available for practitioners in the field.

2\. OBJECTIVES OF MEAL AND PROGRAM DATA MANAGEMENT CAPITALIZATION CONSULTANCY

2.1. GENERAL OBJECTIVE

Provide a one-month support on sorting out mission MEAL and Program Data Management best practices documents to feed the upcoming PUI MEAL and Program Data Management library.

2.2. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES

1\. Propose a folder tree organization in English for the PUI library of MEAL best practices documents;

2\. Pick up the best MEAL tools/SOPs for each type of documents among the mission MEAL best practices documents in English capitalized since 2022 and apply personal data protection filter to all selected documents;

3\. Pick up the best XLS forms from the centralized Kobo plan library for the different typologies of data collection;

4\. Complement the library with some missing documents from capitalization (lessons learnt workshop, examples of specific M&E surveys, specific evaluations) conducting some consultations with all MEAL Cos and HQ Program officers;

5\. Make several propositions of catchy names for this library;

6\. If time, propose a list of target MEAL-Program Data Management empty tools/templates and SOPs to design at PUI global level for the upcoming associated MEAL and Program Data toolbox;

3\. METHODOLOGY

The consultant will need to base his/her selection on the existing raw documentation capitalized since 2022 and make the folder tree and the selection coherent with PUI background and culture in terms of MEAL and Program Data Management.

4\. ORGANISATION OF THE CONSULTANCY

4.1. COLLABORATION WITH PUI MEMBERS

Firstly, the consultant will be required to collaborate regularly and closely with Deputy Head of Technical Department (STC) for the MEAL and Program Data Management Branch as well as the other technical focal in each mission (mainly MEAL Co). Furthermore, the consultant will meet with some program officers at headquarters.

4.2. LOGISTICAL, SECURITY AND ADMINISTRATIVE ARRANGEMENTS

- PUI will be able to provide a professional email address for the duration of the consultancy and the raw data on a PUI computer
- There is no need for the consultant to come to headquarters for this consultancy, he/she can work remotely

4.3. MONITORING ARRANGEMENTS

The consultant’s work and progress will be monitored through:

- Induction and recommendations to develop the consultancy action plan
- Weekly meetings with the Deputy Head of Technical Department for the MEAL and Program Data Management Branch at HQ.

4.4. DURATION OF THE CONSULTANCY

The consultancy is expected to start in December for a duration of 1 month.

5\. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

- Deliverable 1 – Folder tree in English for the library
- Deliverable 2 – Proposed names for the library
- Deliverable 3 – Selection of best practices documents in the proposed folder tree (and sub folders with “documents not selected”) including XLS forms
- Deliverable 4 – If time, list of target MEAL-Program Data Management empty tools/templates and SOPs to design at PUI global level

6\. BUDGET

The budget must be provided by the consultant as part of the financial proposal. The consultant must submit a budget covering a period of 1 month (fees/hourly rates…).

7\. APPLICATION

Interested parties must submit in English:

- A 1 pager narrative to explain your understanding of the consultancy objectives and deliverables
- A short action plan to carry out the work
- A financial proposal
- An up-to-date CV
- Proven expertise in MEAL and Program Data Management within the humanitarian sector (≥5 years).
- Proven experience in MEAL and Program Data Management strategy and tools/SOPs design
- Experience of working with international NGOs – with PUI being clearly an asset
- Fluency in English (spoken and written)
- References

Selection criteria :

- Overall quality of the 1 pager and action plan
- Past experiences and references
- Proposed budget

Comparative advantage:

• Experience with PUI as a MEAL Co

[TdR MEAL External Consultancy](https://www.coordinationsud.org/wp-content/uploads/2026_PUI_ToRs_HQ-Consultancy-MEAL-Program-Data-Management.pdf)

jobs.description:
**Job title:** MEAL Officer

**Location:** Syria /Aleppo/ Afrin

**Reports to:** MEAL Manager

**About AMAL Organization For Relief& Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established and registered in Turkey on 6/6/2014, to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war turned

**About the Job:**

A Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Officer manages information and reporting processes and products to ensure professional, high-quality communication in an organization's activities and results. A MEAL Officer also plays an important role in improving information management and data quality, and in strengthening knowledge sharing and learning across the organization.

MEAL Officers are also responsible for full-cycle monitoring and evaluation of programs, developing appropriate methodologies and tools to design evaluations.

**Duties and responsibilities:**

- Coordinate data collection and synthesize and analyze quantitative data from the field.
- Conduct regular field visits to the projects sites, and collect the relevant data according to the MEAL Plan.
- Update and add to the MEAL field guide as necessary.
- Synthesize and analyze M&E quantitative data received monthly
- Conduct need assessment, baseline survey, project review, end-line survey, and impact assessment of the relevant projects as per need and requirement.
- Assist in creating reports based on quantitative M&E data gathered
- Assist in creating M&E policies and procedures.
- Assist in preparing timely regular monthly, mid-year, and annual progress reports on all activities.
- Ensure that the M&E database is up to date with all relevant attachments.
- Responsible for the management of the M&E database, a compilation of monthly results reporting, analysis of raw data, and oversight of data quality checking.
- Responsible for the implementation of the project M&E plan and design of related monitoring tools.
- Conduct regular field visits to the projects sites, and collect the relevant data according to the MEAL Plan.

**Skills and qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree required, Master’s degree in statistics, demographics, public health, or international development preferred
- Minimum of five years of experience working in the field of monitoring and evaluation
- Proven success in designing, implementing, and operating M&E systems from project initiation to close out
- Experience in strategic planning and performance management, including indicator selection, target setting, reporting, database management, and developing M&E and performance monitoring plans
- Knowledge of the major evaluation methodologies (qualitative, quantitative, mixed method, and impact) and data collection and analysis methodologies
- Ability to manage critical relationships with diplomacy and tact and engage a wide range of stakeholders
- Excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Strong attention to detail, organizational. and time management skills
- Willingness and ability to travel
- Computer proficiency
- Experience in planning and managing surveys, developing and refining data collection tools, and with data quality assessments and oversight
- Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment, set priorities, and meet deadlines
- Ability to synthesize complex information and communicate it effectively to diverse audiences;
- Ability to design and implement efficient work flows and procedures

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so the maintaining equal opportunities and nondiscrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy. This policy underscores our dedication to safeguarding the well-being of our staff by promoting a workplace culture characterized by mutual respect and professionalism. The role holder plays a vital part in this commitment, ensuring a supportive atmosphere and contributing to the safeguarding of their colleagues through promoting positive employee relations.
