jobs.title: Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

In the MENAU region (Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, oPt, Iraq, Libya, and Yemen) IRC responds to displaced people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives.

**The IRC's MENA Early Childhood Development Portfolio**

The IRC's MENA Early Childhood Development (ECD) portfolio builds on over eight years of programming, starting with the Ahlan Simsim and Play to Learn initiatives, launched in 2018. These initiatives reached millions of children and caregivers with ECD services, generated a library of high-quality ECD content, and established a resource bank of proven program models. Partnerships with Ministries of Education, Health, and Social Development produced co-designed programs that are now embedded within government services across the region.

The portfolio today spans multiple grants and donors across the MENA region, with an overarching aim of supporting the youngest children and their caregivers — particularly those affected by crisis and conflict — with high-quality, scalable, and sustainable interventions. Interventions target children directly and through their caregivers and communities. The portfolio also strengthens the capacity of the ECD workforce — including teachers, multi-sector facilitators, and health workers — advances national systems and policy through advocacy efforts, and delivers innovative digital technology solutions. The IRC works alongside key public and private stakeholders across health, protection, education, and economic recovery and development to co-design and expand partner-led interventions. For more information on the IRC's ECD work in the region, visit: [https://www.rescue.org/ahlansimsim](https://www.rescue.org/ahlansimsim).

The MENA regional ECD team manages core regional grants, supports country programs on country-specific awards, and actively contributes to business development efforts to expand programming reach, deepen impact, and mobilize resources from a growing base of public and private donors. The team also supports country programs in program quality and fidelity, content development, research, learning and monitoring, policy, advocacy and communications, project and financial management, and digital technology solutions.

**Job Overview/ Summary:**

The Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager will be responsible to coordinate, design, manage, implement, and disseminate research and learning related to ECD in the MENA region, and support country teams to collect, store, analyze, validate, use, and disseminate research and learning internally and externally. He/she will work closely with IRC’s global team, MENA regional ECD team and country-based teams in support of quality evidence-building and actionable learning activities. This role also serves as a key coordination point between the IRC, its internal research teams and external research partners, ensuring alignment across technical design, implementation timelines, and evidence dissemination.

**Major Responsibilities:**

The Regional Senior Research and Learning Manager will lead and support a broad range of research and learning activities, including the following:

**Lead, Coordinate and Manage the Operationalization of the Research and Evaluation Agenda:**

- Lead and/or contribute to the design of the research agenda, in coordination with relevant IRC HQ, regional and country-program ECD and MEAL teams, and external stakeholders (such as donors and external evaluators).
- In collaboration with IRC’s relevant research teams, external evaluators and donors, support in Randomized Controlled Trials (RCT) preparation across countries, including support with path to scale planning, RCT design, timelines, data collection strategies, logistics, etc.
- In coordination with relevant IRC research, regional and country-program teams, external partners and donors, lead the planning, management, and implementation of research and evaluation studies, that utilize a range of methods and analytical strategies, including:
- Coordinate on study design, data management, budget/level-of-effort alignment, and quality assurance of research outputs.
- Ensure communication and harmonization between research activities and program implementation, including ensuring fidelity of research design implementation.
- Secure required approvals – IRC’s Institutional Review Board (IRB) and any local IRB or government approvals if needed.
- Ensure that research instruments are adapted and contextualized, including piloting of tools across languages and cultures.
- Coordinate programming of tools as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
- Conduct or support in enumerator recruitment and trainings, as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
- Oversee implementation of research work plans, ensuring that field data collection is accurate, standardized, complete, and timely.
- Lead and/or contribute with data cleaning and analysis, including both quantitative and qualitative analysis.
- Ensure compliance with IRC research standards and protocols, and implement best practices in research ethics, data protection, and data management throughout all stages of the research process.
- Support in and contribute to the write-up, quality assurance, and review of research products and peer-reviewed articles, as needed.
- Translate research results into user friendly-briefs, reports, Powerpoint presentations, and other products, for dissemination to non-research audiences.
- Serve as a key point of contact and coordination lead between the various IRC teams and external stakeholders (donors and external evaluators).

**Lead the Regional ECD Learning Agenda design and implementation:**

- Co-design and lead the implementation of the Regional ECD Learning Agenda and Learning and Reflection Cycle, including a range of learning studies and questions utilizing quantitative and qualitative methods.
- Provide support to country teams in the implementation of the learning agenda and learning questions, such as developing data collection tools, training, analysis and reporting.
- Support the collection, storage, analysis, use, and dissemination of learning across global, regional, and country avenues.
- Recruit consultants to support with the implementation of learning studies, as needed.
- Facilitate learning activities, including learning and reflection meetings, workshops, presentations, webinars, etc.
- Co-develop and/or input into learning products (including reports, briefs, blogs) and disseminate findings to influence practice and policy.
- Provide high-quality connections with IRC’s HQ to connect with broader organizational and Education sector learning, strategy and programs.
- Serve as a focal point for learning, providing strategic thinking and design to establish a culture of learning and viable learning products and opportunities.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position Reports to: Regional Research, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Lead, MENA Regional ECD Team
- Position directly supervises: N/A
- Indirect Reporting: N/A
- Other Internal and/or external contacts:
- Internal: IRC Research Teams, relevant award-management and leadership teams; Regional ECD Team, Country Program and MEAL Teams, Education Technical Unit within IRC, other IRC projects contributing to connected learning agendas.
- External: Partners including international, national and local entities, External Evaluators, Donors, Academic Institutions, consultants and service providers.

**Required Education, Skills and Competencies**

- University degree in public health, Public Administration, International Relief and Development, Statistics, Applied Statistics, Social Sciences, Education, Early Childhood Development or any relevant related field.
- At least four years of experience implementing mixed-method research or evaluation studies in emergency, humanitarian, or development settings.
- Experience conducting randomized impact evaluations (or randomized controlled trials) of development or humanitarian interventions.
- Experience coordinating research and evaluation activities across multiple institutional partners (e.g., research organizations, academic institutions, or external evaluators).
- Demonstrated experience managing large scale quantitative and qualitative data collection in the field.
- Experience analyzing qualitative data using Dedoose, nVivo or other qualitative data analysis software.
- Experience analyzing quantitative data using SPSS, Stata, or other statistical analysis packages.
- At least three years of experience in training and facilitation.
- Excellent writing and oral skills (in English and Arabic).
- Experience working in MENA Region.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills across a wide range, including clients, community members, government officials, academics, partners, donors, etc.
- Demonstrated experience communicating complex research results to non-research audiences, including program teams and policymakers.
- Strong ability to work independently, organize work, meet deadlines, prioritize work under pressure, proactively coordinate multiple tasks, and maintain attention to detail.
- Excellent knowledge of and experience with humanitarian guidelines and principles.

**Preferred Education, Skills and Competencies**

- Experience working on research or evaluation studies in education or ECD in low-resource environments.
- Experience publishing in peer-reviewed journals is a plus.
- Experience supporting the implementation of measurement and learning systems in complex programs.
- Master’s Degree in Public Health, Public Administration, International Relief and Development, Statistics, Applied Statistics, Social Sciences, Education, Early Childhood Development or any relevant related field is a plus.

**Working Environment:**

- Standard office working environment; partial remote work is possible.
- Travel required ~ 15%.
- The position may be based in Jordan or Lebanon.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: HR Admin Officer
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** HR Admin Officer

**Code:** SR-00-10283

**Duty station:** HQ Rome (hybrid)

**Starting date:** 01/01/2027

**Contract duration:** 36 months

**Reporting to:** HR Generalist

## **General context of the project**

INTERSOS is a humanitarian organisation founded in 1992 that operates on the front lines of crises. In the countries where it operates, INTERSOS intervenes to assist the most vulnerable populations affected by conflict, extreme poverty, and natural or man-made disasters. The organisation works in complex, hard-to-reach areas where humanitarian needs remain acute, and the humanitarian presence is often limited. In these contexts, INTERSOS focuses on providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to displaced populations and host communities, primarily in the sectors of Protection and Health & Nutrition.

INTERSOS’s operations are guided by its Charter of Values and the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence. Specifically, INTERSOS is an organisation that is borderless, impartial, independent, culturally sensitive, committed to leveraging local capacities, professional in its solidarity, and transparent. INTERSOS also adheres to the Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief.
The INTERSOS HR department operates globally through Recruitment, HR Admin, and Learning & Development units, complemented by Regional HR Coordinators. You will join an international team that is closely connected to field operations, where you will play a direct role in managing our international and headquarters staff.

## **General purpose of the position**

The HR Admin Officer will support the daily administrative functions of the HR administration unit, assisting the team with personnel administration for both HQ and site-based staff. Specifically, they will provide support in managing contracts and preparing documentation related to payroll processes, audits, and staff mobility.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks:**

**Contract Management and Onboarding**

- Support the team in preparing staff contracts in compliance with legal requirements, handling notifications to relevant hiring authorities (e.g., ANPAL), and managing the administration of contract amendments, extensions, resignations, and terminations.
- Enter and maintain personnel records in the company management system as part of the onboarding process for new hires.
- Manage the filing and archiving of contracts for international and HQ staff.
- Provide operational support for administrative procedures related to staff mobility.

**Personnel Administration, HQ Support, and Audit Support**

- Assist in gathering and preparing administrative documentation required for internal and external audits and financial reporting, in coordination with the admin team.
- Assist in the preparation of staff tax statements (\*Certificazioni Uniche\*).
- Assist in managing meal vouchers and tracking leave/vacation time.
- Support the administration of workplace safety-related procedures.

## **Required profile**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Economics, Law, Political Science, Labour Consultancy, or related fields.

**Professional experience**

- Brief experience (including internships or traineeships) in administration, HR management, or back-office roles is desirable.
- Junior profile (not above 29 years old)
- Work experience or an internship abroad—preferably with humanitarian organisations or in the third sector—represents a significant asset.

**Professional requirements**

- Excellent knowledge of key IT tools.
- Basic understanding of HR-related administrative processes.

**Languages**

- Italian: Native speaker or C2 level.
- English: Excellent written and spoken proficiency.
- French: Knowledge of the language is an asset.

**Personal requirements**

- Strong organisational and priority-setting skills.
- Aptitude for teamwork.
- High level of accuracy, confidentiality, and attention to detail in handling sensitive data.

jobs.title: Graphic Design & Layout Artist
jobs.description:
## **Project Overview**

The Project “**Enabling the Philippines to prepare its Second Biennial Transparency Report with a combined Third National Communication (BTR2/NC3) and Third Biennial Transparency Report (BTR3)**” aims to assist the Philippines in responding to the reporting requirements under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement to address climate change and its impacts and to take part in review processes that consider the information Parties provide.

Under this project, BTR2/NC3 and BTR3 reports will be prepared in close coordination with any other climate-related ongoing project and activity in the country, funded by the GEF and/or other donors.

The main objective of this project is to to support the Philippines prepare and submit to the UNFCCC the Second Biennial Transparency Report with a combined Third National Communication (BTR2/NC3) and Third Biennial Transparency Report (BTR3) all in compliance with the UNFCCC Convention and Paris Agreement’s reporting obligations.

## **Roles and Responsibilities**

1. Co-develop the visual identity, including the style guide and visual guidelines with the BTR2/NC3 Project Team

a. Propose a design concept and visual identity for BTR2/NC3 (colour palette, typography, publication template/masterpage, iconography, charts, graphs, tables, and at least three (3) cover designs) consistent with relevant CCC, FAO, GEF and OML Center branding and logo-use guidelines

b. Revise and finalize the design concept based on what is agreed with the Project Manager and lead authors
2. Produce the publication layout, including graphics, infographics, and data visualizations.

a. Infographics on key results, including the national GHG inventory by sector (Energy, IPPU, AFOLU/LULUCF, Waste), NDC progress tracking, mitigation and adaptation actions, and support needed and received

b. Diagrams and flowcharts explaining processes such as the MRV/transparency arrangements, institutional arrangements, and data flows

c. Maps, icons and illustrations for vulnerability, impacts and adaptation content

d. Gender-responsive and inclusive visuals, consistent with the project’s gender mainstreaming commitments as needed.
3. Develop the BTR2/NC3 as an interactive publication, with print version as needed

a. Interactive PDF versions of the main reports, with hyperlinked tables of contents, cross-references and page navigation

b.Prepare a print-ready version, complete with its packaged files based on the digital BTR2/NC3 document.
4. Quality checking and finalization

a. Quality check of laid-out outputs for readiness for printing, digital publication and submission to the UNFCCC

b. Ensure all figures, tables and annexes are consistent with the approved style guide and visual guidelines.

c. Prepare print-ready files (with print specifications) and optimized digital files with manageable file sizes.
5. Prepare all assets and images created for turnover

a. Turn over all source files (editable design files, fonts and image licenses, templates and raw graphics) in .indd and .ai complete with its package and/or embedded link to OML Center at project completion.

## **QUALIFICATION**

- Should have extensive experience in publication design in both digital and print
- Experience in reports publication (experience in similar climate change projects an advantage)
- Experience in visual storytelling and developing infographics based on technical information
- Knowledgeable in the use of InDesign (for layout), Illustrator (for vector images) and Photoshop (for raster images) or similar software for the respective graphics needs as itemized (use of generative AI highly discouraged).

jobs.title: Consultant: US Business Development and Fundraising
jobs.description:
At ATNi (Acess to Nutrition initiative) we're looking for a US Business Development and Fundraising Consultant to work with our team.

## **Organization and overall purpose**

ATNi (Access to Nutrition initiative) is a global nonprofit actively challenging the food industry, investors and policymakers to shape healthier food systems. We analyze and translate data into actionable insights, driving partnerships and innovations for market transformation so that all people have access to nutritious and sustainable food. ATNi is registered in the Netherlands with approximately 22 staff and consultants around the world. The majority of staff work from the Netherlands. For more information on ATNi, please visit our website [www.accesstonutrition.org](http://www.accesstonutrition.org/).

## **The role and candidate profile**

ATNi has been undergoing steady growth since 2021. Raising additional resources is required to deliver our [2023-2027 Strategy](https://accesstonutrition.org/news/why-access-to-nutrition-initiatives-new-strategy-aims-to-transform-markets-for-healthier-food/#:~:text=ATNi's%20Policy%20Platform-,Why%20Access%20to%20Nutrition%20Initiative's%20New%20Strategy,Transform%20Markets%20for%20Healthier%20Food&text=Building%20on%20ten%20years%20of,2027%29%20focused%20on%20transforming%20markets.) and our 2030 strategic goal to ensure at least 50% of global food sales are based on healthier and affordable options. We aim to raise resources equivalent to approximately 3.8-4M USD a year until 2029 (our current annual revenue is about 3M USD). In total, our objective is to raise approximately 18M USD total between mid-2026 and end 2029. Establishing new donor relationships in the USA is essential to reach these financial and strategic goals.

Establishing new donor relationships in the US remains essential to reach these financial and strategic goals — but the US funding landscape has changed fundamentally since this target was set. US assistance now flows increasingly through bilateral, multi-year, co-financed country agreements rather than direct NGO grants. Given this volatility, ATNi's US resource mobilization strategy — and this role — must pursue a more diversified funding mix across US government and quasi-governmental sources, private philanthropy, and blended finance. The financial targets above should be reviewed periodically against this shifting landscape.

Reporting to the Head of Business Development and working closely with the Executive Director and ATNi’s management team, the consultant will bring significant and successful resource mobilization experience working with US government institutions and philanthropies. S/he will also interact as needed with some ATNi’s US-based Board members. S/he will have strong partnership development and writing skills, familiarity with international programs and projects, and technical/programmatic understanding of nutrition, food systems transformation and global public health. S/he will have extensive experience successfully positioning for and responding to donor-funding (solicited and unsolicited). This is a part-time engagement at approximately 50% for an initial period of three months, with the possibility of extension.

This role offers a unique opportunity to have a substantial positive impact on a small but growing and influential global nonprofit.

## **Primary responsibilities**

Resource development leadership

•Serve as a senior ATNi representative in the US

•Support fundraising for ATNi's programmatic priorities in the US market, including MarketFit Nutrition and our sodium reduction work, by identifying and cultivating funders active in diet-related disease prevention, and positioning these workstreams within broader pitches to government, and philanthropic donors.

•Design and deliver a US fundraising outreach strategy and plan with identified targets for relevant US government and quasi-governmental funders and philanthropies who fund international work including in low- and middle-income countries. This should also include:

o Establish and maintain an active US-based donor mapping database for ATNi a targeted plan of outreach to potential partners who are already grantees/subcontractors in the US of relevant funders key performance metrics to inform donor revenue forecasting and improve win/loss performance

o Ongoing monitoring of US foreign assistance policy (State Department, USDA, Congress) to anticipate shifts that affect funding availability, given the volatility of the current environment

• Build ATNI’s network by leveraging ATNi’s new fiscal sponsorship arrangement with the [Myriad USA](https://myriadusa.org/)

• Network strategically and widely seeking out partnerships with organizations active in the food, nutrition, health and development finance space to broaden fundraising reach.

• Mentor ATNi’s fundraising team on proposal development processes and good practices, updating internal systems and tools as needed.

• Inform ATNi’s strategic direction based on evolving US funding priorities, identifying key areas for organizational growth and diversification of funding streams while ensuring alignment with ATNi’s mission and long-term goals.

Proposal and capture processes

•Develop, update and maintain compelling ‘pitch decks’ and cases for support tailored to government, philanthropic, and private-sector audiences

•Monitor and analyze trends in the donor landscape, with particular focus on the State Department's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy, USDA, and major US foundations funding nutrition and food systems, to inform short- and long-term strategic planning and positioning

•Pro-actively apply or respond to funding opportunities (i.e., calls for proposals, spontaneous proposals, foundation grant cycles, etc.)

•Lead the coordination of or support the submission of new concepts and proposals for US-based donors. Support other concepts and proposals as needed (e.g. for the EU)

•As needed, coordinate proposal development to ensure timely decision making with inputs from relevant technical experts

## **Qualifications**

- Minimum 8 years' experience in resource mobilization/business development for a global nonprofit, including a minimum of 3-5 years working with US government funding mechanisms and/or major US private foundations.
- Master’s degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Experience in public health, food systems, nutrition, health economics, health promotion or relevant field would be beneficial.
- Exceptional English writer/editor with a solid understanding of nutrition and public health and experience mobilizing resources for non-profit organizations.
- In-depth knowledge and existing network of institutions, partners and leaders working in global public health and nutrition, food systems, agriculture, water, health economics.
- Hands-on experience working with key US government and private funders and knowledge of different funding mechanisms (e.g., grants, contracts) of each.
- Proven track record coordinating and contributing to successful business development and proposal efforts that have secured substantial funding from US government, multilateral and/or private funders
- Ability to prioritize, assume responsibility for work, and follow through to completion.
- Flexible, self-starter and innovator, with ability to develop and implement new ideas independently and as a member of a team.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to exercise diplomacy and tact as demonstrated in previous roles that required communication with a broad and diverse set of partners.
- Ability to work independently but with strong accountability, driving projects effectively from conceptual stages to launch, and handling multiple and often competing deadlines.
- Ability and willingness to work under pressure with a positive attitude, as a part of a team.
- Demonstrable respect for all persons regardless of religion, ethnicity, class or gender, with a high comfort level working in a diverse environment with a demonstrated commitment to high professional ethical standards.
- Personal commitment to ATNi’s organization’s mission and goals and our values.

Candidate must be eligible to work in the USA.
