jobs.title: ICT Officer
jobs.description:
Plan International is an independent child rights and humanitarian organisation committed to children living a life free of poverty, violence and injustice. Plan actively unite children, communities and other people who share our mission to make positive lasting changes in children’s and young people’s lives. Plan support children to gain the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to claim their rights to a fulfilling life, today and in the future. Plan place a specific focus on girls and women, who are most often left behind. Plan have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years and are now active in more than 70 countries. Plan International Jordan is established in 2016 and has programmes in governorates in the centre, north and south regions as well as host communities and Azraq camp.

**Role PURPOSE**

The ICT Officer reports to the Head of Operations and Finance and is responsible for providing IT support to staff, and for maintaining the IT infrastructure of the office according to Plan's policies and procedures. The role supports the management of IT assets, networks, devices and servers, and implements ICT standards, security and policies within Plan Jordan.

**Dimensions of the Role**

The ICT Officer will be responsible for supporting and following on Operational ICT policies, goals, objectives and guidelines and for the ICT planning and implementation. Specifically, s/he will support the Head of Operations and Finance in leading an effective administration, procurement of IT assets , services and ICT Road Map and plans, supervise and/or implement the necessary administration, procurement & logistics processes to ensure the purchase and delivery of ICT supplies and capital equipment in line with the approved response budget.

The role encompasses a broad range of responsibilities, including the effective management and tracking of IT assets, maintenance of ICT infrastructure, and provision of timely technical support to staff to ensure smooth and efficient operations.

**Accountabilities**

**ICT Duties:**

1\. ICT Infrastructure and Systems Administration

- Administer, maintain, and support PIJO's ICT infrastructure, including servers, networks, storage systems, hardware, software, and related technology resources, ensuring reliable and efficient operations.
- Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Windows Server environments, including Active Directory (AD), DNS, DHCP, Group Policy (GPO), file services, print services, and user profiles.
- Manage and maintain virtualized server environments using Microsoft Hyper-V, including virtual machines, resource allocation, and system availability.
- Administer and maintain network infrastructure, including LAN, WAN, wireless networks, switches, access points, routers, and network connectivity.
- Configure, manage, and monitor network security appliances, including Cisco Meraki MX Firewall, security policies, traffic filtering, intrusion detection and prevention, and network access controls.
- Manage and troubleshoot VPN connectivity and remote access services, ensuring secure access to organizational resources in accordance with approved security policies.
- Monitor internet connectivity, network performance, bandwidth utilization, and ISP services, coordinating with telecommunications providers to resolve service interruptions.
- Administer and monitor wireless network infrastructure, including access point configuration, connectivity, coverage, and performance.
- Maintain and support CCTV systems, including cameras, recording devices, monitoring systems, and associated network connectivity.
- Monitor the performance, availability, and capacity of ICT infrastructure and recommend corrective or preventive actions to minimize service disruptions.
- Maintain and support ICT infrastructure across all Plan International Jordan locations, including field offices and camps, ensuring reliable network connectivity, system availability, and technical support.
- Conduct ICT infrastructure assessments for new offices, premises, and field locations, identifying connectivity, hardware, network, security, and system integration requirements to ensure operational readiness before staff deployment.

2\. Helpdesk and End-User Technical Support

- Manage and maintain an effective ICT helpdesk support process, ensuring that user requests, incidents, and technical issues are properly recorded, monitored, prioritized, and resolved.
- Provide first- and second-line technical support to employees and beneficiaries, where applicable, through onsite, remote, telephone, and other approved support channels.
- Install, configure, maintain, upgrade, and troubleshoot desktops, laptops, printers, scanners, mobile devices, and other ICT equipment.
- Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, operating system, network connectivity, email, login, user profile, and access permission issues.
- Provide support for Microsoft Windows operating systems, Microsoft Office applications, email clients, and other organizational software.
- Perform software installations, system configurations, hardware upgrades, operating system updates, and troubleshooting in accordance with organizational ICT standards.
- Coordinate laptop and equipment preparation, configuration, allocation, and delivery for new employees.
- Provide technical guidance and awareness sessions to employees on ICT systems, applications, cybersecurity, and appropriate technology usage.
- Maintain records of ICT incidents, support requests, troubleshooting activities, and recurring technical issues to identify improvement opportunities.

3.Cybersecurity, Backup and Business Continuity

- Implement and monitor ICT security measures, including firewalls, VPNs, endpoint protection, access controls, MFA, and security updates.
- Administer backup, storage, and recovery solutions, ensuring data integrity, availability, and business continuity.
- Monitor security alerts, vulnerabilities, and backup logs, and coordinate incident response and corrective actions.
- Support phishing awareness campaigns, security testing, and employee cybersecurity awareness initiatives.
- Document security incidents, vulnerabilities, corrective actions, and mitigation measures.
- Coordinate with regional and global ICT security teams to address security incidents, implement security requirements, and ensure compliance with organizational standards.
- Maintain backup schedules, recovery procedures, and disaster recovery documentation.

4.Microsoft 365, Cloud Services and Document Management

- Administer Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and related cloud applications.
- Manage user accounts, licenses, shared mailboxes, distribution groups, security groups, permissions, and email services.
- Administer SharePoint sites, document libraries, access permissions, and departmental file structures.
- Support digital document archiving, file migration, and SharePoint–OneDrive integration to improve document accessibility and promote paperless workflows.
- Manage and support Google Workspace, organizational domains, DNS records, hosting, and related digital platforms.
- Provide technical guidance and user support on Microsoft 365 applications, cloud services, and collaboration tools.

5\. ICT Projects, Digital Transformation and Strategic Planning

- Contribute to the development and implementation of annual ICT work plans, technology roadmaps, and initiatives aligned with organizational objectives and operational requirements.
- Plan and support ICT infrastructure upgrades, system migrations, technology deployments, and digital transformation projects.
- Coordinate the implementation, testing, and verification of new systems, Microsoft 365 services, data migrations, and other approved technology solutions while minimizing operational disruptions.
- Identify opportunities to improve ICT services, automate manual processes, enhance cybersecurity, and increase operational efficiency through appropriate digital solutions.
- Evaluate and test new technologies, applications, and equipment to ensure compatibility, security, and suitability before implementation.
- Provide technical advice and recommendations to management on ICT infrastructure, technology investments, system improvements, and operational risks.
- Coordinate with internal departments, regional and global ICT teams, and external service providers to ensure the successful implementation of ICT projects.
- Prepare periodic ICT reports covering infrastructure performance, service delivery, security, asset management, ongoing projects, and technology requirements.
- Provide technical training, guidance, and knowledge-sharing sessions to employees and ensure proper handover of ICT projects, systems, documentation, and ongoing activities

6\. ICT Procurement, Vendor Management and Documentation

- Provide technical input into ICT procurement processes, including preparing technical specifications, evaluating technical proposals, and recommending suitable hardware, software, and services.
- Coordinate with procurement and finance departments, vendors, suppliers, internet service providers, and maintenance companies to ensure the effective delivery and maintenance of ICT services and equipment.
- Follow up on service requests, warranties, software licenses, subscriptions, maintenance agreements, and service contracts.
- Verify the delivery, installation, configuration, and acceptance of ICT equipment and services against approved technical specifications.
- Maintain and regularly update ICT documentation, including network diagrams, server configurations, system inventories, asset records, user access records, and infrastructure documentation.
- Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) covering user onboarding and offboarding, account management, equipment allocation, software installation, backups, recovery, and incident reporting.
- Maintain secure records of system configurations, administrative access information, security procedures, and technical changes to support operational continuity and knowledge transfer.
- Serve as the local ICT focal point for technical coordination with regional and global ICT teams and external service providers.

**Other Duties (IT related)**

- Act as a focal point for Electronic signatures
- Follow all asset management procedures effectively at Plan’s offices for IT items.
- Responsible for Asset database (developing database and entry of data);
- Manage a consistent record of the Office's IT asset to ensure accuracy in the current location of all asset with the support of the asset’s custodian.
- responsible for certificates of completion of the receipt of assets and that all assets described in a classified card according to the procedures in Plan’s policies and asset assigning cards.
- Coordinate with the Admin and Logistics Officer for the annual physical asset inventory, ensuring IT asset records reconcile with physical counts and discrepancies are documented and resolved.

***Other Duties***

- Any other tasks requested by the line manager.

Child protection, gender equality and inclusion

- Ensures that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children, Young People and Programmes Participants and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant Implementation Standards and Guidelines as applicable to their area of responsibility. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan

**Key relationships**

**Internal:** Head of Operations and Finance (line manager). All departments within Plan Jordan.

**External:** Local Partner, Plan International GH, Plan International’s IT Vendors

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

**Qualifications and Job Skills**

- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
- 2–5 years of relevant experience in ICT operations, IT infrastructure, systems administration, and technical support.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Windows Server, Active Directory, Group Policy (GPO), DNS, and DHCP.
- Practical experience in computer hardware, software, network administration (LAN/WAN), switches, wireless networks, firewalls, VPNs, and cybersecurity.
- Knowledge of CCTV systems, IP cameras, video surveillance, and electronic access control systems (door access systems).
- Experience in implementing, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining ICT systems, servers, and business applications, including SAP.
- Knowledge of data backup, recovery, storage management, ICT asset management, and user access administration.
- Basic knowledge of website administration, WordPress, HTML, CSS.
- Good analytical, problem-solving, communication, negotiation, and teamwork skills.
- Good command of written and spoken English and Arabic.
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a dynamic work environment.
- Ability to work independently, take initiative, learn new technologies, and undertake additional responsibilities as required.

**​​Plan International’s Values in Practice**

**​We are open and accountable**

- ​Promotes a culture of openness and transparency, including with sponsors and donors.
- ​Holds self and others accountable to achieve the highest standards of integrity.
- ​Consistent and fair in the treatment of people.
- ​Open about mistakes and keen to learn from them.
- ​Accountable for ensuring we are a safe organisation for all children, girls & young people

**​We strive for lasting impact**

- ​Articulates a clear purpose for staff and sets high expectations.
- ​Creates a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenge and new ideas.
- ​Focuses resources to drive change and maximise long-term impact, responsive to changed priorities or crises.
- ​Evidence-based and evaluates effectiveness.

**​We work well together**

- ​Seeks constructive outcomes, listens to others, willing to compromise when appropriate.
- ​Builds constructive relationships across Plan International to support our shared goals.
- ​Develops trusting and ‘win-win’ relationships with funders, partners and communities.
- ​Engages and works well with others outside the organization to build a better world for girls and all children.

**​We are inclusive and empowering**

- ​We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential
- ​We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge equality in our programs and our workplace
- ​We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives. ​

**Physical Environment**

Typical office environment

**Level of contact with children**

Low contact: No contact or very low frequency of interaction

**ROLE PROFILE**

**Type of Role:** Fixed-Term

**Contract Duration:** 6 months fixed term contract, renewable subject to the availability of funds and satisfactory performance.

**Reports to:** Head of Operations and Finance

**Location:** Amman, Jordan

**Grade:** Level 13

*Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply. Plan International operates an equal opportunities policy and actively encourages diversity, welcoming applications from all areas of the international community.*

*Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early.*

*Please note that only applications and CVs written in English will be accepted.*

*A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Child Safeguarding Policy.*

jobs.title: Operations Manager, Korea
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW/SUMMARY:**

The Operations Manager who will play a cross-functional Operations role encompassing the functions of Supply Chain (SC), Safety & Security (S&S), Facilities Management (FM), and Information Technology (IT) infrastructure for the IRC **Korea, Seoul** Office. The job holder will serve as the primary focal point for the HQ-based Senior Director of Business Operations, and the primary liaison for functional staff supporting the Korea office, including the Regional Supply Chain Director (RSCD), Regional S&S Director, Regional IT Director and Facilities Management. This position is expected to contribute to setting strategic direction and operational problem-solving through the areas of professional expertise. This position reports directly to the Head of Finance & Support Functions. Read more about the IRC here: [https://www.rescue.or.kr](https://www.rescue.or.kr/)

**KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Supply Chain (40%)**

- Manage all procurement for IRC in compliance to IRC and donor policy and procedures
- Maintain complete procurement files on docutrail (digital) and hard copy files.
- Lead on RFQ and tender processes.
- Collaborate with other functions to ensure procurement plans are in place to enable strategic and efficient procurement.
- Lead on market assessment to ensure contextual awareness of supplier capacity and collect market intelligence.
- Liaise with Finance to ensure suppliers are paid in time.
- Provide training for staff on Supply Chain policy and procedures.

**Integra System (30%)**

- Be the subject matter expert (SME) for supply chain and provide training to staff when required.
- Ensure all procurement is done through Integra system.
- Work with regional Integra Advisor to resolve system issues in timely manner.
- Lead on monthly, quarterly and annual period Supply Chain period close activities.

**Safety and Security (10%)**

- Serve as the office’s primary focal point for day-to-day S&S matters.
- Coordinate immediate incident management, including filing police reports.
- Reporting of S&S incidents involving covered persons in accordance with established IRC protocols.
- Coordinates all the office safety and security related work procedures and files compliance reports to the central S&S QH function advises HQ External Relations on security regarding security incidents.
- Develop office-specific S&S onboarding materials, ensuring the provision of S&S briefings to new staff and covered persons.
- Coordinate a minimum of one emergency evacuation exercise at the office or program site level per year and other appropriate trainings, as advised by Security Risk Assessment findings.

**Information Technology (IT)(10%)**

- Serve as the office’s primary focal point for IT and communications infrastructure, hardware, and software matters.
- Coordinates with the Regional IT unit all procedures and steps regarding IT.
- Educate staff about IT support resources, including appropriate channels for incident reporting.
- Work with regional and HQ IT teams to address any internet or telecommunications service disruptions, liaising with local internet and telecommunications service providers.

**Facility Management(10%)**

- Manage office and equipment leases, coordinate repairs and improvements with property managers as needed.
- Coordinate the allocation of workspaces and support related employee lifecycle needs such as building access.
- Coordinates with Global Real Estate & Working Solutions all facility management activities.
- Support the smooth functioning of office infrastructure, including communications equipment and service.
- Assist with planning and coordinating office events and meetings.
- Other tasks as requested in line with the scope of responsibilities.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Sr. Manager, HR & Supporting functions
- **In coordination with**: Regional Supply Chain, Regional IT, Regional Security, Regional Integra

**Internal and/or external contacts:**

- **Internal:** Global Supply Chain Director (GSCD), S&S Director (SSD), Regional IT Director (RITD) and Facilities Managements.
- **External:** Vendors, local police, fire representatives, facility owners/managers, etc.

**Job Requirements:**

- University Degree in related fields
- Minimum 3 years experience in procurement.
- Clean record.
- Proficiency in spoken and written Korean and English,
- Diligent with an excellent sense of judgment.
- Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills.
- Ability to work simultaneously on multiple tasks.
- Willingness and ability to work effectively with a wide variety of people.
- Be part of a team and coordinate with project personnel.
- Excellent digital literacy, especially working with spreadsheets (Excel).
- Knowledge/experience in ERP systems desirable.

**Disclaimer Clause:** This job description is not an extensive list of the skills, effort, duties and responsibilities associated with position.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Human Resources Manager
jobs.description:
**Location**: Damascus

**Job summary**

The Human Resources Manager is responsible for leading and managing the Association’s overall Human Resources function through developing HR strategies, policies, and organizational plans, and overseeing the implementation of all HR operations to ensure alignment with the Association’s needs and enhance institutional performance. The role also ensures compliance with applicable legislation, approved policies, and donor requirements, while leading the HR team and developing its systems and procedures to achieve organizational objectives.

**Qualifications and education requirements**:

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Human Resources Management, or an equivalent field.

**Required Skills and Experience**:

- Leadership, guidance, and delegation
- Strategic planning
- Effective communication
- Priority setting and time management
- Negotiation and problem-solving
- Strategic decision-making
- Interpersonal and presentation skills
- Ability to work remotely
- Team motivation
- Resource and budget management
- Analytical and critical thinking
- Report preparation and writing
- Computer proficiency, including:
- Microsoft Outlook
- Microsoft Teams
- Microsoft Word
- Microsoft Excel
- Microsoft PowerPoint
- Microsoft OneDrive

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

- Participate with senior management in defining organizational objectives related to Human Resources, contribute to the development of the Association’s overall strategy, and lead the development, review, and improvement of HR strategies, policies, and objectives. Participate in organizational decision-making within the scope of assigned responsibilities and authority.
- Lead the review and development of the Association’s organizational structure in coordination with relevant departments. Analyze organizational needs and provide recommendations regarding the establishment, modification, or abolition of organizational units and administrative reporting lines, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and the effective distribution of responsibilities and authorities. Submit proposals to senior management for approval.
- Prepare presentations and reports reflecting the activities and achievements of the HR Department internally and externally.
- Represent the HR Department as its primary focal point before donors, partners, and relevant external stakeholders on all HR-related matters, providing necessary clarifications and information within the scope of assigned authority.
- Develop the HR Department’s annual operational plan and budget in alignment with the Association’s vision and objectives. Monitor implementation, periodically assess progress, and take necessary corrective actions.
- Establish, develop, and review HR operational procedures to ensure that approved policies are translated into clear and effective working mechanisms that meet the Association’s needs and donor requirements.
- Lead and manage the HR team by providing technical and administrative guidance and support. Oversee the allocation of tasks and responsibilities, delegate appropriate authority based on priorities and capabilities, monitor performance and achievements, and motivate and develop team members to ensure the efficient and effective achievement of departmental objectives.
- Lead workforce planning across the Association in coordination with relevant departments by analyzing current and future staffing needs in terms of positions, headcount, and competencies. Develop and review the workforce plan and budget to ensure alignment with operational priorities and available financial resources.
- Lead and follow up on addressing departments’ HR needs by assessing opportunities to fill vacancies and staffing gaps through internal resources, including transfers and redistribution, or external recruitment when necessary, in accordance with the approved workforce plan, budgets, and relevant policies and procedures.
- Oversee, review, and approve recruitment processes within the scope of assigned authority, ensuring compliance with recruitment policies and procedures, the workforce plan, and approved budgets, and verifying that all required approvals are obtained before completing hiring procedures.
- Serve as a focal point between senior management and employees on HR-related matters by following up on employee inquiries, feedback, and employment-related concerns, coordinating with relevant departments to address them, and escalating matters requiring senior management intervention or decisions, thereby strengthening organizational communication and facilitating appropriate solutions.
- Oversee personnel administration processes, including leave management, transfers, promotions, retirement, salary increments, allowances, disciplinary actions, grievances, complaints, termination of employment, and other related matters.
- Ensure that employee files are complete, updated, and securely maintained, and verify their compliance with internal policies and procedures and applicable labor legislation in coordination with the Legal Department. Follow up on addressing any deficiencies or cases of non-compliance.
- Follow up on employee inquiries and complaints and ensure they are addressed in accordance with approved procedures. Participate in investigation committees related to employment matters and oversee the follow-up of grievances and completion of related procedures in accordance with approved policies and regulations.
- Oversee payroll preparation and review the integrity of payroll procedures, ensuring the proper application of approved policies and procedures and the accuracy of employee data, entitlements, and deductions, in coordination with the Finance Department. Ensure that all required reviews and approvals are completed before disbursement.
- Develop the performance appraisal policy, system, and implementation plan to ensure fairness, transparency, and alignment with the Association’s objectives.
- Approve the sharing of performance appraisal results with senior management, ensuring the confidentiality and sensitivity of information and preventing conflicts of interest in handling appraisal outcomes.
- Manage matters arising from performance appraisal results, including grievances and corrective actions. Link appraisal outcomes to promotions, salary increments, and rewards, while following up on the implementation of performance improvement plans.
- Analyze training needs in coordination with relevant departments.
- Develop training plans within the approved budget to ensure that organizational needs are met.
- Coordinate with supporting entities and partners to implement training programs.
- Oversee the evaluation of training program effectiveness and measure their impact on employee performance and their responsiveness to training and organizational needs. Analyze evaluation results and use them to improve future training plans and programs.
- Coordinate with the Digital Transformation Unit to follow up on the development of the ERP system in relation to HR operations. Identify functional requirements and review and approve proposed modifications to ensure that the system aligns with approved procedures, policies, and operational needs, in coordination with relevant departments within the Association.
- Attend regular meetings with the direct supervisor, subordinates, and relevant colleagues to discuss and review the latest updates.

**Protection Policy:**

Ataa Association considers any type of child abuse unacceptable, as it recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. Ataa Association confirms that it is committed to ensuring a safe environment for children and takes a strict stance against any type of child abuse and exploitation.

**Discrimination, Abuse, and Harassment Policy:**

Ataa Association provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, or harassment (sexual or otherwise) based on race, religion, origin, age, marital status, nationality, or disability. , or the military situation.

jobs.title: Gender Officer
jobs.description:
**The Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund**

**About Us**

AECF is a leading African-based development organization that leverages the power of the private sector to address systemic issues of rural poverty and employment across the continent. We find and fund innovative, game changing commercial businesses in the agribusiness and renewable energy sectors that transform the lives of low-income households. By catalyzing funding, we help companies surface and commercialize new ideas, business models, and technologies that increase agricultural productivity, expand energy access, and alleviate poverty, particularly where these efforts impact women and young people. AECF works in frontier markets, fragile contexts, and high-risk countries where few mainstream financing institutions go. We back bold enterprises to tackle climate risk, expand opportunity for women and youth, and build resilience in fragile contexts so rural and marginalized communities can rise out of poverty

Since 2008, we have deployed over US$290 million, leveraged $916 million in additional capital, provided funding to 698 businesses in 27 countries – impacting 36 million people.

**About the Programme**

AECF is implementing Investing in Women’s Entrepreneurship for a Greener Economy in Benin and Burkina Faso, a six-year gender equality and economic inclusion programme funded by Global Affairs Canada. The programme provides investment capital and technical assistance to women-owned and women-led enterprises, financial institutions, cooperatives and associations operating in climate-positive sectors. It also works with women’s rights organisations and other local actors to address structural barriers, strengthen women’s agency and advance policy advocacy and social norm change at community and national levels.

**About the Role**

This role supports implementation of AECF’s current Gender Lens Investing Strategy through the Investing in Women Benin and Burkina Faso programme (IFEV-Benin and Burkina Faso). The role will lead and coordinate gender-responsive activities, help the programme achieve its gender equality and women’s economic empowerment targets, and ensure that gender considerations are integrated across investment, technical assistance, advocacy, learning and results measurement.

The successful candidate will work closely with women entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises, agricultural cooperatives and farmer associations, financial institutions, women’s rights organisations, gender champions and other programme partners.

The incumbent will be based in Burkina Faso. This role will report to the Programme Manager, Benin/ Burkina Faso.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of gender equality and women’s economic empowerment activities across the programme, in accordance with the programme management framework, approved workplans, budget and results framework.
- Assess the gender capacity of programme investees and provide tailored technical assistance that enables enterprises, cooperatives and micro-finance institutions to adopt gender-responsive business practices, inclusive workplace policies, climate-smart solutions and products or services that better meet women’s needs.
- Design of gender tools, and guides for portfolio companies in ensuring inclusive climate-smart practices and policies.
- Design and supervise the delivery of women empowerment and norm-shifting activities by women’s rights organizations, and other local community-advocacy groups.
- Strengthen the capacity of gender champions to influence formal and traditional institutions, promote women’s voice and decision-making, and advocate for women’s social and economic empowerment in target communities in Burkina Faso.
- Work with the programme and impact teams to monitor gender equality and women’s economic empowerment indicators, analyse sex-disaggregated and other relevant data, and document outcomes, lessons, case studies and participant stories.
- Deliver quality programme reports outlining gender activities, insights and impact created during donor reporting cycles.
- Lead in the development of evidence-based policy briefs, advocacy frameworks and other materials that champion women’s empowerment in Burkina Faso, together with the women rights organizations.
- Support the larger IFEV-Burkina Faso programme team on gender integration across the investment process.
- Build a network of gender champions, allies and actors that can collaborate with the IFEV-Burkina Faso programme to advance gender equality in Burkina Faso.
- Support the development of knowledge products and organize knowledge sharing events
- Contribute actively to AECF’s Gender Department by sharing programme learning, supporting the development of institutional tools and approaches, and contributing to cross-programme gender equality priorities.

**Suitable candidates should possess:**

- A bachelor’s degree in Gender Economics, Gender Studies, Development Studies, Economics, Development Finance, or other relevant fields of study.
- A minimum of five (5) years of post-training experience in one or more of the following areas: gender economics, social entrepreneurship, impact investing, management consulting, private sector development, renewable energy. agribusiness, SME finance, rural financial services and/or renewable energy and adaptation to combat climate change.
- Hands-on experience in the agribusiness sector is preferred.
- A strong understanding of climate-smart agriculture and solutions.
- Previous experience working with women rights and gender advocacy organizations is strongly preferred.
- Strong experience/ interest in the international development field.
- Experience working in an international team and proven ability to deliver in a complex environment with multiple, divergent stakeholder interests.
- Be fluent in English and French.

jobs.title: Head of Programmes CARE Ukraine
jobs.description:
## **Is this you?**

**Contract Start Date**: early 2027, no later than 1 March, 2027
**Contract Duration:** 1 year
**Duty Station:** Kyiv (Ukraine)

As a member of the Senior Management Team, reporting directly to the Country Director, the Head of Programmes leads the development and implementation of high-quality programmes in Ukraine, ensuring delivery against scope, time and budget, and overseeing quality management and impact across the portfolio. The role line-manages the Programme Implementation Lead, Technical Advisors and Coordinators, and MEAL Coordinator, while ensuring close cross-departmental coordination. It places particular emphasis on programme quality and strengthening partners’ technical capacities in relevant sectors. Working closely with the Country Director, Programme Development Lead, Partnership Coordinator, Advocacy Advisor and department heads, the Head of Programmes contributes to strategic direction, programme implementation and partnership development.

## **Your mission**

## Overall Programme Implementation and Quality

- Provide inclusive and cohesive leadership to CARE Ukraine’s programme teams, ensuring coordinated, high-quality implementation in line with the Country Strategy.
- Maintain a strong understanding of Ukraine’s social, political and economic context, initiating assessments to identify emerging needs and opportunities for programme expansion.
- Ensure projects are delivered on scope, time and budget, with day-to-day oversight delegated to the Program Implementation Lead and technical guidance provided by relevant teams.
- Regularly review programme priorities against the Country Strategy, adapting them based on contextual changes, evidence, learning and priorities identified with partners.
- Ensure effective coordination between programme implementation, technical teams, MEAL and Program Development to address challenges, strengthen cross-sector integration and inform new initiatives.
- Oversee strategic programmes and initiatives, ensuring their contribution to CARE Ukraine’s long-term objectives.
- Mainstream gender equality, protection and inclusion across all programmes, ensuring consistent application of CARE’s programme quality standards.
- Lead regular programme review meetings covering progress, quality, risks and monitoring findings, ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
- Resolve operational bottlenecks between the Programme Department and other Country and Area Office departments.

## Oversight and Management of Programme Implementation and Budget

- In collaboration with the SMT, define and oversee an effective, efficient and sustainable programme implementation model, clarifying the roles of CARE and its partners and ensuring appropriate SOPs and systems are in place.
- Support the Partnership Coordinator in overseeing partner due diligence, capacity development plans and partnership agreements, ensuring compliance with CARE requirements, including PSEA.
- Ensure effective use and follow-up of project management tools, including Detailed Implementation Plans, MEAL Plans and monitoring reports, through the Program Implementation Lead and MEAL Coordinator.
- Ensure programmes are responsive to communities, particularly women and girls, and comply with CARE’s principles, values, strategic plans and CI procedures.
- Act as overall budget holder for all programmes, delegating day-to-day budget management to the Program Implementation Lead while retaining accountability for expenditure and donor compliance.
- Oversee financial forecasting, expenditure monitoring and corrective actions, ensuring budget risks and variances are addressed and resources are aligned with programme priorities, in coordination with Finance and Operations.
- Provide direction on significant budget adjustments and resource allocation, and directly oversee specific grants where required.

## Programme Quality, Technical Support and Learning

- Maintain and adapt CARE Ukraine’s programme quality framework in line with CARE International and humanitarian standards, including the Core Humanitarian Standard.
- Guide technical leads in ensuring compliance with minimum technical standards and consistent application of appropriate tools, guidelines and SOPs, providing the necessary support to Programme Managers and partners.
- Promote coherent and integrated technical approaches across sectors, particularly regarding gender equality, protection and inclusion.
- Lead regular programme quality reviews with technical teams, MEAL and the Program Implementation Lead, ensuring gaps, risks and improvement actions are identified and addressed.
- Oversee MEAL and information management systems through the MEAL Coordinator, ensuring reliable and timely evidence on programme quality and outcomes and addressing significant system and capacity gaps.
- Set priorities for needs assessments, evaluations, external monitoring and research, ensuring their quality and relevance to programme effectiveness and changing needs.
- Lead the development of a research and learning agenda with MEAL and technical teams, ensuring evidence, implementation experience and good practices inform technical approaches and programme adaptation.
- Ensure learning and recommendations are shared with CARE teams and partners, translated into improvements and reflected in programme strategy.
- Oversee CARE Ukraine’s accountability mechanism, ensuring community feedback informs programme reviews and adaptations in line with CARE standards.
- Ensure partner capacity strengthening addresses identified quality gaps and its effectiveness is regularly reviewed with technical leads and the Partnership Unit.

## Business Development

- Support the Country Director in developing and adapting the funding strategy, diversifying donor engagement in line with CARE Ukraine’s Country Strategy.
- Coordinate technical inputs to new programmes, proposals and reports with the Program Development Lead, Program Implementation Lead, technical teams and MEAL Coordinator, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and quality standards.
- Ensure programme design builds on contextual analysis, monitoring findings, lessons learned and priorities identified with communities and partners.
- Promote the meaningful participation of partners and communities in programme design, including the development of logical frameworks, activities and budgets, ensuring proposals address identified needs and include appropriate MEAL components and resources.

## Representation and Networking

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with strategic and implementing partners and peer organisations.
- Maintain strong links across CARE International and its membership to mobilise technical expertise and resources in support of the Country Strategy.
- Engage with UN agencies, humanitarian clusters and sector working groups to inform strategic priorities and operational planning, share programme evidence and learning, and fulfil CARE’s coordination commitments, including co-leadership responsibilities.
- Provide programme evidence and technical input to advocacy and communications strategies, working closely with the Advocacy Advisor and Communications Coordinator to promote the visibility and uptake of programme learning.

## Team Management and Coordination

- Manage the performance and development of direct reports in line with CARE policies, providing coaching, mentoring and training to strengthen leadership and team effectiveness.
- Oversee recruitment, training and promotion of programme staff, ensuring that key functions are adequately staffed.
- Foster a collaborative and respectful team environment, promoting staff resilience and well-being in challenging contexts.
- Identify staff capacity development needs in collaboration with Human Resources.
- Supervise managers and technical leads, ensuring coordinated implementation of workplans and budgets.
- Lead safeguarding prevention and response across CARE Ukraine’s workplaces, programmes and communities, ensuring compliance with CARE standards and policies on PSEA-CP, Gender Equality and CARE Performance Standards, in coordination with the CARE DE Safeguarding Focal Point and CARE Ukraine HR Manager.

## **Your profile**

**Essential**
**Experience and Technical Expertise**

- At least 7 years’ experience in humanitarian and/or development work with national or international NGOs, including 5 years in senior management roles and significant field operations experience.
- At least 2 years’ experience living and working in an emergency or conflict setting.
- Master’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences or a relevant discipline.
- Good understanding of at least one of CARE’s key programme sectors (Protection, WASH/Shelter, SRH or Livelihoods).
- Strong knowledge of international humanitarian and development systems, institutions and donors.
- Proven project management skills, including knowledge of accountability frameworks and substantial experience in financial and budgetary management.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender equality and gender-transformative programming.
- Sound understanding of MEAL systems and experience using data, evidence and learning to assess programme quality, adapt implementation and inform programme design.
- Experience in partnership-based approaches, civil society development and strengthening the capacity of local partner organisations.

**Leadership and Management Skills**

- Proven ability to lead, motivate and develop teams through coaching, mentoring and capacity building, including cross-functional teams.
- Strong results orientation, with the ability to challenge existing approaches and drive improvements.
- Excellent analytical and strategic thinking skills, including the ability to assess information, evaluate options and plan effectively.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, negotiation and influencing skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Ability and willingness to work flexible hours and operate in environments with security restrictions.
- Strong commitment to CARE’s mission, values and principles.
- High levels of political and cultural sensitivity, patience, tact and diplomacy.
- Strong sense of responsibility, integrity and trustworthiness.

**Desirable**

- Significant experience designing and supporting partner-led programmes.
- Strong and up-to-date knowledge of the humanitarian context in Ukraine.
- Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or other relevant regional languages.
- Experience in training and capacity development.
- Proven representation and networking skills, including the ability to represent CARE effectively in external forums.

## **Why us?**

CARE Ukraine is a country office which comes under the management of CARE Germany. It has been operating in Ukraine since March 2022.

CARE prioritizes a locally led response and is partnering primarily with Civil-Society Organizations (CSOs), National NGOs, local authorities, and when needed, INGOs with a longstanding presence in the country and access to hard-to-reach areas. CARE Ukraine deliberately and strategically prioritizes partnerships with local and national Women Led and Women Rights organizations (WLO’s/ WRO’s), in accordance with Gender in Emergencies (GiE) principles.

CARE Ukraine’s FY25 portfolio was approx. EUR 13 million, funded by GFFO/ BMZ, ECHO, DANIDA, Czech MOFA, ADA (Austrian Development Agency), AFD (Agence Francaise de Developpement), LDS (Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints) and others. We implement primarily humanitarian programs, in the protection/ GBV, SRH, integrated humanitarian response and WASH/ shelter sectors. Some 10-15% of our programs are recovery/ response, primarily in livelihoods, WASH and womens empowerment sectors. The focus of most programming is the frontline oblasts of Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, and Dnipropetrovsk oblast. We also have some programming in Odesa. The country office is in Kyiv, with a support office in Lviv and field offices in Dnipro and Kharkiv. We plan to phase out the Lviv support office in the second half of 2026.

CARE Ukraine currently partners with 12 local/national organizations, almost all of which are WLO’s/WRO’s. We channel some 80% of our funding through local/national partners. Through the activities that have been implemented so far, CARE Ukraine has been able to reach over 750,000 people, including IDPs and affected populations in hard-to-reach areas.

## **General information**

CARE values equal opportunities and diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.

**Accountability within CARE**
A commitment to CARE values and CARE’s integrity framework is critical to working with CARE. Any candidate offered a job with CARE will be expected to adhere to the following key areas of accountability:
\- Comply with CARE’s policies and procedures with respect to safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, confidentiality, do no harm principles and unacceptable behavior protocols.
\- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.
\- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior of a CARE staff or partner.

**Safeguarding**
Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with CARE as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that CARE shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Gender equality**
CARE is committed to meeting the standards of the CARE International Gender Policy (2019). Through this policy, CARE seeks to promote the equal realization of dignity and human rights for girls, women, boys and men in all diversities, and the elimination of poverty and injustice. Specifically, this policy seeks to improve the explicit incorporation of gender in programmatic and organizational practices.

## **Our offer**

- Competitive salary
- Housing allowance
- Risk allowance
- Relocation package
- Vacation according to the country office policies, plus additional days off on public holidays
- Generous R&R policy
- 24/7 group accident insurance
- Health insurance
- Coverage of relevant training and development opportunities

We are looking for highly motivated team members who identify with CARE’s goals and values. We offer a varied role with numerous employee benefits within a supportive, international team.

## **About us**

**About CARE Germany**
Founded in 1980 and based in Bonn, CARE Germany is a member of the CARE International confederation—a global humanitarian network dedicated to fighting poverty and delivering life-saving aid in times of crisis. We work with communities to promote sustainable development, gender equality, and resilience, addressing the world’s most pressing challenges from climate change to conflict-driven displacement.
At CARE Germany, our staff are the cornerstone of our humanitarian efforts. Committed to the principles of CARE International and working tirelessly to uplift disadvantaged communities worldwide. Whether based in our headquarters or in our Country Offices in the Balkans, Ukraine, Iraq, or Libya, each team member plays a vital role in delivering aid, supporting long-term recovery, and advocating for those most in need. Regardless of their role, all staff contribute to a collective mission—one rooted in solidarity, compassion, and impactful action.

jobs.title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Flying Manager - Nigeria - M/F
jobs.description:
**THE ALIMA ASSOCIATION**

**ALIMA’S ETHOS:** *ALIMA’s purpose is to save lives and provide care for the most vulnerable populations, without any discrimination based on identity, religion or politics, through actions based on proximity, innovation, and the alliance of organizations and individuals. We act with humanity and impartiality in accordance with universal medical ethics. To gain access to patients, we undertake to act in a neutral and independent manner.*

**Our CHARTER defines the VALUES and PRINCIPLES of our action:**

1. Patient First – Patient centered medical care
2. Revolutionizing humanitarian medicine through research
3. Responsibility and freedom: encourage decision-making by those closest to patients
4. Commitment to a dynamic of continuous quality improvement
5. Creating a climate of trust among colleagues
6. Collective intelligence
7. Environmental liability

**CARING - INNOVATING - TOGETHER:**

Since its creation in 2009, ALIMA has treated more than 13 million patients and today deploys its operations in 15 countries. In 2023, ALIMA cared for 2.8 million patients, including over a million children under the age of 5, received 157,393 people for mental health consultations, assisted 67,617 births, carried out 64 projects in 14 countries. Whenever possible, we work in partnership with local NGOs to ensure that our patients benefit from the best and most relevant expertise wherever it is, whether within their own country or in the rest of the world. In addition, to improve the humanitarian response, we are carrying out operational and clinical research projects, particularly in the field of the fight against malnutrition and viral hemorrhagic fevers.

**ALIMA’S TEAM:** More than 2000 people currently work for ALIMA. The field teams, as close as possible to the patients, receive their support from the coordination teams generally based in the capitals of the countries of intervention. These receive support from the 4 desk teams and the emergency and opening service team based at the operational headquarters in Dakar, Senegal. The Paris and New York teams are actively working on fundraising as well as representing ALIMA. The rest of the ALIMA Galaxy includes individuals and partner teams who work on behalf of other organizations such as medical NGOs BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, research organizations PACCI, INSERM, Universities of Bordeaux or Copenhagen, the NGO Solidarités International and many others.

**COUNTRIES WHERE WE WORK IN 2021:** Mali, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Democratic Republic of Congo, Cameroon, Guinea, South Sudan, Mauritania, Senegal, Sudan, Ethiopia and Haiti.

**THE WORK WE DO** covers: Primary and Secondary Health Care, with a main focus on children and women - including treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition, maternal health, mental health, response to epidemics (Ebola, Cholera, Measles, Dengue, Lassa Fever), surgery, displaced populations, and gender based violence, Covid 19.

**ALIMA IN NIGERIA** : ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) has been active in Nigeria since 2016, with interventions guided by a regional strategy addressing health and nutrition emergencies, maternal-infant care, mental health, epidemic response alongside operational research to enhance health outcomes for vulnerable populations—particularly internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities.

The organization operates across several states: North-East: Borno (MMC and Jere LGAs) and Yobe (Bade, Yusufari, Nguru and Karasuwa LGAs) North-West: Katsina (Kaita, Batagarawa, Batsari and Katsina LGAs) , South-West: Ondo (Owo LGA).

**PROTECTION OF BENEFICIARIES AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS**

Level 3: As part of his/her duties, the incumbent will visit programs and come into contact with children and/or vulnerable adults. Therefore, a criminal record check or a certificate of good character will be required. In situations where a criminal record check or character reference is not possible, a declaration of honor will be requested.

**FUNCTIONAL AND HIERARCHICAL LINKS**

- He/she reports to the Medical Coordinator (line manager), and to the Mental Health referent at HQ (technical manager).
- He/she manages the mental health team
- He/she works in close collaboration with the coordinators (medical, logistics and projects).

**MAIN MISSION**

The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Activity Flying Manager (MHPSS) is responsible for the mental health strategy and the implementation of the psycho-social support for patients, their families, the community and the teams. He/she ensures the functioning of the mental health pole on the Nigeria projects.

1. **Implementation of ALIMA programs**

- Contribute to Implement and evolve the mental health care strategy, care circuit and referral in each intervention site;
- Ensures the implementation and monitoring of psychological support for beneficiaries in the various projects, patients or isolated people and families
- Organize the mental health department in collaboration with the Mental Health project teams, Medical coordination and HQ.
- Ensures and follow the psychological support for the team in the fields and in the mission
- Supervise the organization of the psychological first aid sessions for patients and victims;
- Supervise and sharing time of practices on specific situations
- Ensures the effectiveness of mental health and psychosocial support activities in accordance with the defined action plan and according to the minimum package of mental health activities vs. the complete package, with a focus on psychological first aid, prevention and management of psychotrauma;

**Position Title:** Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Expert Consultant (Perinatal Mental Health)

**Department:** Country Office - Liberia

**Location:** Monrovia, Liberia with travel to pilot health facilities in Granda Bassa County

**Reports to:** Country Director, Americares Liberia; with dotted line to Americares MHPSS AEMEA Region technical unit

**Assignment Type:** Consultancy - Deliverable Based

**Length :** 7 months (December 2026 – June 2027), with an expected full-time level of effort

**Application Requirements:** Resume and application questions

**About the position:** Americares Liberia, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and partners, is supporting integration of perinatal mental health services within maternal, newborn and community health platforms. Foundational activities including situational analysis, stakeholder engagement, and co-creation of a PMH integration approach have been completed. The consultant will provide technical continuity and implementation leadership during pilot rollout and early scale-up.

**Key Outcomes:**

**Weeks 1–2** **Planning and orientation:** Implementation plan and risk register agreed with the country team and the MHPSS Technical Unit.

**Months 1-2** **Training package finalization and readiness:** Finalized and validated training package, including facilitator and participant materials, validation findings and agreed revisions; detailed training plan; and documented support to the country team on participant coordination, venue, materials, scheduling and other training logistics.

**Months 2–4 Training delivery:** Training and/or training-of-trainers sessions conducted or co-facilitated; attendance records, pre- and post-training assessments and participant feedback compiled; and a brief training report with results, lessons and follow-up actions submitted.

**Months 4–6 – Supportive supervision:** Supervision approach, tools and visit schedule established with the country team; planned supervision visits conducted; and visit reports and action trackers completed to document findings, provider support needs, responsible persons and follow-up timelines.

**Months 5–7 – Support with Fidelity assessment and quality improvement:** Fidelity assessments completed at pilot sites using agreed tools; findings analyzed and shared with relevant stakeholders; and a fidelity assessment report with corrective actions and recommendations for quality improvement and scale-up submitted.

**Final:** Final consultancy report, sustainability and transition plan, and complete handover package submitted, including finalized tools, training records, supervision documentation, and outstanding action items

**Key Consultant Activities:**

- Agree on implementation plan for communication routine with the country team and the MHPSS Technical Unit.

**SUPPORT WITH TRAINING PACKAGE FINALIZATION**

- Support with finalization of facilitator guides, participant materials, clinical tools, job aids and competency-assessment instruments for the Liberia context;
- Confirm alignment with the agreed PMH approach and relevant national guidance;
- Support with planning and facilitating final technical validation activities with the Ministry of Health, County Health Team, providers and partners; document feedback and decisions;
- Incorporate agreed revisions; and prepare a complete, implementation-ready training package.

**TRAINING PLANNING AND LOGISTICS:**

- Support with the coordination and development of the training and/or training-of-trainers plan, agenda and facilitation schedule;
- Support the country team to identify and invite appropriate participants and facilitators; clarify participant selection criteria and expected competencies;
- Support with preparation training materials and logistics with country team.

**TRAINING DELIVERY AND CAPACITY BUILDING:**

- Facilitate or co-facilitate competency-based training and training-of-trainers sessions using participatory methods, demonstrations, role plays and supervised practice;
- Administer and review pre- and post-training assessments; observe participant skills using agreed competency tools; provide targeted coaching and remediation; compile attendance and participant feedback; and identify providers requiring additional mentoring or follow-up support.

**PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION:**

- Support country team with coordination of pilot start-up with the country team and participating facilities;
- orient facility leadership and providers on the PMH service-delivery model;
- conduct routine field visits to identify and resolve implementation bottlenecks;
- support integration of PMH screening, assessment, risk management protocols and follow-ups, brief intervention, referral and follow-up within maternal, newborn and community health workflows;
- strengthen referral and counter-referral pathways between facilities, communities and specialized services.

**SUPPORTIVE SUPERVISION AND MENTORING:**

**STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND COORDINATION:**

- convene or support regular review meetings; provide concise implementation updates
- promote alignment of pilot activities with RMNCAH priorities.

**MONITORING, DOCUMENTATION AND LEARNING:**

- Support with reviewing routine program data for completeness, quality and use; track progress against the implementation plan and agreed indicators;
- Synthesize training, supervision and fidelity findings; document challenges, adaptations, promising practices and lessons learned; prepare concise activity and progress reports;
- Help with assessing adherence and fidelity to the intended PMH model, including screening, intervention delivery, referral, documentation and follow-up;
- Share findings with relevant stakeholders; and contribute evidence-based recommendations for sustainability, transition and potential scale-up.

Support integration of PMH indicators into routine facility registers and HMIS reporting, so that data collection continues beyond the consultancy.

**Degrees and/or experience required for the role:**
