jobs.title: Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
**Miyamoto International** ("Miyamoto") is a global engineering and disaster management firm that delivers expert solutions to sustain industries and safeguard communities worldwide. The Global Disaster Risk Management (GDRM) Group manages a portfolio of humanitarian, disaster response, reconstruction, resilience, and international development programs funded by institutional donors. As Miyamoto expands its programming, the organization seeks to strengthen and standardize its grants and awards management systems to ensure full compliance with applicable donor requirements.

We are seeking a dedicated **Compliance Specialist (Consultant)** to support a full compliance review of existing tools, templates and guides and update existing toolkits for current and future programs.

**Position Title:** Compliance Specialist (Consultant)
**Period of Performance:** o/a November 23, 2026 - December 23, 2026
**Location:** Remote
**Reports To:** Sr Princial, Global Disaster Risk Management (GDRM) Group

**Objective**

The objective of this consultancy is to conduct a comprehensive compliance review of Miyamoto's existing grants management, subaward management, procurement, finance, and project administration templates, tools, and procedures to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements federal assistance programs. The consultant will identify compliance gaps, recommend improvements, and update or develop standardized templates and guidance documents to support effective award management across current and future federally funded programs.

**Scope of Services**

**1. Compliance Assessment**

- Review existing Miyamoto templates, forms, checklists, and guidance documents related to:
- Prime award management
- Subaward management
- Procurement and vendor selection
- Grant file documentation
- Partner due diligence
- **Assess alignment with:**
- U.S. Department of State award requirements
- 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance
- Federal subaward management requirements
- Audit and record-retention requirements
- Procurement standards applicable to federal assistance awards

**2. Gap Analysis and Recommendations**

- Conduct a formal gap analysis of existing organizational compliance systems.
- Identify areas of noncompliance, inconsistency, or elevated organizational risk.
- Recommend practical corrective actions and system improvements.
- Develop a prioritized implementation roadmap for compliance strengthening.

**3. Template and Toolkit Development**

**Review, revise, and standardize key organizational templates, including as applicable:**

- Subaward agreements
- Subrecipient monitoring plans
- Risk assessment tools
- Due diligence questionnaires
- Cost-reimbursement documentation
- Procurement justifications
- Sole-source memoranda
- Consultant agreements
- Grant file checklists
- Monitoring visit reports
- Compliance review checklists
- Closeout documentation packages

**4. Internal Controls and Processes**
- Assess current internal controls related to grant administration and compliance oversight.
- Recommend process improvements to strengthen accountability and documentation.

**5. Advisory Support**
- Provide technical advice to Miyamoto regarding compliance risks and mitigation measures.
- Respond to staff questions regarding federal assistance requirements during the review period.
- Support interpretation of donor compliance requirements when requested.

**Deliverables:** The consultant will provide the following deliverables during the period of performance:
- **Compliance Review Report** Comprehensive assessment of existing templates, forms, policies, procedures, and tools related to grant management, subaward management, procurement, consultant management, monitoring, and award administration. The report will identify areas of alignment with USG requirements, 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance, and federal assistance regulations, as well as any compliance gaps requiring corrective action.
- **Estimated Deadline** 5 working days for review, 2 days for reporting
- **Revised Compliance Toolkit** Review, revise, and standardize existing templates and supporting documentation related to award management, including subaward agreements, subrecipient monitoring tools, due diligence questionnaires, risk assessment tools, procurement documentation, compliance checklists, grant file management tools, and closeout documentation. Updated templates will incorporate federal compliance requirements and best practices.
- **Estimated Deadline** 10 working days for revision

**Qualifications and Experience**
- **Education:**
- Bachelor's degree required.
- Advanced degree in law, public administration, international development, business administration, compliance, finance, or related field preferred.
- **Experience:**
- Minimum 7 years of experience managing compliance, grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, or awards funded by U.S. Government agencies.
- Demonstrated experience supporting U.S. Department of State, USAID, or other federal assistance programs.
- Experience conducting compliance reviews and institutional capacity assessments.
- Experience developing policies, procedures, templates, and operational guidance.
- **Knowledge/Skills:**
- Expert knowledge of 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance.
- Familiarity with Department of State assistance awards and grants management requirements.
- Knowledge of subrecipient management, procurement standards, and audit requirements.
- Understanding of donor-funded humanitarian and international development programs.
- Strong analytical and organizational abilities.
- Exceptional policy and technical writing skills.
- Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical operational tools.
- Strong attention to detail.
- **Languages**
- Professional fluency in English required.
- Spanish proficiency preferred.

jobs.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Supply Chain & Logistics Officer
jobs.description:
**Work on a global humanitarian program contributing to saving lives and alleviating suffering.**

Australia Assists is an Australian Government program that deploys skilled humanitarian specialists to support multilateral agencies, governments, civil society and communities to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and conflict. Australia Assists’ Goal is to: Save lives, alleviate suffering, and maintain human dignity during and in the aftermath of conflict, disasters and other humanitarian crises, and strengthen preparedness for the occurrence of such situations. The program’s Objective is: Targeted deployment of humanitarian expertise that meets the priorities and needs of Australia's multilateral, bilateral and civil society partners and advances Australia's international humanitarian priorities.

For more information [please visit our website.](https://www.australiaassists.org/)

**The Opportunity:**

- Based in Honiara, Solomon Islands
- Open to national and international candidates
- Duration: 12 months from start

**The Role:**

The EPR Supply Chain Officer will support the NDMO in the design and implementation of supply chain/EPR capacity strengthening activities for the Solomon Islands. Based in the NDMO, with support from the WFP Pacific Multi-country office. The EPR Supply Chain Officer's primary responsibilities are to support the Government of Solomon Islands and its partners in emergency preparedness and response, and capacity strengthening initiatives. The role requires a hands-on humanitarian logistics specialist with prior Pacific experience who can quickly provide practical operational support to the NDMO.

**Key Responsibilities:**

The incumbent’s main responsibilities include:

- Support the NDMO in strengthening logistics preparedness and response readiness for El Niño -related drought and associated supply chain disruptions, including contingency planning, stock visibility, prepositioning options and coordination with relevant government agencies and partners.
- Following the outcomes of the 2024 Capacity Needs Mapping and Business Process Mapping exercises, continue engaging with the NDMO to define and implement the recommendations.
- Guide the NDMO in the development, standardization, and implementation of key logistics forms (e.g., Stock Report, Service Request Form, Delivery Notes), and support the training and capability development of NDMO staff and key stakeholders (NGOs, Red Cross, government agencies) on their use.
- Support the NDMO in developing and implementing an Excel-based Consolidated Stock Report template, including setting submission deadlines (e.g., last Friday of each month), establishing communication protocols with stakeholders, and conducting a pilot test with sample stock data to validate functionality.
- Support the NDMO’s engagement in the Pacific Humanitarian Warehousing Program and the national humanitarian warehouse project in Honiara, focusing on operational readiness, warehouse management procedures, inventory management, staff capacity and coordination arrangements before, during and after warehouse construction.
- Assist the NDMO in optimizing logistics processes and data flows, generating actionable insights from monthly stock consolidations, introducing a unique identifier-based tracking system for submitted forms, and refining workflows based on feedback and performance.
- Lead the planning and execution of a SimEx based on a disaster response scenario to test the effectiveness of operational planning and workflows.
- Provide ongoing mentoring to NDMO staff on humanitarian logistics and supply chain.
- Actively and systematically monitor and analyze the overall context in Solomon Islands and act as a focal point for information gathering and consultation for WFP, linking with the appropriate unit and officer(s) in Fiji.
- Be the first line of response when emergencies are anticipated to impact Solomon Islands. Act, if requested by the Government of Solomon Islands and authorized by Senior Management in Fiji, as surge capacity and be embedded as part of the national emergency response team.
- Support the NDMO in planning, coordinating, and conducting the Provincial Logistics Capacity Assessment. Sections can be updated partially and frequently when significant changes are identified.
- Work closely with NDMO staff to provide mentoring and exchange of knowledge where requested.
- Engage with other UN agencies in Solomon Islands, (including UNICEF, IOM, FAO and others) to ensure greater UN coordination and coherence.

**Selection Criteria**

- Advanced university degree in Transport Economics, Supply Chain, Logistics, Emergency, and Disaster Management, or other related fields; or a Bachelor's degree in one of the above disciplines with additional years of relevant experience. 5+ years of experience in disaster risk management, humanitarian response, emergency planning, or crisis coordination in government, non-government, or international organizations.
- 4–6 years of relevant professional experience, including at least three years of progressively responsible experience in logistics and/or supply chain operations.
- Demonstrated hands-on experience in humanitarian logistics operations, including warehousing, inventory management, transport and distribution, is required.
- **Prior experience in humanitarian logistics in Pacific Island countries is required, with experience working in Melanesia highly desirable.** Candidates should demonstrate familiarity with Pacific operating contexts and experience working closely with national government counterparts.
- Experience working with Governments for effective capacity strengthening. • Experience working in collaboration with a diverse array of humanitarian actors, including governments, NGOs, U.N. agencies, civil society, community-based organizations and the private sector.
- Experience working with or for National Disaster Management Offices and teams, and/or experience in business processes mapping and optimization is desirable.

For a complete position description please click [here](https://intdev.tetratech.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/AA-PD-EPR-Supply-Chain-Logistics-Officer-SI.pdf).

jobs.title: Infrastructure Specialist - (Dir Hafir)
jobs.description:
**Job Purpose**

The project intends to engage a qualified Infrastructure Specialist to provide specialized engineering consultancy services for reviewing and validating the technical specifications, engineering designs, and Bills of Quantities (BoQs) prepared for all irrigation canal rehabilitation interventions, including both open and covered canals.

The consultant will ensure that all technical documentation and proposed rehabilitation interventions are consistent with the applicable engineering standards, design requirements, and technical specifications approved by the Directorate of Water Resources. The assignment aims to minimize technical risks, enhance the quality of engineering designs, and ensure technical compliance before the commencement of rehabilitation works.

**Key Responsibilities**

1. Review of Engineering Designs: Review and assess engineering designs, drawings, calculations, and technical documentation for all proposed irrigation canal rehabilitation interventions, covering both open and covered canals.
2. Review of Technical Specifications: Verify that the technical specifications are complete, appropriate, and fully aligned with the standards and requirements approved by the Directorate of Water Resources.
3. Review of Bills of Quantities (BoQs): Examine and validate the BoQs to ensure the accuracy and consistency of quantities, construction items, technical descriptions, and proposed rehabilitation activities in relation to the approved designs.
4. Technical Compliance Assessment: Assess the proposed interventions against applicable engineering standards, design criteria, and relevant technical guidelines to identify potential gaps, inconsistencies, and non-compliance issues.
5. Identification of Technical Risks: Identify potential engineering, design, construction, and implementation risks and recommend appropriate corrective measures to mitigate them.
6. Recommendations and Technical Improvements: Provide practical technical recommendations to improve the quality, feasibility, durability, and cost-effectiveness of the proposed rehabilitation interventions.
7. Coordination and Technical Consultation: Coordinate with the project team, relevant engineers, and concerned technical authorities, as required, to clarify technical issues and ensure consistency with approved standards.
8. Final Validation: Provide final technical comments and recommendations and confirm whether the engineering designs, technical specifications, and BoQs are technically sound and ready for implementation, subject to addressing any identified issues.

Note: The primary responsibilities listed above are illustrative. Additional responsibilities may be assigned to the position in the future based on the department's organizational structure.

**Qualification (Education/Work Experience)**

1. **Essential:**

- A Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Irrigation Engineering, or a closely related discipline. A Master's degree in a relevant field will be an advantage.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in irrigation infrastructure, water resources engineering, canal design, rehabilitation, or related civil engineering works.
- Demonstrated experience in reviewing and validating engineering designs, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities.
- Sound knowledge of irrigation canal rehabilitation, including open and covered canal systems.
- Familiarity with applicable engineering standards and technical specifications approved by the Directorate of Water Resources.
- Proven ability to identify technical discrepancies, assess engineering risks, and provide practical recommendations.
- Strong analytical, technical reporting, and communication skills.

1. **Desirable:**

- English language is an assist

**Core & Managerial Competencies**

1. **Core Competencies:**

- Communication
- Teamwork
- Planning and organizing
- Accountability
- Creativity
- Stakeholder Orientation
- Commitment to Continuous Learning
- Technological Awareness.

1. **Supervisor/Managerial Competencies:**

- Leadership
- Building Trust
- Vision
- Managing Performance
- Empowering Others
- Judgment/Decision-making.

1. **Technical Competencies:**

- Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, Outlook.)
- Well organized, self-motivated, and detail oriented.
- Experience in working with NGO’s.
- Ability to work under pressure.

**Duration and Modality of Engagement**

- The consultant will be engaged on a daily basis, with remuneration calculated based on the actual number of days worked and approved by the project.
- The number of working days will be determined according to the volume and complexity of the technical documentation requiring review and validation.
- The assignment will be carried out in accordance with the agreed work plan, schedule, and terms of reference.
- Payment will be subject to the submission and approval of timesheets and the required deliverables, in accordance with the applicable contractual arrangements.

**Eligibility and Conflict of Interest Requirements**

- Applicants must demonstrate the required professional qualifications, relevant experience, and technical expertise.
- If the selected individual is currently employed by a government institution or public authority, they must obtain and submit formal written approval or a no-objection letter from their employer authorizing them to undertake this consultancy assignment.
- Such approval must be provided before signing the consultancy contract or commencing any assignment-related activities.
- The consultant must disclose any potential conflict of interest and maintain professional independence, confidentiality, and impartiality throughout the assignment.

**Compliance to Anti-Harassment, PSEA, and Child Safeguarding**

- Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to IYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. IYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.
- IYD employees and related personnel must not under any circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside IYD.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) - GUARD
jobs.description:
**PROGRAM SUMMARY**

GUARD America (Global Urgent Activation for Response to Infectious Diseases) is an International Medical Corps-led consortium funded by the U.S. Department of State Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD) to support rapid outbreak activation and response, early detection and containment, operational coordination, and stronger national and subnational outbreak-response systems. GUARD is currently supporting the BVD response in DRC, while retaining a broader platform and consortium structure that may support additional country responses as activated.

International Medical Corps is implementing a large and evolving Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with additional regional and multi-country programming. The response spans multiple projects and funding streams and includes case management through Ebola Treatment Centers and transit/triage structures; surveillance, alert management and community-based surveillance; infection prevention and control (IPC) and WASH; risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); mental health and psychosocial support; and continuity of essential health services. The scale and complexity of the response requires a coordinated M/E approach that harmonizes indicators, tools, data systems and reporting across projects while meeting government, donor and internal requirements.

The Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) - GUARD will provide senior technical M/E leadership and oversight for International Medical Corps' global project team for GUARD. The role will augment, not replace, the existing country M/E team and leadership. The role will also provide targeted M/E support to the GUARD consortium, including management of the results framework and indicator tracking, donor reporting, consolidation of partner results, and coordination with consortium partners on M/E standards and requirements. As GUARD's response remit evolves, the position is expected to transition to a broader multi-country or global GUARD M/E role.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The role of the Senior Specialist is to support better performance and greater accountability by implementing evidence-based project management at the field level, to guide and improve performance. The Senior Specialist will lead the design of methodologies and tools to ensure the availability of clear and accurate information at the project level. The Senior Specialist also plays a vital role in data management, surveys and quality by designing an M/E system that adheres to the International Medical Corps (IMC) M/E Global Guidelines, the M/E Minimum Standards for Quality, and the guiding M/E policies and procedures, among others. The Senior Specialist, M/E will provide technical support to the project and build capacity in the country mission through strengthening learning and knowledge sharing across the IMC and with the wider humanitarian community.

For this assignment, the Senior Specialist will provide senior technical M/E leadership and oversight for IMC's highly infectious disease responses led by GUARD, providing technical direction to the country M/E team to ensure coherent monitoring, data quality, analysis and reporting across multiple projects and funding streams, while also supporting GUARD consortium-level performance monitoring, reporting and partner M/E coordination.

**REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- The country-based M/E lead will have a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation, for technical direction and oversight, while keeping their solid-line reporting relationship to country leadership.
- Sets the technical scope, standards, methods, tools and quality expectations for M/E across the Ebola response and GUARD-supported activities. Provides technical guidance, review and capacity building to the country M/E lead and team.
- Country leadership keeps line management of the country M/E team, including day-to-day work assignments, deadlines, performance management, and hiring and separation decisions. The Senior Specialist gives technical input to these processes as appropriate.
- Where GUARD operates in countries with an existing IMC mission, the same model applies. Country M/E leads reports to the Senior Specialist on a dotted line for technical matters, and country leadership keeps solid-line management and operational accountability.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**IMC's policies, guidelines, and procedures**

- Mainstream the Global M/E Guidelines across all related M/E activities at the field level and ensure the guidance notes for monitoring and evaluation are functional at the field level.
- Apply and adapt existing Global M/E Guidelines, tools, and templates at the relevant stages of the project cycle.
- Actively promote the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards within IMC and amongst its beneficiaries.
- Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the Code of Conduct, ethics, values, and standpoint with regards to internal and external actors.

**Ebola Response and GUARD M/E Leadership**

- Provide senior technical leadership and oversight of M/E for IMC's Ebola response in DRC across multiple projects and funding streams, providing technical direction to the country M/E lead and team to ensure that project-specific requirements are met within a harmonized response-level M/E approach.
- Maintain and strengthen the consolidated Ebola response M/E framework, including harmonization of indicators, definitions, data collection tools, reporting flows and performance tracking across projects and implementation areas.
- Lead routine review of response performance, data quality and indicator achievement, working with program, technical and field teams to identify discrepancies, implementation gaps and required corrective actions and to strengthen the use of data for operational decision-making.
- Coordinate donor and internal M/E deliverables for the Ebola portfolio, including M/E plans, indicator tracking tables, performance reports, data calls and other quantitative reporting requirements, ensuring consistency of results across submissions.
- For GUARD, maintain and update the project results framework/log frame and indicator tracking systems; coordinate consolidation and quality assurance of results reported by IMC and consortium partners; and contribute M/E evidence and analysis to GUARD donor reporting, reviews and planning.
- Provide M/E guidance and capacity strengthening to GUARD consortium partners as required, including clarification of indicator definitions, reporting requirements, data-quality expectations and supporting documentation.
- Ensure that GUARD country-response monitoring is integrated with existing Ebola response systems to the extent feasible, avoiding unnecessary duplication of indicators, tools, databases and reporting processes.
- Coordinate closely with the Information Management/Data Manager, epidemiology staff, country M/E staff, technical leads and relevant HQ technical teams to establish clear responsibilities for data collection, management, analysis and reporting.
- Support adaptation of M/E systems for additional GUARD-supported country responses if activated and be prepared to assume a broader multi-country/global GUARD M/E remit as the program evolves.

**Project design and planning**

- Lead or support the development and updating of project and response-level results frameworks, theories of change, log frames, M/E plans and indicator tracking tables, including harmonization of indicators across Ebola response projects and GUARD.
- Identify the budget/resources needed for M/E activities of the project.
- Support project planning processes related to M/E aspects (M/E work plan and budget). M/E system
- In coordination with the implementation Team and M/E field Focal Points, establish a reliable participatory M/E framework according to donors' requirements for the project to ensure quality.
- Follow full M/E procedures and operating plans within the project and develop harmonized data collection tools involving the different stakeholders (project team, partners).
- Establish M/E system in line with donors and project requirements and ensure donors' requirements are followed through the project management life cycle.
- Develop and maintain data gathering strategies and clear data and reporting flows across projects, implementation sites and, for GUARD, consortium partners.
- Oversee the collection and timely reporting of data and statistics from the service delivery points.
- Consolidate and reconcile results across technical sectors, projects, geographic areas and relevant implementing partners, ensuring consistency between project-level and response-level reporting.
- Implement DHIS2 where appropriate and applicable, control and manage DHIS2 data entry and management.
- Collaborate with the M/E and DHIS2 teams at HQ to develop and maintain the data management system, including updating, troubleshooting and promptly addressing all problems as they arise
- Lead the implementation of Satellite-based Tracking and Remote Monitoring (STARM) system
- Conduct regular site visits or when required to monitor service provision and ensure data quality.
- Support project team to organize regular review and planning meetings to assess project progress.
- Set project monitoring system for the project (monitoring plan, monitoring tools and strategies) and disseminate all monitoring tools within project.

**Data quality management**

- Collaborate with technical staff on data quality maintenance and routine monitoring of project.
- Assess the quality of data collected for the indicators and ensure that data pitfalls and issues are mitigated.
- Coordinate routine data quality audits conducted in different sites, compile results at the level of a project, and develop action plans to implement corrective measures.
- Manage tools and methods for assessing data quality and security.
- Ensure ethical practices are followed in the collection and management of all data; informed consent practices are used in all interviews, and privacy risks are mitigated in the storage and transfer of data.
- Identify and locate back-up documentation for reporting against indicators.
- Maintain data at the mission level according to IMC's data protection protocols.
- Work closely with Information Management and epidemiology colleagues to establish interoperable reporting flows and clearly delineated responsibilities for epidemiological/surveillance data, routine program monitoring data, case-management data and donor performance reporting, minimizing parallel data systems and duplicate data collection.

**Sampling techniques**

- Use proper sampling (probability and non-probability) techniques considering desired power, type of survey or evaluation (e.g., single point or multiple points; baseline vs endline), the objective of the survey or evaluation (e.g., testing for change or getting the point prevalence), and budget limitations.
- Review the sampling approach proposed by an expert/consultant (if applicable).
- Develop the sampling frame and calculate the sample size for surveys, including implementation of donors’ recommendations for the surveys. Qualitative and quantitative techniques:
- Develop and use different qualitative and quantitative methods of data collection, including structured/ semi-structured interviews, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, group discussions, focus group discussions, and direct observations as an M/E tool.
- Conduct training on quantitative and qualitative techniques for data collection for M/E, project, and interviewers.
- Keeping the social dynamics in mind, manage errors/bias, and strategize to minimize them and to ensure the data collected is representative of populations without power (avoiding over-dependence on community leaders, local authorities, and/or government authorities as primary sources for defining communities' needs and preferences).
- Coordinate the logistics of data collection, data management, and ensure adequate resources are available.
- Develop questionnaires for monitoring purposes and apply the different interview techniques (structured/semi-structured).
- Develop database structures to store and manipulate quantitative data.
- Implement appropriate and recommended survey guidelines
- Conduct regular site visits or when required to monitor and assist partners in the data collection process to ensure data quality.

**Mobile and manual data collection**

- Determine the appropriate data collection tool based on the purpose, advantages, and disadvantages of mobile data collection techniques.
- Design simple and complex questionnaires using XLS or form builder (Kobo form builder, Ona form builder, etc.)
- Support in installing and configuring mobile data collection tools (ODK collect, Kobo collect, CommCare, etc.) on smartphones or tablets and managing data on mobile servers
- Increase the capacity of other staff in developing XLS forms and setting up mobile data collection.

**Data analysis, including use of statistical software**

- Apply standard methodologies for the analysis of data to allow for comparison and aggregation across time and different areas.
- Support M/E and the implementation team on conducting statistical analysis, including descriptive (univariate and bivariate data analysis) and inferential analysis using statistical software.
- Perform qualitative textual analysis and develop topical outlines (coding).
- Triangulate findings from several qualitative and quantitative sources.
- Interpret statistical data for use in decision-making and synthesize quantitative and qualitative information for write-up/reports and decision making.
- Support development and maintenance of response dashboards, analytical products and routine performance summaries that integrate programmatic and epidemiological information where appropriate for operational decision-making.

**Evaluation design**

- Support in developing Terms of Reference (TOR) for internal and external baseline surveys, mid-term evaluations, final evaluations, and frame the different types of study questions such as barrier analysis, market analysis, and Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Surveys (KAP).
- Identify the needed resources for evaluation, such as information, expertise, personnel, instruments, and budget.
- Manage the administrative and logistic process of evaluations involving external evaluators.
- Support in training and supervising data gathering of internal performance evaluation and design and synthesize the findings from participative evaluation techniques (actively involving affected communities in the evaluation exercises).
- Support operational and implementation research and other studies using appropriate epidemiological, quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods approaches, in coordination with HQ research, epidemiology and relevant technical teams.

**Presenting information**

- Write full narrative reports (internal reviews, progress reports, survey reports) and executive summaries.
- Present information and tell the story of the project to multiple audiences and decisionmakers based on the findings from the analysis and monitoring.
- Verify reports' accuracy and presentation of information, including the use of appropriate graphs and tables.
- Disseminate qualitative and quantitative results using the established dashboard or system as per agreed frequency.
- Report and share evaluation findings with stakeholders.
- Generate past performance sheet with updated trend analysis of the key project indicators

**Capacity development and training**

- Provide coaching/mentoring of staff and on-the-job training to improve the skills of the staff in M/E.
- Provide training and on-the-job learning to project staff and volunteers based on required skills for M/E activities
- Support project staff with additional training and mentoring on routine monitoring procedures and surveillance techniques.

**Knowledge management learning:**

- Support in developing Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) mechanisms and processes for the project while ensuring these mechanisms are in line with IMC's guidelines.
- Establish basic learning systems and framework that incorporate project studies' findings, lessons learned, achievements and gaps, and develop all the tools required to support learning practices.
- Facilitate review and lessons learned exercises, including data collected through assessments, surveys and other participative forms of community engagement and feedback collection.
- Collect and document project Most Significant Change Stories (MSCSs) from direct beneficiaries. Community-based feedback and response mechanism:
- Lead the implementation of methodologies to consult communities on their preferences based on the operational context.
- Contribute to planned and ongoing operational research, implementation research, learning and other evidence-generation initiatives related to Ebola and broader outbreak preparedness and response, in coordination with technical, epidemiology, research and program teams. This may include contributing to study design and protocols, development of data collection approaches and tools, data quality and analysis, interpretation of findings, documentation of lessons learned, and translation of evidence into program adaptation and learning.
- Support systematic documentation and synthesis of evidence across GUARD activations and the wider Ebola response, including after-action reviews, implementation learning, operational lessons and cross-country learning, and support dissemination and uptake of findings as appropriate.

**Cross-cutting themes**

- Support project staff to mainstream critical concepts around sex, age, disability protection, and conflict sensitivity by supporting dedicated sex, protection, and conflict sensitivity analyses as may be required by project.
- Integrating the collection of information related to demographic vulnerabilities and contextual risks (sex, age, disability, environment, etc.) into all M/E exercises to provide an evidence base.
- Following up with implementation teams to utilize findings and strengthen activities in line with sex, protection, and conflict-sensitive approaches.
- Coordinate M/E with consortium and implementing partners, including agreement on indicator definitions, reporting timelines, supporting documentation, data-quality expectations and consolidation of partner results; lead relevant M/E coordination meetings and represent IMC as required.
- Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Typically, a bachelor’s degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development, with experience or background in M/E, epidemiology, public health, and health information management. Master's level or a higher degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development preferred. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.
- Typically, 10+ years of applied experience in the humanitarian or international development sector, including 7+ years designing, implementing and overseeing monitoring and evaluation systems in relevant sectors.
- Demonstrated experience providing technical leadership and capacity building to M/E teams in complex programming, including leading staff through matrixed or dotted-line reporting relationships.
- Significant international humanitarian field experience, preferably including outbreak or emergency health response; willingness to be based in DRC, with the potential to transition to a multi-country/global remit.
- Experience with M/E approaches for key donors such as US Dept of State, USG, OFDA, ECHO, EU, DfID, UN, etc. Strong experience with U.S. Government-funded program monitoring and reporting; Department of State experience strongly preferred.
- Experience in database design and other tools for information and data management such as DHIS2
- Experience in the use of qualitative and quantitative software for data analysis.
- Experience with mobile data collection platform
- Able to identify gaps in staff knowledge of M/E concepts and skills and provide training in these topics.
- Ability to write full narrative reports (needs assessments, internal reviews, progress reports) and executive summaries.
- Demonstrated understanding of data protection and confidentiality as part of data collection and management practices and ability to respect and maintain confidentiality.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Teams.
- Competency in statistical analysis software; proficiency in R/RStudio, Python, or another programming language for data management and analysis is strongly preferred. Broader data science skills are an asset.
- Possess skills in qualitative data analysis, with or without software
- Possess skills in mobile data collection software such as Ona, Kobo, ToolBox.
- Communicate the organizational goals to the team.
- Support innovation and organizational change when needed.
- Have analytical, conceptual, and strategic thinking skills.
- Build collaborative relationships and foster teamwork.
- High-level English proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing).
- High-level local language proficiency preferred (Speaking – Reading – Writing).

## Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

## Equal Opportunities

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

## Misconduct Disclosure Scheme

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Supply Chain and Operations Manager - Sudan
jobs.description:
We are currently recruiting a **Supply Chain and Operations Manager** to join our **Supply Chain and Operations** team.

This is a **country-based position** in **Khartoum, Sudan**, with regular travel to field locations subject to access and security conditions.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks and enhanced due diligence**.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

We work with local actors to deliver safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs. Relief International is an alliance of multiple international entities operating under a one-team approach with a shared mission and leadership structure.

**About the Opportunity**

This is a critical leadership role supporting Relief International's operations in one of the world's most complex humanitarian environments.

The Supply Chain and Operations Manager leads the delivery and continuous improvement of procurement, warehousing, medical supply logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and office operations across Sudan. Based in Khartoum and supporting teams operating in dispersed and often insecure locations, the role is responsible for ensuring country operations remain reliable, cost-effective, compliant and responsive to programme needs.

Working closely with Area Managers, programme teams, Finance, HR, Security, IT and global supply chain colleagues, you will strengthen systems, build the capacity of field teams, improve operational visibility and ensure supply chains continue to function effectively in challenging circumstances.

This is a hands-on leadership position requiring someone who has successfully managed complex field operations and can balance strategic oversight with practical problem-solving.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead and manage supply chain and operations functions across country and field offices, providing leadership, supervision and clear accountability for operational performance.
- Oversee procurement planning and implementation, ensuring timely, competitive and compliant procurement of goods and services while maintaining strong supplier relationships and value for money.
- Manage warehousing, inventory control and medical supply logistics systems, ensuring accurate stock visibility, quality standards, reconciliation processes and reporting.
- Lead fleet, transport, asset and office operations management across country and field locations, ensuring operational continuity, cost controls and compliance with organizational and donor requirements.
- Strengthen procurement, inventory, fleet and asset tracking systems through practical, user-friendly tools and reporting mechanisms.
- Produce regular operational performance reporting, identifying risks, bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement and ensuring corrective actions are implemented.
- Support cross-border supply chain activities and importation processes where required, including medical commodities and specialized programme supplies.
- Work closely with Finance and programme teams to strengthen controls, reconcile commitments and proactively address operational, compliance and fraud risks.
- Build and develop high-performing teams through coaching, mentoring, performance management and capacity strengthening initiatives.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- University degree in logistics, supply chain management, business administration or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Minimum seven years' experience in humanitarian supply chain, logistics or operations management, including at least three years in a senior management role within conflict-affected, post-conflict or similarly fragile environments.
- Demonstrated hands-on experience across procurement, warehousing and inventory management, medical logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and multi-site operations.
- Proven ability to lead and support geographically dispersed teams operating in challenging and low-connectivity environments.
- Experience designing or improving practical operational tracking systems and using data to strengthen controls, decision-making and performance management.
- Strong knowledge of donor procurement compliance requirements, supplier management, inventory controls, operational budgeting and risk management.
- Excellent leadership, coaching and problem-solving skills, with the ability to simplify processes while maintaining effective controls and accountability.
- Strong written and spoken English and willingness to travel regularly to field locations.
- Arabic language skills would be an advantage.
- Previous experience in Sudan, Chad, Darfur or similar humanitarian contexts would be a bonus
- Experience supporting health and nutrition supply chains, emergency scale-ups and complex humanitarian donor-funded programmes is desirable.

jobs.title: Oficial Shelter - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a **Oficial Shelter** altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a DRC está buscando un/a **Oficial Shelter** será responsable de liderar y ejecutar acciones de recuperación temprana en los sectores de Shelter e Infraestructura.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de Equipo de Shelter y el acompañamiento técnico del Especialista Nacional de WASH, Shelter & Infraestructura, el Oficial de Shelter será responsable de liderar y ejecutar acciones de recuperación temprana en los sectores de Shelter e Infraestructura. Asegurará la ejecución oportuna y de calidad de las actividades de evaluaciones de necesidades, distribuciones de insumos y mejoras de infraestructura comunitaria e institucional afectada por la emergencia. Asimismo, apoyará la coordinación con autoridades, líderes comunitarios y otros actores humanitarios para garantizar una respuesta integrada, centrada en la protección y alineada con los estándares humanitarios aplicables.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Evaluaciones**

- Realizar evaluaciones rápidas multisectoriales y sectoriales para identificar necesidades de alojamiento e infraestructura en contextos de recuperación temprana.
- Realizar la identificación de viviendas que hayan recibido la inspección de daños por los organismos competentes y que requieran reparaciones ligeras y medias.
- Realizar la identificación de las infraestructuras comunitarias (como escuelas, centros de salud, u otros espacios que presten servicios esenciales), que hayan sido afectadas por la emergencia y que requieran reparaciones no estructurales.
- Completar los diagnósticos técnicos para las obras de rehabilitaciones de infraestructuras comunitarias y reparaciones ligeras y medias de viviendas.
- Apoyar la identificación y selección de comunidades y hogares beneficiarios que requieran apoyo con asistencia de NFIs.
- Identificar, analizar y escalar oportunamente necesidades críticas, riesgos emergentes, brechas de asistencia y desafíos operacionales que requieran decisiones inmediatas o movilización adicional de recursos.

**Implementación**

- Planificar, ejecutar y documentar la distribución de artículos no alimentarios (NFI) relacionados con alojamiento, garantizando la calidad, trazabilidad y rendición de cuentas del proceso.
- Elaborar especificaciones técnicas, estimaciones de cantidades de obra y planes de trabajo para la contratación de servicios de rehabilitación de infraestructuras comunitarias esenciales.
- Supervisar obras de rehabilitación de infraestructuras comunitarias.
- Preparar las especificaciones técnicas para la compra de materiales y kits de reparación.
- Elaborar las especificaciones técnicas para los trabajos de reparaciones ligeras y medianas de viviendas; lo que implica la definición de kits de reparación o la documentación necesaria para la contratación del servicio por contratistas.
- Brindar capacitación técnica a las familias asistidas sobre técnicas de reparación segura, incorporando elementos de reducción de riesgos de desastres.
- Monitorear la calidad técnica de las obras ejecutadas por contratistas
- Realizar el seguimiento del avance físico de las actividades y verificar el cumplimiento de estándares técnicos, de calidad, seguridad, protección y gestión ambiental, preparando los informes técnicos correspondientes y los documentos administrativos necesarios para los pagos y cierres de contratos.

**Registros**

- Documentar de manera continua resultados operacionales, desafíos, brechas y lecciones identificadas para apoyar la adaptación rápida de la respuesta y la planificación de la recuperación temprana.
- Garantizar la correcta recopilación, almacenamiento y protección de los datos de las personas beneficiarias y demás información requerida para el reporte de actividades e indicadores de los proyectos.

**Coordinación y enlace**

- Cuando sea requerido participar en los mecanismos de coordinación humanitaria a nivel nacional, regional y local, incluyendo Grupos Sectoriales/Clusters u otros espacios relevantes, compartiendo información sobre necesidades, brechas, avances y prioridades de intervención.
- Cuando sea requerido coordinar con autoridades competentes, organizaciones humanitarias y actores comunitarios para evitar duplicaciones, promover complementariedades y asegurar una respuesta oportuna e integrada.
- Participar en los espacios de coordinación dentro de DRC con los equipos de otros sectores programáticos como EcRec y Protección, para garantizar la implementación integrada con una planificación adecuada de las actividades.

**Transversales**

- Representar a la organización de manera profesional y ética en todas las actividades realizadas, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos, la adecuada gestión de la información y la seguridad de la documentación del proyecto.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el especialista WASI.
- Realizar las actividades de campo conforme a los procedimientos de seguridad, acceso humanitario y gestión de riesgos de la organización, reportando oportunamente incidentes, restricciones y cambios en el contexto operacional.
- Garantizar que todas las actividades incorporen los enfoques de protección, inclusión, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP), prevención de la explotación y abuso sexual (PSEA) y participación comunitaria.

**Experiencia y competencias técnicas:**

- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia en la implementación de programas humanitarios de Shelter y/o infraestructura comunitaria.
- Conocimiento de los estándares nacionales y humanitarios aplicables al sector.
- Experiencia en supervisión de obras, contratistas y actividades de construcción o rehabilitación.
- Buen manejo de normas, estándares y prácticas sobre obras de construcción.
- Título universitario en Ingeniería Civil o Arquitectura. Se valorará experiencia demostrable en programas humanitarios de WASH, Shelter e Infraestructura.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas (Microsoft Office) y experiencia en recolección y gestión de datos mediante plataformas digitales como Kobo Toolbox o similares.
- Capacidad de coordinación con autoridades locales, organizaciones humanitarias y líderes comunitarios.
