jobs.title: Humanitarian Access and Safety Manager Haiti
jobs.description:
Tous les employés du NRC doivent travailler conformément aux valeurs de l'organisation. Être dévoué, innovant, inclusif et responsable sont des attitudes et des convictions qui doivent guider nos actions et nos relations. NRC s'engage en faveur de la sécurité et du bien-être et, ensemble, nous construisons une culture de travail positive pour se sentir valorisé, responsabilisé, soutenu, en sécurité et avoir un sentiment d'appartenance. Le NRC ne tolère pas que des employés exploitent ou abusent des gens et a une tolérance zéro face à l'inaction.

## Contexte

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés (NRC) est une organisation humanitaire indépendante qui apporte une aide d’urgence et un accompagnement à long terme aux personnes contraintes de fuir, et défend leurs droits.

En Haïti, la violence armée, les catastrophes naturelles et la dégradation de la situation économique aggravent les besoins humanitaires et limitent l’accès à l’aide. En janvier 2026, l’OIM estimait à 1,45 million le nombre de personnes déplacées à l’intérieur du pays. NRC intervient dans la zone métropolitaine de Port-au-Prince et dans l’Artibonite dans les domaines de l’éducation en situation d’urgence, de la protection contre les violences, de l’assistance juridique et de la réponse d’urgence.

Pour accompagner le développement de la mission, NRC recrute un ou une Responsable de l’accès humanitaire et de la sécurité (HAS Manager). La personne recrutée pilotera la stratégie d’accès humanitaire et la gestion des risques de sécurité, conseillera la direction sur l’évolution du contexte et accompagnera les équipes pour maintenir l’accès aux populations tout en veillant à la sécurité du personnel.

Rôles et responsabilités

## Le responsable de l'accès et de la sécurité humanitaires (HAS) soutient l'équipe pays dans la mise en œuvre et le maintien de ses activités dans le pays et permet une réponse humanitaire basée sur des principes et de manière sûre pour les communautés et les partenaires avec lesquels nous travaillons et notre personnel. Le rôle fournit un accès, un soutien en matière de sûreté et de sécurité, des conseils et une formation aux opérations du NRC en Haïti et rend compte au Directeur.rice Pays, avec une ligne technique avec le conseiller régional de HAS. Le responsable HAS peut également contribuer à la gestion des budgets HAS et doit collaborer avec l'équipe People and Organisation (P&O) pour s'assurer que le devoir de diligence est respecté.

- Soutenir la mise en œuvre et la conformité du système de gestion de l'accès humanitaire et de la sécurité (HAS) du NRC, y compris le respect des politiques et procédures HAS mondiales et spécifiques aux pays.
- Soutenir le Directeur.rice Pays dans la mise en œuvre du système de gestion HAS global de NRC au niveau national, préparer les rapports nécessaires et exécuter le plan opérationnel HAS.
- Contribuer à une culture permettant une réponse humanitaire sûre et fondée sur des principes et soutenir la mise en œuvre de normes minimales de programmation sûre et inclusive.
- Soutenir le Directeur.rice Pays et le Country Management Group (CMG) dans l’analyse contextuelle. Préparer et soumettre des rapports de situation et des analyses liés à la sécurité et à l’accès selon les besoins de la direction.
- Contribuer à l'élaboration des documents HAS au niveau des pays, y compris les plans d'urgence, les stratégies d'accès et les procédures opérationnelles standard (POS) adaptées au contexte, conformément aux normes organisationnelles, et veiller à ce qu'ils soient effectivement mis en œuvre dans tous les domaines d'activité du NRC.
- Soutenir le Directeur.rice Pays dans la réalisation d'évaluations des risques de sécurité et d'accès, y compris les évaluations rapides des risques pour les nouveaux sites opérationnels, et collaborer avec la direction pour mettre en œuvre des mesures d'atténuation pertinentes et soutenir une programmation sûre, en mettant l'accent sur le bureau de pays.

Veuillez trouver la[ Job Description -HAS Manager Haiti ](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQA5WLzOool5SrRcN9ZvtiIWAd_qPH7s-_yJLRRSmJX0Rls?e=icBlFO)

Compétences professionnelles pour ce poste

Compétences professionnelles générales :

• Au moins 3 ans d'expérience dans un rôle similaire en Haïti.

• Expérience antérieure dans des contextes complexes et instables. Une expérience à l’international constitut un atout

• Expérience avérée dans l'exercice des responsabilités du poste, notamment en matière de gestion des risques et d’encadrement d’équipe.

• Connaissance du style/profil de leadership.

• La maîtrise de l'anglais parlé et écrit, du français et du créole haïtien est exigée.

• Une expérience antérieure de la formation à la sécurité et/ou aux accès est considérée comme un atout.

Compétences, connaissances et expérience spécifiques au contexte :

• Bonne connaissance du contexte haïtien et des contraintes d’accès humanitaire et de sécurité.

• Expérience avérée en analyse de contexte et capacité à traduire cette analyse en recommandations opérationnelles.

• Capacité à conduire ou à appuyer des négociations d’accès humanitaire, à établir des relations de confiance et à coordonner efficacement avec des interlocuteurs variés, dans le respect des principes humanitaires et du cadre d’engagement de NRC.

• Capacité à anticiper les difficultés, à prendre des initiatives et à alerter la direction en temps utile.

Compétences comportementales

• Gérer les ressources pour optimiser les résultats.

• Gérer la performance et accompagner le développement de l’équipe.

• Analyser les situations et faire preuve de discernement, y compris lorsque les informations sont incomplètes.

• Garder son sang-froid sous pression et savoir hiérarchiser les urgences dans des environnements à risque.

• S’adapter à l’évolution du contexte et des priorités.

• Travailler efficacement au sein d’équipes multiculturelles et pluridisciplinaires.

• Faire preuve d’écoute, de tact et de diplomatie dans les échanges sensibles, et traiter les informations confidentielles avec discrétion.

Ce que nous offrons

- Duty station: Port-au-Prince, Haiti
- Contract: fixed national contract signed with ECSI 12 months (renewable subject to funding and performance)
- Travel: 40% to areas of intervention
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Apprenez sur les avantages de travailler avec NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

**Informations importantes:**

- Pour postuler en tant que candidat interne, connectez-vous avec votre adresse électronique officielle ou cliquez sur Opportunity MarketPlace.

- Si vous avez des questions sur ce rôle, veuillez envoyer un e-mail à aela.recruitment@nrc.no avec le titre du poste comme objet.

**Pourquoi NRC?**

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés (NRC) est une organisation humanitaire indépendante qui vient en aide aux personnes contraintes de fuir. Nos 15 000 collaborateurs travaillent lors de crises dans 40 pays, apportant chaque année une assistance vitale et à long terme à des millions de personnes.

Regardez [cette courte vidéo](https://vimeo.com/736782633) pour voir NRC en action.

- effectuer un travail exigeant et professionnel, souvent dans des contextes difficiles
- rejoignez une culture de travail qui permet à chaque employé de partager des idées et d'assumer ses responsabilités

### About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: PIR Caseworker
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency . The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired; including Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation: ($21.00 - $23.00 / hour).** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.”

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator Delegate (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
The Austrian Red Cross (AutRC) is seeking an experienced and committed **Programme Coordinator** to join the Joint Delegation of the Austrian and Finnish Red Cross (AutRC/FinRC) in Kyiv, Ukraine. Working closely with the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and partners within the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, you will help translate humanitarian priorities into effective programmes supporting conflict-affected communities.

**Your mission**

- Serve as the primary AutRC/FinRC counterpart to URCS programme departments, including health and social care, civil protection and disaster management, and livelihoods, and provide input into planning, budgeting and prioritisation processes.
- Oversee and support regional programme staff, ensuring clear priorities, effective programme implementation and strengthened staff capacity.
- Coordinate the implementation, monitoring and reporting of AutRC/FinRC-supported programmes in close collaboration with project managers, PMER and finance teams.
- Oversee grant management, ensuring high-quality proposals, budgets and donor reports, as well as transparent and compliant use of financial resources.
- Ensure that cross-cutting priorities, including protection and inclusion, are integrated across all programmes and activities.
- Maintain a regular field presence through visits to programme locations.
- Represent AutRC/FinRC with Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners and external organizations, contributing to coordination and knowledge sharing through established mechanisms and networks.
- Represent the Country Representative in her/his absence, as required.

**Your Profil**

- EU work permit is required.
- At least five years’ experience in operational management in international humanitarian and/or development programming (NGO, IO or charity).
- Experience within the Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement is a strong asset.
- Experience in one or more core areas of cooperation with URCS is a strong asset: health and social services, civil protection, disaster management, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH).
- University degree or diploma in international development, business management or another relevant discipline.
- Proven experience in supporting a National Society or local partner in programme development and management, including assessments, design, implementation, monitoring and reporting.
- Core competencies for all delegate positions: National Society relations, teamwork, results orientation, communication, trust-building, integrity, and diversity and cultural sensitivity.
- Role-specific competencies: self-motivation, critical and analytical thinking, excellent coordination and negotiation skills, strong time management, and ability to travel frequently to programme locations.
- Strong motivation for humanitarian and development work, commitment to Red Cross values and principles, and sensitivity to diversity. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.
- Solid skills in donor reporting, accountability and compliance.
- Capacity-building, facilitation and presentation skills, with the ability to build strong interpersonal relationships.
- Ability to work under pressure in a demanding security environment.
- Very good English skills; Ukrainian, Russian and German skills are an asset.

**We offer**

- Location: Kyiv, Ukraine, with in-country travel as required.
- Start date: 1 March 2027.
- Contract duration: one year, with the possibility of extension.
- Working hours: full-time.
- Compensation: minimum € 3.812,70 gross per month, depending on qualifications and experience, plus applicable hardship allowance.
- Accommodation: provided in Ukraine by AutRC/FinRC.

jobs.title: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR) Regional Climate, Environmental & Anticipatory Action Modelling Consultant
jobs.description:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR)**

**Regional Climate, Environmental & Anticipatory Action Modelling Consultant**

**REF: PD-RLC-01288**

**Summary Table**

**Position Tittle**

Regional Climate, Environmental and Anticipatory Action Modelling Consultant

**Donor**

Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations of the European Commission (DG ECHO)

**Contract Type**

Consultancy

**Primary Program & Role**

IMPAACT: Institutionalizing Interoperable Multi-Hazard Preparedness and Anticipatory Action

**Contract Duration**

10 months contract duration to be executed on a phased approach over the program period.

**Program Period**

1st December 2026 – 30th April 2028

**Geographic Coverage**

Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti with strong regional-level engagement

**Duty Station**

Regional /HEARO-Nairobi

**Reports to**

IMPAACT Consortium Coordinator

**Technical Coordination**

ACF regional and country technical teams; IMPAACT Data Analyst, IGAD/ICPAC; local partners and relevant national institutions

1. **Background**

Action Against Hunger leads the global movement to end hunger. We innovate solutions, advocate for change, and reach millions of people every year with proven hunger prevention and treatment programmes. As a non-profit organisation working across multiple countries, Action Against Hunger partners with communities to address the root causes of hunger, including climate change, conflict, inequity and emergencies. We strive to create a world free from hunger, for everyone, for good.

Action Against Hunger-USA (ACF-USA) is an independent international NGO and is part of the Action Against Hunger International Network, which provides humanitarian relief in over 50 countries worldwide in Nutrition, Health, WASH, FSL and MHPSS, Gender & Protection sectors. Action Against Hunger-USA currently manages operations in 8 countries: Kenya, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Ethiopia, Somalia, Zambia and Haiti. It has over $100 million in programs, and approximately 2,000 staff based in various country offices and the three Head Quarters Locations namely New York City, Washington D.C, and Nairobi.

1. ## Summary of the consultancy

Action Against Hunger (ACF), in consortium with the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC), is implementing a DG ECHO-funded regional disaster preparedness program, Institutionalizing Interoperable Multi-Hazard Preparedness and Anticipatory Action (IMPAACT), across Ethiopia, Somalia, and Djibouti. The program aims to strengthen interoperable, government-owned, and community-responsive systems for multi-hazard disaster preparedness and anticipatory action by operationalizing the SCALAA methodology and IGAD Anticipatory Action Roadmap through four interdependent result areas. These include strengthening early warning and anticipatory action protocols, standard operating procedures (SOPs), cross-border triggers, preparedness and contingency planning, and Crisis Modifier arrangements.

Achieving these objectives requires specialized technical expertise in climate and environmental risk analysis, anticipatory action modelling, trigger development and validation, and the integration of early-warning information into operational decision-making. The **Regional Climate, Environmental and Anticipatory Action Modelling Specialist/Consultant** will therefore provide targeted, time-bound technical support, working closely with ACF, IGAD/ICPAC, and relevant country-level stakeholders and consortium partners to ensure that climate and environmental risk information is translated into scientifically robust, context-specific, and operationally actionable anticipatory action mechanisms. The consultancy will also support the consistent integration of environmental considerations and compliance with DG ECHO’s Minimum Environmental Requirements across relevant program interventions. In addition, this specialized expertise is essential to safeguarding the scientific rigor and validation of trigger thresholds, ensuring consistent application of environmental requirements, and enabling the program to contribute meaningfully to ICPAC’s regional early-warning products, the SCALAA trigger harmonization framework, and the broader evidence base on climate-informed anticipatory action. Without this support, the technical credibility and regional added value of the program could be significantly constrained, limiting its ability to strengthen interoperable, evidence-based, and risk-informed anticipatory action systems across Ethiopia, Somalia, and Djibouti.

**Purpose:** To provide specialized regional expertise in climate science, environmental risk analysis, and anticipatory action modelling to strengthen multi-hazard early warning, risk analysis, preparedness, and anticipatory action under the IMPAACT program, translating regional and national climate information into scientifically robust, practical, and timely operational decisions.

**Engagement**: the consultant is expected to engage directly with IGAD/ICPAC, national meteorological and hydrological services, FAO modelling teams, National DRM authorities including EDMRC, SODMA, NDRMC, CIGRC, ONARS and SSMD, IGAD AA TWG, IGAD Prepare, FEWS NET, IPC, SCALAA project team and humanitarian coordination platforms, ensuring climate intelligence is systematically embedded in operational preparedness and early warning systems.

**Delivery**: the consultant is expected to deliver technically sound, operationally relevant and context-sensitive climate and environmental outputs including calibrated trigger matrices, validated modelling products, risk assessments, capacity-strengthening tools, NEAT+ screenings and scientific briefs, that can support Early Action Protocols and Anticipatory Action Plans directly applied to protect vulnerable populations across the Horn of Africa, including the three IMPAACT targeted countries. A summary of the indicative, time-bound deliverables expected during the consultancy period is provided in Section 5.

1. ## Overall and Specific Objectives

**Overall objective:** Strengthen the operational use of climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information within IMPAACT preparedness and anticipatory action processes through an integrated, decision-support model product that builds on and adds value to existing IGAD/ICPAC forecasting and multi-hazard modelling capabilities, while strengthening regional-to-national linkages and translating risk information into actionable early-warning and anticipatory action decisions.

## Specific Objectives:

1. Develop a complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product(s) that build on existing IGAD/ICPAC climate forecasting, environmental monitoring and multi-hazard modelling capabilities, adding value through enhanced risk interpretation, impact-oriented analysis and the translation of existing information into operational preparedness and anticipatory action decisions.
2. Strengthen the integration and application of existing regional climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information within IMPAACT preparedness, early-warning and anticipatory action processes, avoiding duplication of existing modelling initiatives and promoting coherence across regional and national systems.
3. Support the review, contextualization and refinement of hazard-specific indicators, risk thresholds and forecast-based triggers, ensuring their relevance to national and local risk contexts and their compatibility with existing IGAD/ICPAC multi-hazard frameworks and products.
4. Provide technical interpretation and value-added analysis of seasonal, sub-seasonal and other relevant climate and environmental information, including the assessment of forecast probabilities, uncertainty, potential impacts and implications for operational decision-making.
5. Strengthen the translation and interoperability of regional climate and multi-hazard information into national and country-level early-warning, disaster risk management, preparedness and anticipatory action systems, including through tailored decision-support products and operational guidance.
6. Support the application of existing regional multi-hazard modelling outputs to strengthen cross-border and transboundary preparedness and anticipatory action, with particular attention to compounding, cascading and interconnected climate and environmental risks.
7. Strengthen institutional and stakeholder capacities to interpret, contextualize and operationalize existing climate forecasts, multi-hazard risk information, environmental indicators, forecast probabilities and uncertainty in support of evidence-based preparedness and anticipatory action.

## 4. Scope of Work

1. ### Climate and Environmental Risk Analysis
2. Review and synthesize existing regional and national climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information, models and analytical products relevant to Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti, drawing on available IGAD/ICPAC and other relevant institutional capabilities and resources.
3. Map and assess existing regional and national climate and environmental datasets, forecasting products, early-warning systems, multi-hazard models and monitoring mechanisms to identify opportunities for integration, complementarity and operational application within IMPAACT.
4. Assess priority climate and environmental hazards, their seasonal and spatial characteristics, and potential compounding, cascading and transboundary impacts across the three countries.
5. Identify critical information, analytical and operational gaps in existing risk assessment and early-warning systems, particularly those affecting the translation of regional forecasts and multi-hazard information into national and sub-national preparedness and anticipatory action.
6. Support the contextualization and refinement of existing climate and environmental risk profiles, drawing on available assessments and models, rather than developing parallel products, to strengthen their relevance for operational decision-making and anticipatory action.
1. ### Early Warning, Thresholds and Triggers
7. Review and assess existing regional and national early-warning indicators, risk thresholds, forecast-based triggers and associated decision-making protocols for priority climate and environmental hazards, drawing on existing IGAD/ICPAC frameworks, multi-hazard models and national early-warning systems.
8. Support the identification, contextualization and refinement of relevant climate and environmental indicators, thresholds and forecast-based triggers for priority hazards, ensuring they are informed by existing regional forecasting capabilities, national risk profiles, historical impacts and local vulnerability contexts.
9. Strengthen the linkage between forecast information, hazard thresholds, anticipated impacts and pre-agreed preparedness and anticipatory actions, including consideration of appropriate forecast lead times, probability levels, decision windows and institutional responsibilities.
10. Support the technical assessment, validation and calibration of existing triggers using historical climate and hazard data, forecast performance, observed impacts and operational experience, with particular attention to forecast uncertainty, false alarms and missed events.
11. Promote consistency and interoperability between regional and national early-warning indicators, thresholds and trigger-setting approaches, ensuring that regional climate and multi-hazard information can effectively inform country-level decision-making without duplicating or undermining existing institutional mechanisms.
12. Support the documentation and operationalization of agreed indicators, thresholds and triggers through practical guidance, decision-support tools and standard operating procedures that facilitate timely, evidence-based and coordinated anticipatory action.
13. Integrate validated indicators, thresholds and anticipatory action triggers into the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product, building on existing IGAD/ICPAC forecasting and multi-hazard modelling outputs to strengthen the translation of regional risk information into actionable national and sub-national early-warning and anticipatory action decisions.
1. ### Integration into EAPs, SOPs and Preparedness Planning
14. Provide technical inputs to the development, review and refinement of existing Early Action Protocols (EAPs), Anticipatory Action (AA) frameworks, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), contingency plans, preparedness plans and Crisis Modifier arrangements, ensuring that they adequately incorporate relevant climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information.
15. Support the integration and contextualization of regional climate forecasts, multi-hazard modelling outputs, environmental risk indicators and validated thresholds and triggers into existing country-level EAPs, SOPs and preparedness planning frameworks for Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti.
16. Strengthen the linkage between risk information, forecast-based thresholds and triggers, institutional decision-making processes and pre-agreed anticipatory actions, ensuring clarity on decision points, activation procedures, lead times, institutional responsibilities and implementation arrangements.
17. Support the alignment of regional early-warning and multi-hazard risk information with national and sub-national preparedness and anticipatory action mechanisms, promoting coherence between IGAD/ICPAC technical products and country-level operational frameworks.
18. Provide technical guidance on integrating evolving climate and environmental risk information, including compounding and cascading hazards, into contingency planning, scenario development, preparedness reviews and Crisis Modifier activation arrangements.
19. Support the development and refinement of practical decision-support tools, trigger-to-action matrices and operational guidance to facilitate the consistent translation of early-warning information into timely, coordinated and evidence-based preparedness and anticipatory actions.
20. Promote the use of the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product to inform EAPs, SOPs and preparedness planning, ensuring that existing regional forecasting and multi-hazard modelling capabilities are translated into context-specific operational decisions and actions.
1. ### Seasonal and Emerging Climate and Environmental Risk Analysis
21. Monitor, review and interpret relevant seasonal, sub-seasonal and other emerging climate and environmental information during agreed deployment periods, drawing on existing regional and national forecasting, monitoring and early-warning systems.
22. Provide technical interpretation and contextualization of ICPAC/GHACOF climate outlooks, National Meteorological and Hydrological Services (NMHS) products and other relevant regional and international climate information to assess their implications for preparedness and anticipatory action in Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti.
23. Translate climate forecasts, evolving climate signals, forecast probabilities and associated uncertainties into concise, country-specific operational risk assessments, scenario analyses and actionable preparedness recommendations, taking into account hazard exposure, vulnerability and potential impacts.
24. Provide timely technical analysis of emerging climate drivers and events, including El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and other relevant ocean-atmosphere interactions, assessing their potential influence on rainfall patterns, drought, flooding and other climate-related hazards across the three countries.
25. Prioritize early technical support and targeted risk analysis of the evolving El Niño-related climate context, including the assessment of potential and evolving impacts, associated uncertainties, seasonal variations and implications for existing preparedness plans, early-warning thresholds and anticipatory action triggers in Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti.
26. Support the translation of emerging seasonal and sub-seasonal climate information into recommendations for reviewing and adjusting existing EAPs, SOPs, contingency plans, Crisis Modifier arrangements and preparedness priorities, where changing risk conditions warrant such adjustments.
27. Feed relevant seasonal and emerging risk analysis into the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product, ensuring that evolving climate information and regional forecasting outputs are reflected in operational risk intelligence and decision-support processes.

### 4.5 Multi-Hazard, Cross-Border and Interoperability Support

1. Support the interpretation and application of existing regional and national multi-hazard risk assessments and modelling outputs, with particular attention to interactions, compounding and cascading effects between climate and environmental hazards and other relevant risks.
2. Analyse the spatial and temporal dimensions of transboundary climate and environmental risks across Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti, identifying shared vulnerabilities, interconnected risk patterns and implications for coordinated preparedness and anticipatory action.
3. Support the identification and contextualization of priority cross-border hazards, indicators, risk thresholds and anticipatory action triggers, promoting consistency and complementarity between national systems and existing regional early-warning and multi-hazard frameworks.
4. Strengthen interoperability between regional and national climate, environmental and multi-hazard information systems by supporting the harmonization, exchange and operational application of relevant datasets, forecasts, risk assessments and early-warning products.
5. Contribute technical inputs towards strengthening cross-border information-sharing, coordination and decision-making arrangements, ensuring that regional risk information can effectively inform national and sub-national preparedness and anticipatory action processes.
6. Support the translation of regional multi-hazard modelling and early-warning outputs into practical cross-border risk intelligence, scenario analyses and decision-support products that inform coordinated preparedness planning and anticipatory action.
7. Where relevant, coordinate with existing Action Against Hunger and regional early-warning and anticipatory analytics initiatives, including Modeling Early Risk Indicators to Anticipate Malnutrition (MERIAM), to identify opportunities for technical complementarity, leverage relevant evidence and analytical outputs, and avoid duplication of ongoing work.
8. Ensure that relevant findings and insights from existing regional initiatives, including MERIAM where applicable, inform the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product without replicating their modelling methodologies, analytical processes or deliverables.
9. ### Capacity Strengthening, Monitoring and Learning
10. Develop practical, simplified and user-friendly technical guidance, tools and training materials to strengthen the capacity of Action Against Hunger (ACF) teams and relevant partners to understand, interpret and operationalize climate and environmental information, including seasonal and sub-seasonal forecasts, forecast probabilities, uncertainty, multi-hazard risk information, indicators, thresholds and anticipatory action triggers.
11. Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of ACF at regional and country levels to interpret, contextualize and apply existing regional and national climate forecasting and multi-hazard modelling products, particularly those generated by IGAD/ICPAC and National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, and translate them into program-level preparedness and anticipatory action decisions.
12. Facilitate targeted technical training sessions, knowledge-sharing engagements and practical learning exercises for ACF teams and relevant institutional partners, focusing on the application of climate and environmental risk information in programme planning, early warning, preparedness and anticipatory action.
13. Support the development and application of appropriate indicators and monitoring frameworks to assess the extent to which climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information is integrated into ACF programme planning, preparedness processes, early-warning mechanisms and anticipatory action decision-making.
14. Contribute to monitoring the operational uptake and application of the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product, including its relevance, accessibility, usability and contribution to risk-informed programme planning and operational decision-making.
15. Document good practices, operational experiences, lessons learned and challenges associated with the interpretation and application of climate and environmental information, including the effectiveness of risk thresholds, triggers and trigger-to-action mechanisms.
16. Facilitate periodic technical reviews and learning engagements to assess the practical application and effectiveness of climate-informed preparedness and anticipatory action approaches, identifying opportunities for refinement and improvement.
17. Provide recommendations for strengthening ACF's institutional systems, technical capacities, coordination mechanisms and information-sharing arrangements to ensure the sustained integration of climate and environmental risk intelligence into existing programme, preparedness and anticipatory action frameworks.

**Key Deliverables:**

Through effective collaboration and the application of specialized expertise in climate science, environmental risk analysis, multi-hazard risk assessment, early warning and anticipatory action, the Regional Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Modelling Specialist (Consultant) will provide technical leadership and support to strengthen IMPAACT's multi-hazard risk monitoring, preparedness and anticipatory action systems across Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti. Key deliverables will include an inception report and detailed technical workplan; a comprehensive review of existing regional and national climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information, models, datasets and early-warning systems; development and operationalization of a complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product that builds on and adds value to existing IGAD/ICPAC and national forecasting and multi-hazard modelling capabilities; technical review, refinement and validation of risk indicators, thresholds, forecast-based triggers, EAPs, SOPs, contingency plans and preparedness arrangements; periodic seasonal, sub-seasonal and emerging climate risk analyses and operational preparedness advisories, including assessment of relevant El Niño-related risks and implications; technical inputs to strengthen multi-hazard, cross-border and regional-to-national interoperability and information-sharing arrangements; development of practical, simplified guidance and delivery of targeted capacity-strengthening sessions to enhance ACF's institutional capacity to interpret and operationalize climate and environmental information; periodic technical reviews and monitoring of the application of climate information in programme decision-making; and a final technical learning report documenting achievements, lessons learned, recommendations, sustainability arrangements and handover of agreed technical outputs. All activities will prioritize complementarity with existing regional and national initiatives, including coordination with relevant Action Against Hunger initiatives such as MERIAM, without duplicating its modelling activities or deliverables. A detailed deliverables evaluation matrix, specifying expected outputs, results, means of verification (MoV), acceptance criteria and corresponding timelines, will be shared with the selected consultant during the inception meeting to establish clear performance expectations and a framework for monitoring progress and assessing deliverable completion.Summary of

**Key Deliverables and Indicative Timeline**

**Deliverable / Output and Indicative Timing**

1.Inception report and detailed technical workplan, including methodology, stakeholder mapping and implementation arrangements- December 2026

2\. Climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk and systems assessment, including review of existing IGAD/ICPAC and national capabilities, identification of gaps and development of the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product - December 2026 to February 2027

**3.**Technical review and refinement of early-warning indicators, thresholds and triggers, including technical inputs to EAPs, SOPs, contingency plans and preparedness arrangements- December 2026 to March 2027, with continued support as required

**4.** Seasonal and emerging climate risk analyses and operational preparedness advisories, including El Niño-related risk assessments, forecast interpretation and anticipatory action recommendations. - December 2026 to September 2027

**5.** Multi-hazard, cross-border and interoperability technical support, including regional-to-national information-sharing, coordination and alignment of early-warning and anticipatory action approaches- December 2026 to September 2027

**6.** Capacity-strengthening, periodic technical reviews and preparedness support, including simplified guidance, training sessions, trigger refinement, monitoring and operational learning - December 2026 to September 2027

**7.** Final technical learning report and close-out package, including lessons learned, model product documentation, sustainability recommendations and handover of technical outputs- September to November 2027

*Note: The indicative timelines will be further refined during the inception phase in consultation with ACF, IGAD/ICPAC and relevant partners. Deliverables will be implemented progressively, with periodic reviews and technical support throughout the consultancy. All modelling and analytical activities will complement existing regional and national capabilities, without duplicating IGAD/ICPAC or MERIAM-specific modelling activities and deliverables.*

## 6. Indicative Consultancy Phasing and Level of Effort

The assignment will comprise a maximum cumulative level of effort equivalent to 10 consultancy months, delivered intermittently across the indicative deployment phases outlined below. The consultancy will be structured around key technical priorities, seasonal climate risk cycles, programme milestones and emerging preparedness and anticipatory action needs. The deployment periods do not necessarily constitute continuous full-time engagement, but will allow for targeted technical inputs, periodic monitoring, analytical support and follow-up as required.

**Phase**

**Main Focus Areas**

**Indicative Timing**

**A**. Inception and Systems Assessment

Inception report and workplan; stakeholder and institutional mapping; review of existing regional and national climate, environmental and multi-hazard risk information, models and early-warning systems; identification of analytical gaps and development of the complementary Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product framework -December 2026 to February 2027

**B**. Priority Risk Analysis and Operational Preparedness Support

Priority seasonal and emerging climate risk analysis, including El Niño-related implications; technical review and refinement of indicators, thresholds and triggers; technical inputs to EAPs, SOPs, contingency plans and preparedness arrangements; initial operational risk advisories- December 2026 to March 2027

**C**. Seasonal Monitoring and Anticipatory Action Support - Continued seasonal and sub-seasonal climate monitoring and interpretation; operational preparedness advisories; trigger validation and refinement; application of the model product; technical support to programme-level preparedness and anticipatory action decisions- March to May 2027

**D**. Capacity Strengthening and Regional-National Integration

Strengthening ACF's institutional capacity through simplified technical guidance and targeted training; multi-hazard and cross-border risk analysis; regional-to-national interoperability and information-sharing support; periodic technical reviews and support to subsequent preparedness cycles - June to August 2027

**E**. Consolidation, Learning and Sustainability

Consolidation and documentation of technical outputs; review of model product application and operational uptake; lessons learned; sustainability and institutional ownership recommendations; final technical report and handover of agreed deliverables- September to November 2027

**Implementation and deployment arrangements:** The detailed allocation of consultancy inputs, deployment schedules, deliverable evaluation matrix, means of verification and acceptance criteria will be finalized during the inception phase in consultation with ACF, IGAD/ICPAC and relevant partners. The phasing and allocation of technical inputs may be adjusted within the approved maximum level of effort to accommodate evolving climate and environmental risks, seasonal forecasting cycles, emerging El Niño-related developments, critical programme milestones and priority operational requirements. Such adjustments will be agreed with ACF in consultation with relevant technical partners, including IGAD/ICPAC, as appropriate.

## 7. Methodology:

**Methodological Approach**

The consultancy will adopt a phased, collaborative, evidence-based and operationally oriented approach, focusing on building on existing regional and national climate forecasting, environmental monitoring and multi-hazard modelling capabilities and translating available information into practical preparedness and anticipatory action decisions. The approach will comprise the following key elements:

- Desk Review and Systems Assessment: Review existing programme documents, climate and environmental risk assessments, multi-hazard models, forecasts, early-warning products, EAPs, SOPs and preparedness frameworks to identify existing capabilities, gaps and opportunities for complementarity.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination: Engage ACF regional and country teams, IGAD/ICPAC, National Meteorological and Hydrological Services and other relevant stakeholders to understand information needs, institutional capacities and operational priorities.
- Climate and Multi-Hazard Risk Analysis: Interpret existing climate forecasts, environmental information and multi-hazard risk assessments to identify priority hazards, emerging risks, seasonal patterns and potential compounding, cascading and cross-border impacts across Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti.
- Development of a Complementary Model Product: Develop an integrated Climate, Environment and Anticipatory Action Model Product that builds on existing regional and national modelling and forecasting capabilities, adding value through risk interpretation, contextualization, impact analysis and operational decision support rather than duplicating existing systems.
- Early-Warning and Preparedness Integration: Review and support the refinement of existing indicators, thresholds, triggers, EAPs, SOPs, contingency plans and Crisis Modifier arrangements to strengthen the link between climate information, risk monitoring, institutional decision-making and pre-agreed anticipatory actions.
- Seasonal Risk Monitoring and Operational Advisories: Interpret seasonal, sub-seasonal and emerging climate information, including relevant El Niño-related developments, and translate forecast probabilities and uncertainty into practical risk assessments, preparedness recommendations and anticipatory action considerations.
- Cross-Border Coordination and Interoperability: Support the alignment and operational application of regional and national early-warning and multi-hazard information, strengthening cross-border information-sharing and coordinated preparedness and anticipatory action approaches while leveraging existing initiatives and avoiding duplication.
- Capacity Strengthening and Learning: Develop simplified technical guidance and facilitate targeted training and knowledge-sharing sessions to strengthen ACF's institutional capacity to understand, interpret and operationalize climate and environmental information. Document lessons and recommendations to improve future preparedness and anticipatory action.
- Technical Validation and Adaptive Review: Validate key analytical outputs and recommendations with ACF, IGAD/ICPAC and relevant stakeholders, and periodically review their operational relevance and application to ensure continuous improvement.

Guiding principle: The consultancy will prioritize complementarity, practical application and institutional capacity strengthening, ensuring that existing regional and national climate and multi-hazard information is translated into actionable risk intelligence, stronger preparedness and timely anticipatory action without creating parallel modelling or early-warning systems.

## 8. Required Qualifications and Experience:

The consultant should possess the following qualifications, technical competencies and professional experience:

- **Education:** Advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in climatology, meteorology, climate science, environmental science, hydrology, data science, geospatial sciences, disaster risk management or another closely related discipline.
- **Professional Experience:** At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in climate services, climate and environmental risk analysis, multi-hazard early warning, disaster risk management, preparedness or anticipatory action.
- **Climate Risk Analysis and Interpretation**: Demonstrated experience interpreting seasonal, sub-seasonal and other climate forecasts and translating climate and environmental information into operational risk assessments, preparedness recommendations and decision-support products.
- **Forecasting and Climate Science**: Strong understanding of climate variability, seasonal forecasting, forecast probabilities, uncertainty, hydrometeorological hazards and relevant climate drivers, including ENSO.
- **Early Warning and Anticipatory Action:** Proven experience reviewing or developing early-warning indicators, risk thresholds, forecast-based triggers, Early Action Protocols (EAPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), contingency plans and anticipatory action frameworks.
- **Multi-Hazard Risk and Modelling**: Demonstrated experience applying existing climate, environmental and multi-hazard modelling outputs, analytical tools and datasets to strengthen risk interpretation, impact assessment and operational decision-making, with an understanding of how to complement existing modelling capabilities rather than duplicate them.
- **Regional and Country Context**: Strong knowledge of the Horn of Africa's climate, environmental and disaster-risk dynamics, particularly Ethiopia, Somalia and Djibouti. Experience working with IGAD/ICPAC, GHACOF, National Meteorological and Hydrological Services or other regional and national technical institutions is highly desirable.
- **Data Analysis and Geospatial Skills**: Practical experience with GIS, climate and environmental datasets, geospatial analysis and relevant statistical or analytical tools for climate risk monitoring and assessment.
- **Institutional Capacity Strengthening**: Demonstrated experience developing simplified technical guidance, facilitating training and strengthening institutional capacity to interpret and operationalize climate information for programme planning and anticipatory action.
- **Coordination and Communication**: Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation, analytical and technical writing skills, with the ability to communicate complex climate information and forecast uncertainty in accessible, practical and decision-oriented formats.
- **Language:** Excellent written and spoken English Knowledge of French and relevant regional languages is an added advantage.
- **Additional desirable qualification**: Experience working with humanitarian organizations, international NGOs or regional intergovernmental institutions, particularly in climate-informed humanitarian programming, environmental risk management and DG ECHO-funded programmes.

## 9. Coordination and Reporting:

**Coordination:** The consultant will work under the overall coordination of the IMPAACT Programme Consortium Coordinator, in close collaboration with the designated ACF and IGAD/ICPAC technical leads, who will serve as the principal technical focal points for the assignment and provide guidance on technical priorities, coordination arrangements and review and acceptance of deliverables. The consultant will maintain regular coordination with ACF regional and country teams, relevant IGAD/ICPAC technical units, National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, government institutions, local partners and other relevant IMPAACT technical personnel to ensure alignment with programme priorities, existing regional and national capabilities, and ongoing initiatives. Particular attention will be given to ensuring complementarity with existing climate forecasting, environmental monitoring and multi-hazard modelling initiatives, avoiding duplication while promoting the operational application of available technical outputs. The consultant will determine the professional approach and organization of the work within the agreed scope, methodology, level of effort, timelines and deliverables, while maintaining regular communication and reporting on progress, emerging risks and any required adjustments. All deliverables will be submitted for technical review and approval in accordance with the agreed consultancy workplan and deliverables evaluation matrix.

**Reporting:** The consultant will report on progress, technical findings, emerging climate and environmental risks, implementation challenges and recommendations through agreed reporting arrangements and periodic technical coordination meetings. All reports, analytical products, technical guidance materials and other outputs will be submitted to ACF for review and approval, with relevant technical validation and consultation involving IGAD/ICPAC and other stakeholders as appropriate.

**Expected reports and continuous engagement:**

- **Bi-weekly progress updates:** Submit brief written updates to the line manager every two weeks, highlighting key activities, progress against milestones, emerging issues, and required follow-up actions, supplemented by ad hoc meetings as needed.
- **Monthly progress reporting:** Submit a monthly written report to the line manager summarizing activities undertaken, progress against planned deliverables, key achievements, challenges, and planned next steps. Reports will be complemented by one-to-one virtual or in-person meetings, as appropriate.
- **End-of-assignment and final reporting:** Prepare and submit an end-of-assignment report to the office and line manager, documenting achievements, deliverable completion, key lessons learned, and recommendations in accordance with the agreed evaluation matrix.

## 10. Duration of the contract:

The consultancy will comprise a maximum cumulative level of effort equivalent to **10 consultancy months**, delivered through phased and intermittent technical inputs within the remaining IMPAACT program implementation period (1 December 2026 – 30 April 2028), commencing from the contract signing date. Given the programe's current implementation timeline and emerging climate and preparedness priorities, commencement of the assignment is expected to be prioritized for December 2026. The 10 consultancy months represent the total cumulative engagement period and do not necessarily imply continuous full-time deployment. The allocation of working days and technical inputs across the agreed deployment windows will be determined during the inception phase in consultation with ACF and relevant technical partners, taking into account seasonal climate risk cycles, programme milestones and emerging operational needs. The consultancy duration will be calculated in accordance with the agreed contractual terms, including the applicable treatment of weekends and public holidays, and will remain within the approved maximum level of effort.

**11. Consultancy Arrangement:**

This assignment will be undertaken as an independent professional consultancy and shall not constitute an employment relationship with Action Against Hunger (ACF). The consultant will be responsible for organizing, managing and delivering the agreed technical inputs and outputs within the approved scope of work, methodology, level of effort, timelines and deliverables. The consultancy will be output-oriented and delivered through phased and intermittent technical inputs, with no fixed daily working hours. However, the consultant will be expected to maintain regular coordination with ACF and relevant technical partners and participate in agreed consultations, technical meetings, workshops, coordination platforms and country or regional missions as necessary to ensure effective delivery of the assignment.

Professional fees will be paid in accordance with the consultancy contract and agreed payment schedule, subject to satisfactory completion, submission and formal acceptance of the agreed deliverables, as assessed against the approved deliverables evaluation matrix and applicable acceptance criteria, and submission of the required invoices. The consultant will be responsible for all applicable taxes, insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The assignment will not carry employee benefits, staff entitlements or other employment-related privileges and will conclude in accordance with the duration, conditions and termination provisions stipulated in the consultancy contract.

## 12. Application and Selection Process

This ToR serves as a call for applications from suitably qualified and experienced individual consultants. Interested applicants are invited to submit a technical and financial proposal demonstrating their relevant qualifications, professional experience, technical expertise and proposed approach to undertaking the assignment. The submitted proposals should address the requirements outlined in this ToR and include the requested supporting documentation. The specified application requirements and evaluation criteria will form the basis for assessing the submitted proposals and selecting the consultant, taking into consideration the applicant's technical competence, relevant regional experience, proposed methodology, understanding of the assignment and financial offer.

**Technical Proposal:**

2. A cover letter expressing interest and outlining relevant experience.
3. Technical proposal (Maximum 5 pages) outlining understanding of the assignment and proposed methodology.
4. Updated CV demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience.
5. Examples/references from comparable assignments.
6. Contact details for at least three professional references.
7. Confirmation of availability, particularly for the immediate deployment, preferably in November 2026.Disclosure of conflict of interest taking into consideration the specific provisions stated under section

**13: Consultancy arrangement.**

**Financial Proposal:**

The financial proposal shall include professional fees and applicable costs (inclusive of all taxes i.e. i.e. VAT and withholding tax)

1. Indicate a detailed breakdown of the calculated expert days.
2. The financial proposal should include any reimbursable costs, where applicable, indicated separately.
3. Quotation shall be in United States Dollars (USD).
4. Tax treatment shall follow applicable ACF and statutory requirements at contracting stage.

**14. Evaluation**

The proposal shall be evaluated as follows: -

1. Technical proposal – 70%
2. Financial proposal - 30%
