**الوصف الوظيفي**

المسمى الوظيفي: مثقف/ة صحي/ة

مكان العمل: سوريا - حمص - المركز الصحي الأولي في الضبعة

يقدم تقاريره إلى: منسق المشروع

**نطاق المسؤولية:**

تنفيذ حملات التوعية الصحية في المركز الصحي الأولي، ومن خلال زيارات المجتمع المحلي والأماكن العامة.

**المهام والمسؤوليات:**

يتولى المثقف الصحي المهام والمسؤوليات التالية:

1\. تنفيذ حملات توعية مستمرة في المركز وفي المرافق العامة، مثل المدارس وأماكن التجمعات المجتمعية.

2\. العمل كصلة وصل بين المستفيدين والخدمات المتوفرة في المركز.

3\. إجراء تقييمات الهشاشة وتحديد الحالات المحتاجة وفق معايير محددة مسبقاً.

ويتركز العمل على تغيير السلوك المجتمعي من خلال التقييم الدقيق للحالات، وتكييف الرسائل بما يناسب كل حالة.

4\. إدارة الحالات مع الالتزام ببروتوكولات الخصوصية والموافقة الفردية.

5\. إجراء الإحالات الداخلية والخارجية للحالات، وتحديث نماذج التغذية الراجعة والإحالة.

6\. تحديث ملفات الحالات بمساعدة الموظف الصحي، وضمان أمن المعلومات وسريتها.

7\. تنفيذ أنشطة الرعاية الصحية الوقائية والتوجيه حول الصحة الإنجابية، وتغذية حديثي الولادة والأطفال، والكشف المبكر عن سرطان الثدي، والنظافة الشخصية والمنزلية، ونظافة الأسنان، واللقاح.

8\. تقديم المشورة والتوجيه للحالات والمجموعات المجتمعية حول الفحوصات التشخيصية، مثل الكشف عن السرطان، ولطاخة عنق الرحم، وفحوصات الزرق (الغلوكوما)، والكشف عن السكري.

9\. تقديم جلسات تثقيفية للنساء الحوامل والأطفال.

10\. تقديم خدمات تنظيم الأسرة، وتعزيز الصحة والنظافة، والكشف عن الأمراض المعدية، وتنفيذ أنشطة التثقيف الصحي، وجمع الإحصائيات، وإحالة الحالات إلى خدمات الرعاية الصحية.

11\. تلبية الاحتياجات الأساسية مثل الإسعافات الأولية.

12\. زيارة مقدمي الخدمات لضمان تنفيذ أنشطة التدخل والتوعية والإحالة في مجال صحة المجتمع بفعالية.

13\. إعداد تقارير أسبوعية وشهرية عن الأنشطة والتدخلات وجلسات التوجيه وأنشطة رسم خرائط الخدمات المنفذة.

**المؤهلات والمهارات:**

يجب أن تتوفر لدى المتقدم المهارات والمؤهلات والخبرات التالية:

1\. شهادة جامعية أو شهادة معهد.

2\. يُفضّل وجود معرفة و/أو خبرة عملية في مجال تنمية صحة المجتمع.

3\. القدرة على تحديد الأولويات والتواصل الفعّال والالتزام بالمواعيد المحددة.

4\. خبرة في العمل ضمن فريق في مجال صحة المجتمع أو التغذية أو التدخلات الصحية ذات الصلة.

5\. معرفة ببرامج Microsoft Office مع إتقان جيد لبرنامج Excel.

6\. مهارات قيادة وتنسيق قوية.

7\. القدرة على العمل باستقلالية وضمن فريق.

8\. تُعد الخبرة السابقة مع المنظمات غير الحكومية في سياق مشابه ميزة إضافية.

jobs.title: Country Director – SYRIA, JORDAN, YEMEN
jobs.description:
**Location** – Damascus, Syria

**Position Status**: National and Expat, Full Time, Regular, Exempt

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [here](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

Mercy Corps is powered by the belief that a better world is possible. To do this, we know our teams do their best work when they are diverse, and every team member feels that they belong. We welcome diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be stronger and have long-term impact.

## **Program / Department Summary**

Mercy Corps implements a variety of programming throughout the AMEE region in response to the diverse humanitarian and long-term development needs of the region. Mercy Corps has ongoing programs in Syria, Jordan and Yemen.

Mercy Corps is committed to delivering high quality, high impact programming that reaches communities or individuals in need, wherever they are.

Mercy Corps just launched its new global ten-year strategy, ’Pathway to Prosperity’’, which reflects our ambitions to not only meet basic needs of communities affected by conflict and climate, but to achieve lasting, transformational change at scale. Pathway to Prosperity (P2P) includes a three-layers resilience approach at its core and aims to deliver impact through three key outcome areas: Addressing Urgent Needs, Accelerating Climate Solutions, Driving Economic and Food Security.

Mercy Corps AMEE Leadership has decided to optimize resources and create efficiencies by creating a new structure for smaller country portfolios under the management of a multi-country office. This role is the product of this structural change decision.

**General Position Summary**

The Country Director for Syria, Jordan, and Yemen is the senior leader accountable for the overall strategic direction, leadership, management, performance, risk and representation of Mercy Corps and the country portfolios under its oversight. The Country Director ensures that country strategies and operations are aligned with Mercy Corps’ regional and global strategic direction and that programs are delivered with quality, impact, accountability, compliance and appropriate stewardship of resources.

The Country Director provides integrated leadership across programs and support functions, including Finance, Operations, Human Resources, Security and Risk. The role establishes clear accountability and decision-making frameworks across geographically dispersed teams while ensuring that each country portfolio receives the level of leadership and support required by its context, size, risk profile and strategic priorities.

The Country Director leads the development and adaptation of country strategies, oversees program performance and business development, ensures strong financial and operational management, and maintains an effective risk and compliance environment. The role is responsible for ensuring that organizational structures, people strategies, systems and resources remain fit for purpose as portfolios evolve, including during scale-up, transition, close-out or changes in funding.

As Mercy Corps’ senior representative for the Syria, Jordan, and Yemen portfolio, the Country Director develops and maintains high-level relationships with donors, government counterparts, partners, peer organizations and other key stakeholders. The Country Director works closely with Regional Leadership and global teams to mobilize support, escalate material risks, and ensure that decisions are timely, evidence-based and aligned with organizational priorities.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

### STRATEGIC VISION & LEADERSHIP

- Provide overall strategic leadership and ensure that country strategies and operational plans are developed, regularly reviewed and adapted to changing contexts, funding environments, and organizational priorities.
- Ensure each country’s portfolio is aligned with Mercy Corps’ regional and global strategy and that strategic priorities guide programmatic, operational and resource-allocation decisions.
- Maintain a deep understanding of the political, social, economic, humanitarian, security and regulatory context across the countries and translate contextual analysis into strategic decisions.
- Lead strategic transitions, including scale-up, consolidation, restructuring, program closure and shifts between humanitarian, recovery and development programming, as relevant.
- Recognize opportunities for innovative action and create an environment in which diverse perspectives, evidence and learning inform decision-making.
- Ensure the countries maintain an appropriate operating model, leadership structure and level of support for the size, complexity and risk profile of each country portfolio.

### PROGRAM LEADERSHIP

- Provide overall leadership and accountability for the design, implementation, quality and performance of all programs.
- Ensure programs are delivered on scope, time and budget and in accordance with donor requirements, Mercy Corps policies, Program Management Minimum Standards and relevant technical and humanitarian standards.
- Ensure robust program review and performance-management systems provide leadership with timely information for decision-making, adaptation and risk management.
- Promote evidence-based and community-centered programming and ensure monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems are effectively used to demonstrate results and inform decisions.
- Ensure strong coordination between country teams, Regional Program and Technical teams, and global technical resources to strengthen program quality, technical coherence and learning.
- Ensure safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, Do No Harm, inclusion and other organizational commitments are embedded throughout program design and implementation.

### FIELD PROGRAM OVERSIGHT

- Supervise the Program team as well as all multi-Country support functions (HR, Operations, Finance, Security) as relevant to ensure close check and controls;
- Ensure strong communication and collaboration lines are maintained with the program field teams;
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all country programs, with regular visits to various countries and field offices, when possible;
- Ensure that learning from the field contributes to development and implementation of compelling evidence-based products to support business development and advocacy initiatives.

### PROGRAM QUALITY, EVIDENCE & LEARNING

- With the support of the Regional Program Teams (Business Development, Award Management, TRaQ and Evidence and Learning), support the program quality, evidence and learning teams (e.g. MEL, CARM) in establishing systems, policies and approaches necessary to ensure and demonstrate the quality of programs and incorporate learning into decision making;
- Ensure that proper Monitoring and Evaluation tools in line with Mercy Corps guidelines and policies are effectively used by the programs teams;
- Ensure that all the programs team members have received training in line with their level of responsibility and receive technical support relevant to their programs;
- Ensure strong coordination and collaboration is happening between Regional Technical teams and field teams to provide expert advice and ensure technical consistency and soundness across programs;
- Promote an evidence-driven culture, contributing to the establishment of the countries’ evidence and learning priorities, in line with the regional Evidence and Learning Agenda.

### BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT

- Lead and oversee business development strategies for the countries, ensuring that funding priorities are aligned with country strategies, organizational capabilities and intended impact.
- Build and maintain strategic donor relationships and position Mercy Corps for relevant funding and partnership opportunities.
- Lead or oversee go/no-go decisions, ensuring proposed opportunities are strategically relevant, operationally feasible, appropriately resourced and consistent with Mercy Corps’ risk appetite.
- Provide leadership and quality assurance for program design and proposal development, drawing on evidence, learning, technical expertise and meaningful partner engagement.
- Monitor donor trends and changes in the funding landscape and ensure we proactively adapts its positioning and portfolio strategy.

### TEAM MANAGEMENT

- Lead the Senior Management Team and create a collaborative, accountable and inclusive leadership environment across countries and functions.
- Directly supervise relevant senior leaders, setting clear expectations, delegating authority appropriately and holding leaders accountable for results.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence and where resilience, well-being, inclusion and psychological safety are actively supported.
- Ensure effective workforce planning, organizational design, succession planning and leadership development in partnership with Human Resources and Regional Leadership.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide regular, constructive performance feedback; ensure performance management processes are timely, fair and meaningful.
- Ensure senior leaders and teams have access to the information, tools, resources, coaching and technical support required to perform effectively.
- Foster collaboration across programs and support functions and between country, regional and global teams.

### FINANCE AND COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT

- Provide overall accountability for the financial health and operational effectiveness and ensure resources are managed transparently, efficiently and in line with donor and Mercy Corps requirements.
- Work closely with Finance leadership to oversee country budgets, financial forecasts, cost structures and master budgets, and ensure timely corrective action where material variances or risks arise.
- Ensure new budgets and funding decisions are aligned with approved organizational structures, workforce plans and operational requirements.
- Work with Operations leadership to ensure procurement, logistics, administration, asset management and other operational systems effectively support program delivery and comply with organizational standards.
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, Mercy Corps policies, applicable laws and internal controls, and ensure material compliance concerns are escalated and addressed appropriately.
- Promote a culture of integrity and ensure adherence to Mercy Corps’ Code of Conduct, ethics, safeguarding and related policies and procedures.

INFLUENCE AND REPRESENTATION

- Represent Mercy Corps at senior levels with donors, government counterparts, consortium partners, local and international organizations, civil society, private-sector actors and other stakeholders, as appropriate.
- Build and maintain strategic relationships that strengthen Mercy Corps’ credibility, influence, partnerships, funding opportunities and program impact across the portfolio.
- Ensure external representation is coordinated across country teams and aligned with Mercy Corps’ strategic positioning, values and risk considerations.
- Connect evidence and analysis from country programs with relevant advocacy, policy and influencing priorities in coordination with Regional Leadership and global teams.
- Maintain a high degree of political and contextual awareness, impartiality and cultural sensitivity when representing Mercy Corps across diverse operating environments.

LEARNING

- As part of our commitment to organizational learning and in support of our understanding that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities they serve, we expect all team members to commit 5% of their time to learning activities that benefit Mercy Corps as well as themselves.

### ACCOUNTABILITY TO AFFECTED POPULATIONS

- Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts towards accountability, specifically to our program participants and to international standards guiding international relief and development work, while actively engaging program participant communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Supervisory Responsibility:** Country program and support functions (Finance, Operations, HR).

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Vice President Asia, Middle East and Europe Region (AMEE)

**Works Directly With:** Country Program Teams, Regional Leadership, Regional Program and Technical Team, Regional Support Services Teams, Global Program Technical Teams (TEQ, Evidence & Learning, Institutional Donors Engagement), additional global support teams as needed.

## **Knowledge and Experience**

- BA/S or equivalent in a relevant field required; MA/S or equivalent preferred.
- At least 10 years of progressively responsible leadership and management experience in international relief and development, including senior country-level or multi-country leadership responsibility; prior Country Director or comparable senior leadership experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience leading complex and geographically dispersed country portfolios across humanitarian, recovery, resilience and/or development contexts.
- Previous experience working in the MENA region and strong understanding of the region’s political, humanitarian, regulatory and donor environment.
- Demonstrated ability to provide integrated leadership across programs, finance, operations, people, security, risk and compliance functions.
- Substantial knowledge of the international humanitarian and development system, institutions and donors, including compliance requirements, accountability frameworks and sector best practices.
- Experience with major institutional donors such as USG, FCDO, ECHO, European donors, UN agencies, foundations and private donors. Experience with DFIs and innovative finance institutions is an asset.
- Robust experience developing, operationalizing and adapting country strategies and leading organizations through transition, growth, restructuring or funding change.
- Demonstrated success in external representation, donor engagement, negotiation and partnership development resulting in strengthened positioning and/or new opportunities.
- Experience managing significant budgets and ensuring sound financial stewardship, internal controls and donor compliance.
- Demonstrated experience leading senior and diverse teams, including remotely, and building strong leadership, accountability and collaboration across functions and locations.
- Experience operating in insecure, politically sensitive or rapidly changing environments and making sound decisions under pressure.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication, influencing, negotiation and coaching skills.
- Outstanding analytical and strategic thinking skills, sound judgment, and the ability to translate strategy into practical action.
- Excellent oral and written English required; proficiency in Arabic is an asset.

## **Success Factors**

The successful candidate is a decisive, critical, and collegial professional with solid management and leadership skills. They have a thorough understanding of what it takes to deliver impactful programs in challenging environments. They are an excellent communicator who can inspire broad and diverse teams towards achieving a shared goal and drive a fast-paced and adaptive program. They are able to create a stimulating working environment encouraging innovation, creativity, ownership and accountability. They are a confident representative in public settings, able to speak up when needed to and influence key stakeholders internally and externally to further and expand Country Programs’ goals in Syria, Jordan, and Yemen. They are able to work effectively with a diverse team in sensitive and highly fluid environments to prioritize team-building and capacity-building of national team members. They have excellent information management skills and is able to translate strategy into action and also an outstanding ability to design, implement and manage innovative programs that respond to current needs and reinforce the future program structures of Mercy Corps in Syria, Jordan, and Yemen.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in Damascus, Syria. This location is currently an unaccompanied position. Housing is individual accommodation with potential movement constraints due to security. Team Members will have access to medical, electricity, water, etc. This position requires (50% of time) of travel to other countries (Jordan, Yemen) and to field offices, some in insecure environments.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme** ](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies ](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies)and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: Regional Communications Officer – Central America Region
jobs.description:
**The Regional Communications Officer** is an execution-focused regional role responsible for translating the global communications and brand framework into high-quality communications products, content, storytelling, digital outputs and country-level communications support across Central America (El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras). The position coordinates regional communications delivery, production planning and operational requirements, while implementing the regional communications strategy established by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications. Indicative balance of time: 45% producing materials and content · 35% planning, coordination and managing demand across the three countries · 20% supporting country offices.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Graphic Design, or a related field.
- At least three years of professional experience in communications or content production, preferably in the humanitarian or international development sector.
- Demonstrated anticipation: evidence of having identified what an organization would need and prepared for it before being asked. Candidates will be asked to demonstrate this during the selection process.
- Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite; Illustrator, InDesign and Photoshop, with a working command of output specifications for print and digital. Premiere Pro or equivalent for basic video editing. Canva is not a substitute.
- Practical field photography and video capture: interview framing, lavalier and directional audio, stabilization, exposure control and use of filters.
- Experience planning production against supplier lead times and working with procurement processes.
- Experience operating organizational social media accounts and reporting on engagement.
- Working proficiency in Spanish and English, written and spoken.
- Competence with collaborative planning tools; experience with Monday.com or equivalent is an advantage.
- Right to work in Guatemala, and able to attend the country office on a hybrid basis in line with regional policy.
- Experience driving standard 4WD vehicles in rough terrain. Valid driver's license.
- Ability to project and maintain a calm work environment while operating in a time and
- deadline-defined environment required by internal and external clients.
- Excellent interpersonal, relational, and communication skills, with a history of inspiring collaboration across multiple functions.
- Possessing a deep connection with the local context of communities in social risk conditions.
- Ability to adopt and promote a positive attitude towards processes of change, renewal, and transformation.
- Committed to creating a positive impact on the world with inspiration, passion, compassion, and a sense of service vocation.
- Ability to travel regularly to program locations, both nationally and internationally.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Oversight and Governance Responsibilities:**

- Ensure that all communications outputs produced in or for the region adhere to organizational policies, brand standards, safeguarding requirements and ethical storytelling standards.
- Identify and escalate to the line manager any reputational, brand or safeguarding risk arising from regional communications activity, including materials produced by implementing partners.
- Maintain complete consent and release documentation for all content produced in the region, and verify it is in place before any material is used or published.
- Ensure that country offices and implementing partners use the organizational identity only through the defined authorization process and report any unauthorized use.
- Maintain accurate records of production, suppliers and communications expenditure, and report them to the line manager.
- Support training and awareness for country staff and implementing partner staff on brand standards, consent and safeguarding in communications.
- Recommend improvements to communications processes and controls to strengthen consistency, accountability and quality across the region.

**Production of Communications Materials**

- Produce communications and visibility materials for the three countries: brochures, reports, IEC tools, banners, signage, event materials, staff identification and program collateral.
- Adapt global campaign materials for regional use, working from approved templates and brand assets.
- Specify materials correctly for their intended use, including application, resolution, color space, bleed, and finishing.
- Prepare supplier briefs and specifications, coordinate with Procurement and Finance on execution, and obtain a printer’s proof before any full production run, without exception.
- Maintain supplier and printer records for the region, with current lead times and costs.

**Content and Storytelling**

- Deliver an agreed monthly volume of approved success stories from the three country offices to the global repository, with complete metadata, working with country program staff to source them.
- Write and edit success stories and donor-facing content to the organization’s global voice and quality standards.
- Capture photography and short-form video interviews in the field to a professional standard, including framing, audio, stabilization and exposure control.

**Planning and Coordination**

- Develop an annual communications work plan jointly with the country office teams, setting out their planned activities, dates and material requirements for the year, so that needs are mapped early enough to be produced properly. Update it through the quarterly Requirements Report.
- Maintain the regional production calendar: record every communications deliverable with its material type, lead time, the date final artwork is required, and the date it must reach procurement. Reviewed monthly with the line manager.
- Submit a Regional Communications Requirements Report before the start of each quarter, listing, for each country, the commemorative dates, program milestones, partner events, and activities that will require communications support, along with the lead time each requires.
- Flag in writing, as soon as it is known, any activity whose timeline is no longer viable, and propose an alternative material or scope.
- Maintain the regional workstream board and keep the status of each item up to date.

**Regional Digital Presence and Media**

- Operate and administer the regional social media accounts: schedule and publish posts, stories, reels and short-form content approved within the global framework, maintain a content calendar one month in advance, and report engagement quarterly.
- Maintain an organizational media contact database for the three countries, held on the regional system and kept current. Personal contact lists are not a substitute.
- Liaise with local and regional media outlets to enhance visibility and maintain the regional media kit: organizational fact sheet, spokesperson protocol, and approved boilerplate.

**Country Office Support and Capacity**

- Train and support country program staff and implementing partner staff in interviewing, photography specifications, consent documentation, and the use of approved templates and brand assets.
- Operate the shared mechanisms through which program teams submit content and requests.
- Work with country teams to incorporate their communication requirements into the annual plan and propose the approaches most likely to work for each country and audience.
- Provide guidance to country offices on brand application so that materials start from approved templates rather than being corrected at approval stage.

**Brand Application and Partner Materials**

- Apply the organizational identity consistently across all regional outputs, and ensure that country offices and implementing partners work from the currently approved assets.
- Route every partner request to use the organizational identity on physical materials through the defined authorization process. The postholder does not approve partner use of the organizational identity.
- Produce final artwork for approved co-branded materials from organizational templates rather than amending partner-originated files.

**Service Standard**

- Acknowledge every internal and partner request upon receipt, and respond with a specific date within two working days.
- Where a request arrives without the information needed to act, obtain it from the requester rather than waiting.
- Report status by stage — not started, in design, pending approval, final artwork ready, with procurement, in production, delivered — never as a general assessment.

**Scope and Interface with Headquarters**

- Held by this post: regional adaptation of global campaigns, field capture, templated and routine production, supplier briefing and coordination, regional channels, local media liaison, and country office support.
- Routed to headquarters Creative Services: campaign concept development, complex design, finished video editing and institutional publications. The postholder is responsible for recognizing which is which and routing in good time.
- The postholder implements the regional communications strategy designed by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications, within the global Marketing & Communications frameork.

jobs.title: Nutrition Technician (Syria - Homs)
jobs.description:
**Job Title: Nutrition Technician**

**Job location: Syria - Homs – AlDabaa PHC**

**Reports to: Project Coordinator**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Nutrition Technician supports the nutrition team in providing nutrition interventions, during emergency situations. Their responsibilities include conducting assessments, distributing food, maintaining records, and providing training. Their role is crucial, in addressing malnutrition during emergencies.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

1\. Nutritional survey of children and pregnant and lactating women.

2\. Detection of malnutrition cases in children under 5 years and pregnant and lactating women.

3\. Admission of children or pregnant and lactating women to the malnutrition program, according to the condition of each one of them, after taking the MUAC measurement a second time after the community health factor.

4\. Prescribing therapeutic or nutritional supplements or vitamins for children, pregnant and lactating women, after the advice of the attending physician.

5\. Enhancing breastfeeding through individual and group sessions.

6\. To be the leader in the group sessions and direct the team with him as needed, in addition to conducting complex individual sessions with the beneficiaries.

7\. Leading IYCF campaigns in communities, providing advice, distributing brochures and vitamins, and referring patients to health centers or nutrition centers.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

1\. University degree in one of the administrative specializations, nutrition or its equivalent.

2\. Two years of work experience in the field of nutrition, mobile team, and health education with non-governmental organizations.

3\. Excellent computer skills, reporting and organizational skills and good time management.

4\. Strong communication skills.

5\. Good organizational and time management skills.

6\. The ability to work under pressure.

**ABOUT MEDGLOBAL**

MEDGLOBAL is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

MEDGLOBAL Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to MEDGLOBAL employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

1\. Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

2\. Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside MEDGLOBAL.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to MEDGLOBAL, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. MEDGLOBAL is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

MEDGLOBAL provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. MEDGLOBAL employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

**Safeguarding & Code of Conduct**

All **MEDGLOBAL** employees must adhere to PSEA's protection policies

Principles and rules of conduct. Strict compliance with safety and ethical standards is required.

jobs.title: Creative Lead
jobs.description:
**Job Title: Creative Lead**

Organization: Greenpeace MENA (GP MENA)

Department: GP MENA Engagement Department

Reports to: Engagement Director

Location: Remote, based in the MENA region

**OVERALL PURPOSE**

The Creative Lead is responsible for identifying and coordinating the design, implementation, and delivery of creative concepts, creative and branding assets (visuals, videos, etc.) across digital, print, and events as required. This role aims to strengthen Greenpeace MENA’s brand and messaging across multiple touchpoints.

**SCOPE**

The postholder is line-managed by the Branding and Communications Manager and will have to provide creative guidance to the organization. By harnessing strategic and technical expertise, the postholder facilitates the continued development, implementation, and delivery of creative assets, as well as oversees relationships with creative agencies and freelancers.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**CREATIVE STEER** Identify and deliver strategic creative concepts and products that can contribute to meeting narrative and audience engagement objectives for online projects and offline events, in coordination with relevant teams, as well as commission freelancers and/or agencies when required.

**MULTIMEDIA CONTENT** Produce visual content for Greenpeace MENA’s social media channels, website, media, and email outreach, including plan, shoot, edit, and distribute photos and videos for traditional and social media.

**COMMISSIONING** Lead the scoping, commissioning, production, and delivery of creative assets, depending on the project needs. Evaluate offers for multimedia production and creative projects, negotiate rates, liaise with admin support for the contracting and payment processes. Expand and nurture a network of creative agencies, freelancers, and multimedia content creators from around the region, and support GP MENA’s goals to expand its creative partnerships and projects. Build and maintain relationships with National Regional Offices (NROs) and Greenpeace International stakeholders.

**BRANDING**
Manage the use of GP MENA’s visual branding and identity. Be responsible for the quality control of multimedia outputs and ensure consistency and compliance with our global and regional brand visual protocols and standards.

**ARCHIVE AND DISTRIBUTION** Update and maintain GP MENA’s multimedia library including photos and videos, keep a record of distribution, and manage archiving. Evaluate the need for stock of photos, video rushes, and audiovisuals, and negotiate rates and licensing agreements as appropriate.

**KNOWLEDGE OF PRODUCTION AND TECHNOLOGY** Keep abreast of developments in video and photo production, particularly regarding cameras, editing software, transmission technologies, and emerging social media platforms.

**MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING** Evaluate the progress and performance of creative projects and support reporting. Ensure that regular learning is incorporated into the optimization of creative work and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

**OTHER:** Any other duty, as appropriate to the post and as delegated by your line manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EXPERIENCE**

**Experience & Skills**

- At least 5-7 years of professional experience in multimedia production, creative work, and film production and distribution.
- Excellent technical knowledge of video, photo, and graphics editing software (e.g., FCPX, Premiere Pro, Photoshop) and production skills, including scripting and camera operation.
- Good connections with photographers, videographers, and creative/production agencies, especially in the MENA region.
- Experience in managing relationships with suppliers including requests for proposals, identification, and solicitation.
- Solid understanding of copyright, licensing, and media law.
- Excellent knowledge in event production specifications, including printing materials and creative installations.
- Proficiency in Arabic and English is a must.
- Ability to translate and present data and other technical information in engaging visual products.

**Organizational Competencies**

- Ability to build strong interpersonal relationships, in particular working with cross-cultural and global teams.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with demonstrated ability to manage multiple competing tasks and demands
- Great organizational and time-management skills
- Autonomous, flexible, and agile
- Knowledge sharing - values diversity, in particular, experience working in an international environment and coordination of rollouts across global markets.

**Behavioral Competencies**

- Assertive and persistent, demonstrate the ability to lead an operation from inception to completion effectively
- Act with integrity consistently
- Demonstrate a positive mindset and solutions-oriented attitude
- Demonstrate openness and curiosity to test new ideas and learn
- Demonstrate commitment and conviction
- Ability to understand and manage one's own emotions, strengths, and limitations

**Commitment**

Commitment to Greenpeace’s core values in response to environmental and peace issues through non-violent, direct action-led campaigning in line with its mission.

**Disclaimer**

Greenpeace MENA is committed to achieving diversity within its workforce and encourages applicants irrespective of gender, nationality, disability, sexual orientation, culture, religion, and ethnic background to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

jobs.title: Finance Manager (National Position)
jobs.description:
**Position: Finance Manager**

**Job location:** Kampala

**Starting date:** January 2027

**Vacancy closing date:** 24th November 2026

**Duration position:** 1-year renewable contract.

**Working hours:** Fulltime (40 hours per week)

**About ZOA**

***We are here for people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster.***

ZOA, as an international NGO, supports people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster. Together, we can come to their aid in emergencies and remain faithful to communities as they recover – providing new opportunities for them to help themselves again. The work of ZOA is coordinated from the Netherlands. We are active in multiple countries in Africa, South America, the Middle East Region, and Asia. We work with approximately 900 employees worldwide and with (local) partners. We invite you to join our team of committed colleagues. In Uganda, ZOA has offices in Kampala, West Nile (Arua), Acholi (Gulu), and Karamoja (Amudat). ZOA Uganda works both in relief and recovery on the themes of food security & livelihoods, education, and conflict management with a special focus on land Rights.

**Your challenge**

The Finance Manager is to ensure that there is significant leadership provided to the team in the implementation of ZOA finance strategies and to ensure financial planning and management activities including budgeting & forecasting, a sound financial reporting systems, compliance and creation of value to support achievement ZOA’s strategic business continuity by having meaningful financial impact on the organisation.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

***Leadership and Team Management***

- Oversee application of ZOA Policy and Guidelines ensuring compliance.
- Communicate to the Finance team a clear and exciting vision for the work of ZOA and for the role of department in supporting the organisation.
- Responsible for induction, performance monitoring, training on the job and staff well-being of finance staff.
- Support team members to grow in their potential capacity and motivate them to grow in their performance e.g. by encouraging and praising good performance, coaching, assisting staff to prevent or resolve problems, providing resources, tools and equipment.
- Ensure gender and conflict sensitive approach to team management;
- Monitor the quality of financial and administrative operations of the field offices.
- Support country office and field offices in acquisition, purchase, contract management and tender procedures in accordance with ZOA internal systems;
- Periodic meetings with the field finance team for relevant accounting needs and deliverables.

***Risk Management and Compliance***

- Provide leadership, and financial insights to the finance and accounting areas of the organization, proposing and implementing improvements in operational management processes to increase efficiency.
- Support management in compliance to donor regulation, local government regulation and ZOA regulations.
- Support and oversee awareness measures for prevention of fraud, bribery and corruption; report any suspected misconduct to Manager of Operations and assist with periodic risk assessments and trainings.
- Advise both finance and non-finance staff over matters of internal control compliance periodically review the suitability of the existing controls to ensure they are adequate to minimise the risk exposure of ZOA and that they reinforce the proper implementation of programs.
- Ensure full compliance with Uganda Revenue Authority, NGO Board and returns requirements and be the key contact with bank support personnel, auditors and tax advisors.
- Coordinate and support the External and Internal Audits and follows on actions for management resolution/address.
- Collaborate with other contracted finance support teams, and lead finance functions, especially with the budget owners/manager/Operations team.

***Financial Reporting***

- Ensure accurate and timely financial reporting for decision making.
- Ensure the monthly budget balances report is up to date and shared with budget holders. Minimize the number of errors from the team reports through constant feedback.
- Confirm expense codes on all requests as they are received, correct where necessary through the budget manager.
- Prepare, analyze, and submit accurate monthly financial and management reports, including; income statement, balance sheet, budget and variance, projections and forecast, and cash flow.
- Coordinate the preparation of the audited financial statements and all tax returns.
- Prepare a variety of ad hoc financial scenarios as requested.

***Financial Control & Accounting***

- Observe and implement the accounting systems, payments, bookkeeping, statutory filing, revenue management, and improvement of payment systems.
- Ensure that all financial transactions are processed accurately, in a timely manner, in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles through the ERP system, identifying and correcting any variances.
- Maintain a system to track financial commitments and outstanding contract amounts by staff and third parties transacting with ZOA and ensure that they are diligently executed when due.
- Develop, implement, and maintain processes and controls that are current best practices related to transaction processing.
- Manage and process all the following transactions: payroll, taxes, accounts payable, revenue and expense, fixed assets, cash, bank reconciliations, and allocations.
- Responsible for periodic update of fixed assets register in ERP, collaborating with the logistics team to ensure accuracy of asset details.
- Perform month-end closing procedures, including account reconciliations, and updating schedules.

***Budget Management***

- Support budget managers to prepare periodic budgets and forecasts while providing clarity where needed.
- Prepare budgets for new proposals, budget modifications and the country year budget.
- Ensure budgets are entered into the ERP system.
- Share monthly and quarterly BVA reports with budget holders for ease of planning.
- Monitor the budget changes and update the approved budgets in ERP.
- Offer periodic training or refresher training to the teams aimed at improving financial management, discipline and accountability as stipulated in our policies and procedures.

**Your profile**

Identity

- The candidate is expected to fully support the vision, mission and Christian values 0f ZOA (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

**Knowledge & experience:**

- University degree in Finance, Business Administration or any related field, CPA an added advantage.
- Proven work experience of 5-7 years in a financial management or senior finance position.
- Proven work experience with International NGO in the humanitarian sector.
- Proven experience with Excel, ERP systems or any other financial related Management Information System at the level of advanced user.
- Good knowledge of procurement and logistics practices.
- Good communicator with a fluent command of English.
- Experience in general team management.
- Cross cultural experience in a development setting.

***Skills and Attitude:***

- Holds oneself accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling ZOA values.
- Result-oriented approach, initiates but also makes sure that initiatives come to a satisfactory result.
- Able to work under pressures, putting first things first, knowing how to prioritize and meeting deadlines.
- Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, external partners and stakeholders.
- Able to work in a sometimes fluid and insecure environment.
- Dares to push ‘the panic button’ when she/he sees that things are going wrong.
- Good conceptual and analytical thinking.
- Flexibility and adaptability
- Interpersonal and cross cultural sensitivity.

**Special conditions/circumstances**

The Finance Manager will be based in Kampala. Regular field travel to the projects and other locations is required (up to 30% of the time). The role is 1.0 FTE (40 hrs/week). Working hours are outlined in the ZOA Uganda Employee Handbook. Some flexibility on working hours may be required, e.g. for travel at weekends.

**Our offer**

- ZOA offers a challenging role in a dynamic context, and you will be part of an inspiring and motivated team.
- We offer good benefits and remuneration which suits the NGO sector.

**Do you need more information?**

For more information about ZOA, please visit our website [www.zoa-international.com](http://www.zoa-international.com/).

jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific peoples, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I)** collective delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The **Tok Pasifika Project Advisor** is responsible for the implementation, coordination and development of the Tok Pasifika project. This position works to improve the accessibility, quality and impact of Pacific language services, by enhancing the project’s visibility, strengthening and assisting the network of language service providers, supporting integration of language issues into SPC practices, and ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning as part of the project. The Project Advisor serves as Tok Pasifika’s point of contact with internal teams and external partners, using an inclusive, culturally appropriate approach that is aligned with the SPC’s institutional priorities.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Improving the Tok Pasifika project’s visibility and outreach**

- Develop a communication plan in collaboration with SPC’s Strategic Communications, Outreach, Publishing and Engagement (SCOPE) team, that takes into account stakeholders’ feedback; and update this plan annually.
- In collaboration with SPC teams, enhance use of existing communication materials and plan and coordinate production of new materials, as needed.
- Create a strong visual identity for the project, and regularly update and track project visibility tools such as the website, intranet page, etc.
- Develop and implement awareness-raising activities for SPC’s technical divisions and other external stakeholders.
- Use the information gathered through Tok Pasifika’s monitoring and evaluation system, take part in efforts to present SPC’s results in a view to raising the profile of Tok Pasifika’s work and results (e.g. drafting performance stories, communicating numerical outcomes).
- Participate in internal, local and/or international cultural events to represent and promote Tok Pasifika.
- Liaise with media outlets to publicise the Tok Pasifika project.

**Building the network of language service providers and improving the quality of the services provided**

- Manage contracts and external contractors, in particular by monitoring and updating the list of preferred service providers (contracts, deadlines, administrative compliance), in collaboration with the Procurement and Finance teams, and ensure that contractual documents are properly filed and accessible.
- Provide support and advice to SPC teams on managing requests for translation into Pacific languages.
- Engage the network on a regular basis (e.g. mailing list, newsletter, focus groups).
- Take part in drafting guidelines for providers and/or organise training sessions (e.g. webinars on translation techniques or administrative procedures, liaison interpreting workshops, etc.), in collaboration with members of the Conference and Languages unit.
- Hold annual meetings (face-to-face or on-line) with language service providers to discuss their needs, difficulties and successes.
- Set up and monitor a system for evaluating the performance of language service providers and their use by SPC teams, with a view to continuously improving the quality, relevance and effectiveness of the language services provided.

**Integrating language issues across SPC and boosting demand**

- Set up and facilitate a Tok Pasifika community of practice in order to strengthen internal coordination, information sharing and ownership of language services within SPC.
- Set up, in collaboration with a focal point within one SPC division, a pilot Pacific language translation project, and identify lessons from that project, in a view to providing better advice to teams and optimising their use of Tok Pasifika services
- Contribute to the integration of language issues from the project design stage, especially in terms of the key forms used, through the relationships established with various relevant SPC teams (SPL, PIRMO, HRSD, Procurement).
- Contribute to the development, adoption and dissemination of an SPC-wide language policy that explicitly recognises the value of Pacific languages and implements the guiding principles for their gradual integration into SPC activities.

**Mobilising project resources and ensuring their sustainability**

- Develop strategic partnerships with institutions, NGOs, universities or companies in the language sector.
- Assist in securing additional funding (grants, partnerships, regional/international calls for projects).
- Optimise existing resources (pooling with other projects, using tools that have already been developed).
- Ensure thorough budget monitoring for the Tok Pasifika project and produce regular financial reports to demonstrate the efficient use of resources and the actual results achieved.

**Monitoring, evaluation and learning**

- Identify and map the Tok Pasifika project’s key internal and external stakeholders and keep this list up to date.
- Undertake an internal assessment, by analysing Pacific language translation needs and carrying out surveys and interviews with the user divisions; and issue a comparison with the previous assessment.
- The approaches to conduct an external assessment are defined (analysis of the needs of SPC stakeholders).
- Develop, implement and refine a framework of indicators to monitor activities, service provider performance, service quality, demand and use of Tok Pasifika services.
- Produce regular monitoring, evaluation and learning reports and use the results and lessons learned to adjust the services Tok Pasifika proposes, as well as the project’s work approaches and communication strategy.
- Draft a project sustainability plan, to be updated annually, which contains the key points, possible project directions and recommendations for integrating multilingualism throughout SPC.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the **online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in project management; Pacific languages, linguistics or cultures; international relations; cultural studies; or a related field, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 10 years in the management of language-related, cultural or international cooperation projects, ideally in a regional or international institutional context
- Demonstrated project management skills and proficiency in project management methods and tools (planning, monitoring, reporting, coordination and partnerships)
- Experience in purchasing processes in private or public entities
- Experience in administrative and budgetary project management, funding-raising and project monitoring and evaluation

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communications skills
- Proficiency in one or more Pacific languages.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Very good knowledge of Pacific context and cultures
- Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This vacant position is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** The **Tok Pasifika Project Adviser** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3727 to 4562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766 to 658,322 (USD 4994 to 6114; EUR 4506 to 5517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale is based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for international staff employees based in New Caledonia** – SPC provides subsidised housing in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy

jobs.title: VA26P186V01 MRC Counsellor (M1)

jobs.description:
MRAPP funded by the Government of the Netherlands, aims to strengthen migration prevention efforts and improve access to migration-related information, counselling, referral and reintegration services in Iraq. The project is implemented by ICMPD in close coordination with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement and other relevant governmental and local stakeholders, with a focus on strengthening and expanding the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) model.

The position will be based within the MRAPP project team and will report to the Project Manager, while working closely with relevant ICMPD colleagues, MRC staff, government counterparts and project stakeholders to support the effective delivery of project activities and results.

## Functional Overview

Working closely with the respective Migration Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator, the MRC Counsellor assists with the implementation of MRC activities and workplans, in support of effective communication, information and service delivery. They contribute to the organisation of events and outreach activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Coordinator and other Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures.

## Key Results

***Support to MRC Activities:*** Via various means and platforms such as face-to-face, phone and online, counselling, guidance, referral and information provided to a variety of clients (prospective or returning migrants, migrants, families of migrants, etc.) who visit or attend MRC activities, initiating and following up on referrals, linking them with relevant agencies depending on their needs, e.g. technical and vocational institutes to upgrade their skills or with the relevant authorities for the processing of their documents for overseas employment. Outreach activities supported via the use of media and social media and participation in online discussions, forums or symposiums, conferences, and other related events. In collaboration with the MRC Coordinator the MRC website and database, Facebook page and other social media accounts regularly updated.

***Support to Outreach Activities:*** In cooperation with relevant agencies both in the public and private sector, networks and contacts effectively established. Community events and outreach activities organised such as briefings in academic and training institutions, symposia with civil society, training of education or emigration consultancies, and the setting-up of booths, kiosks, or similar structures in public places to disseminate information and materials on safe, orderly, and regular migration, including on return and reintegration.

***Preparation of Information Materials:*** In collaboration with the ICMPD team and whenever applicable, with consultants or experts, research or mapping undertaken of available migration-related programmes, services, and activities of various stakeholders. Knowledge materials compiled on migration that are helpful in the full operation and functioning of the MRC. Additional knowledge products andinformation materials revised, prepared, or further developed, as necessary, such as brochures, handbooks, audio-visual products, web-based information documents, etc. Online discussions relevant to migration, regularly maintained and populated, initiating regular and timely responses to issues raised and information requested.

***Support to the MRC Coordination Activities:*** Assistance provided to the respective MRC Coordinator to ensure the timely, efficient, and effective implementation of MRC activities, and with the monitoring and updating of the workplans, as necessary, ensuring that outputs and outcomes are aligned and integrated with the national priorities and strategies of government partners, and of the projects. Substantive contributions provided to the preparation of relevant reports, responses to client feedback and monitoring and reporting to relevant agencies on any policy or programmatic recommendations. Information materials compiled and prepared for dissemination. The MRC database regularly updated recording relevant activities, events and outreach activities undertaken. Effective support provided to the MRC Coordinator in preparing weekly, quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity andmission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests on agreed formats, and other documentary requirements.

## Required Expertise

- ​Solid organizational, planning and prioritizing skills and abilities.
- Upon consultation with the supervisor, ability to make decisions in full compliance with ICMPD’soperational regulations and rules.
- Analytical thinking to gather, analyse and compile information, identifying critical relationships and patterns among data and proposing workable solutions.
- An understanding of migration dynamics in the country.
- Experience in the area of migration in the country.
- High sense of initiative and good judgement to be able to work independently with minimum supervision.
- Strong sense of client orientation and good understanding of effective service delivery, community engagement, outreach, and social work.
- Ability to work effectively with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds.
- Capability to establish effective relationships across the organisation at all levels.

## Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field. High school diploma or equivalent with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the bachelor’s degree.
- Minimum of 2 years of position-specific experience.
- Working experience with international organisations is an asset.
- Experience in office administration and management.
- Experience working with local authorities and businesses.
- Solid organizational skills.
- Proficiency in English, Kurdish and Arabic (verbal/written) is required.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

> Note: Please note that this vacancy has been republished. Applicants who have already submitted an application do not need to reapply.​

## **Functional Overview**

Within the Directorate of Management (MGT), and specifically the Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Unit, the Junior ICT Officer – Service Desk supports the organisation-wide ICT ticketing system (Service Portal) and contributes to the timely resolution of ICT incidents and service requests in accordance with established ICMPD/ICT procedures, service standards and continuous improvement processes. As an active member of the ICT Service Desk Team, the incumbent provides client-oriented and efficient first-level technical support to end-users across ICMPD, contributing to the smooth day-to-day operation of ICT services and the consistent application of ICT policies and guidelines.

The position is based in one of ICMPD’s regional offices and serves as the first point of contact for end-users at the assigned duty station. In line with the Service Desk’s centrally coordinated operating model, all incidents and service requests are logged and managed through the single Service Portal and assigned based on priority, workload and required technical expertise. While priority is given to requests originating from the assigned duty station, the Junior ICT Officer may also be assigned to handle service requests across multiple regions. Likewise, service requests from the regional office may be handled by other Service Desk team members, ensuring continuity and adherence to defined service levels.

The incumbent functionally reports to the ICT Team Lead – Service Desk, based at ICMPD Headquarters in Vienna, Austria, who provides technical guidance and performance supervision.
