Background

The UNDP Regional Hub for Latin America and the Caribbean provides strategic policy advice and technical support for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) implementation at the national and sub-national levels. It notably does so through comprehensive analysis of national policies and the development of proposals for policy alignment, technical support for the establishment of monitoring systems, capacity-building efforts in national statistical systems, the publication of flagship reports, and facilitating the systematization and transfer of good practices. It supports initiatives to track SDG progress while developing and improving granular, disaggregated data to better identify and target vulnerable and excluded groups. By aligning national priorities with regional and global goals, it fosters coordination between national and regional actors, building national-level efforts to ensure coherence and consistency.

LAC’s economy is predominantly composed of SMEs, which account for 99.5% of all companies, employ 60% of the workforce, and contribute approximately 25% of the GDP. The financial market in the region is primarily banking-oriented, with limited capital markets. SMEs in LAC rely largely on bank loans and microfinance, presenting challenges for access to capital and the creation of locally tailored financial solutions that drive sustainable job creation, environmental improvements, and economic stability at the community level.

UNDP in Latin America and the Caribbean has extensive experience in implementing inclusive business methodologies, such as “In Motion” (En Marcha, in Spanish), the Suppliers Development Program (Desarrollo de Proveedores, in Spanish), “Starting with Your Business” (Iniciando Con Su Negocio, in Spanish), and “Growing with My Business” (Creciendo Con Su Negocio, in Spanish), among others. UNDP's approach to supporting the SME ecosystem is holistic and inclusive: from working to strengthen value chains to supporting governments in designing and implementing national policies for SMEs and partnering with business associations such as Chambers of Commerce to promote the export of national products and facilitate dialogue with the private sector. These policies are pivotal in structuring effective support systems for enterprises, enhancing their resilience and market value.

At the same time, the IVC Programme sits within a wider body of work on inclusive growth carried out by UNDP's Regional Hub, spanning related areas such as financial inclusion, entrepreneurship ecosystems, and productive inclusion more broadly. There is a clear opportunity to build stronger synergies between the IVC Programme and this broader inclusive growth portfolio — sharing knowledge, methodologies, partner relationships, and communications across initiatives that currently operate somewhat separately.

To support both the coordination needs of the IVC Programme and these cross-portfolio synergies, the Programme is seeking to bring on an Inclusive Value Chains Analyst who will provide dedicated technical and administrative support, helping ensure effective implementation, consistent follow-up on results and commitments, and stronger connections across UNDP's inclusive growth work in the region.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Regional Inclusive Growth Policy Specialist, the Inclusive Value Chains Analyst will perform the following responsibilities and related tasks:

1. Support the transfer and institutionalization of inclusive business methodologies.

- Coordinate with UNDP Country Offices and public institutions to adapt, transfer, and apply inclusive business methodologies that strengthen SMEs.

- Prepare implementation guidance and capacity-development materials; and follow up on adoption, delivery, and lessons learned.

2. Review and strengthen UNDP inclusive business tools and methodologies.

- Assess existing tools, methodologies, and baselines; compile feedback and evidence from implementation; recommend updates.

- Support the preparation, validation, and dissemination of revised technical resources.

3. Support results monitoring, data management, and digital knowledge platforms.

- Maintain and update the regional website and related monitoring tools; collect, validate, and organize information from participating Country Offices.

- Track outputs, results, and impact indicators; and prepare periodic analytical summaries to inform programme decisions.

4. Provide technical assistance for the development of inclusive business ecosystems.

- Support Country Offices in engaging governments, chambers of commerce, business associations, financial institutions, and private-sector partners.

- Contribute to ecosystem and value-chain assessments; and help design practical interventions that improve SME participation, resilience, and market access.

5. Systematize, communicate, and facilitate the exchange of knowledge and good practices.

- Document project experiences, results, lessons learned, and scalable solutions; prepare knowledge products, briefs, presentations, and communication materials.

- Organize regional and global knowledge-sharing activities with internal and external partners.

6. Contribute to programme coordination, partnerships, and resource mobilization across the inclusive growth portfolio.

- Support work planning, progress reporting, coordination meetings, and follow-up on agreed actions; identify synergies with financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, and productive inclusion initiatives.

- Contribute to concept notes, proposals, partner mapping, and engagement with donors and private-sector partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Inclusive Value Chain Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Regional Inclusive Growth Policy Specialist.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- ACHIEVE RESULTS - LEVEL 1 : Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- THINK INNOVATEVELY - LEVEL 1 : Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- LEARN CONTINUOUSLY - LEVEL 1 : Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- ADAPT WITH AGILITY - LEVEL 1 : Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- ACT WITH DETERMINATION - LEVEL 1 : Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- ENGAGE AND PARTNER - LEVEL 1 : Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- ENABLE DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION - LEVEL 1 : Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional Competencies

- BUSINESS DIRECTION & STRATEGY SYSTEMS THINKING : Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT KNOWLEDGE FACILITATION : Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

- BUSINESS MANAGEMENT PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT : Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management COMMUNICATION : Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Technical Competencies

- 2030 AGENDA: PROSPERITY INCLUSIVE GROWTH - DEVELOPMENT PLANNING. INCLUSIVE GROWTH - ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION. INCLUSIVE GROWTH - FUTURE OF WORK.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics, Social Sciences, or related fields is required, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor´s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional 2 years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in inclusive growth, economic inclusion, economic development, and inclusive business in the above fields at the national or international level.

Additional desirable criteria:

- Experience and knowledge of UNDP's inclusive business methodologies, including their application, adaptation, and scaling.

- Experience transferring UNDP methodologies and building local capacity to sustain inclusive business initiatives.

- Technical expertise in project design, monitoring, and evaluation, with a focus on economic inclusion and development outcomes.

- Familiarity with UNDP’s work in the Latin America and Caribbean (LAC) region, including collaboration with Country Offices (COs) and Regional Hubs.

- Experience in designing and managing economic development projects, especially those targeting SMEs and inclusive growth.

- Proven experience in managing development programs at country and regional levels, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.

- Demonstrated ability to provide technical assistance to public institutions, private sector actors, and civil society.

- Experience in mobilizing funds, preparing fund management reports, and ensuring transparency in resource utilization.

jobs.title: Internship - Governance and Advocacy
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Bhutan has established a strong legal and institutional foundation for the rule of law and access to justice. The justice sector continues to strengthen coordination, professional capacity, service delivery and institutional accountability so that justice services are responsive to people’s needs.

The Justice Sector Strategic Plan II provides a framework for coordinated reform, including effective leadership and collaboration, competent justice service providers, responsive and accountable services, accessible and inclusive justice services, and adequate infrastructure. These priorities are also aligned with Bhutan’s 13th Five-Year Plan objective of strengthening inclusive, effective and accessible institutions and promoting transparent rule of law and public oversight.

The EU- and UNDP-supported project “Strengthening People-Centric and Inclusive Access to Justice in Bhutan” contributes to these priorities by supporting justice institutions and partners to improve access to justice, particularly for women, persons with disabilities and other groups that may face barriers when seeking legal information, assistance and remedies. The project promotes people-centred justice, disability inclusion, gender equality, legal aid, institutional coordination, capacity development, accessibility, and evidence-based programming.

The internship will provide a structured learning opportunity for a motivated young professional to contribute to the implementation, monitoring, documentation and communication of project activities while gaining practical exposure to UNDP programme management and Bhutan’s justice sector.

The internship is intended to support the Access to Justice Project with research, coordination, documentation, monitoring, knowledge management, communications and administrative tasks. The intern will work under close supervision by Project Manager and will be given assignments that contribute to both project delivery and professional learning.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Governance Portfolio Manager and the direct supervision of the Project Manager or designated supervisor, the intern will support the following areas:

- Research and Technical Support

- Conduct desk research on access to justice, people-centred justice, legal aid, disability inclusion, gender equality, youth participation, digital justice and related governance issues.

- Assist in preparing background notes, briefing materials, presentations and summaries of good national, regional and global practices relevant to the project.

- Support the collection, organization and basic analysis of project data, including information disaggregated by sex, age, disability and location where such data are available and appropriate.

- Support preparation of technical input for trainings, consultations, accessibility audits, monitoring visits and stakeholder meetings.

- Programme Implementation, Monitoring and Reporting

- Support preparation and updating of activity plans, participant lists, agendas, minutes, action trackers and follow-up notes.

- Assist with documentation of project activities, outputs, results, lessons learned and emerging risks.

- Contribute to draft progress reports, donor updates, presentations, human-interest stories and other project documents.

- Support compilation and filing of evidence required for project monitoring, results reporting and quality assurance.

- Stakeholder Coordination and Event Support

- Provide coordination support for engagement with justice sector institutions, civil society organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, Local Governments, academia, development partners and other stakeholders.

- Assist in organizing workshops, meetings, trainings, consultations, monitoring visits and public awareness activities.

- Prepare logistical and administrative documents, including invitations, attendance records, meeting materials and activity files.

- Participate in relevant project activities and prepare concise records of key discussions, decisions and action points.

- Knowledge Management and Communications

- Support development of knowledge and advocacy products such as briefs, presentations, factsheets, stories, social media content and communication materials.

- Document good practices and lessons from legal aid, disability-inclusive justice, accessibility, capacity building and community-level initiatives.

- Administrative Support and Learning

- Provide routine administrative and logistical support to the project team as required.

- Participate in team meetings, learning sessions and relevant UNDP events.

- Undertake other related tasks that are consistent with the purpose and learning objectives of the internship.

Competencies

Skills and Competencies:

- Curiosity, Creative thinking, and ability to make new and useful ideas;

- Good analytical skills in gathering and consolidating data and research for practical implementation;

- Communicate effectively when working in teams and independently;

- Strong organizational skills, the ability to multi-task, and strong attention to details;

- Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability;

- Ability to support team and team building skills;

- Excellent oral and written communication skills;

- Responds positively to feedback and differing points of view; and

- Consistently approaches work with energy and a positive, constructive attitude showing willingness to learn.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Candidates must at the time of application be enrolled in the final academic year of a Bachelor of Laws programme.

- Applicants must have knowledge in relevant fields such as Access to Justice, Human Dignity, Legal Writing & Research, and Advocacy & Awareness.

Experience:

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of work

3.1. Identification of suitable candidates primarily UN Volunteer assignments

- Provide recruitment services in adherence to established UN Volunteers’ Conditions of Service, regulations and policies;

- Verify quality and consistency of Description of Assignments (DOAs), and provide guidance on designing DOAs to UN host entities, UNV Regional Offices and Field Units;

- Advertise relevant assignments in line with established processes;

- Identify suitable candidates for UN Volunteer assignments in diverse areas of expertise and for various host entities, as per corporate Key Performance Indicators, and according to DOA requirements and in compliance with UNV’s Recruitment and Selection policy;

- Alert supervisor about deficiencies or risks, liaise with Regional Offices and Field Units on exceptional situations and provide guidance on applicable regulations, rules and policies to ensure full compliance with accountability framework;

- Keep relevant parties updated on status of identification and negotiate adjustments when required;

- Contribute to a fair workload distribution by supporting the identification and submission of candidates for UN Volunteer assignments across regions when needed;

- Record actions and data in the volunteer management systems;

- Ensure accurate data management in official databases;

- Facilitate timely resolution of queries related to volunteer recruitment.

3.2 Outreach and support to talent acquisition

- Coordinate with the Volunteer Solutions Section, Regional Offices and Field Units to remain informed of evolving demand for UN Volunteer profiles;

- Use social media and other sourcing channels to identify candidates, identify gaps in the existing talent pool, and support regional and national outreach campaigns and networks of talent sources in coordination with the Talent Acquisition team and relevant communication colleagues;

- Manage communication with candidates as it relates to the outcome of their applications;

- Contribute to the production of insightful recruitment analytics reports with regards to critical vacancies taking into account UNV’s priorities of gender parity and workforce diversity.

3.3 Recruitment compliance, clearances and case management

- Conduct reference checks, obtain relevant pre- and post-submission clearances, and verify performance appraisals for selected candidates against established standards of competence and integrity;

- Flag deficiencies, risks and exceptional situations to the supervisor; liaise with Regional Offices, Field Units and Host Entities; and provide guidance on applicable rules, policies and the accountability framework;

- Keep relevant parties informed of recruitment status, negotiate adjustments when required, record actions and data in volunteer management systems, and support the timely resolution of recruitment-related queries.

3.4 Knowledge building and continuous improvement

- Contribute to recruitment training materials and corporate activities that strengthen the recruitment capacity of UNV personnel;

- Capture and share lessons learnt from candidate identification; contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice; and provide input on recruitment policies, systems and processes to improve the timeliness and quality of VSC services;

- Serve, on a rotational basis, as a VSC focal point on assigned topics and perform other duties within the functional profile as required for the efficient functioning of the office and the organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Recruitment Associate is part of the Volunteer Services Centre and is administratively supported by the respective Regional Office. The position will report to the Operations Associate, Recruitment (G6) under the substantive guidance of G7 Operations Associate, Volunteer Recruitment and overall leadership of Chief, Volunteer Services Centre (VSC). The position has no supervisory or managerial responsibilities.

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Antecedentes /Descripción de la oficina / Unidad / Proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Desde hace 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

El proyecto 1005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el desarrollo”, busca contribuir al posicionamiento del INADEH como rector de la formación profesional, al fortalecimiento institucional, a la mejora de la calidad de la oferta educativa de hoy y del futuro, y a la mejora de la gestión operativa.

De esta manera, la acción del PNUD se centra en apoyar en la generación de una visión del sistema de formación técnica profesional con alternativas diferenciadas que sirvan a las personas, a la economía y a la sociedad. Organizar la gobernanza de la formación técnica y profesional, la vinculación educación – empleo, superar la sexta frontera, y poner el talento y capacidad de las y los panameños en reactivar nuestra economía y desarrollar la estrategia del cambio del proyecto definida como “Formación profesional como instrumento para fortalecer competencias, asegurar medios de vida y hacer una economía competitiva”.

La Oficina de Proyectos del INADEH es la instancia principal de comunicación y gestión de proyectos que ejecuta el INADEH con diversos organismos e instituciones, por lo que su rol principal es brindar estrecho seguimiento a la ejecución de los proyectos que se ejecutan como aquellos que se proyectan ejecutar en la institución, tanto en el corto como en el mediano plazo.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asistente en Ingeniería Electromecánica brindará apoyo técnico a la Oficina de Proyectos de Transformación y Mejora Integral del INADEH, contribuyendo a la planificación, diseño, supervisión, seguimiento y control técnico de las obras y proyectos que ejecuta la institución, en el ámbito de su especialidad y de conformidad con los requerimientos técnicos, contractuales y la normativa aplicable.

Apoyo en levantamientos, planos y presupuestos

- Participar en los levantamientos de requerimientos y en las visitas de campo, apoyando la verificación y rectificación de medidas, condiciones existentes y demás información técnica necesaria para el diseño y ejecución de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de especificaciones técnicas para la contratación y ejecución de obras, suministros e instalaciones electromecánicas, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad.

- Apoyar la elaboración y revisión de planos de instalaciones y sistemas electromecánicos, con base en los levantamientos, requerimientos y especificaciones técnicas de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de presupuestos, cómputos métricos y cálculos de materiales, equipos y componentes correspondientes a los sistemas electromecánicos de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la revisión del cumplimiento de la normativa legal y técnica vigente aplicable a los diseños de los sistemas eléctricos, de aire acondicionado y refrigeración, gas, plomería, protección contra incendios y sistemas especiales, según corresponda a su ámbito de competencia, e informar al profesional responsable sobre las observaciones identificadas.

Apoyo en la inspección y seguimiento técnico de obras

- Participar en visitas de campo e inspecciones técnicas y apoyar el seguimiento de las obras y proyectos del INADEH, de acuerdo con la ubicación asignada y las necesidades del Proyecto.

- Apoyar el seguimiento del cronograma y la ejecución de las obras, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad, verificando, bajo la orientación del profesional responsable, su correspondencia con los planos, especificaciones técnicas, términos de referencia y condiciones contractuales.

- Apoyar la revisión de los materiales, equipos, acabados y sistemas electromecánicos propuestos para las obras y preparar los insumos técnicos requeridos para su evaluación por parte del profesional responsable.

- Apoyar la revisión de los planes de calidad y seguridad presentados por las empresas contratistas en los aspectos relacionados con su especialidad, así como identificar y documentar desviaciones, deficiencias o posibles incumplimientos técnicos durante la ejecución de las obras, para consideración y gestión del profesional responsable.

- Apoyar las acciones orientadas a promover la calidad de las obras, el uso eficiente de los materiales y recursos y la incorporación de soluciones sostenibles y amigables con el medioambiente.

Apoyo en la gestión contractual, documental y financiera de las obras

- Apoyar la revisión y verificación de la documentación técnica presentada por las empresas contratistas, identificando posibles inconsistencias con los requerimientos establecidos y las condiciones contractuales para consideración del profesional responsable.

- Recopilar y preparar los insumos técnicos necesarios para el análisis de cuentas, reclamos, órdenes de cambio, obras adicionales y demás solicitudes relacionadas con la ejecución de las obras, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad.

- Apoyar la preparación del detalle y la documentación técnica requerida para la tramitación de cuentas ante la Contraloría General de la República de Panamá, de acuerdo con el avance de las obras.

- Apoyar la preparación de las certificaciones de satisfacción correspondientes a las obras asignadas, mediante la recopilación y verificación preliminar de la información relacionada con el cumplimiento de los cronogramas, planos, especificaciones técnicas y condiciones contractuales.

Informes, seguimiento y apoyo a la gestión del Proyecto

- Apoyar la preparación de informes técnicos semanales y periódicos sobre las actividades realizadas y el avance de las obras asignadas.

- Apoyar la elaboración de registros e informes preliminares sobre las incidencias, deficiencias o posibles incumplimientos identificados durante las visitas de campo.

- Recopilar y preparar información técnica sobre las obras asignadas para apoyar el seguimiento y la toma de decisiones del Proyecto.

- Brindar asistencia técnica, dentro del ámbito de su especialidad, a las actividades e iniciativas desarrolladas en el marco del Proyecto y del Programa País del PNUD, bajo la orientación del profesional responsable.

Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos relacionados con el proyecto.

- Participar en la capacitación del personal del proyecto sobre procedimientos internos y brindar apoyo en la organización de actividades de formación y fortalecimiento de capacidades, según sea necesario.

- Realizar aportes valiosos a las redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica.

- Mantener registros organizados de datos del proyecto, actividades de campo, estudios de caso, historias de interés humano, fotografías y otros documentos relevantes que puedan utilizarse para apoyar el intercambio de conocimientos y las actividades de incidencia.

El/la titular desempeñará otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Proyecto, la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

- Supervisión: El/la Asistente en Ingeniería Electromecánica trabajará bajo la supervisión general del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto y del/de la Director/a del Proyecto. Sus servicios se prestarán en el marco del Proyecto 01005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el Desarrollo”. La relación contractual se establecerá directamente con la Oficina de País del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), en coordinación con el equipo del Proyecto, el Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental y el Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH).

- Lugar de trabajo: Se contemplan dos (2) posiciones, con las siguientes ubicaciones y áreas de cobertura: Una (1) posición con sede en la provincia de Chiriquí, con disponibilidad para movilizarse a los proyectos, centros y sedes regionales del INADEH ubicados en las provincias de Chiriquí, Veraguas y Bocas del Toro. Una (1) posición con sede en la sede principal del INADEH, ubicada en Vía Tocumen, con disponibilidad para movilizarse a los proyectos, centros y sedes regionales ubicados en las provincias de Darién, Panamá, Panamá Oeste, Coclé, Veraguas, Herrera y Los Santos.

- Horario : El/la profesional deberá laborar en horario regular de lunes a viernes. Cuando las necesidades del Proyecto lo requieran, deberá tener disponibilidad para laborar en horario extendido.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development. SFH work is delivered through three interconnected portfolios: 1) Public Finance for the SDGs; 2) Private Finance for the SDGs; and 3) Global & Country Financing Policy Frameworks.

The European Commission (EC), together with EU Member States, development agencies, EU financial institutions and UN organizations, have embarked on coordinating their offer of EU expertise and resources for low- and middle-income countries in the area of sustainable finance, inspired by EU experience, through the EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, of which UNDP is an implementing partner, focusing on supporting countries on sustainable finance taxonomy development, disclosure frameworks and thematic/green bond framework development.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Debt and Investments and with a cross-reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Africa, the Investment and Debt Finance Specialist will primarily be responsible for the delivery of activities under the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub implemented by UNDP. The role is hosted within the SFH Private Finance Portfolio, under the Investments and Debt unit.

Working closely with colleagues across the SFH portfolios and the Global Policy Network in Africa, the Specialist will provide technical and analytical support to partner governments, financial institutions, and issuers on sustainable finance instruments, with a focus on green and sustainability bond issuance. This includes pre- and post-issuance support, knowledge generation on fixed-income markets and other debt instruments, identification and assessment of green investment opportunities, and design of monitoring and reporting frameworks for environmental and climate impacts. The role will also contribute to building in-house capacity and institutional knowledge on debt and investment finance, ensuring effective translation of these skills into the design and implementation of innovative financing instruments at the country level, in line with the objectives of the Global Green Bond Initiative and the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub both being linked to Global Gateway.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Investments and Debt Finance Specialist will play a central role in advancing UNDP’s Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) agenda in Africa, while also contributing to global workstreams. Based in UNDP Sustainable Finance Hub for Africa, the incumbent will be responsible for the following functions and duties:

1. Provision of thematic debt instruments and country support

- Advise and support the development and implementation of UNDP’s thematic debt offering and lead the design and piloting of innovative development bond frameworks in selected countries across the Africa region, in close coordination with SFH portfolios, UNDP Country Offices and SFH Regional Advisors;

- Provide tailored technical advice to governments and partners to address country-specific financing needs with a particular focus on green bonds with the European Commission under the EU Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub.

2. Strategic alignment with European commission initiatives

- Ensure key focus and coherence with the European Commission’s Global Green Bond Initiative;

- Contribute to joint EC-UNDP workplans and reporting, promoting alignment with EU sustainable finance frameworks and global standards;

- Provide technical inputs as an implementing partner of EC Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub, in coordination with SFH portfolios;

- Prepare donor reports, and contribute to monitoring frameworks, ensuring consistency with regional priorities and global strategies and UNDP/SFH systems.

3. Ensure partnerships and scaling of sustainable finance solutions

- Contribute to UNDP’s broader financing and investment agenda by leveraging networks, fostering partnerships, and identifying opportunities to scale sustainable finance solutions at global and country-levels with a focus on blended finance structures.

4. Provision of methodological guidance and flagship initiatives

- Contribute to the development of methodological tools and guidance related to thematic bonds and debt instruments

- Provide support to SFH Portfolios, enhancing their application and impact in - countries in Africa.

5. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia;

- Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application;

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on development and project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area;

- Promote advocacy for UNDP’s work and opportunities for collaboration in address in development trends in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Investment and Debt Finance Specialist will carry out relevant duties under the guidance and direct supervision of the Head of Debt and Investments and with a cross-reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Africa, the Investment and Debt Finance Senior Specialist.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

Cross-Functional and Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Strategy

- Negotiation and Influence: Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management

- Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively. Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Programme and Policy

- SDG Finance: SDG-aligned Fiscal and Debt Instruments

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Finance, Economics, Development Finance or closely related field is required or;

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of experience in sustainable finance, thematic bond issuance or related areas, is required.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing thematic bond frameworks, including impact measurement, evaluation, and reporting.

Sandra Onwualu

- Proven track record in structuring thematic debt, including green and blue bonds, with issuers in Africa or other developing country contexts;

- Proven track record of conducting market analyses and preliminary studies for green bond and/or other investment opportunities;

- Experience in advising on sovereign, sub-sovereign, and/or corporate bond development, including structuring, partnerships, and use of proceeds (experience in Africa is an advantage);

- Experience working in corporate bond issuers;

- Strong experience in working with complex projects and datasets, with the ability to synthesize information, support partnership building, present to senior/board-level stakeholders and mobilize resources;

- Experience in blended finance or other financial instruments for green/sustainable investments;

- Familiarity with EU and international best practices for green bond issuance.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and French.

- Knowledge of another UN language is an asset.

Professional Certificates

- Supplementary financial certifications (i.e. CFA, CAIA, CPA) are highly desirable.

OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions.

The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has responsibility for inter-agency coordination in complex emergencies and natural disasters. In the context of the deteriorating humanitarian situation in the occupied Palestinian territory, the OCHA Office has specific responsibility for (a) disseminating information and policies to the humanitarian community, authorities, and donors, as well as supporting resource mobilization efforts; (b) assisting in the identification of humanitarian priorities and needs and the coordination of resource mobilization efforts; and (c) disseminating information on the impact of natural disasters, response there too and the need for international assistance.

This fixed term job opening is being advertised for the position of Finance Associate in East Jerusalem, Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT). Under the guidance of the Head of the Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager and direct supervision of the Finance Officer.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Finance Associate will be responsible for the following duties:

Provide support in the allocation and financial management processes of the oPt Humanitarian Fund (HF)

- Provide support to the strategic review committees by reviewing submitted project budgets and assigning scores for cost-effectiveness.

- Review project budgets to ensure compliance with the HF global guidelines and oPt operational manual and submit them to the Finance Officer for clearance.

- Conduct meetings with partners to discuss financial comments and finalize budget review.

- Draft grant agreements and amendments as per oPt allocation modalities.

- Review budget amendments and revision requests and submit them to the Finance Officer for clearance.

- Regular follow-up with implementing partners to obtain financial reports.

- Review interim and final financial reports to ensure compliance with the signed agreements, budgets, and guidelines and submit them to NY for approval.

- Follow up on disbursement of funds and refund of balances from partners.

Provide support in the implementation of operational and financial management strategies of the oPt HF Accountability Framework

- Assist in conducting financial capacity assessments for newly registered partners to determine eligibility and assign appropriate risk levels.

- Conducting Financial Spot Checks (FSC) for implementing partners as per the oPt operational manual. Assist in reviewing financial documents, preparing FSC reports, and following up with partners on FSC recommendations and required actions.

- Provide the audit company with the needed financial supporting documents to facilitate the auditing of projects.

- Follow up on auditing status for ended projects and assist in reviewing audit reports.

- Draft confirmation letters to the Audit company regarding funds received by partners each year.

- Promote awareness of global guidelines, opt operational manuals, and Grant Management Systems.

- Assist in conducting training for implementing partners and other stakeholders.

- Support in preparing a synthesis of lessons learned and best practices in financial management.

- Contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Assist in providing financial figures for the monthly and annual reports.

Facilitate knowledge-building and knowledge-sharing within oPt HF implementing partners

Provide support for other Financial and Administrative tasks as needed

- Monitor and Support response to partners as per directives from the Head of HFU.

- Provide logistical and other support for the organization and execution of HF workshops and events.

- Provide administrative support to the HF unit as needed.

- Provide other support to OCHA as needed.

- Perform other duties as required.

Competencies

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of, and ability to apply financial rules, regulations, and procedures in the UN environment. Knowledge, skills, and ability to extract, interpret, analyze, and format data across the full range of finance and budget functions, including program development and database management, claims, and treasury operations. Ability to identify and resolve data discrepancies and operational problems. Shows pride in work and achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines, and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work.

PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

ACCOUNTABILITY: Takes ownership of all responsibilities, and honors commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within the prescribed time, cost, and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight, and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required.

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Project Management, or any related field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

- (6) Six years of progressively responsible experience in finance and accounting at the national level is required.

OR

- (3) Three years of the above qualifying experience with a bachelor’s degree.

- Experience in working with spreadsheets is required.

- Experience in budgeting and analyzing financial reports is desirable.

- Experience in applying UN Financial Rules and Regulations is desirable.

- Experience with the UN common system or equivalent international organization is desirable.

- Knowledge of Grant Management System (GMS) is desirable.

Language:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Descripción de la Oficina / Unidad / Proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

El PNUD trabaja en más de 170 países y territorios, dando asistencia para desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo y asociación, capacidades institucionales y construcción de resiliencia, fomentando el desarrollo humano sostenible. En Panamá trabaja a nivel nacional, nivel municipal y comarcal. El PNUD hace parte de las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Panamá aportando al logro del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible (UNSDCF en inglés).

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional: Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

El Plan Estratégico de Gobierno 2025-2029 y con los marcos programáticos del Marco de Cooperación de Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá (UNSDCF) 2026-2030 y del Programa de País del PNUD 2026-2030, que priorizan el crecimiento económico inclusivo y un ambiente sostenible, fomentando el bienestar y la equidad en la población, y promoviendo sistemas de gobernanza inclusivos, eficaces y responsables. De esta forma, el proyecto en la cuenca del río Indio se posiciona como un modelo innovador y replicable para integrar catastro, desarrollo humano y sostenibilidad ambiental en territorios de alta importancia estratégica para Panamá.

En su rol como socio para el desarrollo y articulador para la Agenda 2030 de Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) brindamos asistencia técnica para acelerar que se logren los ODS como catalizadores para lograr que todas las personas vivan mejor en armonía con el planeta.

En el área de Ambiente, Cambio Climático y Gestión de Riesgos (donde hay confluencia de los otros clústeres y portafolio) la gestión integrada de cuencas hidrográficas es una de las herramientas para lograr la mejor u óptima asignación de uso / actividades humanas de agua y del territorio para garantizar a largo plazo recursos hídricos, la salud de los ecosistemas y prosperidad para las personas.

La ACP, con socios estratégicos y la coordinación interinstitucional, impulsará el desarrollo de iniciativas de mejorar la calidad de vida de las personas a través de una eficiente administración del agua en la cuenca hidrográfica de río Indio, lo que a su vez fortalecerá el sistema de lagos del Canal de Panamá fomentando beneficios a las comunidades locales, traducidos en favorecer un desarrollo humano sostenible para la cogestión socioeconómica y ambiental.

Avanzar en transformaciones estructurales debe hacerse desde lo que las propias comunidades han reconocido como exitoso y de alto valor, que es el aseguramiento de los derechos sobre la tierra a través de un programa de catastro y titulación en los territorios dentro de esta cuenca hidrográfica, de tal manera que las personas que allí habitan tengan seguridad jurídica de sus tierras y que este derecho sirva no solo para empoderar hombres y especialmente mujeres, sino como catalizador para mejorar sus condiciones de vida.

Con la integración de la Cuenca del río Indio a la Cuenca del Canal de Panamá, se continúa un enfoque integral de gestión del territorio, que incluye el programa de catastro y titulación, similar al desarrollado en la CHCP, donde se han entregado más de 12,080 títulos desde 2006. En este marco, se aprobó el ProDoc del Proyecto de Catastro y Titulación del río Indio, cuyo objetivo es abordar la falta de seguridad jurídica sobre la tierra, una situación que aumenta la vulnerabilidad de las comunidades y limita sus oportunidades de inversión y participación en la gestión sostenible del territorio.

La ACP impulsa un proyecto de catastro y titulación en la Cuenca del río Indio para fortalecer la seguridad jurídica de la tierra y promover un desarrollo sostenible. Además de la titulación, la iniciativa incluye capacitación, fortalecimiento de la gobernanza local y uso responsable del territorio.

El objetivo es avanzar en la regularización de áreas no tituladas y completar los procesos iniciados entre 2017 y 2019, apoyando también el diseño conceptual de un futuro reservorio multipropósito y otros proyectos integrales en la cuenca.

Para su ejecución, se requiere una unidad técnica que realice levantamientos de campo, tramite resoluciones de regularización, gestione expedientes pendientes, actualice el catastro y desarrolle nuevos procesos de titulación en áreas adicionales de la cuenca.

Objetivo del Proyecto

Desarrollar barridos catastrales en aproximadamente 60,000 hectáreas como parte del proceso de regularización territorial en la Cuenca de río Indio y gestionar la emisión de los títulos de propiedad correspondientes, así como participar en la verificación técnica de medidas y linderos de las fincas requeridas en los procesos de adquisición de tierras para los reasentamientos del Proyecto del Lago de río Indio, asegurando de manera transversal la implementación de acciones que garanticen la participación y la inclusión efectiva de las mujeres como propietarias de predios.

El Proyecto de catastro y titulación estima:

- El barrido catastral de aproximadamente 60,000 hectáreas.

- La inscripción ante el Registro Público de aproximadamente 2,600 fincas.

- La rectificación de medidas y linderos de aproximadamente 5,000 hectáreas.

Alcance del trabajo

Bajo la dirección general del/la Coordinador/a del Proyecto, el/la Asociado/a de Proyecto brindará apoyo en la gestión financiera, presupuestaria y administrativa de los proyectos ejecutados con la Autoridad del Canal de Panamá (ACP), mediante el seguimiento y análisis de la ejecución financiera y su correspondencia con el avance físico, metas, productos e indicadores establecidos.

Asimismo, apoyará la consolidación y análisis de información, elaboración de informes, seguimiento presupuestario, gestión documental y atención de requerimientos de control, auditoría y rendición de cuentas, contribuyendo a que la ejecución de los proyectos se desarrolle de manera oportuna, eficiente y conforme al presupuesto, los procedimientos establecidos y los estándares de calidad aplicables.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Apoyo al seguimiento financiero y presupuestario del proyecto

- Consolidar y analizar la información financiera y presupuestaria del proyecto, incluyendo ejecución, compromisos, desembolsos, saldos y proyecciones.

- Identificar variaciones, riesgos y necesidades de ajuste, y presentar los resultados al Coordinador del Proyecto para su seguimiento y toma de decisiones.

2. Apoyo al seguimiento de la ejecución física y financiera del proyecto

- Recopilar, verificar y consolidar información sobre el avance físico y técnico de las actividades, metas, productos e indicadores del proyecto, en coordinación con los diferentes componentes y asociados.

- Contrastar los avances físicos y técnicos con la ejecución financiera y presupuestaria, identificando desviaciones y generando insumos para el análisis del desempeño del proyecto y de los equipos responsables, para consideración del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto.

3. Apoyo en la gestión de información y elaboración de informes

- Mantener actualizados los registros, bases de datos, matrices y demás herramientas de seguimiento financiero y administrativo, asegurando la integridad, consistencia, disponibilidad y trazabilidad de la información.

- Preparar y consolidar informes, reportes y cuadros financieros, presupuestarios y administrativos, integrando la información suministrada por los diferentes componentes y organizando los soportes requeridos para revisión y validación del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto.

4. Apoyo a la gestión documental, el control y la rendición de cuentas

- Apoyar la organización, actualización y disponibilidad de la documentación financiera y administrativa requerida para los procesos de rendición de cuentas, auditorías, revisiones y controles internos.

- Dar seguimiento a las acciones y requerimientos que le sean asignados en el marco de dichos procesos, asegurando la disponibilidad y trazabilidad de la documentación de respaldo.

5. Apoyo a la gestión y cierre del proyecto

- Participar, cuando sea requerido, en reuniones y actividades de seguimiento del proyecto, proporcionando información y apoyo financiero-administrativo para facilitar el monitoreo de la ejecución y la toma de decisiones.

- Contribuir al cierre de los períodos de ejecución y del proyecto mediante la organización y consolidación de documentación, evidencias y lecciones aprendidas relacionadas con su ámbito de responsabilidad.

6. Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto.

- Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción.

- Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro de la oficina de país y a nivel regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado.

- Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

El/La titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la Asociado/a de Proyectos trabajará bajo la supervisión del/la Coordinador/a del Proyecto, del Proyecto de Catastro y Titulación de la cuenca hidrográfica de río Indio.

La sede del proyecto se encuentra en la Oficina de la Unidad Técnica de Apoyo de la Cuenca Hidrográfica del río Indio, ubicada en Capira, provincia de Panamá Oeste, sobre la vía Panamericana. Las actividades se desarrollarán principalmente en la Cuenca Hidrográfica del río Indio, comprendida entre las provincias de Coclé, Colón y Panamá Oeste, así como en otras subcuencas de la Cuenca Hidrográfica del Canal de Panamá. En función de las necesidades operativas, las labores podrán ejecutarse tanto en la sede del proyecto como en instalaciones de instituciones asociadas y en áreas de intervención, incluyendo zonas de difícil acceso.

El horario regular de trabajo será de lunes a viernes; en atención a la naturaleza de las actividades de campo y los requerimientos del proyecto, podrá ser necesario laborar en horarios extendidos, fines de semana y días feriados, así como participar en giras que impliquen desplazamientos y permanencia temporal (pernoctar) en las áreas de intervención. Los gastos extraordinarios de movilización y hospedaje que se deriven exclusivamente de estas actividades serán cubiertos por el proyecto, conforme a la planificación y los procedimientos establecidos.

Se requiere que la persona contratada cuente con licencia de conducir vigente y experiencia comprobada en el manejo de vehículos 4x4, con capacidad para desplazarse de manera segura en terrenos complejos y condiciones propias del trabajo de campo.

2. Piensa de manera innovadora

2. Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) DRC Country office is part of the United Nations system working to support the country’s development agenda. Its overall aim is to ensure that people attain a better standard of living through sustainable development. To achieve this goal, UNDP’s work is anchored on the Global Development Agenda, also known as the Sustainable Development Goals with the target date of 2030, is guided by the United Nations Development Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF 2025-2029), the UNDP Strategic Plan and the Country Programme Document (CPD 2025-2029). UNSDCF and CPD are developed and implemented in coordination with the Government, civil society and development partners.

The work of UNDP DRC office is guided by the recently developed UNSDCF, which describes the collective vision and response of the UN system to the Government of DRC development priorities outlined in the National Strategic Development Plan (PNSD 2024 – 2028), and the CPD, through its “Output 4.2: Equitable access to clean, sustainable, and affordable energy and energy services for populations in rural and peri-urban areas is improved”.

The overall goal of the project is a sustainable, carbon-neutral living environment in rural areas, achieved by improving energy access and promoting sustainable energy production and consumption in Kwango Province. To reach this goal, the project pursues two outcomes. First, it aims to increase the use of renewable energy in the target area, mainly through a solar photovoltaic mini grid in Kenge serving the General Referral Hospital, nearby households, SMEs and public facilities. Second, it aims to strengthen capacities related to carbon neutrality and renewable energy within national and provincial institutions and local communities, laying the foundation for wider renewable energy deployment in the DRC.

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Analyst will work under the strategic guidance and direct supervision of country office. He/she promotes a collaborative, client-focused, quality, strategic, and results oriented approach to all tasks; and works in close collaboration with monitoring and Evaluation Unit and project teams in the Country office and other relevant stakeholders.

3. Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the Energy Programme Manager, the Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Analyst will work in close collaboration with Inclusive Growth and Sustainable Development Pilar colleagues, the Country office Monitoring and Evaluation Unit, and other relevant stakeholders and will have the following duties and responsibilities:

1.Ensure effective monitoring of the project results

- Develop an M&E plan for the project to ensure effective and efficient implementation of the project and to ensure that activities and outputs result in positive outcomes.

- Develop/update project monitoring tools including forms, questionnaires, check lists etc.

- Undertake regular field trips to the project sites and provide monitoring reports on progress.

- Perform data monitoring and analysis as per Project’s Results Framework having ensured triangulation of qualitative, quantitative and impact level data and prepare relevant reports.

- Develop/update the project dashboard analytical tool and provide recommendations for improvements.

- Monitor overall progress of the project and ensure tracking performance through the collection of appropriate and credible data and other evidence on achievement of results.

- Analyse evidence to inform management decision-making, improve effectiveness and efficiency, and adjust programming as necessary.

- Participate in annual project reviews and planning workshops and assist the Project Manager in preparing relevant reports.

- Prepare Issues Log and Risk Log for the project.

- Prepare and maintain a database to track progress on the project’s indicators and targets.

- Provide input and update information related to progress project outcome in UNDP.

- Provide support in the drafting of ToRs for Baseline and End-line project evaluation.

- Assist international and local evaluators to conduct mid-term and final evaluations of the project.

- Provide technical inputs in the review of outputs by consultants hired under the component activities

2.Ensure effective report writing

- Provide inputs, information and statistics for quarterly, annual and other reports.

- Provide support to the Programme Manager by drafting high-quality project-related and donor reports, consolidating data, and ensuring adherence to donor reporting standards

- Liaise with the UNDP Country office relevant teams and provide requested inputs for the corporate strategic reports.

- Prepare materials for the outreach activities.

- Conduct synthesis of the works, reports and other outputs of consultants and sub-contractors involved in the Project

-

3.Facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing:

- Organize and conduct training on M&E for the project and government-relevant stakeholders if needed.

- Closely work with project personnel and provide support, when necessary, on the topics related to M&E.

- In coordination with Project Manager to develop scale-up proposal of best practices of the project;

- Effective support to the establishment of showcase to external stakeholders on progress made and impacts delivered

- Provide support with other tasks required by the pillar and the office in M&E and reporting

- Provide support in ensuring donor visibility in close collaboration with the Country Office Communications Team, in strict compliance with the UNDP and donor's visibility guidelines.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Energy Programme Manager and in close collaboration of the Country office monitoring and evaluation unit.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management - Monitoring and Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Management Results-based Management Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved

performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Partnership Management Resource Mobilization Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities, and establish a plan to meet funding requirements

Business Management Risk Management Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks Finance Audit Risk Management Ability to address risks and audit issues raised in the course of an audit and propose solutions in order to ensure a true and fair audit opinion is achieved

Business Management Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Education requirements

• Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Monitoring and Evaluation, Economics, Finance, or related field is required. or

• A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Min. years of relevant work experience

• Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively relevant working experience in the field of monitoring and evaluation is required.

Required skills

• Proven experience in collecting, analysing, synthesizing and interpreting data is required;

• Proven experience in production of high-quality reports is required

• Proficiency and proven experience in the use of Microsoft Office suite (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint) is required.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Previous professional experience in least developed countries (LDCs), developing countries, fragile and crisis-affected countries would be an asset.
