jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia for its current Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

- Human Development

- Nature, Decarbonisation and Resilience

- Economic and Digital Transformation

The Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) portfolio supports governance institutions and development actors to strengthen public-sector effectiveness, local governance and capacity building, promoting transparency and accountability, and building resilience towards climate change and other development risks. The portfolio promotes collaboration across levels of government and locally driven solutions that translate national priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals into measurable results for communities.

The Local Governance Analysist provides substantive technical, analytical and programmatic support across the HDRG portfolio, with emphasis on local governance, local economic development, sub-national institutional capacity building, municipal planning and budgeting, and quality public service delivery, inclusive participation, development financing, evidence and data, partnerships, quality assurance, and knowledge management.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.Local governance policy and technical advisory support

- Lead the local governance pillar for UNDP Indonesia by providing applied policy and technical advice on decentralization, multi-level governance, local public administration, digitalised public service delivery and innovations, and national and sub-national institutional capacity.

- Assess and translate national policy directions and sub-national priorities into practical programme options, technical recommendations, implementation pathways and scalable solutions.

- Conduct political-economy, institutional, stakeholder, capacity and policy analyses, combining quantitative and qualitative evidence and clearly identifying implementation constraints, incentives, risks and opportunities.

- Integrate human rights, gender equality, disability inclusion, Leaving No One Behind, conflict sensitivity, social and environmental standards, and digital and data considerations into technical analysis and advice.

- Prepare high-quality technical briefs, policy notes, issue papers, talking points and presentations for engagement with government at national and subnational levels, as well as development partners to strengthen local governance and local development .

2. Programme and project design

- Lead or substantively contribute to concept notes, project documents, theories of change, result frameworks, workplans, budgets, risk registers, monitoring frameworks, implementation arrangements and sustainability strategies.

- Develop options for piloting, testing, adapting and scaling local governance interventions, including digital or data-enabled approaches where suitable and responsible.

- Apply results-based management principles and ensure clear causal logic, measurable indicators, baselines, targets, assumptions, evidence sources and learning mechanisms.

- Ensure alignment of local governance and local development opporunities with UNDP strategic priorities, the Country Programme, national and sub-national development plans and priorty works streams of UNDP Indonesia across the three clusters

- Ensure programme designs are operationally feasible, risk-informed and supported by credible stakeholder ownership and institutional arrangements.

3 Partnerships and multi-stakeholder engagement

- Establish strong partnerships with public sector actors who have a role in enabling strong local governance and local development by engaging with regional governments, Ministry of Home Affairs, Bappenas, Ministry of Finance, sectoral ministries and agencies, provincial and district/municipal governments, universities, think tanks, civil society, private-sector actors and development partners.

- Design and facilitate inclusive policy dialogues, consultations, technical working groups, missions, workshops and peer-learning processes involving stakeholders with different interests and levels of technical expertise.

- Identify opportunities for diversified partnerships to unlock public financing to strengthen local development and local governance with clear entry points for UNDP

- Identify opportunities for joint programming, knowledge exchange, and capacity development while promoting complementarity with government and partner initiatives.

4 Resource mobilization and development finance

- Identify and assess funding and co-financing opportunities linked to local governance and sustainable human development, including public finance, private-sector participation, philanthropy and development-partner funding.

- Prepare donor intelligence, funding maps, partnership pipelines, investment cases, pitch materials, proposal narratives and substantive inputs to financing strategies.

- Develop technically credible options for blended finance, public-private collaboration, pooled or catalytic funding and other financing approaches, with explicit attention to feasibility, additionality, safeguards and risk.

- Coordinate substantive follow-up on partnership and funding opportunities, maintaining clear ownership, decision points, documentation and next steps.

- Support due diligence and risk analysis for proposed partnerships and financing arrangements in coordination with relevant UNDP functions.

5. Knowledge management and capacity development

- Generate and curate knowledge from programme implementation, field engagement, peer exchange and research, including lessons, good practices, innovations and evidence of results and convert learning into recommendations for programme adjustments and scale

- Produce or coordinate policy briefs, case studies, guidance notes, analytical products, presentations, learning materials and data-informed narratives for policy and programme audiences.

- Design and facilitate communities of practice, peer exchanges and capacity-development activities for national and sub-national stakeholders.

- Ensure knowledge products are technically accurate, accessible, inclusive, appropriately sourced and responsive to the needs of intended users.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: N/A

Institutional Arrangement

The Local Governance Analyst (LGA) will work under the overall supervision of the Team Leader HDRG, providing policy, analytical and technical advisory support on local governance, decentralization and sub-national development. The incumbent will work closely with HDRG programme and other units to translate policy priorities, institutional analysis and evidence into practical programme solutions, technical recommendations, partnership opportunities and knowledge products. The LGA will also provide substantive inputs to programme and project design, stakeholder engagement, resource mobilization and capacity development, and may coordinate technical contributors supporting relevant workstreams.

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Rio de Janeiro Mayors Challenge (Office Based) [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

Em linha com o compromisso de preservar a capacidade institucional e apoiar o pessoal já presente na Organização, a maioria das vagas do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV é publicada utilizando um processo de candidatura em camadas, no qual:

• Tier 0: Funcionários internacionais do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos permanentes (PA) e de prazo fixo (FTA), cujos postos serão abolidos ou cujos contratos serão encerrados ou não renovados durante 2026.

• Tier 1: Outros funcionários do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos permanentes (PA) e de prazo fixo (FTA).

• Tier 2: Funcionários do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos temporários (TA), pessoal com contratos PSA regulares, e Voluntários da ONU nas categorias Especialista e Expert.

• Tier 3 ou sem tier indicado: Todos os demais tipos de contrato do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV e de outras agências, bem como candidatos externos.

Por favor, observe o(s) Tier(s) indicado(s) no título da vaga, se aplicável, e certifique-se de que atende aos critérios de elegibilidade para candidatura.

Escritório/Unidade/Descrição do Projeto

O PNUD oferece soluções integradas de programa, políticas e financiamento para a realização dos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Nesse contexto, o PNUD criou a Rede Global de Políticas (GPN), uma rede de especialistas técnicos locais e globais em uma ampla gama de áreas de conhecimento, em apoio às soluções emblemáticas e às capacidades organizacionais previstas no Plano Estratégico. O Birô de Políticas e Apoio a Programas (BPPS) e o Birô de Crises (CB) são os dois birôs âncora da GPN. Nesse contexto, o Hub de Governança, Estado de Direito e Construção da Paz (GRP), iniciativa conjunta com o BPPS, oferece liderança e serviços de assessoria para ampliar o impacto do PNUD na governança e na construção da paz, assegurando a integração da governança democrática e dos direitos humanos à resposta e à recuperação em contextos de crise.

Os governos locais e regionais já são responsáveis por mais de 65% das metas dos ODS, a maioria delas ligada à prestação de serviços básicos, como água, saneamento, mobilidade, ação climática, saúde e educação. As cidades e os territórios têm um papel central na implementação dos ODS, que vêm se tornando um novo instrumento de planejamento estratégico e orçamentação de médio e longo prazo. Desde 2015, os governos locais e suas associações têm atuado de forma cada vez mais ativa na promoção dos ODS, por meio de advocacy e do trabalho com a população local e com parceiros, para levar o espírito da Agenda 2030 às cidades e aos territórios. Os governos locais também passaram a usar os ODS como marco estratégico para oferecer serviços públicos melhores e mais inovadores, vinculados às metas e aos indicadores dos ODS. No âmbito do projeto SDG Local Action, o PNUD é um dos parceiros implementadores do Mayors Challenge (Desafio de Prefeitos), iniciativa global para repensar os serviços mais essenciais que as cidades prestam aos moradores.

Nesse contexto, o projeto SDG Local Action busca contratar um(a) Engenheiro(a) de Dados para apoiar a implementação do projeto Mayors Challenge 2025 no Rio de Janeiro, Brasil. O projeto implementa uma metodologia de políticas públicas orientada por dados para antecipar as necessidades dos cidadãos e oferecer serviços de forma proativa, com potencial de replicação em diferentes públicos-alvo. Sua aplicação inicial ocorre por meio da Plataforma Pequenos Cariocas, iniciativa prioritária da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro voltada à primeira infância. O projeto utiliza o Registro Municipal Integrado (RMI), uma base de dados consolidada no data lake municipal que integra informações de Saúde, Educação e Assistência Social, permitindo análises avançadas e uma visão mais integrada dos cidadãos. Com base nessa infraestrutura, o projeto combina modelos analíticos e comunicações proativas, especialmente via WhatsApp, para ampliar o acesso aos serviços e gerar dados que apoiem políticas públicas mais eficazes.

O(A) Engenheiro(a) de Dados será responsável por construir e manter a infraestrutura de dados, integrando dados de múltiplas secretarias municipais, modelando pipelines de dados robustos e garantindo a qualidade e a governança dos dados, para que as informações certas cheguem ao lugar certo, com confiabilidade.

Deveres e responsabilidades

A. Garantir o desenvolvimento e a operação dos pipelines de dados

• Desenvolver e manter pipelines de ingestão, transformação e entrega de dados entre sistemas heterogêneos.

• Implementar e operar integrações com ferramentas como Airbyte, Prefect e similares.

• Implementar sistemas de alertas e notificações para detectar e comunicar falhas nos pipelines.

• Monitorar a saúde dos pipelines em produção, agindo de forma proativa diante de falhas e degradações de desempenho.

B. Garantir a qualidade e a governança dos dados

• Modelar dados e construir transformações que assegurem qualidade, consistência e rastreabilidade.

• Incorporar boas práticas de qualidade de dados, como testes e observabilidade de pipelines.

C. Garantir a articulação com as equipes e a evolução da infraestrutura

• Colaborar com as equipes de produto, engenharia e dados para mapear necessidades e traduzi-las em soluções de dados.

• Participar das decisões técnicas sobre a evolução da infraestrutura de dados.

D. Apoiar a documentação e o compartilhamento de conhecimento

• Documentar fluxos de dados, contratos de integração e decisões de arquitetura.

• Facilitar a construção e a gestão do conhecimento.

O(A) contratado(a) desempenha outras atividades compatíveis com seu perfil funcional, conforme necessário para o bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

Esta posição reporta-se ao(à) Gerente de Projeto do Rio Mayors Challenge. O(A) contratado(a) trabalhará em estreita colaboração com a IplanRio, as secretarias municipais relevantes, as equipes técnicas e as contrapartes do PNUD, para apoiar a implementação, a coordenação e a elaboração de relatórios do projeto.

Competências

Alcançar resultados:

LEVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo

Pensamento inovador:

LEVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, é pragmático para resolver problemas, faz melhoria.

Aprendizagem continua:

LEVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar com agilidade:

LEVEL 1: Adapta-se à mudança, lida de forma construtiva com a ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Atuar com determinação:

LEVEL 1: Mostra determinação e motivação, capaz de entregar com calma diante da adversidade, confiança

Engajar-se e ser parceiro:

LEVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão para com os outros, forma relacionamentos positivo

Promover diversidade e inclusão:

LEVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação.

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Digital - Data engineering:

• Domínio de linguagens de programação como SQL, Python e R, habilidade para encontrar soluções de armazenamento de dados (data warehousing), uso de ferramentas de ETL (extração, transformação e carga) e compreensão básica de aprendizado de máquina e algoritmos.

Digital - Data governance:

• Conhecimento de ciência de dados, habilidade para desenvolver ferramentas de gestão de dados, organizar e manter bancos de dados e operar tecnologias de visualização de dados

Digital - Data strategy and management:

• Conhecimento para elaborar ou executar uma estratégia de dados ou um marco de gestão de dados

Business Management - Communication:

jobs.title: Technical Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Guided by the global UNDP Strategic Plan (2022 – 2025) and the UNDP Country Programme Document (CPD) for Lao PDR (2022 – 2026), UNDP in Lao PDR works closely with the line Ministries, mass organizations, civil society, development partners, and the private sector at both national and sub-national levels in pursuit of the national socio-economic development priorities defined in Lao PDR’s five-year National Socio-Economic Development Plan (NSEDP) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

UNDP has a long history working in Lao PDR. UNDP’s comparative advantage has been its ability to work closely with a broad range of government and local institutions at all levels. UNDP’s work is focused on the provision of policy advice and technical support in the design and implementation of national legislation and strategies across three broad priority pillars – (1) inclusive growth and reduced inequalities, including UXO clearance and risk education, (2) natural resources, climate change and disaster risk reduction, and (3) effective, responsive, and accountable governance.

The UNDP country programme is aligned with the 9th NSEDP and aims to support Lao PDR to recover from the economic and social impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic and to ensure a smooth transition from Least Developed Country status, with a particular emphasis on supporting inclusive growth and reducing inequality.

The current project is a Child Project under the GEF-8 Regional Indo-Malay Critical Forest Biome Integrated Programme that has the long-term goal of maintaining the integrity of globally important primary forests of Indo-Malaya for maximizing multiple global environment benefits related to carbon and biodiversity. As a contribution to the above-referenced long-term goal of the integrated programme, the Lao PDR child project's objective is to promote nature-positive development to reduce ecosystem degradation and generate multiple benefits through strengthened protection of primary forest landscapes (PFLs) in Lao PDR. It will operationalize the integrated management of the primary forest landscapes in Lao PDR to generate multiple benefits including effective conservation and protection of globally threatened species and ecosystems, reduce or stop deforestation and degradation of primary forests landscapes, conserve and enhance their ecosystem services and support sustainable local livelihoods from local communities that are dependent on these forests. The project recognizes that these globally important primary forest landscapes, which are important for the conservation of species, habitats and natural ecosystems, underpin the lives and livelihoods of local communities (in providing forest and natural resource products and critical ecosystems services). To achieve this objective, the GEF alternative aims to (i) take into account the interconnectivity of primary forest and other natural ecosystems in key biogeographic regions in the country, and in particular in the Annamite Range; (ii) ensure that relevant agencies and actors have adequate capacities to promote integrated approaches and tackle the threat to primary forests, biodiversity and natural resources management; and (iii) advocate science based approaches and use of traditional and good practice knowledge systems to promote sustainable forestry, agricultural and livelihood management practices. The project objective will be achieved through the following six inter-linked components:

- Component 1: Enabling environment for ensuring durable protection of Primary Forests Landscapes

- Component 2: Strengthening management and governance capacities for empowering local communities for management of Protected Areas

- Component 3: Strengthened stakeholder collaboration to improved/inclusive management of primary forests outside PAs, including buffers and connectivity corridors

- Component 4: Strengthen sustainable PA financing and reduce the financial gap and scaling-up investments for primary forest conservation

- Component 5: Coordination, knowledge management and strengthen effective regional cooperation on durability of primary forests

- Component 6: Project Monitoring, evaluation and reporting ensured

The Technical Specialist will work under the supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Lao PDR , and work closely with the Team Lead for Natural Resource Management, Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Unit, UNDP in Lao PDR and the Project management Unit (PMU) as well as the key government counterparts. Below is the project organizational structure – depicting the reporting lines for this position.

This position will be located at the Department of Forestry (DOF), Misnitry of Agriculture and Forestry (MAF), Vientiane Capital, with occasionally travel to project offices in Savannakhet, Saravan, Chamapsack and Sekong provinces.

Duties and Responsibilities

The position will have lead technical responsibilities under the overall guidance of the Director General of the Department of Forestry (DOF), who serves as the National Project Director, and the supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Lao PDR and the Head of the Natural Resources Management, Climate Change, and Disaster Risk Reduction Unit. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: (i) technical project activities with a focus on monitoring, evaluation, and reporting; (ii) developing annual workplans and budgets, (iii) ensuring integration with all outcomes; (iv) guiding activities in provinces; (v) coordinating with other related projects; (vi) day-to-day project management; (vii) and following up on monitoring results and findings related to project outputs and outcomes.

S/he will provide high level advice and guidance to DOF/Government of Lao PDR and UNDP in the following areas:

- Technical and strategic guidance : Provide rigorous analysis and advice to the Government of Lao PDR on the assessment and formulation of national policies and regulations related to Primary Forest Landscapes (PFL). This includes capacity assessment and development planning for key institutions and private sector entities to mainstream PFLs in safeguard assessment and planning approaches. Develop the Annamite Management Strategy, ensuring consultation with all relevant stakeholders, prioritizing investments for PFLs, establishing coordination mechanisms, and monitoring the effectiveness of the planning process. Support the re-alignment of policies, planning, and financial systems to promote the implementation of the Annamite Management Strategy.

- Provision of technical advice: Offer technical advice, capacity building, institutional support, and project management support to the Government to ensure the effective and timely delivery of the Project.

- Support resource mobilization : Strengthen partnerships with relevant development organizations, UN agencies, and within the government network. Enhance coordination with key stakeholders to generate multiple benefits through strengthened protection of primary forest landscapes in Lao PDR

1. Strategic guidance, rigorous analysis and advice to the Government of Lao PDR to effectively consider, develop and implement sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry.

- Provide technical input and policy advice and supervise implementation of project activities with a special attention on planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting, and quality control of project outputs;

- Advise the Government and UNDP on the linkages with other major programmes or projects of other agencies, organizations or departments and UN agencies;

- Advisory and support in drafting and review of strategic and technical documents on sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, strategic environmental assessment, sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry such as policy papers or other analytical products in collaboration with other technical staff and consultants and Government counterparts;

- Ensure the development of cross-project linkages with other relevant UN and development partner projects for maximizing impact;

- Facilitate information sharing and dialogue within the donor community and prepare briefs and policy papers related to the context and focus of the project;

- Assist the Government in information sharing/knowledge management in the themes related to the scope of the project;

- Provide other advice and support as may be required by the Government and UNDP as is to be expected in a dynamic process of project implementation and changing circumstances;

- Systematically record the results of the project and provide substantive contribution to the UNDP/GEF annual reports as well as knowledge products.

2. Provision of technical advice, capacity building, institutional support, project management and implementation support to the Government to ensure effective and timely delivery of the project.

- Advise, support the relevant parties to develop a realistic annual and quarterly workplans and a corresponding budget plan with clearly stated milestones contributing to the achievement of target outcomes and outputs defined in the project document;

- Ensure the participation and involvement of relevant stakeholders in project activities at national, provincial and district levels in the project planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting;

- Support implementation of project activities to ensure delivery of resources and results according to planned targets, activities, and prepare the budget plan at the national, provincial and district levels;

- Ensure the development of linkages across the project outcomes and outputs, as well as advice and update the National Project Director and UNDP on the project progress on a regular basis;

- Advise, support and implement Annual Project Reviews, annual audits, mid-term evaluation and final evaluation of the Project in collaboration with the project team and consultants;

- Support recruitment of competent national and international experts that are needed by different outcomes/components of the project;

- Organize and oversee consultant input, develop detailed Terms of References for national and international consultants and contractors in collaboration with Project Manager, National Project Director, UNDP and support in procurement of goods, organization of training sessions, seminars, etc;

- Liaise with all consultants and project teams to ensure that the planned deliverables are completed in timely manner within the contract period;

- Support and be involved in organizing and facilitating project meetings, workshops etc. with relevant substantive inputs;

- Identify and develop synthesis of best practices and lessons learned for organizational sharing and learning;

- Closely work with the Project Coordinator/Monitoring & Evaluation and Reporting Officer to provide capacity development for key government staff at the national, provincial and district levels to support better informed and planned for the project, protected area conservation, sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry;

- Closely work with the Project Coordinator/Monitoring & Evaluation and Reporting Officer to provide capacity development for key government staff at the national, provincial and district levels to support and complete the Protected Area sites’ Management Effectiveness Tracking Tool (METT), Capacity Development Monitoring Scorecard and other tools as required by GEF 8;

- Ensure results of all training activities and workshop feeds into the progress reports with an emphasis on results-orientation;

- Support DOF and UNDP in closing projects operationally in accordance with rules and regulations of UNDP and the Government;

- Undertake technical oversight daily including monitoring technical aspects of project activities;

- Support on developing initial concept note to mobilize funds in scaling up the project.

3. Support resource mobilization and provide leadership on sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, community forest management, land use planning, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry within the government network, UN and strengthen partnerships/coordination with key stakeholders for better coordinated support for integrated sustainable development.

- Support the government and the UNDP in strengthening partnership/coordination with key stakeholders, particularly the donors/development partners, private sector, and the Government to identify opportunities, formulate joint initiative with maximum impacts and efficiency, minimize duplication of efforts and reduce traction costs in the area of sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, community forest management, land use planning, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy

- Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Effective Decision Making: Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

- Negotiation and Influence: Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Management

- Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

- Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks.

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Nature: Water Governance: Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM)

- Climate: Climate Change Adaptation: Water Resource Management and Access to Water

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in Protected Area Management, Land Use Planning, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Management and Planning, Sustainable Forest Management, Environmental Management, Environmental Economics, and/or relevant field of studies is required, OR:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor´s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of master´s degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 5 (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant working experience within protected area management, land use planning, natural resource management, environmental management and planning, sustainable forest management, environmental management, environmental economics, and/or relevant field of studies.

Required skills:

- At least 5 years of proven experience in project management, in providing management advisory services, hands-on experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development projects;

- Experience with project planning and consulting;

- Experience in fostering networks and partnerships;

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Skills:

- Demonstrated track record of experience in developing and providing sound policy advice, strategic planning, organizational guidance and critical analysis in relation to protected area management, land use planning, natural resource management, environmental management and planning, sustainable forest management, environmental management, environmental economics, and/or relevant field of studies;

- Experience with community-based conservation and multiple-use protected areas;

- Experience in developing and/or reviewing environmental law, policy, guidelines, and strategies;

- Previous work experience in South East Asia and in Lao PDR or developing countries;

- Availabilty to travel within and outside Lao PDR;

- Prior similar responsibility in UNDP/GEF programme/projects;

- Experience in UNDP Project and Programme NIM with Country Office Support.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English is required.

Equal opportunity

Background

The Energy and Environment Unit of UNDP Kazakhstan supports national efforts to advance a green, low-carbon and climate-resilient economy and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Its portfolio covers climate change mitigation and adaptation, renewable energy, energy efficiency and power system modernization, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture and food systems, sustainable land and water management, waste management, disaster risk reduction and sustainable natural resource use.

Working with government institutions, the private sector, civil society, academia and international partners, the Unit provides policy advice, technical assistance and capacity development. It promotes green and sustainable finance, supports access to international environmental and climate funding, and helps develop investment opportunities and innovative financing instruments aligned with national development priorities. The Unit also strengthens institutional frameworks and supports the application of innovative and digital solutions, while integrating gender equality and inclusive development across its work.

Within this portfolio, the Government of Japan-funded project “The Project for Development of Sustainable Rare Metal and Rare Earth Minerals Value Chains through Environmental Measures” supports the sustainable development of Kazakhstan’s minerals sector. The project combines policy and analytical support, environmental monitoring and capacity development to promote environmentally responsible mineral value chains.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Policy Advice

- Provide specialized knowledge and expertise in critical minerals, sustainable mineral value chains and natural resource governance within the context of the project;

- Analyze existing policies, frameworks and regulations governing the minerals sector at various levels to identify opportunities, gaps, and barriers for sustainable sector development;

- Assess the regulatory landscape to ensure alignment of mineral sector policies with national development priorities and relevant international environmental and sustainability standards;

- Support the development of policies, strategies and action plans for environmentally responsible mineral sector development, considering input from stakeholders and best practices;

- Establish mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of relevant sectoral policies, providing recommendations for improvements;

- Analyze financial mechanisms and funding opportunities for sustainable mineral value chains and related environmental measures, identifying potential sources of support;

- Advocate for the integration of environmental sustainability, responsible resource management and value chain development into relevant sectoral policies, plans, and programs;

- Support the strengthening of institutional arrangements and procedures for sustainable mineral resource governance in Kazakhstan.

Collaborate with relevant government, industry representatives, research organizations and other stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of sustainable mineral sector policies and practices;

- Engage with policymakers, government officials, the private sector, NGOs, and community leaders to build consensus and support environmentally responsible mineral sector development;

- Coordinate between various stakeholders involved in mineral sector policy development and implementation to ensure coherence and efficiency;

- Translate complex technical and policy concepts into accessible language and communicate the importance of sustainable mineral value chains and environmental responsibility to different audiences;

- Design and conduct capacity-building activities related to critical minerals, sector governance and environmental sustainability, enabling stakeholders to understand and contribute to effective policy development and implementation;

- Prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and communication materials to communicate policy analysis, progress, and recommendations.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the project.

- Organize training, workshops, and capacity building activities in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- Promote advocacy on development trends and opportunities to collaborate in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Analyst reports to the Project Manager. The job holder will ensure to provide quality advice to Project manager and comply with appropriate UNDP policies and procedures.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Business Acumen Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

- Negotiation and Influence Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Development

- Human-centered Design Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process. Knowledge and understanding of human centered design principles and practices.

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Collective Intelligence Design Ability to bring together diverse groups of people, data, information, ideas, and technology to solve problems and design solutions or services. Knowledge and understanding of Collective Intelligence Design principles, methodology and practices.

- Development Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

jobs.title: Operations Associate
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities and build resilience in order to sustain development results. UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The key 2030 Agenda principle of leaving no one behind and stamping out inequality is at the core of everything we do. UNDP focuses on helping countries build and share solutions in three main areas:

- Sustainable development

- Democratic governance and peacebuilding

- Climate and disaster resilience

In all our activities, we encourage the protection of human rights and the empowerment of women, minorities and the poorest and most vulnerable.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Jordan supports national efforts to achieve sustainable development through integrated programmes aligned with the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). UNDP Jordan works across key pillars including Governance and Social Cohesion, Inclusive Growth, Climate Change and Energy, and Environment and Biodiversity, with a strong focus on advancing resilience, institutional effectiveness, and inclusive development.

The Governance and Social Cohesion Pillar at UNDP Jordan Country Office leads the design and implementation of integrated programmes that support inclusive governance, social cohesion, rule of law, and peacebuilding. The Pillar focuses on strengthening institutional effectiveness, promoting civic engagement, enhancing accountability and transparency, and supporting national efforts in preventing violent extremism (PVE), human rights, and inclusive political participation.

The Programme Analyst will contribute to a diverse and evolving portfolio of projects implemented in close partnership with government entities, civil society organizations, development partners, and UN agencies. The role supports evidence-based policymaking, programme innovation, and cross-sectoral collaboration, ensuring alignment with the Country Programme Document (CPD), UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), and national priorities.

The position plays a key role in advancing UNDP’s strategic positioning in governance and social cohesion by supporting programme delivery, strengthening partnerships, and contributing to knowledge generation and policy dialogue at national and sub-national levels.

The Programme Analyst will work under the guidance of the Programme Manager/DRR and will be integrated into a dynamic team focused on Governance and Social Cohesion initiatives.

The Analyst will contribute to the overarching goals of the Programme and align actions with the objectives of other Office Units such as Climate Change and Energy, Inclusive Growth, and Environment and Biodiversity.

- Contribute to the preparation of project documents, budgets, results frameworks, and implementation strategies.

- Ensure effective delivery of programme outputs in line with UNDP rules, procedures, and quality standards.

B. Provision of Technical and Analytical Support

- Conduct policy research, analysis, and evidence generation to inform programme development and strategic positioning.

- Support development of concept notes, policy briefs, and knowledge products.

C. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting

- Support implementation of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including tracking of results, risks, and performance indicators.

- Contribute to preparation of donor reports, internal progress reports, and evaluations.

- Ensure compliance with results-based management (RBM) principles and reporting requirements.

D. Build Partnership and Coordination

- Liaise with government counterparts, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders to support programme delivery.

- Facilitate coordination mechanisms, technical working groups, and inter-agency platforms.

- Support resource mobilization efforts through partnership development and proposal preparation.

E. Quality Assurance and Knowledge Management

- Ensure quality assurance of project documents, deliverables, and communication materials.

- Capture lessons learned and best practices to support knowledge sharing and programme improvement.

- Contribute to visibility and communication efforts for programme achievements.

F. Team Support and Supervision

- Provide guidance and technical oversight to project personnel UNVs, consultants, and interns where applicable.

Background /Project Description

The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria was created to significantly increase resources to fight three of the world’s most devastating diseases, and to direct those resources to areas of greatest need. The Global Fund attracts, manages and disburses resources in a public-private partnership that makes a sustainable and significant contribution to the reduction of mortality and morbidity caused by the three diseases and to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

UNDP is a key partner to the Global Fund to Fight HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM) and is the UN agency assuming the role of Principal Recipient of GFATM grants in South Sudan for TB and HIV/AIDS. In its role as Principal Recipient, UNDP ensures quality financial management, timely procurement of supplies, and efficient monitoring and delivery service. UNDP’s management role consists of implementing grants, ensuring financial accountability, and training of national and international counterparts on programme management, financial accountability and timely programmatic reporting to the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) and Global Fund (GF) Secretariat.

Position Purpose

The Monitoring and Evaluation Analyst will report to the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist and will work within the Programme & M&E unit to support the Finance & QA unit, the PSM & Procurement unit and the Warehouse/Supply Chain Management team. Under the guidance of the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist, the Analyst will liaise with the Local Fund Agent (LFA), the CCM, the SSAC, the MOH, the technical working groups responsible for HIV and TB, and U. S. Department of State Implementing Partners, Sub Recipients, various other partners and stakeholders. The incumbent will be required to travel to service delivery sites for the purpose of monitoring and supporting project activities including integration of HIV/TB services into primary health care, a key deliverable for the GC8 grant.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist (Global Fund), the Monitoring and Evaluation Analyst will be responsible for the following key tasks:

Support the GC8 monitoring and evaluation framework and plans:

- Support the development and updating of M&E frameworks and plans for the HIV, TB and RSSH portfolio in coordination with MOH, national programmes, SSAC and partners.

- Support regular analysis of grant performance against GC8 targets, identify implementation gaps and emerging risks, and recommend concrete corrective actions in coordination with programme teams and sub-recipients.

- Work with MOH, Service Delivery SR, SSAC, and NEPWU to develop quarterly joint field supportive supervision including service delivery and community interventions.

- Develop quarterly supportive supervision reports, including issues, remedial actions, timelines and responsible parties.

- Manage the tracking tool for issues identified from quarterly supportive supervision visits, providing monthly updates and presenting the issues during internal team meetings and as well as SR review meetings.

- Prepare data Power BI analytics for presentations during meetings with the Global Fund, LFA, CCM, MOH, partners and stakeholders.

- Support the develop M&E tools, indicator reference sheets and training materials for the PMU, SRs and implementing partners.

- Support SRs to strengthen their M&E systems for timely and accurate reporting.

- Supervise and monitor the work of assigned M&E consultants assigned to support the team.

- Conduct M&E capacity assessments of SRs and national partners and implement a capacity development plan.

- Review progress reports against targets and propose remedial actions for under-performing indicators.

- Monitor implementation bottlenecks and provide analytical inputs to programme decision-making.

- Support the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to develop quarterly Management Letters to Sub Recipients following review of quarterly combined programme and financial reports, summarising feedback on performance and recommendations.

- Develop an individual workplan

Deliver grant performance reporting to the Global Fund:

- Support the preparation of Programme Updates and Disbursement Requests (PUDRs), bi-annual and annual updates to the Global Fund.

- Consolidate quarterly programmatic information and ensure timely submission through corporate systems and the Global Fund transparency portal.

- Organize and document programme review meetings, including preparation of background data, presentations and follow-up action points.

Ensure Data quality assurance for the HIV, TB and RSSH portfolios:

- Review data from HMIS/DHIS2 and programme sources for completeness, accuracy and consistency.

- Plan and conduct routine data quality assessments (RDQA/DQA) and support sub-recipient site quality assurance (RSQA).

- Mentor and support the sub-recipient M&E Focal Points (TB/HIV, RSSH).

- Support the strengthening the use of routine programme data, including DHIS2 and community-level reporting, to identify service delivery gaps, monitor coverage among key and vulnerable populations, and inform programme adjustments.

Manage surveys, evaluations and learning

- Support the coordination of baseline, mid-term and end-line surveys and evaluations, including drafting Terms of Reference and providing technical direction.

- Support the dissemination of evaluation findings and the preparation of management responses.

- Support the documentation of lessons learned and promote their use in programme design and grant revisions.

Build M&E capacity and support nationalization:

- Deliver M&E and health information systems (HIS) training to SSAC, MOH, National Programmes staff and SRs, including NEPWU, SSNEP+ and NASOSS.

- Support the Country Dialogue Transition Plan (CDTP) and capacity transfer for progressive nationalization of the PR role.

- Support the development and monitoring of measurable milestones for transferring M&E responsibilities to national institutions, including strengthened national ownership of data quality assurance, analysis and Global Fund reporting.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the PMU, Country Office and the Organization.
