- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP supports sustainable human development in Cuba by focusing on economic, social, and environmental progress. Working alongside the country, UNDP helps implement the National Economic and Social Development Plan through 2030, as well as the objectives of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The organization encourages a dynamic economy, protects social achievements and equity, and promotes practices that ensure the sustainable use of natural resources. This includes advancing renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, and building resilience to climate change and natural disasters.

Guided by national priorities and strategies set with the Cuban government in the Country Programme Document (CPD) and aligned with the United Nations Cooperation Framework, UNDP’s work in Cuba centers on four main areas: Local Human Development, Disaster and Risk, Nature, Climate and Energy, and HIV/AIDS prevention and control. Gender equality is integrated into all these areas. UNDP also promotes decentralized, bilateral, multilateral, and South-South cooperation.

Within the Nature, Climate and Energy (NCE) area, UNDP develops initiatives that align with Cuba’s goals to enhance the conservation and resilience of both natural and built environments. These projects integrate environmental concerns into development plans and economic activities, support environmental finance, and address climate change adaptation and mitigation. Attention to gender and social equity is included throughout these efforts.

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

In Cuba, the SGP began activities in 2005 to support local initiatives in the focal areas of biodiversity, land degradation, and climate change, while generating sustainable livelihoods in communities. Since then, it has provided support to 177 community projects across the country. Project grants have benefited more than 100 Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs).

To ensure the desired environmental, economic, and social quality and impact, the national coordination of the SGP has developed a strong strategic alliance with scientific and academic institutions throughout the country. This has allowed projects to be innovative, characterized by the transfer of technology and knowledge that guarantees environmental sustainability, while also contributing to the fulfillment of national policies and the country’s international commitments.

During the period 2005–2024, projects have addressed three key environmental areas: land degradation, biodiversity conservation and Climate Change. The emphasis of the projects has been focused on:

- The gradual recovery of productive capacity on degraded lands through the implementation of sustainable land management principles, agroecological practices, and the establishment of agroforestry and silvopastoral systems.

- The efficient use of water resources and the conservation of water resources, including the reduction of pollution in watersheds.

- The conservation of terrestrial and marine landscapes, with an emphasis on areas of high value for biological diversity; including the conservation and sustainable use of threatened or high-value species.

- Support for the energy transition in communities and agricultural cooperatives.

- The diversification of livelihoods and subsistence means in rural communities.

Currently, the SGP has two sources of funding to support the implementation of projects in Cuba: the GEF (which is the traditional source that finances the program) and the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (which was recently incorporated).

Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the NCE Programme Officer, the SGP National Coordinator will report to the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist., the SGP National Coordinator will be responsible for the implementation of the overall work of SGP, the SGP Programme Associate/ Assistant, and the National Steering Committee at the country level.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNOPS rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations ( CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

Background

The RBM/M&E Associate position falls under the PMSU unit within the UNDP Egypt office. In this context, the Programme Management Support Unit in UNDP Egypt provides a critical function by serving as the essential bridge between the office's programme and operations teams, ensuring that development initiatives are both strategically aligned and operationally sound. By offering centralized guidance on Programme Finance, Results-Based Management (RBM) and quality assurance, the unit enhances the impact of the UNDP Egypt Country Programme (2023–2027) through systematic monitoring, evaluation, and strict adherence to corporate compliance standards.

Under the direct supervision of the Programme Management Analyst (NOA), the RBM/M&E Associate provides support to the leadership in the execution of oversight and management performance, and supports the formulation, planning and management of the country programme and integrated support team by managing data and facilitating implementation of various initiatives and activities aiming to effectively deliver development results. The RBM/M & E Associate promotes a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. In this context, the incumbent is responsible for the continuous identification and updating of project risks (strategic, operational, financial, and political) within UNDP’s enterprise resource planning system (Quantum).

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Supports timely implementation and effective management of RBM and M&E for the country office and projects focusing on achievement of the following:

Prepares project operational and administrative reports by collecting, selecting, reviewing and maintaining a wide range of information. Verifies that all projects are monitored in accordance with the monitoring plan. Informs deviations from the planned activities and identifies needs for reprogramming;

- Provides technical assistance for quality assurance of the implementation of the monitoring process, results framework and management arrangements of projects to guarantee a result-based management approach. This includes regular review of progress against set targets at project level. Assists in the provision of guidance/inputs at the design stage of projects;

- Supports the development of instruments to ensure a high quality of monitoring activities. Participates in results-oriented monitoring and evaluation training efforts in the Country Office;

- Assists in the development, updating, effective and efficient implementation of the CO programme and projects’ Monitoring and Evaluation plans;

- Assists in development of measurement and monitoring tools and identify data sources for programme and/or projects’ performance and indicators;

- Supports establishment and coordination of effective mechanisms of monitoring the programme and projects’ implementation including development of evaluation processes using innovative approaches;

- Supports preparation of the programme/project(s) Monitoring and Evaluation Plans capturing qualitative and quantitative aspects according to the annual work plans and log-frames;

- Supports the programme/project team with data management and identifying programmatic/project issues and prompt corrective actions to enhance the programme/project objectives;

- Supports the development and testing of M&E methods, revises and assists in the implementation of recommendations to improve the efficiency of current monitoring systems;

- Prepares necessary M&E forms and format to capture necessary data and information from the field;

- Supports and/or works to capture, document, and analyze that information and data from the projects’ activities in a results-based and timely manner;

- Provides and/or supports coordination of inputs in developing the Annual Work Plans (AWPs), projects’ implementation plans, etc.;

2. Assists the effective management and implementation of the evaluations policies, strategies and processes focusing on achievement of the following:

- Prepares reports and submits documents to the Government, UN Agencies and UNDP Headquarters by collecting and selecting relevant data from documents, legislation extracts, specialized publications and websites;

- Drafts preliminary presentation of information;

- Provides inputs in the formulation of Terms of Reference for outcome evaluations. Assists in the revision of TORs for specific project/thematic/sectorial evaluation missions and/or desk evaluations/reviews;

- Participates in consultant and evaluation team selection and technical feedback on evaluations;

- Assist in the process of carrying out evaluations (review of reports, participation in meetings, participation in the management and/or organization of seminars, meetings and other special events).

3. Provides administrative supports in preparation of reports completion of corporate online tools focusing on achievement of the following:

- Enters and/or reviews projects’ data to the data management system (Quantum, Quantum+, IMRP and other systems), updates project-related data on websites, as needed;

- Schedules and assigns responsibilities for activities/events needed for monitoring;

- Assists in the identification of potential implementation problems and bottlenecks and contributes to the common M&E activity of the UNDP Country Office;

- Supports programme/projects’ teams in conducting surveys, studies, assessments and similar activities;

- Liaises with the Field Moniroting Assistants within broader UNDP M&E activities and efforts;

- Maintains sound filing system including in the online SharePoint/MS Teams systems and appropriates use and recording of programme/project’s experience, activities and results;

- Provides inputs, information and statistics for quarterly, annual and other reports;

- Assists in the preparation of background documentation and working papers for its utilization in meetings with the Government and project authorities;

4. Facilitates knowledge building and knowledge sharing focusing on achievement of the following:

- Identifies and formulates lessons learned and documents best practices from evaluations and studies to be integrated into programme reports;

- Contributes to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Under the supervision of the Head of Unit, establishes connections, coordinates and disseminates information, in both ways, within the team, with other relevant units and the whole office;

- Contributes to regular capacity building of the programme/project(s) and CO staff on RBM, M&E and other relevant topics;

- Supports programme/project teams in the promotion of monitoring and evaluation standards, quality assurance/control and capacity development;

- Supports knowledge sharing and learning programme-wide in the MSU Team and the entire CO;

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Background

The UNDP Sierra Leone’s Country Programme Document (CPD), 2025-2030, represents UNDP contributions to the National Development Plan and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. Developed through extensive consultations and guided by independent evaluations, the CPD seeks to reduce multidimensional poverty and enhance justice, peace, social cohesion, and resilience. One of the two pillars focuses on Inclusive governance, peace, and prosperity, embodying harmonious development, effective resource management, and equitable governance aligned with UNDP signature solutions. UNDP has recently developed its Inclusive Governance Peace and Prosperity Portfolio for 2025 -2030 around four main pillars: Pillar I – Fostering Peaceful, Credible and Inclusive Elections; Pillar 2 – Rule of Law and Human Right; Pillar 3 – Strengthening Democratic Institutions; and Pillar 4 – Strengthening Security, Peace and Social Cohesion.

These pillars seek to support an inclusive constitutional review process; promote social accountability and transparency; enhance capacities of oversight institutions, EMBs and CSOs to deliver inclusive, transparent, and peaceful elections; and equip media entities to manage mis- and disinformation. It supports legal, policy and regulatory reforms; gender equality, women’s empowerment and SGBV reduction initiatives; and empower women and youth to assert their political and economic rights and participation. The country office also seeks to improve national capacities to anticipate and respond to threats to peace, security, and stability at community, national and cross-border levels; support justice and security sector reform; and enhance access to justice and the protection of human rights.

Position Purpose

The Portfolio has outlined the goals under peacebuilding and social cohesion for which UNDP seeks to strengthen the infrastructure for peace, social cohesion, conflict prevention, mediation, and reconciliation, addressing inequalities, promoting economic transformation, and emphasizing women, youth, peace, and security. Under the Portfolio, UNDP provides support to improve capacities to anticipate and respond to threats to peace and stability at the national, community, and cross-border levels and promotes gender equality and women’s empowerment for effective peacebuilding.

In achieving these goals, UNDP is channeling resources from the United Nations Peacebuilding Fund, the United Nations Trust Fund for Human Security, the Government of Japan, and other critical partners, with aim to promote and social cohesion in collaboration with a wide range of partners.

Based in the Sierra Leone country office, and under the direct supervision of the Inclusive Governance Peace and Prosperity Portfolio Team Leader, the Programme Analyst will provide support for the Country Office’s work on peace and security under the UNDP CPD 2025-2030. The incumbent will work across portfolio programmes, support programme integration, and ensure the development and implementation of quality projects working closely with the RCO, UN agencies, national actors, and other relevant partners.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Ensure effective planning and implementation of projects and initiatives in the field of peace and security

- Provide strategic advice and propose courses of action to the Team Lead and Senior management on peace and social cohesion issues

- Support the planning, execution and monitoring of the country office’s peace and security projects and initiatives

- Ensure activities are aligned with national priorities and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework

- Collaborate with government counterparts, civil society organizations, private sector actors and local and community actors among others

- Support joint projects and programmes with other UN agencies in the field of peace and social cohesion, including the United Nations Peacebuilding Fund-funded project

- Provide technical support and capacity-building to partners to enhance their contribution to peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and social cohesion initiatives

- Monitor emerging trends, risks, and opportunities in the peace and social cohesion landscape

Conduct peace and conflict analysis to inform programme design, project implementation and other work of the country office

- Mainstream gender equality and human rights-based approaches throughout peace and security programming

- Support additional portfolio priorities and initiatives as assigned, ensuring flexibility and responsiveness to emerging needs

2.) Building strategic partnerships and resource mobilization

- Support the country office’s resource mobilization efforts by contributing to proposal development, identifying funding and collaboration opportunities, exploring synergies with ongoing initiatives, and engaging with relevant stakeholders

- Support the drafting of concept notes, project proposals and project documents in the area of peace and security in collaboration with the country office colleagues and other partners

- Support the country office’s engagement with development partners, national counterparts and civil society organizations among other partners

- Proactively identify and cultivate new strategic partnerships with bilateral and multilateral partners, foundations, and private sector actors among others

- Prepare briefing notes, statements and talking points and other written inputs as required by senior management

- Facilitating linkages between United Nations Peacebuilding Fund-funded initiatives and other UNDP programmes to maximize synergies

3. ) Facilitate knowledge management and communications

- Prepare, compile and support reporting on the country office’s peace and social cohesion projects and initiatives and other projects and initiatives under the portfolio

- In collaboration with the country office’s communications team, support efforts to raise visibility of the country office’s support and the contributions from donors

- Document and package good practices, lessons learned, and human-interest stories that demonstrate programme impact at community, local and national levels

- Contribute to the development of other knowledge products of the country office

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Background and Organizational Context

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC) is part of UNV's Management Services, supporting ever growing number (over 15,000 in 2025) and providing timely and high-quality delivery of services on volunteer HR pre-assignment activities, contract administration, payroll, and evacuation UN Volunteers assigned to agencies, funds, and programs, and UN missions throughout the UN system.

With a presence in nine locations globally, VSC ensures timely and high-quality delivery of services in volunteer HR pre-assignment activities, contract administration, payroll, and evacuation support.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS) and other relevant sections at Headquarters, Regional Offices, Field Units, and the UNDP Global Shared Service Centre (GSSC) to deliver seamless, consolidated services in accordance with UN Volunteers Conditions of Service, regulations, policies, and best practices. In delivering its functions, VSC also liaises with UNDP Country Offices, other UN Agencies, Service Centers and operations counterparts.

Position Purpose

Reporting to the Deputy Chief, VSC, the Operations Analyst manages day-to-day activities of the integrated volunteer management pillar, with a focus on timely and quality delivery of volunteer deployment and lifecycle management services. S/he oversees the work of regional teams outposted to multiple locations, monitors service risks and supports consistent application of agreed workflows, validation points and escalation arrangements. The incumbent works in close collaboration with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders contributing to the provision of operational services to candidates, UN Volunteers and their host entities. The Operations Analyst promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and supports the maintenance of high-quality service delivery and client satisfaction.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

Oversight of volunteer deployment

- Coordinate and monitor the timely provision of volunteer deployment services as per business objectives and key performance indicators (KPIs);

- Monitor deployment speed across regional portfolios; identify bottlenecks and propose improvement measures for consistent application;

- Support consistent implementation of agreed workflows and validation points related to UN Volunteer deployment globally.

Oversight of volunteer lifecycle management

- Coordinate and monitor the quality and timeliness of volunteer lifecycle administration, including hiring, contract management and separation as per corporate policies, procedures and key performance indicators (KPIs);

- Ensure timely follow-up on open items and complex cases; Identify operational hurdles, queue and backlog patterns and recurring issues, and propose improvements to workflows and controls;

- Support consistent implementation of agreed workflows and validation points related to volunteer lifecycle management globally.

Coordination of payroll impacting lifecycle actions

- Coordinate with VSC Payroll Team to support timely and accurate handover of lifecycle actions with payroll impact, including effective dates, extensions, separations, funding updates and retroactive changes;

- Support first-line validation of lifecycle data before payroll-impacting actions are triggered, in line with agreed workflows and escalation arrangements;

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP provides support to the Solomon Islands Country Coordinating Mechanism (SICCM) to enable it to effectively fulfil its governance, oversight and coordination responsibilities for Global Fund investments.

The SICCM brings together government, civil society, communities affected by HIV, tuberculosis and malaria, technical partners and other stakeholders to guide and oversee the country’s coordinated engagement in the response to the HIV, TB and Malaria, supported by the Global Fund. The CCM Secretariat plays a central role in ensuring that the SICCM operates effectively, transparently and inclusively and that its decisions are implemented and followed up in a timely manner.

The Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM[1]) is a national committee of voluntary members that submits funding applications to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, oversees the grants on behalf of their country and ensures alignment with the national response. The Secretariat of a CCM facilitates the mandate and supports the CCM in both the execution of its decisions and coordination of its activities. The roles and responsibilities of the CCM Secretariat shall be to assist the CCM to execute its core functions in the areas of Oversight, Engagement, Positioning and Operations.[2]. The Country Coordination Mechanism (CCM) agreement was launched in August 2016 with Global Fund to provide Secretarial Support to Solomon Islands Country Coordination Mechanism.

The Executive Officer will work under the contractual and administrative supervision of the UNDP Country Manager or designated UNDP supervisor. The incumbent will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the SICCM Chair, in consultation with the Vice-Chair and Executive Committee, and will support the SICCM General Assembly in implementing its approved decisions. The annual performance assessment will be completed by the designated UNDP supervisor, informed by documented feedback from the SICCM Chair.

Under direct supervision of designated UNDP supervisor in Solomon Country Office, and programmatic reporting to UNDP Effective Governance Team Lead and in consultation with the SICCM Executive headed by the CCM Chair and other responsible parties, the Executive Officer will be responsible for supporting the CCM in the overall implementation of its mandate. The Executive Officer leads as CCM Secretariat and is accountable to the CCM. Through the coordination of various donor and partner resources the CCM Secretariat supports the CCM to effectively implement a national disease strategy that pursues the goal of ending the diseases as pandemics by 2030. The CCM Secretariat facilitates the work of the CCM by enabling an effective governance mechanism using highly proficient political and technical skills. They maintain a repository of CCM documents, mediate in areas of dispute amongst members and act as an advisor for the CCM in-country. They also serve as a bridge between national stakeholders and the Global Fund Secretariat.

The Executive Officer is expected to provide strong and proactive support to the CCM members, exercise sound judgment, anticipate and address operational and governance challenges, and ensure timely follow-up on CCM decisions and commitments. The role requires a high degree of initiative, diplomacy and political awareness, as well as the ability to build trust and work effectively with senior government officials, civil society and community representatives, Principal Recipients, development partners and the Global Fund.

[1] For purposes of this paper, CCMs includes Regional Coordinating Mechanisms (RCMs) as further defined in the CCM Policy.

[2] Definitions of the four core areas can be found here https://www.theglobalfund.org/en/country-coordinating-mechanism/evolution/

Duties and Responsibilities

The Executive Officer receives strategic and day-to-day functional guidance from the SICCM Leadership Chair/Vice Chair and supports the implementation of decisions of the CCM General Assembly. Administrative supervision, performance assessment, leave approval, and contractual oversight are the responsibility of the designated UNDP supervisor. In addition the SICCM Secretariat/Executive Officer serves the SICCM as well as its appointed committees. The Secretariat is under the direct supervision of the Chair of the SICCM

Scope of Work – Key areas of Responsibilities

- Operations – Serve as the CCM Secretariat and support the operational structures of the CCM.

- Oversight - Enhance efficiency of oversight procedures as per Global Fund processes

- Positioning - Facilitate political discussions and strengthen sustainability efforts

- Engagement – Foster meaningful, inclusive and active participation of key stakeholders

Operations: Contribute to the effective functioning of the SICCM

- Plan, coordinate and document SICCM General Assembly, Executive Committee and other standing or ad hoc committee meetings, including preparation of agendas and papers, logistical arrangements, minutes, decision records and follow-up actions.

- Respond to the operational needs of the CCM particularly supporting CCM leadership, including ensuring all members are knowledgeable about Global Fund strategic and technical directives and guidelines, and enabling member engagement as required (coordinating logistics, facilitating participation and circulating minutes).

- Serve as the Secretariat in supporting CCM members and fulfilling its obligations to the Global Fund such as financial reporting on CCM funding and adherence to CCM eligibility requirements.

- Proactively identify operational, governance and coordination issues that may affect the effective functioning of the CCM; propose practical solutions to CCM leadership; and ensure that agreed actions and decisions are followed through in a timely manner. S

- Support CCM committees: those that are permanent (e.g., executive, oversight, governance) and temporary (e.g., elections).

- Provide orientation and training to new CCM members or refresher trainings to CCM members.

- Support the process related to the custodian and mediator of ethical and governance matters to protect the integrity of the CCM as a whole, such as applying the Ethical Code of Conduct to all CCM Secretariat staff and CCM members and resolving issues as they arise in coordination with the Global Fund Country Team, assist the CCM leadership in the development, costing and implementation of annual CCM priorities, including identifying related capacity gaps.

- Develop procedures (including ToRs informed by all relevant stakeholders) and templates for Global Fund-related processes, such as assessments of the performance of the CCM, and financial management of the CCM Secretariat budget.

- On a continuous basis, document information regarding CCM operations and ensure robust management of key documents.

- Provide support to the Global Fund Country Team and other stakeholders from the Global Fund, for example, Board members and parliamentarians from donor countries, working towards the common goal of ending the three diseases as pandemics by 2030.

Oversight: Support effective grant oversight and access to funding

- Under the CCM leadership, support all relevant aspects of the Global Fund access to funding processes - national strategic plan, gap analysis, request for funding design stages through the final signature of Global Fund grants by Principal Recipients (PRs) - and ensure that all processes are documented, led and informed by appropriate data-based decision-making.

- Support the oversight committee in its mandate of gathering and analyzing grant and national data and developing recommendations to CCM leadership to resolve bottlenecks or suggest solutions such as technical cooperation needs. In transitioning contexts, support the oversight committee in overseeing transition workplans and implementation of transition readiness assessment recommendations.

- Accompany the CCM through the process to access Global Fund support, including coordinating the country dialogue and PR selection process. The funding request will be aligned to the country context and global goals to end the pandemics.

- After the grant-making process, in partnership with the Global Fund Country Team and with the relevant resources from the CCM Secretariat team, oversee a “knowing your grant” orientation of the CCM.

- Advocate on behalf of national stakeholders and CCM members on areas of Global Fund-related requirements linked to accessing the country’s full Global Fund grant allocation. This includes the country adhering to co-financing commitments and/or PRs improving grant performance.

Positioning: Ensure coordination, sustainability and transition

- Develop proposals for the CCM leadership and the Global Fund on the appropriate positioning of the CCM and document the necessary linkages between the CCM and all other significant coordinating platforms in the country. The main purpose being to support harmonization and strengthened efficiency (both in terms of governance bodies and in the fight against the three diseases). In countries where a disease component/s is preparing for or transitioning from Global Fund financing, focus on documenting links to other platforms that are relevant to transition preparedness, planning and implementation.

- Attend and support other national health platforms to help convey the views of the CCM and also to identify synergies in the coordination of health and donor investment.

- Facilitate the CCM’s role in sustainability and transition planning and implementation, including ensuring strong inclusion of civil society and participating in efforts to strengthen sustainability of Global Fund investments.

Engagement: Facilitate inclusive and informed stakeholder participation and knowledge management

- Work with the Global Fund Country Team, PRs and CCM to discuss Global Fund communications, and guide the CCM on their implications for actions and relevant adjustments.

- Engage with senior government officials to promote the role of the CCM in the national health landscape. • Ensure that credible and verified community input on the CCM is brought to high-level government discussions in order to drive a more informed response to the three diseases.

- CCM decisions and agreed actions are systematically tracked and followed up, with delays, bottlenecks and issues requiring leadership attention identified and escalated in a timely manner.

- Carry out additional tasks under all the above-mentioned functional areas as requested by the CCM, according to its context and threshold level.

- Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: Level 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: Level 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: Level 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: Level 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: Level 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: Level 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: Level 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System thinking. Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Effective Decision Making. Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

- Negotiation and Influence. Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Management

- Partnerships Management. Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Operations Management. Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organization’s assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

External Relations & Advocacy (General (across the functions))

- Public Relations. Ability to build and maintain an overall positive public image for the organization, its mandate and its brand, while ensuring that individual campaigns and other communications and advocacy initiatives are supported in reaching the public.

2030 Agenda People

- Health. Sustainable financing for HIV and health

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Public Health, Finance, Public Administration, Business Administration, or related field is required. OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of professional experience (international or national) working in planning, and management in the public health and/or development sector.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with government, civil society, communities, UN entities, donors and technical partners;

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired skills:

- Experience in public health or disease programmes, particularly HIV, tuberculosis and/or malaria, is desirable;

- Experience coordinating multi – stakeholder processes, meetings and follow up actions with government institutions, donor agencies, multilateral organizations or civil society is desirable;

- Proven experience in Global Fund or comparable donor and technical-partner processes, governance requirements and funding models is an asset;

- Experience supporting a board, committee, secretariat or other multi-stakeholder governance mechanism is an asset;

- Experience in budget monitoring, financial reporting or administrative coordination is an asset;

- Demonstrated experience in programme or project planning, implementation support, monitoring, reporting and records management is desired;

- Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement, manage competing priorities and deliver quality outputs within deadlines is desired.

Required Languages:

- Working knowledge of another Solomon Islands language is an asset.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

- Human Development

- Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

- Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrates its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities

INSIGHT

To translate Indonesia’s ambitious climate and digital transition priorities into concrete action, UNDP Indonesia partners with national institutions to build robust, scalable financing enablers. A cornerstone of this effort is the Institutional Strengthening for Indonesian Environment Fund Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT) Project, which bridges high-level policy advice with practical, localized execution.

The Institutional Strengthening for Indonesian Environment Fund Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT) Project is implemented by UNDP in partnership with IEF/BPDLH, with financial support from the Government of Norway. The project runs through 31 August 2028 and seeks to strengthen IEF/BPDLH as a trusted, accountable and internationally credible climate and environmental financing institution capable of mobilizing, managing and governing increasingly diverse sources of finance.

The Indonesian Environment Fund, or Badan Pengelola Dana Lingkungan Hidup (IEF/BPDLH), is Indonesia’s national environmental financing institution and a Public Service Agency under the Ministry of Finance. I IEF/BPDLH mobilizes, manages, invests and channels domestic and international finance for climate action, environmental protection and sustainable development. Its role supports Indonesia’s RPJMN 2025–2029 priorities, Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution and FOLU Net Sink 2030 agenda. As the scale and complexity of its portfolio grows, IEF/BPDLH is expected to maintain governance, fiduciary, environmental and social safeguards, transparency, data, monitoring, reporting and accountability systems that are consistent with evolving national and international standards. It manages grants, revolving funds, Results-Based Contributions, and other financing arrangements serving national programmes and community-level initiatives. Its institutional credibility therefore depends on the consistent application of appraisal, financial management, safeguards, data governance, portfolio management, and public accountability arrangements across a diverse portfolio.

INSIGHT addresses institutional transformation at three interconnected levels: the enabling environment, including policies, regulations, mandates and inter-institutional relationships; organizational capacity, including governance, systems, processes, structures, resources and accountability mechanisms; and individual capacity, including leadership, technical competencies, skills, knowledge and organizational behavior. The project emphasizes practical application, institutional ownership, and sustainability rather than stand-alone policies, systems, or training products.

The INSIGHT project is implemented by UNDP. and housed under the Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) Unit. Day to day management is carried out by a Project Management Unit (PMU) led by a National Project Manager, who reports to the Head of the HDRG Unit or delegated authority and is supported by technical and operational staff to ensure effective delivery, compliance, and coordination across project activities.

Scope of Work

The INSIGHT project is implemented by UNDP and housed under the Human Development and Responsive Governance HDRG) Unit, Day to day management is carried out by a Project Management Unit (PMU) led by a National Project Manager, who reports to the Head of the HDRG Unit or delegated authority and is supported by technical and operational staff to ensure effective delivery, compliance, and coordination across project activities.

The Chief Technical Advisor reports to the Deputy Resident Representative and matrix manager to the Head of Unit of the and works closely with IEF/BPDLH counterparts, relevant government institutions, UNDP technical and operations units, project personnel, consultants and institutional service providers. The position may coordinate technical contributors assigned to the relevant workstreams but does not hold overall project accountability; approve financing, accreditation, procurement or institutional decisions; certify expenditure; or acceptcontractual deliverables outside delegated authority.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative and matrix manager to Team Leader/Human Development and Responsive Governance (HDRG) and close coordination with National Project Manager, the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) will perform the following five key functions:

Provide senior technical and strategic advice on climate and environmental finance

- Advise UNDP and IEF/BPDLH on climate and environmental finance priorities, institutional financing architecture and strategic linkages with national and international initiatives.

- Coordinate technical work on programme and project appraisal, including fiduciary, environmental and social safeguards, gender, results, sustainability and conflict-of-interest requirements.

- Coordinate accreditation-readiness planning, gap tracking, cross-directorate evidence generation and quality review without performing independent accreditation assessments or replacing specialist reviewers.

- Support readiness reviews and decision-gate documentation for priority financing mechanisms or windows, including applicable legal, fiduciary, safeguards, gender, monitoring, grievance, operational and financing conditions.

- Advise on qualified investment-pipeline development, eligibility and appraisal standards, risk considerations, institutionalization and potential funding sources.

- Contribute technical specifications and terms of reference and support technical review of deliverables within assigned authority and UNDP procedures.

Lead strategic stakeholder engagement and ecosystem coordination

- Maintain a strategic stakeholder, and partnership plan linked to financing, institutional strengthening, accountability and resource mobilization.

- Coordinate inter-institutional processes involving IEF/BPDLH, and other key actors such as the Coordinating Ministry of Food Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, and Ministry of National Development Planning/Bappenas, Plan and facilitate senior-level consultations, policy and technical dialogues, inclusive finance forums to identify readiness constraints, financing barriers and options for institutional or ecosystem-level resolution.

- Document material stakeholder inputs, responsible follow-up and responses, and how relevant inputs informed recommendations, tools or decisions.

- Build working relationships with development partners, climate and environmental funds, financial institutions, private-sector actors, civil society, academia and other relevant stakeholders.

Support resource mobilization, financing partner engagement, impact reporting and institutional positioning

- Lead opportunities with potential financing partners, including those from public and private sectors, both national and international.

- Provide substantive inputs to financing strategies, partner-engagement plans, partnership proposals, donor briefs, concept notes, presentations and management communications;

- Position IEF/BPDLH as a credible partner for transparent, accountable and inclusive climate and environmental finance, and promote complementarities with related initiatives.

Lead and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area(s) and UNDP

- Support capacity development through advisory services, structured learning, technical referral, peer exchange and practical tools for climate and environmental finance and stakeholder engagement.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training and other relevant capacity building activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia. Lead workshops with senior level officials and stakeholders.

- Proactively identify and pursue opportunities for the documentation and communication of best practices, programme results, and lessons learned under the project.

- Actively participate in and make substantive contributions to external networks and communities of practice to promote advocacy for UNDP’s work and opportunities for collaboration in addressing development trends. Represent UNDP in relevant technical meetings and working groups under the direction of CO management.

- Support establishment of knowledge platforms and innovative mechanisms for capturing and disseminating knowledge from the project; and ensure development of knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

The incumbent of the position should avoid any kind of discriminatory behavior including gender discrimination and ensure that:

- Human rights and gender equality are prioritized as an ethical principle within all actions.

- Activities are designed and implemented in accordance with “Social and Environmental Standards of UNDP”.

- Any kind of diversities based on ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, disability, religion, class, gender are respected within all implementations including data production.

- Differentiated needs of women and men are considered.

- Inclusive approach is reflected within all actions and implementations, in that sense an enabling and accessible setup in various senses such as disability gender language barrier is created.

- Necessary arrangements to provide gender parity within all committees, meetings, trainings etc. are introduced.

- Ensure gender-related economic, environmental, public research and analysis, to contribute to the formulation of policies, programme interventions, procedures, guidelines, and tools.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Required Skills and Experience

Competencies:

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results-LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively-LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously-LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility-LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination-LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner-LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion-LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Digital:

- Alternative finance: Ability to identify potential alternative forms of finance and mobilise them for the purpose of addressing development challenges. Ability to review the skills, capacities, procedures and protocols that are needed to enable new financial mechanisms. Ability to assess the risks, limitations and implications of using new financial mechanisms. Set up the processes and structures to design, testing and implement new financial mechanisms. Managing outreach and stakeholder engagement Set up the processes and structures to design, testing and implement new financial

Business Management:

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, governments, civil society and private-sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

2030 Agenda:

- Partnerships SDG Finance Blended Finance for the SDGs

2030 Agenda:

Education:

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of an advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible relevant experience at the national or international level in providing technical advice on substantive responsibility in climate finance, or environmental finance or development finance or public financial reform or institutional strengthening or strategic stakeholder engagement or partnership development or related fields is required.

Required Skills:

- Proven experience of engaging and negotiating with high level personnel in governmental institutions, external agencies etc.

- Demonstrated experience in providing strategic and/or technical advice, including the ability to conceptualize strategic intervention or translate analysis into practical recommendations and decision-support products.

- Demonstrated experience in engaging, facilitating and/or coordinating with senior-level stakeholders, including government institutions and/or other institutional partners.

- Experience working with government institutions, public funds, development partners, international financial institutions (IFIs), climate or environmental funds, private-sector actors, and/or civil society organizations (CSOs) is desirable.

- Experience with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the United Nations (UN) system, or another international development organization is an asset.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Description du bureau/unité/projet

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est une organisation internationale avec plus de 17 000 employés travaillant dans environ 170 bureaux dans le monde pour aider les gouvernements à développer des politiques, des institutions et des partenariats solides pour atteindre le Programme de développement durable et ses 17 objectifs de développement durable à l’horizon 2030. Dans le cadre de son mandat, le PNUD contribue aux efforts des pays dans le renforcement de leurs capacités de résilience face aux effets du changement climatique et à la gestion durable des ressources naturelles.

Afin de concrétiser et de renforcer son engagement en faveur de la conservation et de la gestion durable des forêts algériennes, le PNUD met en œuvre une initiative en partenariat avec la Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF) et le soutien du Fonds pour l’Environnement Mondial (GEF), visant à promouvoir la restauration et la gestion forestière durable de l’écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie. L’écosystème de Pin d’Alep, qui s’étend sur plus d’un million d’hectares dans les Hauts Plateaux, est soumis à des pressions croissantes liées à la dégradation des terres, aux effets du changement climatique (sécheresse, incendies, attaques parasitaires) et aux activités anthropiques non durables. Face à cette situation, le PNUD Algérie soutient la Direction Générale des Forêts afin de mettre en œuvre une série d’actions visant à restaurer les paysages forestiers dégradés, renforcer les capacités de gestion durable des forêts et contribuer au développement des économies locales dans les wilayas ciblées.

À la lumière de ce qui précède, le bureau du PNUD à Alger prévoit de recruter un/e Coordinateur/trice de projet pour soutenir l’exécution et la mise en œuvre de l’initiative « Restauration et Gestion Forestière Durable de l’Écosystème de Pin d’Alep en Algérie ». Le/la coordinateur/trice devra travailler en collaboration avec l’équipe programme Nature, Climat et Énergie et avec la Direction Générale du Projet, et devra prévoir des déplacements fréquents dans les wilayas d’intervention.

Portée des travaux

En étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et la supervision directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF.

Le/la Coordinateur/trice du projet travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le Directeur National du Projet, l’associé(e) administratif (ve) et financier (e) et Team Leader du portefeuille Nature, Climat et Énergie du Bureau Pays du PNUD ainsi qu'avec les diverses parties prenantes parmi lesquelles, principalement, la Direction Générale des Forêts et le Ministère de l’Agriculture et du Développement Rural et de la Pêche.

Résumé des fonctions:

- Gestion de projet : Assurer la gestion administrative et financière du projet selon les règles et procédures du PNUD, et veiller à la réalisation des activités et l’atteinte des résultats du projet dans les délais fixés via un plan de travail détaillé ;

- Appui et conseil technique : Veiller à la qualité des produits techniques et à la coordination des travaux techniques, au besoin ;

- Appuyer le développement de réseaux/partenariats : Appuyer la communication des résultats, le développement du réseau de parties prenantes à impliquer dans le projet, et assurer la circulation de l’information et bâtir des relations en vue de maximiser l’engagement des acteurs dans le processus de mise en œuvre du projet

Axe 1 – Gestion administrative, financière et opérationnelle du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice assure la gestion quotidienne du projet conformément aux règles, procédures et politiques du PNUD (POPP), notamment :

- Coordonner et superviser le travail des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) déployées dans les 3 wilayas ciblées par le projet

- Coordonner le travail de l’équipe chargée de préparer et réviser les plans de travail et les programmes financiers, veiller à la soumission dans les délais des rapports financiers et des rapports d’avancement trimestriels, du rapport annuel du projet et autres rapports ;

- Élaborer et mettre à jour les plans de travail annuels (PTA) et pluriannuels du projet, en coordination avec la DGF et l'équipe NCE du PNUD, et en assurer le suivi continu

- Gérer le cycle de vie du projet : planification, mise en œuvre, suivi, ajustements et clôture

- Assurer la liaison permanente entre les consultants, l'UGP, la partie nationale (DGF/MADR) et le bureau de pays du PNUD

- Planifier et coordonner les activités de terrain sur les trois sites du projet (Telagh, Beni Imloul, Senalba) et y effectuer des missions régulières de supervision

- Identifier, suivre et atténuer les risques liés à la mise en œuvre du projet

- Organiser les réunions périodiques du Comité de Pilotage (Board de Projet) et en assurer le secrétariat et le suivi des décisions

- Préparer les rapports d'avancement : rapports mensuels d'activités, rapports trimestriels, Rapports annuels de mise en œuvre (PIR) destinés au GEF, et rapport de fin de projet

- Assurer le suivi des décaissements et des dépenses par rapport aux budgets approuvés, en coordination avec l'assistant(e) administratif(ve) et financier(ère)

- Préparer et soumettre les rapports financiers trimestriels au PNUD

- Mettre à jour régulièrement les Indicateurs de Base du GEF (Core Indicators 3, 4, 6 et 11) pour les rapports d'étape et les évaluations (MTR et TE)

Axe 2 – Supervision technique et assurance qualité des livrables du projet

Le/la Coordinateur/trice veille à la qualité scientifique et technique des produits du projet :

- Rédiger et valider les Termes de Référence pour le recrutement de consultants, d'experts et de prestataires (experts en SFM/FLR, spécialistes en PSE, experts genre, M&E, etc.) recrutés par le PNUD

- Superviser, orienter et évaluer les travaux des consultants recrutés par le PNUD, et valider leurs livrables en coordination avec la DGF, le DNP, le PNUD et les parties prenantes concernées.

- Veiller à l'intégration transversale des questions de genre et d'inclusion sociale dans tous les livrables et activités du projet (marqueur genre GEN 2)

- Suivre la mise en œuvre des outils de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (ESMF, SESP) et veiller au respect des normes environnementales et sociales du PNUD

- Contribuer aux apports techniques permettant d'aligner les produits du projet avec la Loi 23-21 sur les forêts et des stratégies nationales de développement forestier

- Apporter un appui à la sélection des experts et consultants/prestataires du projet, et prendre part au processus de sélection en cas de besoin ;

Axe 3 – Communication, partenariats et gestion des connaissances

Le/la Coordinateur/trice est responsable de la visibilité du projet et de la mobilisation des parties prenantes :

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec l'ensemble des parties prenantes du projet

- Appuyer l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de communication du projet, en lien avec le/la chargé(e) de communication de la DGF et du PNUD

- Fournir les éléments nécessaires à la production d'articles, notes d'information, messages-clés et supports de communication relatifs aux résultats et enseignements du projet

- Assurer une veille active sur les initiatives complémentaires (FAO, IFAD, GEF SGP, programmes gouvernementaux) pertinentes pour les thématiques du projet

- Promouvoir le partage des bonnes pratiques, des enseignements tirés et des innovations du projet au sein des réseaux nationaux et internationaux pertinents

- Représenter le projet dans les forums, ateliers et réunions techniques nationaux et internationaux, au besoin

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Résultats attendus :

Sur la base de la description détaillée des tâches qui précède, les résultats attendus du/de la coordinateur/tric du projet, seront principalement :

- Mise en œuvre efficace et dans les délais du Plan de Travail Annuel du projet

- Qualité et conformité de tous les livrables techniques du projet aux standards du PNUD et du GEF

- Rapports financiers et programmatiques soumis dans les délais impartis

- Comité de Pilotage du Projet fonctionnel et réuni au moins deux fois par an

- Intégration effective du genre et des sauvegardes dans tous les aspects du projet

- Mobilisation active et constructive des parties prenantes à tous les niveaux

- Promouvoir le plaidoyer sur les tendances du développement et les opportunités de collaboration, en coordination avec les partenaires du projet, les parties prenantes et le personnel de communication du PNUD.

Dispositif institutionnel

Le/la coordonnateur/trice travaillera en étroite collaboration directe du Directeur National du projet et sera sous la supervision Directe du Directeur National du projet et du chef d'équipe du portefeuille Nature, climat et énergie du PNUD, l'objectif principal de la mission est de coordonner et de gérer les activités prévues dans le cadre de l’initiative d’appui à la DGF. Le/la coordonnateur/trice assurera la supervision de l’équipe des coordinateurs(trices) locaux(les) composée de trois (3) personnes déployées dans les trois wilayas visées par le projet.

Compétences :

Essentielles

Atteindre des Résultats

Niveau 2 : Faire monter en échelle les solutions et simplifier les processus, tout en équilibrant rapidité et précision dans l’exécution du travail.

Pensée Innovante

Niveau 2 : Proposer de nouvelles idées / être ouvert à de nouvelles approches, démontrer une pensée systémique et intégrée.

Apprendre en Continue

Niveau 2 : Sortir de sa zone de confort, apprendre des autres et soutenir leur apprentissage.

Adapter avec Agilité

Niveau 2 : Adapter les processus et approches à de nouvelles situations, impliquer les autres dans le processus de changement.

Agir avec Détermination

Niveau 2 : Être capable de persévérer et de gérer simultanément plusieurs sources de pression.

Engager et Partenaires

Niveau 2 : Être facilitateur/intégrateur, rassembler les personnes, construire et maintenir des coalitions/partenariats.

Permettre la Diversité et l’Inclusion

Niveau 2 : Faciliter les conversations pour rapprocher les points de vue et tenir compte de la diversité dans la prise de décision.

Gestion du personnel
