the GSF, and other relevant security actors, as required and at the appropriate levels. • Contributes to the development and maintenance of effective liaison and coordination mechanisms between UNSOH, the GSF and other relevant military, police and security counterparts. • Monitors, analyzes and reports on military-related developments that may affect mission support requirements, operational planning and the provision of support to the GSF. • Contributes to the planning and coordination of logistical support for projected GSF military operations, including the identification of support and follow-up. • Prepares and delivers Standard Operation Procedures (SOP), briefings and presentations to mission leadership and relevant stakeholders on military deployments, operational developments and associated mission-support requirements. • Performs other related duties as required. Ability to analyze information from multiple sources and translate operational requirements into clear recommendations and support priorities. Familiarity with data analysis, visualization and decision-support tools is required. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues and counterparts to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places the team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decisions, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Demonstrates the ability to work effectively within a multi-stakeholder environment involving military, police, security and civilian counterparts. Planning and Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments and adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate time and resources for completing work; anticipates operational requirements, risks, dependencies and constraints and provides for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Demonstrates the ability to coordinate multiple interdependent activities in a dynamic operational environment. Managerial Competencies: Judgement/Decision-making: Identifies the key issues in a complex situation and gathers relevant information before making a decision; considers positive and negative impacts of decisions; checks assumptions against facts; determines that the actions proposed will satisfy the expressed and underlying needs for the organization; makes tough decisions when necessary. Education Graduation from a National Command and Staff College is required. Such qualification may be considered in lieu of a first-level university degree, as applicable. An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in international relations, security studies, defence studies, military science, political science, public administration, business administration, logistics, supply chain management, or a related field is highly desirable. A first-level university degree in combination with relevant qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Service as a commissioned military officer, having attained the rank of Army Lieutenant Colonel or an equivalent rank in another military service, is required. Working experience at Ministry of Defence or equivalent strategic nation-level military headquarters is required. Experience in liaison, planning and coordinating logistics support for military operations or deployments in an international peacekeeping operation is required. Experience in planning, coordinating and monitoring the generation, deployment, rotation of military troops and contingent-owned equipment (COE) in a peacekeeping or comparable multinational operational environment is required. Experience in using data analysis and visualization tools, including Power BI Dashboard, to monitor operational or logistics activities and support management decision-making is required. jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The position is located within the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH). UNSOH is also tasked with providing technical assistance to the Organization of American States (OAS). The position is based in Port au Prince and is located in the Life Support Section. The incumbent will report to the Chief Life Support P-5. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Fuel Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Provide effective and timely planning, expert guidance, oversight, management and coordination of mission fuel supply in all phases of operations; • Develop Mission Fuel Plan specifying requirements for fuel and other Petroleum, Oil and Lubricants (POL) products, fuel delivery and distribution assets, storage and dispensing equipment, fuel reserves, other resources, and ensure its implementation; • Plan, coordinate and oversee the work carried out in the Unit determining priorities and allocating resources for the completion and timely delivery of outputs; • Develop, review, monitor, assess and manage outsourced contracts for fuel and associated support services including preparation of Statements of Work, technical evaluations, requisitioning, contract quality control and quality assurance, accounting and invoicing verification;
